author: andrelandgraf
body:
## Breaking change — v2.0.0

This PR bumps `add-mcp` from `1.14.0` to `2.0.0`.

Re-installing a server under an existing name now replaces that server's entire entry instead of deep-merging new fields into the old entry. Callers that relied on omitted fields surviving a re-install must pass the complete desired server configuration.

This fixes invalid hybrid configurations such as stale stdio `command` / `args` / `env` fields remaining beside a new remote `url`. The behavior applies to TOML, JSON, and YAML. Unrelated servers and every other section of the config file are still preserved.

## What changed

- add Grok Build as a first-class agent with `grok-build` and `grok` selectors
- write project config to `.grok/config.toml` and global config to `$GROK_HOME/config.toml`, falling back to `~/.grok/config.toml`
- map stdio, HTTP, and SSE servers to Grok's native `[mcp_servers.<name>]` TOML schema
- preserve headers and `${VAR}` placeholders and map add-mcp timeouts from milliseconds to Grok's `tool_timeout_sec`
- replace an existing server entry atomically when its transport or fields change
- document the breaking replacement contract and Grok Build support in the README, docs, package metadata, changelog, and website

## Why this replaces the earlier PRs

This consolidates and supersedes #78 and #83 on top of current `main`.

#78 established the core Grok Build integration, but its branch became conflicted and the current Grok documentation also requires `$GROK_HOME` support. Direct runtime testing additionally exposed stale fields when reinstalling a server under the same name with a different transport; the atomic replacement work from #83 is included here and released as a documented major-version behavior change.

## Credit

Thank you to @franjorub for the original Grok Build implementation in #78. Francisco's two original commits are preserved in this branch under his GitHub author identity, and the changelog credits him directly.

Thank you to @vishk23 for the atomic replacement fix in #83. That commit is likewise preserved under its original author identity.

## Validation

- `bun run registry:verify` — 1,326 entries verified
- `bun run build`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run test` — 352 tests passed
- real CLI coverage for the `grok` alias, project/global scope, custom `$GROK_HOME`, default fallback, SSE, headers, literal `${VAR}` values, timeout conversion, and both stdio/remote replacement directions
- official Grok Build CLI 0.2.111 smoke test in an isolated temporary home:
  - `grok inspect --json` discovered the generated server and identified its SSE transport
  - `grok mcp list --json` accepted the headers and `tool_timeout_sec = 2`
- full repository Prettier pass in an isolated worktree; every file touched by this PR was unchanged

Implementation follows the current official Grok Build MCP and settings documentation:

- https://docs.x.ai/build/features/mcp-servers
- https://docs.x.ai/build/settings/reference


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added support for Grok Build, including the `grok` alias and project or global installations.
  * Added support for Grok Build remote server settings, headers, and timeouts.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Reinstalling a server now replaces its existing configuration instead of retaining outdated settings.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated supported-agent lists, configuration guidance, aliases, and release notes.
* **Chores**
  * Released version 2.0.0 and streamlined the default test command.

body:
## Summary
Across the app, DB/queries were wrapped in `try { ... } catch (\Exception $e) {}` (or catches with only a comment) that fall back to mock/session data. Before, `includes/db.php` was the *only* place that logged anything — every other failure was swallowed with zero trace, so a real DB outage looked identical to normal preview mode.

This change keeps the intentional mock-data fallback behavior but makes every catch record the failure, so problems are observable in the PHP error log.

- Added a shared logger in `includes/db.php`:
  ```php
  function log_error($context, \Throwable $e) {
      error_log("[deenzorganics] $context: {$e->getMessage()} in {$e->getFile()}:{$e->getLine()}");
  }
  ```
- Instrumented all 20 previously-silent catch blocks with `log_error("<context>", $e)`, e.g. `index.php` featured products, `shop.php` filters, `product.php` (product/review insert/reviews), `cart.php`/`checkout.php` product lookups, `checkout.php` order persistence, `contact.php` message insert, `track.php` order lookup, and the admin add/edit/delete product, save settings, seed DB, review approve/reject/delete, and dashboard/list queries.

No behavior change for end users — the same fallbacks fire; failures are now logged rather than silently dropped. No empty catch blocks remain. All touched files pass `php -l`.

### Note (not changed)
`checkout.php` still returns a "success" screen when the order INSERT fails (design choice for preview robustness); the failure is now logged. Happy to make that surface a real error to the customer if you'd prefer — flagging since it's a genuine correctness concern for production.

author: robobun
body:
## What does this PR do?

`src/js/node/child_process.ts` had four stdio-validation throws that didn't match Node's `getValidStdio()`:

| input | before | Node |
|---|---|---|
| `stdio: ['pipe', new Writable(), 'pipe']` (stream, no fd) | `Error: TODO: stream.Readable stdio @ 1` (no `.code`) | `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE]` |
| `stdio: ['pipe', {foo:1}, 'pipe']` (unrecognized entry) | `Error: Invalid stdio option[1] "[object Object]"` (no `.code`) | `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE]` |
| `stdio: 'bogus'` (unknown top-level string) | `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_OPT_VALUE]` (code removed from Node in v15) | `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE]` |
| `stdio: 42` (non-string, non-array) | `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_OPT_VALUE]` | `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE]` |

User code that branches on `err.code === 'ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE'` or `err instanceof TypeError` was taking the wrong path, and the first message leaked an internal TODO rather than describing the caller's mistake.

## Repro

```js
import cp from 'node:child_process';
import { Writable } from 'node:stream';
try {
  cp.spawn('true', [], { stdio: ['pipe', new Writable({ write(c, e, cb) { cb(); } }), 'pipe'] });
} catch (e) {
  console.log(e.name, e.code, JSON.stringify(e.message.split('\n')[0]));
}
// node : TypeError ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE "The argument 'stdio' is invalid. Received Writable {"
// bun  : Error undefined "TODO: stream.Readable stdio @ 1"
```

## Fix

All four sites now go through `$ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE("stdio", ...)`. The duplicated readable/writable branches in `nodeToBun()` are merged since they did identical work, and the `ERR_INVALID_OPT_VALUE` helper is deleted as dead code. Streams that do carry an fd (an `fs.WriteStream` after `'open'`, `process.stdout`, a numeric fd) are unaffected.

## How did you verify your code works?

Tests in `test/js/node/child_process/child-process-stdio.test.js`: four stream kinds (Writable / Readable / Duplex / PassThrough), a non-stream array entry, an unknown top-level string, and a non-string/non-array top-level value. Each asserts `instanceof TypeError`, `code === 'ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE'`, and the Node-shaped message prefix.

```
bun bd test child-process-stdio.test.js -t ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE   # 7 pass
```

body:
Backlog-only Scout run (no code change; `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` only). Baseline suite was green (1692 passed, 2 skipped) before the run; no code touched.

## QA audit — stacking engine + QC/ingest + webapp pipeline (came back essentially clean)
Deep adversarial read of `seestack/stack/*`, `seestack/calibrate/*`, `seestack/qc/*`, `seestack/io/ingest.py`, and `webapp/pipeline.py`/`watcher.py`/`jobs.py`/`rejection_summary.py`. No verified wrong-result bug found — the hot path (accumulators, quality/photometric weighting, κ-σ & min/max dispatch, align/reproject, drizzle two-pass reject, mosaic canvas, calibrate apply/masters, output↔preview parity, auto recipe) is genuinely hardened. Two reproduced items filed (both low severity, neither corrupts pixels):

- **`webapp/pipeline.py:1411-1412`** — `_auto_stack_frame_count` uses the *newest* stack run of any kind for its `n_frames_used` fallback. A channel-combine / editor-export creates a small-count newest run and doesn't set `AUTO_STACK_ATTEMPT_META_KEY`, so when the marker is absent (pre-marker upgrade data, or after a survivable-error clear) the guard under-counts and redundantly re-stacks unchanged data. Wasted compute + duplicate master row only — no frame loss, no wrong pixels. Fix direction recorded (max-over-runs / skip non-genuine runs).
- **`seestack/qc/streaks.py`** — `streak_count` over-reports one trail as 2–5 collinear PHT segments. Web-invisible today (surfaced only in the historical desktop GUI); doesn't affect stacking or `auto:streak`. Filed in the minor/low-priority bucket.

## Curation
De-duplicated the "Features that serve real workflows" list: five shipped features (v0.161 "What should I shoot next?", v0.160 `.ics` calendar, v0.159.2 "Why were some frames left out?", v0.170 wallpaper, v0.166 "Combine these") each left a stale OPEN copy of their spec under the struck SHIPPED entry — folded each into its SHIPPED entry as provenance so the Builder won't re-discover finished work.

## New ideas
- **Beginner feature:** "Scan to get it on your phone" — client-side QR beside the finished-picture download so a beginner pulls the JPEG to their phone (fits the headless/LAN model; offline; no server dep).
- **Autonomy:** "Try harder to locate these" — a more-sensitive plate-solve re-pass for accepted-but-unsolved subs, attacking the root-cause half of the ⭐⭐ top owner bug (faint-field solve failures → thin gibberish stacks). author: wananing
body:
## Description

Reduce recurring request-time Driver discovery latency in the shared
`AgentBuilder` path:

- serve the last valid MCP capability snapshot immediately after its 10-second
  TTL expires, while refreshing it in a single background task;
- collect cold capabilities from independent Drivers concurrently, with
  cancellation cleanup if one Driver fails;
- cancel an in-flight MCP capability refresh during handler teardown;
- add one INFO-level `perf_counter()` breakdown to the existing
  `builder: built agent` log line.

The new timing fields cover config loading, skill reconciliation, governor
initialization, Driver capability collection, model/Scroll/toolkit/prompt
construction, middleware and agent initialization, state loading, and total
Builder time.

This is implemented at the shared Runtime/Driver layer used by every channel.
It does not add a WeCom-specific workaround, cache mutable agent/session state,
or change the separate Scroll `index_evicted` path.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #6307

**Security Considerations:** Stale capability schemas still go through the
existing invocation-time Driver policy and approval checks. No credentials or
authorization results are cached.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (not needed; no user-facing configuration change)
- [x] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [ ] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes
- [ ] **Contract test** exists in `tests/contract/channels/test_<channel>_contract.py` (REQUIRED)
- [ ] Contract test implements `create_instance()` with proper channel initialization
- [ ] All 19 contract verification points pass (see `tests/contract/channels/__init__.py`)
- [ ] **Optional**: Unit tests in `tests/unit/channels/test_<channel>.py` for complex internal logic

## Testing

The focused tests use blocked fake clients/handlers instead of elapsed-time
thresholds. They prove that:

- an expired MCP snapshot returns while refresh I/O is still blocked;
- stale and cold refreshes are single-flight;
- teardown cancels an active refresh;
- independent Drivers begin discovery concurrently;
- a failed Driver cancels and awaits sibling discovery tasks.

Verification matrix:

- MCP warm cache: unchanged
- MCP expired cache: stale-while-revalidate covered
- MCP cold cache: single-flight covered
- Multiple Drivers: concurrent discovery and failure cleanup covered
- Channels: shared Builder path; no channel-specific changes
- Scroll/native: timing only; context behavior unchanged

## Evidence

```bash
$ pytest tests/unit/drivers tests/unit/runtime -q --no-cov
94 passed in 24.24s

$ pytest \
    tests/integration/test_driver_mcp_approval_level_policy.py \
    tests/integration/test_driver_mcp_env_ref_flow.py \
    tests/integration/test_driver_mcp_http_flow.py \
    tests/integration/test_driver_mcp_oauth_flow.py \
    tests/integration/test_driver_mcp_stdio_flow.py \
    tests/integration/test_driver_workspace_lifecycle.py \
    -q --no-cov
18 passed in 4.66s

$ pre-commit run --files \
    src/qwenpaw/drivers/handlers/mcp.py \
    src/qwenpaw/drivers/manager.py \
    src/qwenpaw/runtime/builder.py \
    tests/unit/drivers/test_capability_discovery.py
# all hooks passed
```

A local synthetic check with two 200 ms Driver providers reduced collection
from 401.2 ms sequentially to 200.6 ms concurrently. Returning an expired
snapshot took 0.02 ms while refresh remained blocked.

`pre-commit run --all-files` passed every hook except full-repository pylint,
which reports four pre-existing `E1120` errors in the unchanged
`src/qwenpaw/sandbox/windows_restricted_sandbox.py` (lines 1822, 1824, 2244,
and 2316). The changed-file pre-commit run above passes pylint.

## Additional Notes

Cold discovery still waits for a valid first snapshot. Once a snapshot exists,
one request may observe it beyond the TTL while the refresh completes; a
failed refresh leaves that last known snapshot available and is logged for the
next retry.

A new **`learning`** plugin whose `self-retro` skill reflects an engineer's own recent work back as a small, evidence-cited, ranked learning plan. **`/learning:self-retro`** — auto-detects its environment:

- **Signals mode** — in a cloud/web routine with no local sessions, builds it from shipped work: GitHub PRs (authored + reviewed), Jira touches, optional Glean docs. Pairs with an LLM wiki (a git-backed Obsidian vault) so each scheduled run leaves a durable, reviewable, pushable report.

author: conormccarter
body:
Two advertised bounds were not real. The step budget was evaluated at the commit boundary — once a commit's record was entered, every delta processed regardless — so a single legal 4,096-operation commit could make a step advertised as 64 MiB read gigabytes, in every deployment mode. And nothing capped how many namespace drivers executed expensive steps concurrently, so a busy multi-namespace server fanned out unbounded object reads while core maintenance next door already had the right idiom.

The budget becomes real through an intra-commit cursor: the manifest's index state gains next_delta_index alongside the watermark — omitted when zero, so the schema change is additive within version one and zero-valued fixtures stay byte-identical — and budgets are enforced per delta, publishing the exact resume position mid-commit when they trip. The correctness crux is the tail: a query now scans the watermark commit's remaining delta suffix plus everything after, preserving exact semantics on both sides of the cursor — a mid-commit freeze test greps 1,000 files and finds each exactly once, indexed prefix and unindexed remainder alike — and an out-of-range cursor reports index_corrupt rather than clamping. The 1,000-file atomic commit now indexes in exactly two steps of 500 objects each, and crash-resume proves disjoint reads with unchanged prefix segments.

Concurrency follows core's max_concurrent idiom: one shared FIFO permit owned by the driver machinery and cloned across both hosts, held only during build/fold execution — parked drivers hold nothing, ownership and wakeups stay per-namespace. One new zero-rejected [grep] knob, max_concurrent_steps, defaulting to core maintenance's value; eight namespaces under a cap of two peaked at exactly two while all converged. No LSM, posting, or result-semantics changes anywhere.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Security scan of the codebase found the app was generally sound (PDO prepared statements everywhere, CSRF tokens on POST actions, `sanitize_html()` on echoed input, `FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL` on contact/checkout). The **critical** problems were all committed secrets and a hardcoded admin login. This PR fixes those; remaining lower-severity items are listed below for follow-up.

### Fixed (critical)

**1. Hardcoded fallback secrets in `includes/db.php`**
Real-looking DB password and Razorpay key/secret were baked in as fallbacks, so they lived in source control:
```php
- define('DB_PASS', getenv('DB_PASS') !== false ? getenv('DB_PASS') : 'A[kvsmv8c)TEG0QJ');
- define('RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET', getenv(...) ?: 'sk_test_kashOrganicsSecretKeyKey');
+ define('DB_PASS', getenv('DB_PASS') !== false ? getenv('DB_PASS') : '');
+ define('RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET', getenv('RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET') ?: '');
```
Secrets now come only from the environment; no dangerous defaults.

**2. Hardcoded admin credentials in `admin/index.php`**
Login accepted the fixed pair `admin` / `admin123` (also printed on the login page). Replaced with env-driven, hashed verification that **fails closed** when unconfigured:
```php
function verify_admin_credentials($u, $p) {
    if (ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH === '') return false;      // no default -> no access
    return hash_equals(ADMIN_USERNAME, $u) && password_verify($p, ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH);
}
```
`ADMIN_USERNAME` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH` (a `password_hash()` value) come from the environment. The login page no longer displays default credentials.

**3. Secrets seeded in `database.sql`**
The `settings` seed stored the Razorpay key/secret and the `admins` seed shipped a bcrypt hash with the plaintext password disclosed in a comment. Payment creds are now empty (read from env), and the admin hash is a `REPLACE_WITH_BCRYPT_HASH` placeholder with generation instructions.

**4. Secret-leak prevention**
Added `.gitignore` (ignores `.env*`, keeps `.env.example`) and `.env.example` documenting all required vars.

### Not fixed — recommended follow-ups (need product decisions / secrets)

- **Payment verification gap** (`checkout.php`): the order is marked `paid` using a client-supplied `razorpay_payment_id` with no server-side Razorpay signature/HMAC verification, so payment success can be forged. Fixing properly requires the live Razorpay secret and the order/verify API flow.
- **No brute-force protection** on the admin login (no rate limiting / lockout).
- **Host header trust** (`includes/header.php`): `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']` is echoed into JSON-LD unescaped; low impact but should use a configured canonical host.
- **Rotate the exposed secrets**: the DB password and Razorpay test secret that were in git history should be rotated regardless of this change.

### Notes
- No dependency manifest (`composer.json`/`package.json`) exists, so no vulnerable dependencies to audit; front-end libs load from CDNs.
- No CORS headers, debug endpoints, `eval`/`system`, or SQL string interpolation were found.
- All PHP files pass `php -l`; new admin auth verified at runtime (correct password passes; `admin123` and unconfigured both rejected).

author: ons96
body:
Resolves the standing `--no-verify` workaround on every push to this repo.

## What
- Add `.gitleaks/config.toml` (singular `[allowlist]` with `paths`) allowlisting 39 manually-verified false-positives so the pre-push hook passes on a plain `git push`.
- Remove tracked `config/virtual_models.yaml.bak` (matched .gitignore `*.bak` but was committed anyway; stale vs live config).

## Why each FP is benign (verified 2026-07-23)
- `config/virtual_models.yaml*`, `render.yaml`: env-var **names** (`api_key_env: G4F_GROQ_API_KEY`, `- key: MISTRAL_API_KEY_1`), not values.
- `.env.example`: literal placeholder `YOUR_PROXY_API_KEY`.
- `*_auth_base.py` CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET: **public** OAuth installed-app secrets (qwen/gemini/antigravity/iflow CLI clients) — public-by-design per RFC 8252, ship inside open-source CLI binaries.
- `ai_output_raw.txt`, `conftest.py`, `docs/iflow_auth_flow_extracted.md`: history-only (deleted), redacted logs / env-name fixtures.

## gotcha documented for future
gitleaks 8.21 **silently ignores** the plural `[[allowlists]]` array form in git-mode (`--log-opts`) history scans; only the singular `[allowlist]` table suppresses. This is why earlier attempts left 46 findings.

## Verify
`git push` (no --no-verify) → hook scans 969 commits → 0 leaks → push_rc=0. Confirmed.

Closes #423

author: eugenelim
body:
## Summary

- Introduces `apps/infra-tf/` as the Terraform root module skeleton (tier 1 of 5 in the CDK→Terraform migration, ADR-0010)
- Implements `versions.tf`, `provider.tf`, `backend.tf`, `variables.tf`, `outputs.tf`, `backend.hcl.example`, and `scripts/bootstrap.sh`
- No AWS resources provisioned; all 12 outputs are `null` stubs filled by subsequent specs

## Key decisions

**`use_lockfile = true` in `backend.tf`** — native S3 state locking (Terraform ≥ 1.11) requires explicit opt-in; omitting it means no locking at all despite the ADR's intent.

**`invoker_role_arn` validation** — ARN is validated as a role ARN at plan time, rejecting root/wildcard/non-role principals. This ARN scopes the Function URL invoke permission (ADR-0004 boundary) so a typo here widens access before any resource is provisioned.

**Idempotent bootstrap hardening** — `bootstrap.sh` applies versioning, public-access-block, SSE-S3 encryption, and TLS-only bucket policy on every run (not just on creation), so pre-existing buckets without those controls are hardened on re-run.

**AC4b verified in-PR** — `terraform plan` with invalid `s3_prefix_list_id` (CIDR) and invalid `invoker_role_arn` (root principal) both exit 1 via local-backend override, not deferred.

## Test plan

- [x] `terraform fmt -check -recursive .` exits 0
- [x] `terraform init -backend=false && terraform validate` exits 0
- [x] 12 output stubs declared (`grep -c 'output "' outputs.tf` = 12)
- [x] `terraform plan` with `s3_prefix_list_id=0.0.0.0/0` → exit 1
- [x] `terraform plan` with `invoker_role_arn=...:root` → exit 1
- [x] `terraform plan` with valid values → exit 0 ("No changes")
- [x] `bootstrap.sh` executable bit tracked (mode 100755)

## Bundled fixes

- `docs/adr/0003-iac-tool-aws-cdk-python.md` status → `Superseded by ADR-0010` (CONVENTIONS.md § 2 requires status field update on supersession)
- `.gitignore`: added `.terraform/`, `backend.hcl`, `*.tfvars`, `*.tfstate`, `*.tfstate.*` for the new Terraform module

author: mantasindrasius
body:
## Summary

Extracts build-target serving into a **new `tddy-bsp` crate** exposing **`bsp.BspService`** — a Build Server Protocol–*shaped* RPC service over the existing protobuf/Connect (`/rpc`) + LiveKit transports (**not** JSON-RPC 2.0; external BSP clients like Metals/IntelliJ are out of scope). Methods: `WorkspaceBuildTargets`, `BuildTargetSources`, `BuildTargetOutputPaths`, `WorkspaceReload`, `BuildTarget{Compile,Test,Run}`.

### What changed
- **`tddy-build`** — `BuildTarget` gains author-declarable `tags`/`languages`/`capabilities` (type-derived when omitted, via new `capabilities.rs` `resolve_target_metadata`); a `BuildMode {Compile,Test,Run}` is threaded through `plugin`/`lower`/`execute_target`/`service::build_json`. Compile behaviour is unchanged; test/run are capability-gated.
- **`tddy-build-rust` / `tddy-build-typescript`** — `lower_mode` emits `cargo test`/`cargo run` and `bun run test`/`start`; other plugins are compile-only.
- **`tddy-core`** — session catalog gains a dedicated typed **`build_targets`** table + `BuildTargetSummary` + `list_build_targets[_for_package]`, written in the same populate transaction as the JSON catalog; enriched `BuildTargetCatalogEntry` + `CatalogCapabilities`.
- **`tddy-bsp`** (new) — `BspServiceImpl`, the enriched `BuildCatalogProvider` (moved from `tddy-coder`; derives sources/outputs by lowering each target), `plugin_registry`, and `to_bsp_target`.
- **`tddy-coder`** — registers `bsp.BspService` (per-session `BspServiceImpl`) on the session participant's LiveKit surface; `build_executor` delegates to `tddy_bsp::plugin_registry`; `catalog_provider.rs` removed.
- **`tddy-service`** — new `proto/bsp.proto` + codegen/descriptor wiring; request messages carry optional `session_token`/`session_id`.
- **`tddy-daemon`** — session-addressed `DaemonBspService` resolves each request's `(session_token, session_id)` → worktree + catalog dir and delegates per-request; registered in `rpc_entries`. Reflection advertises the surface automatically.

## Test plan
Scoped, per-package verification (the branch's other history is already on `master`):
- `cargo test` green: `tddy-bsp` (lib 4 + acceptance 5), `tddy-daemon` `bsp_service` (2), `tddy-build` (incl. capabilities 4), `tddy-build-rust` (incl. modes 2), `tddy-build-typescript`, `tddy-core` (274 lib, incl. build_targets round-trip 2).
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean: the six logic crates (`--all-targets`) + `tddy-coder`/`tddy-daemon` (lib+bins).
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `tddy-coder` + `tddy-daemon` build clean.

## Follow-ups (tracked in `docs/dev/TODO.md`)
- Per-session cache for the daemon's per-request `BspServiceImpl`.
- Provider lowering failures are currently swallowed to empty sources/outputs (no `log` dep on `tddy-bsp`).
- Unify the shared `catalog` build_target rows with `build_targets` via a view; structured diagnostics; remaining BSP methods; streaming progress.

author: adv11
body:
## What
`feedbackModal.js`'s `renderForm` (complexity 17) and `gatherFormValues` (complexity 15) were the highest-complexity pair in the codebase outside `roadmapStore.js` (issue #281). This PR extracts named, module-scope helpers to bring both under the ESLint `complexity: 10` gate.

## How
Pure structural refactor — no behavior change, no user-facing copy touched:

- **`gatherFormValues`**: its complexity came from seven repeated `field?.getValue() || null` reads. Collapsed into one `readFieldValue(field)` helper; each call site is now complexity 1.
- **`renderForm`**: its complexity came from (a) a nested title-placeholder ternary chain and (b) an `if (type === 'bug') { ... } else if (type === 'feature') { ... } else { ... }` block building each feedback type's fields inline. Extracted:
  - `resolveTitlePlaceholder(type)` — replaces the ternary chain.
  - `applyRadioPrefill(radioGroupField, value)` — the repeated "find and check a prefilled radio option" logic (previously duplicated for `severity` and `usageFreq`).
  - `buildBugTypeFields`/`buildFeatureTypeFields`/`buildFeedbackTypeFields`, dispatched via `buildTypeFields(type, opts)` — replace the inline per-type field-construction branches. Each returns `{ fields, ...namedFieldRefs }`, destructured back into `renderForm`'s local scope so every downstream reference (`gatherFormValues`, `handleSubmit`, etc.) is unchanged.

Field construction order, prefill values, placeholders, and every string literal are preserved exactly.

## Testing
- `npx eslint src/ui/components/feedbackModal.js --format json` — **before**: `renderForm` complexity 17 (line 128), `gatherFormValues` complexity 15 (line 183). **After**: neither function is flagged for complexity at all. Only the pre-existing, out-of-scope `max-lines-per-function` warnings remain (unchanged in kind, and `renderForm`'s own line count dropped from 163 to 129).
- `npm test` (unit + integration, 1258 tests) — all pass, including the existing `feedbackModal`/`feedbackForm` suites, unmodified.
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors, 28 warnings (down from the pre-PR baseline; none for this file's complexity).

## Docs updated
- `CHANGELOG.md` — added an entry under `[Unreleased]` → `### Changed`, matching the precedent set by #319's identical-shaped refactor for issue #279.
- `CLAUDE.md`/`.claude/rules/*.md`/`docs/architecture.md`: not applicable — pure internal refactor, no new file, no contract change, no convention change.
- `sw.js`'s `CACHE_VERSION` bumped (34 → 35) since this touches `src/`.

## Judgment calls
- My worktree's local `main` ref was stale (5 commits behind `origin/main`) when I started, so my first attempt branched off the wrong base and duplicated CHANGELOG/CACHE_VERSION work already merged in #319 (which also touched this file's neighbor, `feedbackForm.js`, and explicitly left `feedbackModal.js`'s pair for this issue). Rebased onto the correct `origin/main` base before finishing; final diff only touches `feedbackModal.js`, `sw.js`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Kept the returned-object destructuring in `renderForm` (`const { severityField, ... } = typeFields;`) without default values — a field absent for a given type resolves to `undefined` rather than the original code's `null`, which is behaviorally identical everywhere it's read (`field?.getValue()`, `field?.setError(...)`, array `.forEach(f => f?.setError(...))`) since optional chaining treats both the same way.

Closes #281

author: mcguinness
body:
Milestone M7 per PLAN.md § 5. Exit criterion met: **scenarios 6 (DTR) and 7 (Transaction Challenge) pass; issued tokens never broaden the originating request and never outlive `approved_until`.** 84/84 total, typecheck + lint clean. Pins O-3/O-4/O-5.

## Both bindings complete through Mission Expansion (D6)
This is the token-issuance completion mode — the deliberate contrast with M6's ARAP reevaluate (no new token). Both realize the approved request as a **successor Mission**:
- **Mission Expansion** (`kernel/expansion.ts`): successor from a fresh approval with a `predecessor` lineage member on both claim and record; successor expiry **bounded by `approved_until`** (never outlives it); predecessor must be active; predecessor → `superseded` atomically on the successor's first grant redemption.
- **AROP / DTR** (`kernel/deferred.ts`): `completion_mode=deferred` → requestable denial → `deferral_code` + `authorization_pending`; **idempotent submission** (same request → same handle); poll stays pending; on approval the expansion issues the successor mission claim; single redemption.
- **AROP / Transaction Challenge** (`kernel/txn-challenge.ts`): the RS signs the challenge (`txn`/`authorization_details`/`iss`=resource/`aud`=AS/`reason`) with its `rs-txn` key; the AS validates it against the RS `txn_challenge_jwks_uri` and issues a **txn-bound, audience-restricted, single-use** token; the RS honors the `txn` exactly once.

## Invariants proven
Authority widens only via a fresh approval; the successor token's `exp` equals `approved_until`; the txn token is single-use on re-presentation; the predecessor is superseded on first redemption.

Both bindings are implemented at the kernel + token level with the HTTP grant/endpoint as the production surface (O-33 precedent). SPEC_VERSIONS +4 rows (expansion, AROP, DTR, txn-challenge). PLAN.md status follows on main.

author: aminchirazi
body:
Independent of #101 (touches only `toolcalls.rs` and `agent_steps.rs`, both already on main). Completes the `assert_tool_call` argument vocabulary.

```yaml
- assert_tool_call: book where seat matches [0-9]+[A-F]
```

For an argument whose **shape** is the contract but whose value is volatile — a seat, a formatted id, a rendered date — `matches` tests it against a regular expression. `equals` and `contains` could never express "this format, any value", which is exactly the case the design doc called out (`seat: { matches: "[0-9]+[A-F]" }`).

## Two correctness choices

- **Validated at parse time.** A broken pattern is a spec error named where it was written (`` `[unclosed` is not a valid pattern ``), not a failure at replay against a live trajectory.
- **The matcher stays total.** It compiles per check and reports an invalid pattern rather than panicking — a `Regex` is not `Clone`/`PartialEq`/`Serialize`, so the expectation stores the pattern string and compiles on use.

## No dependency cost

`regex` was already in the lockfile (v1.13.1, pulled transitively), so this adds nothing to the build — the same reasoning that put `ureq` behind the `agent` feature. It's wired into the workspace deps and the two crates that use it.

## Testing

Matcher: a seat and an id matched by pattern, a mismatch reported with the value shown, and an invalid pattern reported rather than panicking. Grammar: the prose form parses, and a broken pattern is rejected at parse time.

Still deferred by the same design fence: the structured `args:` form and per-call result sequences.

🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The `X-API-Key` was being validated using insecure `==` and `!=` operators in `backend/app/api/v1/router.py` and `backend/app/api/v1/lgpd_direitos.py`.
🎯 Impact: Using standard string equality operators for secrets allows for timing attacks, where an attacker can guess a secret byte by byte based on the response time.
🔧 Fix: Replaced string equality operators with `hmac.compare_digest` for constant-time comparison.
✅ Verification: Ran unit tests and validated via `git diff` that `hmac.compare_digest` is used.

author: matute289
body:
## BL-82 EM-8.3b — sim-side outgoing-message capture hook (chat/outcome/dialogue bridge for the real dedicated server)

Closes the ledger's remaining **Part A1** items EM-8.3 (PR #190) could not: `ChatBridgePlugin`
(chat broadcast), `SfxOutcomeBridgePlugin` (outcome→SFX), and social's NPC→player dialogue capture
were all listen-server-only because they read `EmbeddedPlayer`'s own inbox — a mechanism a real
dedicated-server (`xindeler-server-app`) replicon-login player never has. Also folds in the small
adjacent Part A2 item: terrain-chunk `SendTargets::All` per-client interest.

### What changed

**New sim-side capture hook** (`server/src/msg_capture.rs`, non-Bevy, `specs::Resource`):
`OutgoingMessageCapture` — `Uid`-keyed (the SAME identity `xindeler_protocol::ActiveReplicaSessions`
already correlates to a real `ClientId`, EM-8.2), append-only during a tick, drained wholesale by the
bevy-side bridge. Registered in `Server::new` so it exists on every shell (the listen server's buffer
just stays empty — its one player always has a legacy `comp::Client`).

**Three sim call sites ALSO push into it** for recipients that have no legacy `comp::Client`
(never *instead of* the existing `Client` send — a `Client`-having recipient's path is unchanged):
- `StateExt::send_chat` (`server/src/state_ext.rs`) — every per-recipient arm reworked via a new
  `deliver_chat` helper (Say/Region/Npc/NpcSay/Faction/Group/Kill's radius branch, all now join on
  `Uid`+`Player` mandatory with `Client` optional instead of `Client` mandatory; Tell/NpcTell/Group's
  error-reply resolve the recipient directly by uid) plus a `capture_chat_for_clientless_players`
  helper for the broadcast arms (alongside the existing `notify_players` call, unchanged).
- `entity_sync::Sys::run`'s outcome-sync loop (`server/src/sys/entity_sync.rs`) — the join changed
  from mandatory `&clients` to `Uid`+`Player` mandatory, `Client` optional; a `Client`-less recipient's
  already-radius-filtered outcomes are captured instead of sent to a socket.
- The `DialogueEvent` handler (`server/src/events/interaction.rs`) — captures keyed by the
  RECIPIENT's uid, not the NPC sender's.

**Bevy-side bridge** (`bevy/xindeler-sim-bridge`): `broadcast_captured_chat` (chat.rs),
`broadcast_captured_outcomes` (sfx.rs), `broadcast_captured_dialogue` (social.rs) — each drains the
capture buffer, resolves `Uid -> ClientId` via `ActiveReplicaSessions`, and targets
`SendTargets::Single` — an uncorrelated recipient is DROPPED, never routed to a guessed fallback
(unlike `crate::social::resolve_recipient_targets`'s `SERVER_ONLY` fallback, which only makes sense
for the listen server's one embedded player). Registered alongside the pre-existing
listen-server-only `broadcast_embedded_*`/`mirror_dialogue` systems in the same plugins
(`ChatBridgePlugin`/`SfxOutcomeBridgePlugin`/`SocialMirrorPlugin`), which are now ALSO registered on
`xindeler-server-app` (`plugin.rs`).

**Terrain-chunk `SendTargets::All` per-client interest** (`bevy/xindeler-sim-bridge/src/lib.rs`):
`resolve_terrain_targets` scopes each streamed chunk to the real connected clients whose
`ClientVisibleRegions` (EM-4.2d, reused here for a one-shot MESSAGE type it wasn't originally built
for) covers it, unioned with the listen server's embedded player. **Falls back to the exact
pre-existing `SendTargets::All` broadcast whenever NO client has any interest data yet** (the listen
server never populates `ClientVisibleRegions` at all) — so the existing persister-only
local-loopback sanity test (`streams_real_chunks_to_local_client`) stays green, unchanged.

### Tests
- `server::msg_capture` — capture/drain roundtrip, drain-clears-buffer, multi-recipient attribution,
  three-buffers-independent.
- `xindeler-sim-bridge::chat` — a real `StateExt::send_chat` `Say` call end-to-end: an in-range
  `comp::Client`-less recipient is captured + relayed to its own `ClientId`; an out-of-range one gets
  nothing.
- `xindeler-sim-bridge::sfx` — a captured outcome relays only to its correlated client; an
  uncorrelated recipient is dropped, never guessed.
- `xindeler-sim-bridge::social` — a captured dialogue turn relays only to its correlated recipient;
  a second, uncorrelated recipient never receives it.
- `xindeler-sim-bridge` (lib.rs) — `resolve_terrain_targets`: no-interest-data falls back to `All`;
  once real interest data exists, only the covering client (never a non-covering one) + the embedded
  player are targeted.

### Gates — all green
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked --features="bin_compression,bin_csv,bin_graphviz,bin_bot,bin_asset_migrate,bin,stat,cli" -- -D warnings`
- `./scripts/check-engine-isolation.sh`
- `VELOREN_ASSETS="$(pwd)/assets" cargo test -p xindeler-server-core --lib` — 25/0
- `VELOREN_ASSETS="$(pwd)/assets" cargo test -p xindeler-sim-bridge --lib -- --test-threads=1` — 123/0 (21 ignored, real-boot tests)
- `VELOREN_ASSETS="$(pwd)/assets" cargo test -p xindeler-server-app` — all pass except
  `interest_management_scoping_boundary_and_bandwidth`, which I confirmed **also fails identically on
  a freshly-checked-out, completely unmodified `origin/development`** under the current (very high,
  ~40 load average) local system load — a real-socket test with a hardcoded 30s connect deadline,
  the exact same pre-existing local-environment flake EM-8.3 (PR #190) already documented for this
  same test. This test doesn't even import anything from `xindeler-sim-bridge`/`server` (only
  `xindeler_protocol`/`xindeler_transport`), so it cannot exercise this diff's code paths.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`

### Docs
- `docs/design/specs/2026-07-18-bl82-technical-debt-ledger.md` — Part A1/A2 marked closed (pushed
  directly to the private design repo per repo convention, not part of this PR's diff).

author: dammnthatscrazy
body:
## 1. Intent

PR-0 established the integration consent control-plane registry and storage surfaces. This PR wires those surfaces into runtime authority so connector enablement, connector sync, and SDK canonical consent receipt writes fail closed through tenant/admin/provider policy instead of bypassing the registry.

## 2. Changed surfaces

- Apps: no direct Aether or Kyber UI changes.
- Services: backend consent authority, consent routes, integration connector registry/routes/service, integration consent policy facade.
- Packages: shared generated privacy integration-consent Python artifact import behavior.
- APIs/routes: `POST /v1/consent/records` now accepts an additive `canonical_receipt` envelope while preserving legacy fields; connector enable/sync paths evaluate the consent control plane when feature flags are enabled.
- Schemas/models: added typed runtime models/repositories for tenant processing profiles, integration policy manifests, connector policy decisions, and consent receipt history.
- Graph/event behavior: no graph projection changes.
- SDKs: no emitted SDK API change in this PR; SDK receipt emission is a follow-up PR.
- CI/workflows: no workflow changes.
- Docs: source-of-truth integration consent registry doc updated for runtime gating, canonical hash, and idempotency behavior.
- Config/env: added default-off integration consent rollout flags.
- Migrations: no new migration; this consumes PR-0 migration tables.
- Generated files/lockfiles: regenerated `generated_integration_consent.py` through the contract generator; no lockfile changes.

## 3. Behavior changes

- Connector enablement and sync can now be blocked by registry-derived governance policy when `AETHER_CONSENT_CONTROL_PLANE_V2` and `AETHER_CONNECTOR_POLICY_GATE` are enabled.
- Generic/high-risk connectors remain fail-closed unless tenant/admin/provider policy, purpose, processing basis, and field allowlists are explicit.
- Canonical consent receipts can be posted as a multi-purpose envelope; the server validates the deterministic receipt id, integrity hash, idempotency key, subject/tenant consistency, and purpose set before persisting one authoritative row per purpose plus append-only history.
- Legacy consent receipt writes remain supported.

## 4. Aether/Kyber impact

- Aether tenant-facing intelligence graph: no direct graph behavior change.
- Kyber internal operator console: no UI change; runtime decisions create persisted decision evidence for later operator surfaces.
- Backend graph/enrichment/orchestration systems: connector runtime paths are now gateable by consent policy before processing.
- SDK/event ingestion: no batch ingestion behavior change; canonical receipt write support prepares SDK receipt emission.
- Tenant data isolation: control-plane repositories and receipt persistence preserve tenant-scoped records.
- Internal-only operator controls: policy gates remain default-off until rollout flags are explicitly enabled.

## 5. Security and tenancy review

Auth/RBAC were not loosened. Tenant isolation is preserved by tenant-scoped repositories and tenant/subject validation on canonical receipt writes. The new connector gate is fail-closed for missing policy, missing admin approval, missing provider install approval, unapproved purposes, unapproved processing bases, and unallowlisted payload fields. PII handling is tightened by policy allowlists and canonical receipt evidence. Secrets are not added. Cross-tenant visibility is not introduced. Compliance behavior changes only behind default-off rollout flags.

## 6. Tests and validation

- `python3 -m pytest -o addopts='' 'Backend Architecture/aether-backend/tests/contracts/test_integration_consent_runtime.py' 'Backend Architecture/aether-backend/tests/contracts/test_integration_consent_registry.py' 'Backend Architecture/aether-backend/tests/contracts/test_consent_control_plane_migration.py' -q` — 8 passed.
- `python3 scripts/generate_contracts.py --check` — passed.

author: refined-element
body:
## Ledger #42 — pin fail-closed on unbounded MPP amounts

**Decision (human-made):** an L402 client must REFUSE an invoice whose amount can't be positively bounded. An MPP `amount=0` (or `<=0`) resolving onto an amountless invoice is a **blank cheque** — the wallet, not the server, picks the spend.

### Assessment: this port already refuses (keep it, make it explicit)
The client prices a request purely from the BOLT11 invoice (`extractAmountSats(challenge.invoice)`) and **never reads the MPP `amount` param**. So an amountless invoice is unbounded (`null`) regardless of any MPP amount, and the request hits the existing `InvoiceAmountUnknownError` refusal. `amount=0` is refused today as a side effect of that design — the safe outcome for #42.

That safety was implicit and untested. This PR pins it explicitly:
- `refuses an MPP challenge with amount=0 on an amountless invoice (ledger #42)` — asserts `InvoiceAmountUnknownError` (reason `no-amount-encoded`, bolt11 `lnbc1ptest`), no payment attempted, nothing logged.

### Explicitly out of scope (deferred)
- **#72** — reading/paying MPP `amount` on amountless invoices (what Python/.NET do). NOT added here.
- **#73** — currency handling. NOT touched.

### Verification
- Suite: **156 → 157 passing**, no regressions.
- Mutation: adding a naive #72-style MPP-amount fallback (no positivity guard) makes the client accept `amount=0` and fails this test, then reverted. Confirms the test pins #42.

No source change, no version bump, not for publish.

author: herenderkumar
body:
## Summary

`build()`'s docstring promises a key-wise union for same-ID nodes, but on the default extract path `deduplicate_entities()` runs first and collapses a same-ID collision by keeping one whole dict and discarding the other. Any attribute the loser carried and the survivor did not — `summary`, `confidence_score` — is gone before NetworkX ever performs the union.

This is exactly the AST↔semantic reconciliation the pipeline exists for: `_semantic_id_remap` forces the AST node and the LLM node onto the same ID so they merge, and the merge then throws away the LLM's contribution the user paid API credits for. The loss is silent — the only output is a `note:` about the *label*, which never mentions that `summary`/`confidence_score` were dropped. `dedup=True` is hard-coded on the CLI path, so this is every `graphify extract` run with a semantic pass.

## Fix

`graphify/dedup.py` — the survivor still wins conflicting keys (so `_collision_rank` ordering and the collision reporting that reads the survivor's own `label`/`source_file` are unchanged), but the loser's *disjoint* keys are now gap-filled via `setdefault` rather than discarded. Storing `dict(node)` for each survivor also stops the caller's input node dicts from being mutated in place.

## Reproduction (from the issue), after the fix

```
dedup=False label='User login handler'   summary='Authenticates a user.' score=0.9
dedup=True  label='login'                summary='Authenticates a user.' score=0.9
```

`dedup=True` now yields at least the attribute set `dedup=False` yields, with the survivor's values winning on genuine conflicts (`label='login'`). Previously `dedup=True` returned `summary=None score=None`.

## Test

`tests/test_dedup.py::test_same_id_merge_preserves_losers_disjoint_attributes` — a same-ID AST/semantic pair with disjoint attributes; asserts the survivor keeps its own `label`/`source_location` on conflicts **and** gap-fills the loser's `summary`/`confidence_score`. Written test-first (failed on `None`, passes after the fix). Full `tests/test_dedup.py` suite green (45 passed); `test_build.py`, `test_semantic_id_remap_root.py`, and `test_export.py` unaffected.

Closes #2091

## What's new

- **`/slots`** — capacity time-slots / class sizes. author: ray-cabrera
body:
**KRY-541** — surfaced during Backend Review Track 5 (finding P). Race-proofs **every** cap trigger. Both migrations **applied + verified on prod `kzsfibg…` 2026-07-23** (all 8 functions confirmed to carry a lock).

## Bug
Caps are **live for all users** (the tier ladder is not gated by `billingLive()` — `entitlements.ts:278`) and the DB cap triggers enforce unconditionally. But they do a non-atomic `count → check → insert` in a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger. Under READ COMMITTED, two concurrent inserts each see `count < cap`, both pass → the cap is exceeded. Low severity (needs concurrency), but current.

## Fix
Serialize the enforcing path with a lock, added to each function (recreated **verbatim from the live prod def** + the lock line only):
- **User-scoped caps** → `perform 1 from public.kr_users where id = new.user_id for update;`
- **Non-user-scoped caps** (per-thread, per-email) → `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(<scope key>))`

## Coverage (all cap triggers)
- `20260723040000` — follow caps: `kr_fund_follow_enforce_cap`, `kr_enforce_follow_cap` (watchlist), `kr_investor_follow_enforce_cap`
- `20260723040100` — the rest: `kr_enforce_user_row_cap` (one function → **8 tables**: notes, saved views, annotations, ask/research threads+messages, mark shares), `kr_enforce_alert_rule_cap`, `kr_enforce_model_scenario_cap`, `kr_enforce_thread_msg_cap` (advisory), `kr_enforce_inquiry_cap` (advisory)

author: jimmyejones
body:
## What & why

A new beginner feature that celebrates a user's finest results across **every**
target in one place — the "look what I made" moment no existing card covered
(Gallery/History/cover are all per-target; Share exports a single picture). After
a few months a Seestar owner has a dozen targets and wants to see their collection
as a body of work, without clicking into each one. Serves the *enjoy + share*
pillar (PRIORITY 3). From the top of `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` → "Features that serve
real workflows".

## Changes

- **Engine** (`seestack/portfolio.py`, new): pure, unit-tested
  `rank_portfolio(entries, *, limit)` + `PortfolioEntry`/`RankedEntry`. Scores each
  target's representative stack on a transparent blend — `PORTFOLIO_WEIGHTS` =
  integration 0.40 / frames 0.25 / noise 0.25 / coverage 0.10 — with every metric
  normalised against the best value *in the user's own collection* (no absolute
  calibration needed), noise scored lower-is-better (`min σ / σ`), and each score
  **renormalised over only the metrics an entry carries** so an old run missing
  `noise_sigma`/`total_exposure_s` is never penalised for the null. Fully
  deterministic ordering (score → integration → frames → key).
- **Webapp** (`webapp/routers/gallery.py`): read-only `GET /api/gallery/best?limit=`
  — each target's newest run with a preview on disk, ranked, returned with the
  ranking `score`. Wraps every `Project.open` in the established
  `except Exception: continue` guard (a broken/rolled-back project is skipped, never
  500s the wall) and **self-hides** below two finished pictures.
- **Frontend**: a `/best` "My best pictures" wall (new nav entry) with a quiet
  #1–#3 rank chip and a plain-language "why it's good" line (e.g. "3.4 h · 500
  frames"), plus a compact **self-hiding Dashboard strip** above Recent stacks. One
  click reuses the existing `ImageLightbox` (download / JPEG / share / scan-to-phone
  / wallpaper).

## Upgrade-safety

Read-only aggregation over columns that already exist — no schema/config/API-shape
change, no default flip, new surface off-by-default (self-hiding). `webapp/static/`
is not committed.

## Tests

- `tests/test_portfolio.py` (+10): ordering, tie-breaks, missing-metric fallbacks,
  single-entry, order-independence, truncation.
- `tests/webapp/test_gallery_best.py` (+5): self-hide floor, deep-cleaner-first
  ranking, newest-per-target, limit, broken-project skip.
- `frontend/.../bestPictures.test.ts` (+5), `BestPictures.test.tsx` (+2).

Full Python suite green (1716 passed, 2 skipped) on the tree merged with the latest
`origin/main`; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx vite build` succeeds.

body: ## Problem Signup did not show API errors to users. `submitSignup()` always returned JSON without checking `response.ok`, so the catch block in the signup form never ran. When the backend returned SQL or technical errors, users saw nothing — or raw database messages. ## Fix - **Client**: `submitSignup` throws on HTTP errors, `success: false`, or missing dashboard link - **UI**: Shows a red error banner and per-field messages (email, company name, tax ID) - **Localization**: French for GN/SN/CI, English for US — including friendly messages for duplicates and technical failures - **Server**: `/api/signup` sanitizes upstream API responses before sending to the browser (SQL errors never exposed raw) ## User-facing error examples (FR) - Duplicate email → "Cet email est déjà enregistré..." - SQL/500 → "Impossible de finaliser l'inscription pour le moment..." - Laravel validation → field-specific messages under the input

author: hututuqqq
body:
## Summary

- harden broker-journaled Git recovery, selection evidence, transaction sealing, approval handling, and Harbor adapter behavior
- recognize compiler, Python, strict shell, Coq, COBOL, and TeX validation evidence against the current mutation frontier
- make tool-argument protocol repair and no-progress convergence deterministic without task-specific behavior
- mount standard Linux runtime state read-only so sandboxed compilers can load system data
- force terminal projection when deadline convergence begins and give the independent reviewer bounded snapshots of goal-referenced workspace reads

## Root cause

Several generic runtime policies did not compose correctly: repository recovery evidence could lose required state, corrected multi-call tool batches were projected as single-call repairs, successful semantic checks were classified as probes, deadline convergence was advisory rather than enforceable, and the reviewer lacked immutable reference-file content needed to check cross-file constraints.

## Impact

The agent can recover Git state safely, execute corrected tool batches, recognize meaningful validation, use system compiler data inside the sandbox, terminate before deadline exhaustion, and review constrained changes with better evidence. Evaluation permissions remain automatic while execution stays sandboxed and network-isolated.

## Validation

- `pnpm typecheck`

- related Vitest suites: 145 unique tests passed; 30 intentionally skipped; one timing-sensitive queue test was rerun alone and passed

author: takeyuweb
body:
## 概要

ADR 検索の評価・改善基盤を導入する。検索の取り逃がし（返るべき ADR が返らない）を観測する手段がなく、SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-27 の再評価条件「取り逃がしの頻発」が点検不能だった問題に対応する。

設計判断は ADR 管理サーバーに登録済み:

- **SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-38**: 検索ログ・取り逃がし報告・ゴールデンクエリ回帰の3段構成を採用（全検索へのエージェント評価登録は不採用）
- **SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-39**: 月次レポートは Solid Queue recurring で自動実行し GitHub Issue で報告

## 変更内容

| 機能 | 内容 |
|------|------|
| 検索ログ | `search_adrs` 両経路でクエリ・フィルタ・結果・件数を記録。記録失敗は検索を失敗させないベストエフォート |
| 取り逃がし報告 | `report_search_miss_tool` を新設。エージェントが検索失敗を実際に検知したときだけ記録（全検索への評価登録はしない）。`search_adrs` の description と0件応答に報告への誘導を追記 |
| ゴールデンクエリ回帰 | `config/adr_search_golden_queries.yml`（初期5クエリ）+ `rake adr_management:search_eval` で recall@10 を測定 |
| 月次自動レポート | `AdrManagement::SearchQualityReportJob` が毎月1日 9時 JST に検索実行数・0件率・取り逃がし報告を集計し、本リポジトリに Issue（label: `search-quality`）を作成。失敗は Sentry で検知 |
| インフラ | `SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA=1` を deploy.yml に追加（puma 内で Solid Queue を起動） |

このブランチには、main に未 push だった先行作業（EmbeddingClient の内部実装を RubyLLM に置き換え、SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-37。3コミット）も含まれる。

## マージ後のセットアップ（必須）

1. **GitHub トークン**: 本リポジトリの Issues: Read and write のみを許可した fine-grained PAT を発行し、`bin/rails credentials:edit` で `github.token` に登録する（未設定の場合、月次ジョブは失敗し Sentry に通知される）
2. **デプロイ**: `kamal deploy`（マイグレーション2本 + Solid Queue 起動）
3. **基準値の測定**: 本番で `bin/rails adr_management:search_eval` を実行し、recall@10 の初期値を記録する（開発 DB には ADR コーパスがないため未測定。以後の検索実装変更はこの値との比較で判断する）

## 運用について

- **月次 Issue が届いたら**: 数値を確認し、`record_reevaluation_check_tool` で SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-38・27 の点検を記録する（Issue 本文に判断の目安を記載済み）
  - 取り逃がし報告が月3件以上 → ハイブイッド再ランク等への切替検討を起票（SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-27 の再評価条件に該当）
  - 報告が3ヶ月ゼロ件かつ検索実行あり → 報告経路（Skill 手順・ツール設計）を見直す
- **ゴールデンクエリの保守**: ADR の置換・削除時は期待側も更新する。存在しない期待 ADR は `search_eval` が明確なエラーで検知する（黙って除外しない）
- **検索ログの増加**: 10万件超でローテーション・保持期間を検討（SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-38 の再評価条件）
- **Solid Queue の同居実行**: puma プロセス内でワーカーが動くため、Web 応答への影響が観測されたら専用ワーカーコンテナへの分離を検討（SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-39 の再評価条件）。なお、この有効化により掲載内容管理支援エージェントの `perform_later` 経路も動作するようになる（副次効果。意図しない場合はこの PR で `SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA` を外すこと）
- **月次 Issue の作成失敗が2回連続**した場合はトークン運用・通知経路を見直す（SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-39 の再評価条件）

## 配布スキル（takeyuweb-tools plugin: documentation/adr-management）への追記内容

本リポジトリ外のため、プラグイン側リポジトリで以下の2箇所を更新する。ツール description での誘導は実装済みのため緊急ではないが、Skill 側にも入れると遵守率が上がる。

**1. 「標準ワークフロー > 1. 実装・設計の前: 関連 ADR の検索と参照」の検索手順の末尾に追記:**

```markdown
**取り逃がしの報告**: 検索で見つからなかった ADR に別経路（キーワード検索・
一覧・既知の番号・置換変遷）で後から到達した場合、または存在すると確信する
ADR が複数の言い回し＋キーワード併用でも見つからなかった場合は、その場で
`report_search_miss_tool` に失敗したクエリと到達経路（または存在すると考える
根拠）を記録する。通常の検索結果への評価・感想は登録しない（失敗を実際に
検知したときのみ報告する）。観測はセッション終了とともに消えるため、
後回しにしない。
```

**2. 「5. 再評価条件の点検」の末尾に追記:**

```markdown
**月次品質レポートとの連携**: ADR 管理サーバーは毎月「ADR検索 品質レポート」
Issue（label: search-quality）を作成する。この Issue を扱う際は、本文の数値
（取り逃がし報告件数・0件率）をもとに検索方式の決定の再評価条件を点検し、
`record_reevaluation_check_tool` で結果を記録する。
```

## テスト

- 878 examples, 0 failures（新規31件を含む）
- RuboCop: no offenses

author: coffiest
body:
## 概要

MTT(マルチテーブルトーナメント)の進行を、これまでの「全卓を1ハンドずつ直列消化する `pump()`」から、**各卓が独立して自分のハンドループを回す全卓並行方式**へ作り替えました。自分の卓は他卓の進行を待たなくなり、実MTTと同じ挙動になります。

## 変更内容

### サーバー(`packages/server/src/mttSession.ts`)
- 単一の `hand` / `activeTableId` / `turnTimer` による直列進行を廃止し、卓ごとの `TableRuntime`(`hand` / `turnTimer` / `pumpScheduled`)で並行進行へ変更。
- `pumpTable(tableId)` が各卓の次ハンドを独立して開始・進行。`startAllTables()` で全卓のループを起動し、`reconcileTables()` がリバランスで人が入った待機卓・新設卓を拾う。`pruneRuntimes()` が解体済み卓の状態を破棄。
- エンジンの座席変更(精算・テーブルバランス/ブレイク・強制敗退・レイトレジ・リエントリ)を `engineLock`(トーナメント単位の排他)で直列化し、並行する精算どうしの席移動・卓消滅の競合を防止。
- 精算時に「今ハンドが進行中の他卓」を `busyTableIds` としてエンジンへ渡し、進行中の卓を解体・移動元にしない。
- ハンド開始/終了イベントの参照を `tableId` で絞り込み(並行進行では他卓のイベントが混在するため)。

### エンジン
- `tableBalancer.ts`: `findTableToBreak` / `findRebalanceMove` に `busyTableIds` を追加。進行中の卓を解体候補・移動元から除外し、対象が無ければ後回し(次のハンド境界で再判定)。
- `multiTableTournament.ts`: `settleFinishedHandOnTable` / `rebalanceTables` / `forceEliminate` / `registerLatePlayer` が `busyTableIds` を受け取り、テーブルバランスへ伝搬。`registerLatePlayer` に `preferredSeat` を追加し、リエントリ/レイトレジ時に元の卓・元の席が空席かつ非進行中なら優先、無ければ最少人数卓へフォールバック。

## テスト
- `tableBalancer.test.ts`: busy卓を解体しない/移動元にしない、対象が全て busy なら後回しになるケースを追加。
- `multiTableTournament.test.ts`: 希望席への復帰と、埋まっている/busy時のフォールバックを検証。
- 既存の全エンジンテスト(95件)・サーバーテスト(13件)・全ワークスペース typecheck が通過。

## バージョン
`2.65.0` → `2.66.0`

author: k1low
body:
## Summary

- Add `tailor.workflow.execJobFunction` as the canonical job function API. It returns the child job function's result via durable suspend/replay — `Exec*` semantics under the platform verb convention (a blocking call that returns a result), while the `Start*` verb is reserved for APIs that return only an `execution_id`.
- Keep `startJobFunction` and `triggerJobFunction` as aliases with identical runtime behavior; flip the `@deprecated` markers so both point at `execJobFunction`. The frozen alias `triggerJobFunction` and the (temporary) alias `startJobFunction` are both preserved.
- Point the bundled workflow output emitted by the SDK at the canonical name. `dispatchTriggerJob` and the CLI trigger transformer now call/emit `execJobFunction`. The deprecated `setupWorkflowMock` helper installs its handler on both `execJobFunction` and `triggerJobFunction` so existing bundled-output tests keep intercepting.
- Update the vitest `mockWorkflow` facade and the default workflow runtime installed by `tailor-runtime` so all three names share the same underlying `vi.fn`: calls through any name are recorded once and handlers set on any name apply to all.
- Update docs (`docs/runtime.md`, `docs/services/workflow.md`, `docs/testing.md`), JSDoc, and the generated schema description so canonical is `execJobFunction` with the two aliases called out.

## Notes

- `packages/sdk/src/types/workflow.generated.ts` is regenerated via `pnpm generate` after the `.describe()` update on `ExecutionPolicyKeySchema`.
- Existing tests that call `.triggerJobFunction` on the mocked platform surface are retained on purpose: they double as regression coverage for the frozen alias path so the two-name contract keeps being checked.
- Changeset: minor bump for `@tailor-platform/sdk`.

body:
Root cause: keyframes every 4s (hero) / 2s (footer) meant the browser had to seek at the loop boundary, causing a ~0.5s stutter every 2 loops (~8s).

Re-encoded both clips:
- 1080p instead of 4K (lighter on decoder)
- Keyframe every 12 frames (0.5s) for instant seek
- No B-frames (simpler decode, faster loop)
- faststart moov atom for instant playback
- VP9 webm at matching quality

Hero: 2MB -> 748KB (mp4), 538KB -> 482KB (webm)
Footer: 15MB -> 5.6MB (mp4), 4.8MB -> 3.6MB (webm)

author: hoyullee
body:
## 배경

에디터 이미지 첨부 기능의 1단계: 도형·메모와 같은 계열의 **캔버스 자유 배치 이미지**. (2단계 노드 이미지는 후속 PR)

## 설계

- **코어**: `Float.img`(데이터 URL) — post-dc 순수 추가. 직렬화는 passthrough, CRDT 바인딩은 필드 제네릭이라 **코어 변경은 모델 1필드뿐**, 골든 픽스처 무회귀 (round-trip 테스트 추가)
- **저장 = 문서 인라인**: `imageAttach.ts`가 첨부 시 클라이언트 다운스케일(긴 변 1024px, PNG는 투명 보존, 그 외 JPEG q0.85, soft limit 초과 시 1회 재압축) → 저장·동기화·협업·오프라인·내보내기가 기존 문서 경로 그대로 동작

## 기능

- **진입 3종**: ① 삽입 메뉴 "이미지 추가" ② 배경 우클릭 메뉴(클릭 지점에 생성) ③ 클립보드 붙여넣기(뷰포트 중앙, 텍스트 입력 중엔 통과) + **캔버스 파일 드롭**(드롭 지점 중심)
- **렌더**: 라운드 이미지 카드 — 접기 토글·텍스트 편집·메모 배경 미적용, 더블클릭은 선택까지만

author: ashiknm
body:
## What & why

The Area Risk Forecast (PR #122) worked locally but returned `available:false` on the deployed app with **"Catalyst headers are empty"**. The SDK predict path (`app.quick_ml().predict`) needs Catalyst gateway request headers that only accompany authenticated end-user requests — absent on anonymous AppSail access (the same limitation the team hit with Zia).

This adds a **server-to-server OAuth REST path** so the deployed forecast carries its own credentials. **Verified live** — `/api/risk?window_days=30` on the deployed AppSail app now returns real per-district QuickML forecasts (Bengaluru City High/68, Tumakuru High/39, Mysuru Medium/38, Belagavi Low/37), and the FORECAST tab renders them.

## Changes

- **`quickml.py`** — mint an access token from a self-client refresh token (cached, thread-safe) and POST to the endpoint's predict URL with the `X-QUICKML-ENDPOINT-KEY`, `CATALYST-ORG`, `Environment` headers. Falls back to the SDK path when no self-client is configured. Honest `QuickMLUnavailable` on any failure.
- **`config.py`** — `KAVACH_QUICKML_RISK_URL` + the Zoho self-client trio (client id/secret/refresh token), accounts URL, org id, environment.
- **`engine.py`** — unwrap QuickML's single-element result list (`{"result":[39.2]}`) via `_first()`; wire OAuth fields into the default client.
- **`deploy_backend.sh`** — inject the new env vars into the generated `app-config.json`.
- **`risk_train_export.py`** — emit an all-numeric training table (features + target only). QuickML rejects any non-numeric column ("Previous stage result contains non-numeric columns"), so district identifiers are dropped; the script now regenerates `data/risk_train_model.csv` exactly (verified byte-identical).

## Safety

- **No secrets in the repo** (ADR-001) — the self-client id/secret and refresh token are AppSail env vars only.
- **Anti-hallucination preserved** — QuickML/computed numbers only; Qwen just rephrases; honest `unavailable` when unreachable.

## Plain-English summaries via live GLM chat (second commit)

Turns on the optional LLM phrasing that was coded but never wired to a live endpoint. Catalyst LLM Serving exposes **GLM 4.7** as an OpenAI-style chat API (`/glm/chat`), reachable with the same self-client OAuth token and scope as the predictor.

- **`quickml.py`** — `llm()` rewritten from the assumed flat `{"prompt"}` body to the real chat shape (`{model, messages:[system,user], temperature, max_tokens, stream:false}`), sends `CATALYST-ORG`, and **disables the model's chain-of-thought** (`chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`). GLM 4.7 is a reasoning model — left on, it dumps its thinking, blows the token budget and trips the number fence, so the polish would never apply. Text is read from the `response` field.
- **`config.py`** — split the LLM model into the API id (`KAVACH_QUICKML_LLM_MODEL_ID`, e.g. `crm-di-glm47b_30b_it`) used in the request, and a friendly provenance label (`KAVACH_QUICKML_LLM_MODEL`, default `GLM-4.7`) shown to users as `summary_source`.
- Anti-hallucination fence unchanged: GLM only rephrases; any output introducing a number absent from the computed facts is rejected and the template kept. Verified live against the deployed GLM endpoint before wiring.

## Verification

- `pytest` — **263 passed** (incl. `tests/catalyst/test_quickml.py`: OAuth request shaping, token caching, bad-refresh honesty, SDK fallback, envelope unwrap, list-shape extractor, and the GLM chat request/response shape).
- `ruff check .` — clean.
- `scripts/check_source_size.py` — OK.
- Live deploy — `available:true` with real numbers on the deployed AppSail app.

The "Assign to segment" action only created individual member assignments, leaving no record of which segments a challenge was pushed to. Segment membership changes over time, so this can't be reliably derived from members' current segments - persist it explicitly instead.

API:
- Add challenge_segment_assignments table (auto-created via create_all) recording each segment a challenge is bulk-assigned to, with a uq_challenge_segment constraint and cascade delete.
- Record the segment in assign-segment, but only when it matched at least one member (so typos / empty segments aren't stored); idempotent.
- Expose segments on ChallengeOut; selectinload them in the list endpoints to avoid N+1.

Client:
- Add segments to the Challenge type and render an "Assigned segments" section with segment badges (or an empty hint) on each challenge card.

author: arthur791004
body:
Fixes DOTMSD-1461

## Proposed Changes

* Fix infinite scroll in the PHP error and web server logs, so more than the first 50 entries are reachable again.
* Replace the hand-rolled scroll handling with the infinite scroll DataViews provides.
* Show progress while the next batch loads, pinned to the bottom of the table.
* Hide the footer on these two screens, where it has nothing to show because they scroll instead of paginating.

## Why are these changes being made?

Customers report that the logs screens are stuck on the first page of results, with no way to reach the rest. Downloading the CSV shows there is much more data available.

These screens deliberately use infinite scroll rather than pagination, so no pagination controls are expected — but the infinite scroll itself silently stopped working, which leaves the remaining entries unreachable.

The screens drove their own scroll-based paging, listening for scroll events on the DataViews wrapper. That element stopped being the scrollable one in `@wordpress/dataviews` v13, when overflow moved to an inner container, so the handler never ran and no further page was ever requested. The upgrade landed a while before the MSD launch, which is why this surfaced as a launch regression rather than at upgrade time.

Rather than chase the new element, this drops the custom handling and uses the infinite scroll DataViews now provides, so nothing here is coupled to its internal DOM.

## Considerations

**Rendering the table before the first batch arrives.** DataViews binds its scroll listener in an effect that gives up when the scroll container isn't mounted yet, and never retries. The container only appears once it has rows. These screens rendered it immediately, while the first request was still out, so by the time the container existed the listener had already been abandoned — the view state was correct, the loaded count was correct, and no page was ever requested. Waiting for the first batch before rendering it is what makes the listener bind.

**Two things that only surface once paging works.** An unfiltered view compared `[]` against `undefined` and so reported a dataset change on every call; harmless when the only calls came from user actions, but with infinite scroll it fires on every window advance and discards the loaded pages. And the effect that bounds the table's height has to re-run once the table mounts, or the table never becomes scrollable and produces no scroll events at all.

**The one local style rule, and it is temporary.** While a batch loads, rows shift and a gap opens below them. The cause is the footer: there is nothing to put in it — these screens scroll rather than paginate — but DataViews mounts it partway through a fetch regardless, and because it takes space below the scroll container, the container resizes while the reader is in it. Hiding it settles the layout.

The rule is scoped to the php and server cards rather than to `.site-logs-card`, which the activity log also carries. The activity log paginates, and its footer is the only way to reach page 2 — hiding it there would have cost more than it saved.

An earlier revision instead pinned the progress spinner to the bottom of the table, on the theory that the spinner was what moved. It wasn't, and that rule has been dropped: the spinner now renders the way DataViews renders it everywhere else. Worth knowing if you saw the earlier diff.

`@wordpress/dataviews` 17.2.0 stops tying the footer's visibility to the loading state, so this rule should come out when that bump lands (#112947). It is a style rule rather than a component change so the revert is a deletion.

**What the windowing costs on 16.0.0.** Handing the paging to DataViews means `useData` keeps a window of rows and drops the ones outside it, which is why this view now passes a slice and lets DataViews reassemble the list. That is the mechanism working as intended, not a conflict — the custom handler it would have fought is gone.

There is one rough edge left, and it is worth knowing about before merging. 17.2.0 carries a second infinite-scroll fix beyond the footer: scroll-anchor restoration currently discards scrolling done while a page is in flight. DataViews records an anchor row when it asks for the next page, then restores that row's position once the page lands, regardless of where the reader has scrolled to in the meantime. Scrolling away mid-load therefore snaps you back. Measured on this branch, parking at three different offsets while a batch was outstanding:

| parked at | after the batch landed | moved by |
|---|---|---|
| 15370 | 37921 | 22551 |
| 15705 | 50343 | 34638 |
| 19283 | 62313 | 43030 |

Scrolling back up once loading has finished is unaffected — stepping from 24107 to 0 in nine moves held position exactly each time. It only bites while a request is outstanding, which on this endpoint can be tens of seconds.

This is not a regression: trunk cannot reach a second batch at all, so the situation never arises there, and the alternative is leaving the data unreachable. It is fixed upstream and lands with the same bump as the footer rule (#112947), so the two should go in close together.

## Testing Instructions

Requires a site with hosting features and more than 50 web server log entries in the selected range.

1. Go to a site → Logs → Web server.
2. Scroll to the bottom of the table.
3. The next batch loads and appends, and the scroll-to-top button appears. Keep scrolling to keep loading, until the data runs out.
4. While a batch is loading, a spinner sits pinned to the bottom of the table, the rows stay put, and no footer appears below the table.
5. Repeat on Logs → PHP errors for a site that has PHP errors.
6. On a site with no PHP errors, check the empty state and the toolbar still render.
7. Go to Logs → Activity and confirm its pagination is still there at the bottom of the table. That screen shares a class with the other two and keeps its footer.

On trunk, step 3 loads nothing and the button never appears.

Verified against the live API on an Atomic site with ~1,200 web server entries: before, the row count stayed at 50 no matter how far you scrolled; after, it goes 50 → 100 → 150, one batch per scroll. The PHP path was verified the same way against a stubbed endpoint, since no test site had PHP errors to page through — 50 → 100 → 130, stopping once the cursor is exhausted. The empty state and toolbar were checked on a site with no PHP errors.

Note when testing manually: the logs endpoint is slow and variable, and a single batch can take anywhere from ten seconds to over a minute to come back. Give it time before concluding nothing is loading.

The footer rule was checked against the live API afterwards. Sampled while a batch was in flight, the footer does mount and is held at zero height, with the scroll container staying at a steady 453px; on the activity log the same footer renders at 57px showing "PAGE 1 OF 3". Paging on the server log ran to 300 rows across six batches during that session.

Still unverified: dark mode and narrow widths where the table shows its horizontal scrollbar, and the PHP path, which has only ever been exercised against a stubbed endpoint because no test site has real PHP errors to page through.

## Pre-merge Checklist

- [x] Has the general commit checklist been followed? (PCYsg-hS-p2)
- [ ] [Have you written new tests](https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/blob/trunk/docs/testing/index.md) for your changes?
- [ ] Have you tested the feature in Simple (P9HQHe-k8-p2), Atomic (P9HQHe-jW-p2), and self-hosted Jetpack sites (PCYsg-g6b-p2)? <!-- Atomic only; these screens require hosting features -->

- [ ] Have you tested accessibility for your changes? Ensure the feature remains usable with various

author: rexx010
body:
Closes #97

## Problem
Security headers were split across `next.config.js` and `vercel.json`
with contradictory values. `vercel.json`'s edge headers win on Vercel
deployments, so `X-Frame-Options: DENY` (vercel.json) silently
overrode `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` (next.config.js) in production.
`vercel.json` also shipped the deprecated, actively-harmful
`X-XSS-Protection` header, and neither file set HSTS.

## Changes
- `vercel.json`: removed the entire `headers` key. All other fields
  (`buildCommand`, `regions`, `env`, `rewrites`) unchanged.
- `next.config.js`:
  - `X-Frame-Options` fixed to a single value: `DENY`
  - Removed `X-XSS-Protection` (deprecated; real fix is CSP, tracked in #9)
  - Added `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload`, gated behind `NODE_ENV === 'production'`
  - Added `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`

## Testing
- `npm install` 
- `npm run type-check` — fails on pre-existing, unrelated errors (missing Radix/TanStack deps, Stellar SDK types); no errors in `next.config.js`
- `npm run build` — fails locally only due to sandboxed network blocking Google Fonts fetch, unrelated to this change
- All grep-based acceptance criteria from #97 verified manually (see PR discussion)

body:
## Summary

Four roadmap features, built to keep the site **static by default**. The two backend-dependent features ship their server code as ready-to-enable `.example` templates, so `output: 'static'` and the build stay green until you provision infra.

| Feature | Status | Live now? |
|---|---|---|
| ⌘K command palette | ✅ complete | Fully (static) |
| `/now` + site changelog | ✅ complete | Fully (static) |
| AI site search | ✅ semantic complete; RAG code-complete | Semantic live; RAG needs infra |
| Guestbook | ✅ core complete; backend code-complete | Core live; backend needs infra |

## What's included

### ⌘K Command palette (live)
- `⌘K`/`Ctrl-K` overlay: locale-aware navigation, actions (theme, language, resume, copy email/GitHub/LinkedIn, "Ask my site"), blog/project search.
- Focus trap, arrow/Enter keyboard nav, `Esc`/backdrop close, body scroll-lock. Desktop `⌘K` pill + mobile search entry.
- Follows the codebase's vanilla-Astro `<script>` + GSAP house pattern (no React island).
- `src/components/layout/CommandPalette.astro`, `src/utils/commands.ts` (+ tests).

### `/now` + site changelog (live)
- Bilingual `/now` (`/now`, `/id/now`): authored "current focus" + live GitHub/WakaTime signals.
- `/changelog` + `/changelog.xml` generated **at build time** from Conventional-Commit git history (`execFileSync`, no shell). Pure parser in `src/utils/changelog.ts` (+ tests).

### AI site search (semantic live; RAG ready)

author: openrung-admin
body:
## Why

Users in Iran and China need local apps and services (messaging, banking,
government, utility, and media services) to stay on the direct local path while
restricted traffic uses the relay.

On a fresh install, split tunneling now starts **on**, with these presets
enabled:

- local network
- Iranian sites and apps
- Chinese sites and apps

No individual Android apps are preselected. Any valid saved preference,
including an explicit master-toggle **off**, remains authoritative after an
upgrade.

## What it does

- **Bypass local network** — private IP ranges skip the tunnel.
- **Country presets** — Iranian and Chinese domain/IP rules are backed by
  bundled sing-box rule sets (`geosite`/`geoip` for `ir`/`cn`). Bypassed
  domains use an in-country resolver over the direct path (Shecan
  `178.22.122.100`; AliDNS `223.5.5.5`).
- **Bypassed apps (Android only)** — selected packages are excluded from the
  VPN at the OS level. iOS consumer packet tunnels do not expose equivalent
  per-app attribution, so iOS supports domain/IP presets only.

## How it is built

- The Android and iOS sing-box generators accept the same optional,
  prevalidated split-tunnel rules and emit canonical route, rule-set, sniff,
  and DNS deltas. Modern UDP DNS servers direct-dial with no `detour`; setting a
  detour to the otherwise-empty tagged direct outbound prevents sing-box from
  starting.
- `setSplitTunnelConfig` persists one versioned snake_case JSON payload in
  native storage so reconnects and network recovery retain the rules.
- React Native owns the UI preference, hydrates it at launch, debounces live
  changes, and flushes initialization before the first connect so a fresh
  install cannot race the native config write.
- Four provenance-recorded `.srs` files under `rulesets/dist` are packaged into
  both apps. Android stages them atomically; iOS reads them from the packet
  tunnel bundle.

## Failure and lifecycle behavior

- Missing/invalid native config, missing rule files, and stale Android package
  selections degrade toward the full tunnel; none can block a connection.
- Reapply only restarts a fully connected tunnel. It does not interrupt an
  in-flight connect or path-loss recovery.
- Native compares effective routing, so redundant serialization, iOS-only
  package changes, and other routing no-ops do not reconnect.
- iOS uses a control epoch so a delayed reapply cannot resurrect a tunnel the
  user stopped.

## Testing

- Jest: **243/243**
- TypeScript: clean
- ESLint: **0 errors**
- Android: complete unit suite passes
- iOS: **91/91**
- Physical-device builds install and launch on Android and iPhone; Android
  country bypass was verified with direct-vs-relay public-IP checks.

The release `libbox` binaries remain ignored supply-chain artifacts and must be
built from the pinned revision. Pinned local artifacts were used for the device
builds above.
