The three crawler data sources (`wikipedia.py`, `baike.py`, `osm.py`) each re-implemented near-identical helpers for page-title generation, HTTP fetching, and station/line name cleaning. This PR consolidates that duplicated logic into two shared modules under `app/crawler/sources/` — behavior is preserved exactly.

New shared modules:

- **`text_utils.py`**
  - `strip_city_suffix(city)` — `city.replace("市","").replace("地区","")`

author: tharindunanayakkara28
body:
## Purpose
This PR adds the ballerinax/ai.azure.storage.blobs data loader, which retrieves documents from Azure Blob Storage containers and returns them as ai:TextDocument values for use with the [Ballerina AI](https://central.ballerina.io/ballerina/ai) module (chunking, embedding, indexing). Inherently textual blobs are decoded directly; PDF and Microsoft Office documents have their text extracted via Apache Tika.

## Goals
Provide a TextDataLoader for Azure Blob Storage that:

- Connects to a container using SAS or Access-Key authentication.
- Loads whole containers or specific blob sources.
- Extracts text from PDF (PDFBox), Microsoft Office (POI), and plain-text/markup formats, returning ready-to-use ai:TextDocument values.

## Approach

- As a developer building an AI/RAG pipeline, I want to load documents straight from an Azure Blob Storage container as ai:TextDocument values, so I can chunk, embed, and index them without writing my own retrieval or text-extraction code.
- As a developer, I want PDF and Office files extracted to text automatically, so mixed-format containers "just work".

author: dchernykh1984
body:
Two fixes from the first live agent run — both about locating an event more precisely.

**1. A venue now gets its real start coordinate from the event's GPS track.** Announcement pages rarely print latitude/longitude, but they link the route: a `.gpx`/`.kml` file, a route.eduha.info track-editor link, or a RideWithGPS route. The first point of that track *is* the start line, which is exactly the venue coordinate. During enrich the agent finds that track, fetches it, and reads the first point, filling a coordinate the model did not supply. Verified on the real brevet: `brm-600-legendy-bayanaula-…kml` → `49.80972, 73.08371` (the Palace of Culture start in Karaganda), instead of the venue landing with no coordinate and sliding to the city centre. New `agent/geo.py` is pure and unit-tested (GPX lat-then-lon vs KML lon-then-lat, wrapper unwrapping, out-of-range/null-island rejection); the one network call is injected.

**2. A city is placed even when the announcement names no region.** The Atlas Mountain Race started in Ouzoud, Morocco, and landed with no location at all — the guidance told the model to leave country/region empty when the announcement did not spell out the region, and a city cannot be filed without its region. But a city's region is geographic fact the model knows, not a guess: Ouzoud is in Béni Mellal-Khénifra. The guidance now tells the model to supply that region from what it knows, and to leave the place empty only when the town itself is genuinely unknown.

**On the run itself:** nothing else was wrong — `proposed: 9, post errors: 0`. The 8 brevets from randonneurs.kz got their real named start venues; the skips were all already-known / past events; the skipped sources need a Telegram login or returned a 5xx of their own (velomania.kz). These two placement gaps were the only real issues.

**Checks:** `pytest agent/tests` passes (135). Guidance is free-text steering (exempt from the ASCII hook).

author: liohtml
body:
## Summary
This PR enhances parameter validation and processing in the SISTRIX MCP server, with a focus on improving compatibility with various client implementations and API requirements.

## Key Changes

- **Target normalization for domain/host scopes**: URLs passed as targets are now automatically normalized by stripping scheme, path, and query components when the scope is `domain` or `host`. The `path`/`url` scopes pass targets through untouched. This handles cases where models pass full URLs (e.g., `https://example.com/blog/?q=1`) when SISTRIX expects bare hostnames.

- **Boolean flag handling**: Explicit `false` values for boolean parameters are now omitted entirely from API requests. Since SISTRIX flags default to `FALSE` and may use presence-based parsing, omitting the parameter is safer than sending `false`.

- **Improved integer parameter coercion**: 
  - Whole-number floats (e.g., `25.0`) are now accepted for integer arguments, accommodating MCP clients that serialize integers as floats
  - String integers are trimmed before parsing to handle whitespace

- **Case-insensitive boolean string coercion**: Boolean string values (`"true"`, `"false"`, etc.) are now converted to lowercase before matching, allowing case variations like `"True"` or `"FALSE"`.

- **Enhanced error handling**: 
  - In-band SISTRIX error 500 (general/internal error) is now treated as retryable with backoff, matching HTTP 500 behavior
  - Added actionable hints for error codes 1000 (no results) and 1001 (invalid date format)

## Implementation Details

- New `normalize_target()` function handles URL parsing and validation for domain/host scopes
- Boolean flag omission logic integrated into `collect_params()` to check stringified values
- Integer parsing enhanced to detect and convert whole floats using `fract()` check
- Retryability logic updated to include error code 500 alongside 429

## Testing
Three new test cases added:
- `url_targets_are_normalized_for_domain_and_host_scopes`: Validates URL normalization behavior
- `false_flags_are_omitted`: Ensures explicit false values are excluded from requests
- `whole_float_limits_are_accepted`: Confirms whole-number float acceptance for integers

Version bumped to 0.1.2 with corresponding documentation updates.

author: james2177
body:
tests/common::TestApp::new() unconditionally started a fresh Postgres testcontainer:

let container = Postgres::default().with_tag("14-alpine").start().await.unwrap();
closes #786

If Docker wasn't reachable, every test built on TestApp panicked with a raw testcontainers error. And even when Docker was fine, every test paid for a brand-new Postgres container (image start + boot), even when a Postgres/Redis instance was already running via docker-compose.yml or a CI service container.

Fix

TestApp::new() now resolves infra in priority order:

  1. TEST_DATABASE_URL / TEST_REDIS_URL — if set, reuse whatever the caller already stood up (e.g. docker-compose.yml services, or a CI service container). No testcontainer is started in this path.
  2. A fresh testcontainers Postgres, only if Docker is actually reachable (probed via a 2s-timeout docker ping, not just attempting a start and hoping).
  3. A clear, specific failure naming exactly what's missing and the exact command to fix it — no raw testcontainers/Docker-daemon error reaches the test output.

Redis is resolved the same way via TEST_REDIS_URL, falling back to the default docker-compose.yml port (redis://127.0.0.1:6379) rather than a testcontainer — every other integration test in this suite already hardcodes that address, so a container on a random port would silently desync from them instead of failing loudly.

Side fix: docker-compose.yml postgres service was broken

While wiring up the "reuse docker compose up -d postgres redis" path, found that postgres never actually started via compose: the WAL/archival flags were passed through POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS, but those are PGC_POSTMASTER settings for the server, not initdb — initdb --help doesn't even have a -c option, so initdb errored out and the container never became healthy. Moved them to command: postgres -c ... instead, which is the correct way to pass runtime GUCs to the official Postgres image. Verified wal_level, max_wal_senders, and archive_command all apply correctly now (relevant to scripts/pitr_restore.sh).

Docs

Added an "Integration Tests" section to README.md and docs/setup.md explaining the priority order and the docker compose up -d postgres redis + TEST_DATABASE_URL/TEST_REDIS_URL workflow for faster iterative runs.

Before/after (measured locally)

cargo test --test health_check_test (16 tests, each independently calling TestApp::new()):

Scenario | Wall clock -- | -- No env vars, Docker-only fallback (fresh Postgres testcontainer per test) | 60.84s TEST_DATABASE_URL/TEST_REDIS_URL pointing at docker compose up -d postgres redis | 8.85s

~6.9x faster for this file when infra is pre-provisioned, since each test pays for its own container in the fallback path.

Also verified:

  • No-Docker / no-env-var case produces a clear message naming the missing piece and the fix, no raw testcontainers error.
  • Full health_check_test + lifecycle_test pass against a real docker compose up -d postgres redis stack via env vars.

Test plan

  • cargo build --tests --package synapse-core
  • cargo test --test health_check_test — testcontainer fallback path (Docker reachable, no env vars)
  • TEST_DATABASE_URL=... TEST_REDIS_URL=... cargo test --test health_check_test --test lifecycle_test — env-var reuse path
  • Neither env vars nor Docker reachable → panics with actionable message (verified via the no-redis case: TestApp::new() needs Redis for integration tests and found none. with the exact fix commands, no raw redis/testcontainers error)
  • docker compose up -d postgres now reaches healthy, and SHOW wal_level / SHOW archive_command confirm the PITR-related settings still apply

author: brownm09
body:
Closes #890

## Problem

Step 10.5's diff-and-replay applied `git checkout "$PREV" -- "$FILEPATH"` to every `A|M` path. That is last-write-wins: for a path **both** branches changed, `origin/main`'s version is discarded wholesale.

During the 2026-07-21 compose (remediating #874), `draft/2026-07-21` conflicted with `origin/main` on 6 READMEs, because `origin/main` had advanced by the 2026-07-20 compose ([engineering-journal PR #181](https://github.com/brownm09/engineering-journal/pull/181)), which had edited the same README sections. Applied as written, the replay would have silently reverted the previous day's entry rows and Progress Summary updates across all 6 files — in a commit with no conflict, no warning, and nothing in the PR body to suggest a published journal had just been reverted. The paths were excluded by hand and re-applied onto `origin/main`'s versions instead ([PR #182](https://github.com/brownm09/engineering-journal/pull/182)).

ADR-104 already named this in its Trade-offs section, accepted on parity grounds with the allowlist it replaced. That reasoning holds for parity but not exposure: the allowlist replayed 3 known paths; diff-and-replay replays *every* changed path, so generalizing the mechanism generalized its one unsafe case from a corner to the default.

## Change

Every path is classified before replay, with one predicate:

```bash
main_touched() { [ -n "$(git -C "$WT" diff --name-only "$MERGE_BASE" origin/main -- "$1")" ]; }
```

| Case | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Uncontested `A`/`M` | replay from `$PREV` — **unchanged**, the common case |
| Contested `M` | 3-way merge vs. the merge base → `AUTO_MERGED`, or `MANUAL_RECONCILE` on conflict |
| Contested `A` (add/add) | `MANUAL_RECONCILE` — no common ancestor, never guess |
| Contested `D` (delete/modify) | `MANUAL_RECONCILE` — never blind-delete main's edit |
| `D` both sides | clean no-op |

Non-empty `MANUAL_RECONCILE` → **exit 2**, and Step 10.5 now makes the commit conditional on exit 0. Fails closed, since the failure being guarded against is a commit that looks clean. The same predicate stops the shard-integrity restore (#787) from resurrecting a shard `origin/main` deliberately deleted (`SHARD_RESTORE_SKIPPED`) — ADR-119's resurrection failure at file scope.

The mechanism moves out of SKILL.md's **two duplicated copies** into `claude/scripts/journal-compose-replay.sh`; pathspecs remain the only difference between the call sites. This follows the `journal-compose-force-resolve.py` extraction precedent in the same skill, and makes the mechanism testable — ADR-104 had conceded no test existed *because* it was bash embedded in markdown. The script also derives `MERGE_BASE` from `$PREV` itself, closing a latent gap where the pre-push-rejection route (which skips the merge-tree probe) left it unset.

### Two real bugs the new test caught on its first run

Neither is visible when reviewing a markdown snippet — part of the argument for extracting:

1. **Blob-vs-work-tree line endings.** `git show` emits the stored LF blob; the checked-out file is CRLF under this machine's `core.autocrlf`. Merging one against the other makes every line differ, so a trivially disjoint merge conflicts. All three sides are now read as blobs. The test sets `core.autocrlf true` on every fixture, on every platform, so this stays pinned.
2. **`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` is all-or-nothing per command.** Required to protect the `<ref>:<path>` argument (ADR-120), but applied to `git -C "$WT" show …` it also stops `-C`'s path from being translated — `fatal: cannot change to '/tmp/…'`. Scoped inside a `cd` subshell instead.

## Testing

`py -3 claude/scripts/run-hook-tests.py`

```
Tests: 79 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (258.1s)
```

New: `bash claude/scripts/tests/test-journal-compose-replay.sh` — **33 passed, 0 failed**. Drives the real script against `mktemp -d` fixture repos with `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main` standing in for a remote; no network, no `gh`. Fixture A pins the mechanical paths plus a disjoint 3-way merge where both sides' edits survive; fixture B pins the four contested shapes (including the literal #890 README shape), each asserting `origin/main`'s content is still on disk; fixture C pins exit 1 on every precondition failure. Both fixtures grep the tree for conflict markers.

**Skips (2)** — both are the runner passing through a gate's own environmental self-skip, neither is a disabled test:
- `run-shellcheck.sh` — shellcheck not installed locally (`SKIP:` self-exit). CI is the gate.
- `test_pyw_stdio.py` — runner-skipped by design (needs a real Windows-subsystem `pyw` host).

**Failure (1) — pre-existing and environmental, not introduced here:** `test-get-project-item.sh` fails with `GraphQL: API rate limit exceeded`. Verified live rather than taken from the message: `gh api rate_limit` reports `graphql.remaining: 63/5000`, resetting 03:17:59 EDT. The test hits the live GitHub GraphQL API; neither it nor `get-project-item.sh` is touched by this PR (`git diff --stat origin/main -- <both>` is empty), and re-running it as the budget drained produced *more* failures, confirming it tracks the rate limit rather than this change. It self-skips in CI, where `gh` is unauthenticated.

Also run clean: `check-script-path-hygiene.sh`, `check-remote-read-hygiene.sh` (the new script uses `git show` with no `2>/dev/null`), `test_testing_index_parity.py`, and the suppression / test-integrity greps (both empty; no suppressions, skip markers, deleted tests, or lowered thresholds in this diff).

## Docs & ADR

- **ADR-104 Amendment 1** — the correction, the extraction rationale, the two implementation traps, and supersession of the `.compose-diff-plan.txt`-in-`$WT` note (no scratch file is written into the compose worktree at all now). Header status/tags and `docs/adr/INDEX.md` updated.
- `## Testing` item **82** + `docs/TESTING.md` item 82 (parity gate green).
- `docs/REFERENCE.md` Utilities + Script-verification-suite rows; `claude/scripts/README.md` row and section count.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Review findings disposition

`/review` reported **1 blocking, 2 non-blocking** ([review comment](https://github.com/brownm09/dev-env/pull/895#issuecomment-5055240731)). All three fixed in this PR — none left as-is.

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **[documentation]** `claude/scripts/tests/README.md` — new test file added without its index row; header counts stale | **Fixed in `e65613c`** — added the row to *Utility & setup scripts*; corrected the counts (69/10/80 → 70/11/82, all three already stale before this PR) |
| 2 | **[maintainability]** `SKILL.md` — `REPLAY_RC=$?` assigned but never read in both Step 10.5 blocks | **Fixed in `e65613c`** — an explicit `[ "$REPLAY_RC" -eq 0 ] \|\| echo "STOP: …"` now sits in both snippets, so the stop is in the code path rather than an adjacent comment |
| 3 | **[reliability]** `journal-compose-replay.sh` — `mktemp -d` fallback dir leaked; exit-1 contract under-described | **Fixed in `e65613c`** — trap now `rmdir`s the dir it created; exit-1 doc covers a mid-loop git failure |

Finding 3 came with a coverage gap worth naming: the fallback is the branch **CI always takes** (the fixed scratch path belongs to a different user there), yet it was unreachable from a local test run. `JOURNAL_COMPOSE_REPLAY_SCRATCH` now overrides the scratch root — test-only, never set by the real invocation — and a new fixture-C case points `TMPDIR` at a private directory and asserts nothing is left behind. That makes the assertion deterministic instead of a racy count of the shared temp root.

### Re-run after the fixes

```
Tests: 79 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (258.1s)
```

`test-journal-compose-replay.sh` is now **34 passed, 0 failed** (was 33; +1 for the fallback-cleanup case).

The previously reported failure is gone without being touched: `test-get-project-item.sh` **self-skipped** this run (`SKIP: gh project query fail

## Motivation

The camera node currently keeps its configuration models, validation, and JSON5 loading in `node.py`, and names the root of its Zenoh key hierarchy `base_key`. Aligning this boundary and terminology with `unitree-go2-zenoh-node` makes the two nodes easier to understand and keeps the camera runtime focused on capture and publication.

## Summary

- Move the strict Pydantic configuration models, Zenoh key validation, and JSON5 loader into `config.py`.
- Rename `base_key` to `zenoh_key_prefix` and centralize `{zenoh_key_prefix}/{device_key}` derivation in `NodeConfig.publisher_key()`.
- Keep the published keys and camera runtime behavior unchanged while rejecting the old field instead of providing a compatibility alias.
- Separate configuration tests into `tests/test_config.py` and retain the existing validation coverage.
- Update the example configuration and English/Japanese usage documentation, including the migration note for existing local configurations.

## Scope

- Node configuration schema and module boundaries.
- Configuration validation and test organization.
- English and Japanese configuration documentation.

## Out of Scope

- Camera capture, JPEG encoding, publish frequency, Zenoh QoS, scheduling, or worker lifecycle changes.
- Zenoh session configuration or CLI changes.
- Automatic migration or a compatibility alias for `base_key`.

body:
اجرای طرحِ **V3** که تأیید کردی: بخشِ «کلیدها» حالا کاملاً منوی هر نوعِ فایل را می‌سازد، با **پیش‌نمایشِ زندهٔ شبیه‌سازی‌شدهٔ تلگرام**.

## قابلیت‌ها (همه در یک صفحه، بی‌ری‌استارت)
- **تب‌های منو**: تصویر / ویدیو / صوت / سند / PDF / آرشیو / اپ — هر کدام منوی خودش.
- **پیش‌نمایشِ زندهٔ منوی تلگرام** بالای صفحه (با JS): دقیقاً همان چیدمان/رنگ/ردیفی که کاربر می‌بیند؛ با هر تغییر بلافاصله آپدیت می‌شود.
- **جابه‌جایی** کلیدها با **کشیدنِ دستگیره** (⠿).
- **نمایش/عدم‌نمایش** هر کلید (کلیدِ روشن/خاموش).
- **عرضِ هر کلید** (تمام‌عرض / نصف / یک‌سوم) که **ردیف‌ها را می‌سازد** — همان «rowهای مختلف».
- **متنِ** هر کلید (per-lang، همین‌جا) + **رنگ** (آبی/سبز/قرمز) + **ایموجیِ پرمیوم**.
- یک دکمهٔ «ذخیره» همه را با هم می‌نویسد؛ «بازگشت به چیدمانِ پیش‌فرضِ این منو» هم هست.

## زیرِ کاپوت
- `MenuButton(kind, op, position, hidden, width)` (Postgres). `textstore` آن را کنارِ متن‌ها/استایل‌ها در همان دیکشنریِ درون‌پروسه نگه می‌دارد و روی همان شمارندهٔ `txtver` تازه می‌شود (bot + workerها زنده می‌گیرند).
- `file_card_kb` حالا **ترتیب + مخفی + عرض** را اعمال می‌کند (عرض → اندازهٔ ردیف‌ها با `_rows_from_widths`). **پیش‌فرض (بدونِ چیدمانِ سفارشی) مو‌به‌مو همان منوی قبلی است** — تا وقتی سفارشی نکنی هیچ تغییری نمی‌بینی. opهایی که بعداً به کد اضافه شوند خودکار ته منو می‌آیند.

## تست (۲۲ چک، همه پاس)
آیتم‌های ویرایشگر، ردیف‌های پیش‌نمایش، هندلرِ ذخیره (reorder/hide/width/color/emoji/text)، بازتابِ کامل روی `file_card_kb` (ترتیب/مخفی/رنگ/ایموجی/متن)، و reset به پیش‌فرض. **بدونِ رگرسیون**: منوی پیش‌فرضِ ویدیو همچنان `[1,3,3,3,3,1]`. رگرسیون‌ها: `textstore`, `buttonstyle`, `router`, پنل، import + parity. اسکرین‌شاتِ صفحهٔ نهایی را در چت فرستادم.

## یادداشت
- استایلِ ایموجیِ پرمیوم نیازمندِ Premium بودنِ اکانتِ ربات است (که داری). فقط منوی کارت (`OPS_BY_KIND`) پوشش دارد؛ زیرمنوها (کیفیتِ فشرده، فرمتِ تبدیل و…) در صورتِ نیاز بعداً.

author: netlify-coding[bot]
bakey
body:
The first real provider pack: repositories, issues, issue comments, pull requests, reviews, commits, workflow runs, and releases as stable SQL tables (packs/github.rs, page-number pagination at GitHub's 100-row maximum), queryable through YAML bindings, open_connector_query, and federated joins.

Engine additions the pack required, each sanctioned by the design spec:

- Per-mapping filter Fidelity (filters.rs): Exact mappings stay fully provider-side; Inexact mappings narrow the fetch and DataFusion reapplies the predicate. issues.updated_at >= maps to GitHub's `since` as Inexact (documented "updated at or after" — a guaranteed superset); commits' strictly-after `since` is deliberately NOT mapped, because a boundary row the provider drops is unrecoverable — the mock pack's `>=` rule applied for real. Timestamp filter literals render as RFC 3339 UTC strings at every DataFusion granularity.
- Utf8ListFromObjectKey (json_to_arrow.rs): the design's `$.labels[*].name` / `$.assignees[*].login` flattening — an array of objects becomes List<Utf8> of one declared key.
- A JSON-null *parent* on a nested path is absence, not a structural failure: nullable leaves under `commit.author: null` / `issue.user: null` become SQL NULL (required ones still fail with a targeted error). Extends the previous PR's JSON-null-to-SQL-NULL rule to nested paths.
- SourcePackTable::fixed_inputs: issues/pull_requests pin `state=all` so SELECT * reads the complete collection (GitHub defaults to open items only); a pushed state predicate overrides the pin, keeping SELECT * and WHERE state='closed' consistent.

Relational caveats encoded rather than papered over: GitHub's issues endpoint returns pull requests, so the stable schema exposes the pull_request marker as nullable opaque JSON (IS NULL selects pure issues). Nullability is conservative — identity fields only. Fingerprint pins stay None like the mock pack until validated against a live gateway's discovered contracts; the redacted per-table fixtures under packs/fixtures/github/ are the build-time conversion contract.

Tests: 180 open_connector total (was 158 on main). Fixture contract suites for all 8 tables (null-bearing, null-parent, empty-list, nested, extra-field rows; empty pages keep the stable schema), bind-time validation of every contract, and end to end through the mock gateway: a 150-row two-page scan carrying state=all and the resource inputs on every request, Exact state override, Inexact since narrowing plus local re-filter (gateway ignores since entirely — the harshest legal Inexact provider — and the boundary row is kept), pull_request IS NULL / IS NOT NULL, LIMIT stopping after one page, and open_connector_query parity with the YAML-bound table.

Docs: docs/open-connector-github.md (per-table filter/limit behavior, authorization/visibility incl. the issues-returns-PRs caveat, rate limits, freshness, compatibility), open-connector.md status, README row, milestone 5.1 ticked in the tasks spec.

author: hanagenuku
body:
## 背景
JRA全10場のコースデータ収集完了後、①データ収集→②特徴量実装の順で実際の特徴量化に
着手しました。当初「ダートの芝スタートフラグのみ実装」という縮小案を提示しましたが、
ユーザーから矛盾データの検証も含めた全項目の実装を求められ、以下の通り対応しました。

## 対応内容

### 1. web検索で拾った数値の矛盾を検証
- 阪神「外回り芝1200m」（JRA公式データでは1200mは内回りのみ）→ 再検索で否定。
  内回り専用、ゲート〜3コーナー243mと確定
- 札幌芝1200m「180m」「276m」の併存 → 再検索で「約400m」にほぼ統一
- 京都ダート1200m「900m」（一周1607.6mに対し不自然に長い）→ 再検索で「約400-410m」
  が正しいと確認

### 2. 内外回りの発走距離リストの見落としを発見・修正
阪神は内回り表・外回り表がそれぞれ独立した`発走距離`列を持つ構造で、`_first_value()`
が最初のtableの値しか見ておらず、外回り専用の1600m/1800m/2400m/2600mが欠落していた
と判明しました（中山・京都・新潟は1つのtableに(内)(外)タグ込みで全距離が入っており
この問題は起きていませんでした）。

### 3. `data/course_distance_profiles.json`を新規作成
venue×surfaceのみだった`course_profiles.json`の制約を解消するため、
venue×surface×distanceの粒度を持つ新規データファイルを作成:
- `dirt_turf_start`: 競馬場ごとのダート芝スタート距離リスト（JRA公式プロース文、高信頼）
- `loop_by_distance`: 中山・阪神・京都・新潟の芝について距離→内回り/外回りの対応表
- `hill`: 競馬場×surface(×内外回り)ごとの主要な坂の高低差・方向・位置
- `corner_tightness`: 同、コーナーのタイト度（Tight/Normal/Wide/Very Wide）
- `_start_to_corner_m_reference`: web検索由来の参考データ（信頼度が不均一なため特徴量化はせず保持のみ）

### 4. `src/features/engine.py`に実装
- `load_course_distance_profiles()` / `calc_course_distance_features()` / `_resolve_turf_loop()`を新規追加
- `calc_features_for_xgb()`に新規3特徴量: `f_dirt_turf_start` / `f_course_hill_diff` / `f_course_corner_tight`
- 内外回りで坂・コーナー特性が同じ場（中山等）はloop接尾辞なしキーにフォールバックする設計
- 未定義の組み合わせは安全なデフォルト値に落ちる

## 学習/推論パリティ
`calc_features_for_xgb()`は学習データ生成と推論の両方から呼ばれる共通関数のため、
コード変更のみでパリティは自動的に保たれます。

## ⚠ 次のアクション（このPRのスコープ外）
今回追加した3特徴量は既存の`xgb_fukusho_model.pkl`の学習時には存在しませんでした。
**次回のColab再学習で特徴量重要度・AUCへの寄与を確認する必要があります**
（North Star「データなしの特徴量追加をしない」に従い、実データ根拠は確保済みですが
モデルへの実際の寄与はまだ未検証です）。

## テスト
`tests/test_features.py`に11テスト新規追加。実装中に「中山は内外回りで坂の値が
同じためloop接尾辞なしキーでしか登録していない」ことに起因するlookup失敗を
実際にテストで検出・修正しました。

```
python -m pytest tests/ -q
323 passed
```

- **tests/fuzz/fuzz_udp_packet_parse.cpp** — Fuzz target for UDP packet deserialization. Exercises all packet types: PlayerInput, ServerSnapshot, ClientHello, ServerWelcome, ServerReject, Heartbeat, ClientReconnect. Also fuzzes ByteReader primitives and snapshot delta parsing.

author: homercles79
body:
Follow-up to #43. Comment and tests only — **no behaviour change**.

## The precondition nobody wrote down

`PlayerSerializer.plays/wins/win_rate` fall back to `0/0/None` via `IntegerField` defaults when a `Player` hasn't been through `with_record()` — the fresh one `POST` hands back. That works, but for a reason living outside the class:

> DRF's `Field.get_default()` raises `SkipField` when `self.default is empty` **or `self.root.partial`**.

So on a PATCH a default isn't a fallback at all — the key *disappears* from the response rather than reading `0`:

```
PlayerSerializer(unannotated_player)               -> {..., 'plays': 0, 'wins': 0, 'win_rate': None}
PlayerSerializer(unannotated_player, partial=True) -> {...}   # three keys gone
```

`PlayerSerializer` is safe purely because nothing uses it with `partial=True`. That's precisely the kind of invariant a later PATCH endpoint breaks silently — the response quietly loses three keys and nothing fails.

## What this adds

A docstring note, and three tests in `PlayerSerializerDefaultsTests`:

1. **the contract** — unannotated Player serializes as `0/0/None`
2. **the failure mode** — the same Player under `partial=True` drops the keys, so the conditional nature of the guarantee is pinned rather than described
3. **the precondition** — scans `api_views.py` and asserts `PlayerSerializer` is not among the `partial=True` usages

### The scan has a control

Test 3 asserts the regex finds *exactly* `['CollectionEntrySerializer', 'PlayLogSerializer']`. Without that, moving the PATCH endpoints to another module or reformatting the call makes the scan match nothing — and it would keep passing while guarding nothing. A silently vacuous guard is worse than no guard.

## Correcting #43

PR #43's description claimed `PlayerSerializer` had a **live latent bug** here. It does not — that claim was wrong, and [a comment on #43](https://github.com/homercles79/bgdb.app/pull/43#issuecomment-5055135607) now says so. `CollectionEntry.play_count` did need `SerializerMethodField`, for the narrower reason that `CollectionEntrySerializer` *is* one of the two partial serializers.

## Verification

268 tests pass (was 265), `ruff` clean.

author: geodro
body:
On macOS `lerd start` prompted to reinstall the DNS sudoers rule on every run, even when the installed `/etc/sudoers.d/lerd` was byte identical to the recorded hash.

The cause is the passwordless-liveness probe that decides whether the drop-in is still active. It lived in the platform-shared setup code and was hardcoded to resolvectl, a systemd tool that only exists on Linux. On macOS the drop-in never grants resolvectl, so `sudo -n` always refused with "a password is required", which the probe read as a conclusive "the grant is gone", forcing a rewrite and a sudo prompt every time.

This makes the probe command platform specific. Linux keeps resolvectl. macOS probes with `mkdir -p /etc/resolver`, a command the drop-in already grants verbatim and which is idempotent, so it succeeds silently when the grant is live and only reports it gone when sudo genuinely refuses.

Refs #1101

author: ymote
body:
## Symptom
A research lane added **via the wizard**, on the **same profile** being viewed,
never appeared in `/research` — it showed "No research lanes configured."

## Root cause (verified by full-flow trace)
The lane was silently saved as the profile's **primary provider**, not a lane.

Picking the route from the guided chain (`SetProviderSelection` on
`MENU_ONBOARD_ROUTE`) rebuilds the wizard root via `close_all_menus()` + reopen.
That momentarily removes `MENU_ONBOARD` from the stack, and the abandon-guard
`clear_research_lane_intent_if_wizard_closed` — which fires on stack teardown —
reads it as "wizard abandoned" and clears `research_lane_intent` **mid-flight**.
At Save, `onboarding_save_provider_command` then sees the flag `false` and routes
to `profile/llm/upsert` (primary provider) instead of
`profile/sub_providers/upsert` (the lane). So `sub_providers` stayed empty and
the cheap/strong picker never opened.

(The competing "no re-list after upsert" theory was **refuted** — the mutation
handler does refresh the cache; the lane just never got saved as a lane.)

## Fixes
1. **Root cause** — `reopen_onboard_root_preserving_lane_intent()` captures the
   intent across the transient collapse and restores it (used at the route pick
   and the family twin). Scoped so genuine abandon-detection (Esc / real close)
   still fires — the existing `research_lane_intent_dies_with_the_wizard_surface`
   test still passes.
2. **Composer pre-fill** — "Add a lane…" now runs the bare `/research add` path
   (opens the picker) instead of `EditComposer("/research add ")`.
3. **Onboarding clutter** — the Workspace/Activate and "Exit octos-tui" rows are
   hidden when `research_lane_intent` (gated so first-launch onboarding is
   unchanged).
4. **Fast vs strong** — the `cheap`/`strong` picker was already correct but
   unreachable (intent lost before Save); fixing #1 restores it.

**Flow now:** `/research` (auto-lists) → Add a lane → model picker (no clutter)
→ family/model/route (**intent preserved**) → Save → **fast (cheap)/strong** →
lane upsert → re-list → lane appears.

## Test
`research_lane_intent_survives_route_pick_in_the_wizard` drives **real**
`SetFamilyId → SetModelId → SetProviderSelection` route navigation and asserts
the intent survives — prior lane tests forced the flag directly and bypassed the
route menu, so none caught this. Full lib suite green (1595), fmt/clippy clean,
validated against git-pinned `octos-core` (rc.13, `8a9cb2c`).

author: panding19
body:
## Root cause

The minimal Bash detachment classifier strips heredoc bodies before looking for shell-level backgrounding, but its heredoc declaration pattern recognized quoted and unquoted delimiters only. POSIX-valid backslash-quoted delimiters such as `<<\EOF` were therefore missed, so an ampersand inside the heredoc data was misclassified as shell-level detachment and the command was rejected.

## Changes

- Recognize a leading backslash-quoted heredoc delimiter when removing heredoc bodies.
- Add a regression case proving that background-like text inside `<<\EOF` data is ignored by detachment classification.

author: alpcaner
body:
The BLE advertising-data budget was **mis-documented and enforced inconsistently across backends** — found on E1M-AEN801 silicon (#480 / PR #888): a 15-char name + one 128-bit service UUID = 38 bytes > 31 failed `advertise_start` with `ALP_ERR_INVAL` on the CC3501E backend, while the Zephyr backend didn't pre-check it at all.

Root cause: the legacy adv PDU is 31 bytes (Flags 3 + 2+strlen(name) + 2+16*num_services), so the true name cap is 26 alone / 8 with one 128-bit UUID — but `include/alp/ble.h:99` documented "≤ 29" (unsatisfiable; Flags always eats 3), and only CC3501E enforced it.

## Changes
- **`include/alp/ble.h`** — `name` doc now states the real 31-byte budget. Comment-only, **no ABI change** (`abi_snapshot.py --diff` clean).
- **`src/ble_dispatch.c`** — new `alp_ble_adv_data_size()` + `ALP_BLE_ADV_LEGACY_MAX_LEN` (31), enforced in `alp_ble_advertise_start()` **before backend dispatch** — one choke point, so Zephyr and CC3501E now reject identically. The calc matches `cc3501e.c` `pack_adv_data()` element-for-element (verified in review); ext-adv (none in the portable API) would relax this.
- **`src/backends/ble/zephyr_drv.c`** — dropped the stale "trust the caller / v0.3.x ext-adv" comment.
- **`tests/unit/ble_registry`** — over-budget (38B) → `ALP_ERR_INVAL`; at-budget (**exactly 31B**) → accepted. Both proven to fail against pre-fix code.

`scripts/test-all.sh --target dev` green (clang-format, metadata, pytest 1481, twister). The `generated-files` stage flags only the `docs/abi/v0.12-snapshot.json` `"generated"` date stamp (2026-07-22→23) — pre-existing base drift, not this diff, and non-required on dev.

Refs #480 (the CC3501E path; complements #888's bench proof). No SoM label — cross-backend portability fix.

body:
Closes plan Category A items A.3 + A.4 in a single PR (per user's
\"reuse one PR, multiple commits\" instruction).

## Summary

Locks the freshly-shipped nexus.search.v1.SearchService wire
contract into CI so v2 refactors (trigram, streaming, adaptive
strategy) cannot silently regress the v1 surface.

The manual grpcurl smoke test that A.3 called out (\"live cluster
serves Glob/Grep\") is subsumed by the CI E2E — the test IS the
verification, per plan principle #9 (\"Docker Docker Docker — never
trust 'cdylib compiles' as done\").

## Commit walk-through

1. **feat(docker): search-plugin-test image** — mirrors
   Dockerfile.local-connector-plugin. Two-stage build compiles the
   \`nexus-search-plugin\` cdylib against the pinned nexus-vfs SHA,
   Ed25519-signs with the same PLUGIN_SIGNING_PRIVKEY secret the
   release pipeline uses, and drops the signed dylib + .sig into
   /plugins in a FROM-nexusd-cluster:latest runtime stage.

2. **feat(docker): federation-test proto stubs** — generates
   search_pb2 + search_pb2_grpc at image-build time from the Rust
   workspace's proto SSOT and installs them under the existing
   /opt/proto stub tree so the runner can speak nexus.search.v1.
   Codegen-at-build (not committed under src/) because there is no
   Python runtime consumer of the proto today.

3. **feat(docker): single-node compose** — new
   \`docker-compose.search-plugin-e2e.yml\`. Single \`node\` service
   using the search-plugin-test image, one \`test\` service using the
   federation-test runner. No federation — v1 search has no
   cross-node semantics.

4. **test(search-plugin): E2E suite** — new \`test_search_plugin.py\`
   + \`search_helpers.py\`. Four cases matching the plan's A.4 punch
   list: recursive glob, grep with context, glob truncation,
   grep-skips-binary. Module-scoped fixture gates on gRPC-reachable
   AND \"plugins loaded from --plugin-dir\" log line — a broken
   plugin load surfaces as a clear diagnostic, not an opaque
   Unimplemented gRPC error.

5. **ci: search-plugin E2E workflow** — mirrors
   cc-tasks-share-e2e.yml shape. Change-gated skip on unrelated PRs,
   buildx + gha cache, PLUGIN_SIGNING_PRIVKEY secret wired through
   compose. 20-min ceiling (half of federation-e2e since this suite
   is single-node + 4 fast tests).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR (workflow runs itself thanks to change-gated regex including this workflow's paths)
- [ ] \`plugins loaded from --plugin-dir\` log line appears in node container logs (module fixture)
- [ ] All 4 test cases pass
- [ ] Follow-up: after v2 trigram lands, extend suite with cross-node cases

## What ships

The headline is #182 — `ChangePasswordForSAMAccountName` and `ResetPasswordForSAMAccountName` wrote the Active-Directory-only `unicodePwd` attribute unconditionally, so **no password could be changed or reset on OpenLDAP or any other non-AD directory**. author: kartben
body:
## What

Bump the main-thread stack for the `qemu_cortex_a53` `accelerometer_chart` build from the upstream default of 4 KB to 8 KB, via a new `zephyr-module/conf/lvgl-accel.conf` fragment wired into `tools/samples.manifest`. Adds `docs/a53-lvgl-stack.md` with the full diagnosis.

## Why

On `qemu_cortex_a53`, `accelerometer_chart` could die with an Instruction Abort at **PC=0** and a register file full of *architecturally-impossible* values (e.g. `x16=0x0000017c0000024c`, `lr=0x13_00000001` — non-zero junk in the upper 32 bits, which a 32-bit AArch64 op can never produce). That is the textbook fingerprint of a wasm32 JIT zero-extension miscompile, and this JIT family has a documented history of miscompiling hot blocks — so it looked like an emulator bug.

**It isn't.** It's a plain guest **main-thread stack overflow**. The sample ships `CONFIG_MAIN_STACK_SIZE=4096`, a value tuned for the 32-bit `native_sim` host it targets upstream. On the 64-bit A53, `lv_timer_handler`'s frames plus `LOG_ERR`'s deferred `cbprintf` packaging overrun 4 KB. The "impossible" registers were just adjacent 32-bit stack words read back as one 64-bit value, and `PC=0` was a `blr` through a clobbered pointer.

## How it was confirmed

Reproduced in-browser on the A53 JIT emulator (with the driver's `SENSOR_CHAN_ACCEL_XYZ` handling temporarily reverted to force the `-ENOTSUP` → `LOG_ERR` path):

| Experiment | Result |
|---|---|
| `LOG_MODE_IMMEDIATE` | still crashes, byte-identical garbage |
| `MAX_XLAT_TABLES` bump | no effect (the "xlat tables low 7/8" boot warning is unrelated) |
| `MAIN_STACK_SIZE` 4 K→16 K | **crash gone** — fatal behavior is stack-*size* sensitive |
| **`STACK_SENTINEL` at 4 K** | **`FATAL ERROR 2: Stack overflow`**, with a register below the stack limit — decisive |

An upstream **TCI** build (`QEMU_AARCH64_ACCEL=tci`) of the same ELF was a red herring: it dies *earlier* on a host-sensor MMIO external abort during init (the upstream/TCI sensor patch wires the device differently and never reaches the timer path), with a clean register file that proves nothing either way.

## Verification

- `STACK_SENTINEL` + broken driver at **8 KB** runs indefinitely (LOG_ERR every tick) instead of overflowing in ~40 ms at 4 KB.
- The shipped build (fixed driver + 8 KB) renders the live chart correctly — driving Accel X raises the red trace while the green Z trace holds at 9.81 m/s².

## Notes for the reviewer

- The crash *trigger* is already gone on `main` (the host-sensor driver answers `SENSOR_CHAN_ACCEL_XYZ`, so the shipped sample never takes the error path). This stack bump is defense-in-depth against the underlying 4 KB fragility.
- Only the shipped config change (8 KB stack) is included; `STACK_SENTINEL` was a debug aid, not committed.
- `lvgl_music` is another LVGL sample on this board worth watching if it ever grows a hot logging path (noted in the doc).

author: macieklamberski
body:
This PR rejoins a url split by a word-break tag before linkifying runs.

Email clients (Gmail/Outlook) and some CMSs break long links across `<wbr>` word-break tags, e.g. `https://youtu.be/<wbr>HnLpU5vd5rI`. A `<wbr>` is invisible and contentless, but it fragments the text node it sits in, so when the url is bare (not already an `<a>`), `linkifyUrls` sees only the part before the `<wbr>` and produces a **dead stub** `<a href="https://youtu.be/">`, dropping the id to plain text after it.

This is **not host-specific**: it is how email clients handle *any* long url, so it lands across blogs, news/newsletter sites, and utility links. YouTube is a small slice of it.

## Fix

New `stripWordBreaks` transform removes every `<wbr>` and merges the surrounding text (via `normalize()`) so the url is whole again. It runs just before `linkifyUrls`. It has **no host or url logic**, it just strips the tag, so it covers every case, including a `<wbr>` that splits the hostname itself (`blogspot.<wbr>com`). The reader controls its own wrapping, so the break hint is not needed downstream.

- **Bare url** (the broken case) → the full url linkifies into one working link.
- **Already-anchored url** (the common, benign case, the `<wbr>` is only in the display text, href already clean) → unchanged behaviour, link keeps working; the invisible hint is just dropped from the text.

## Prevalence (corpus)

`<wbr>` appears in ~0.15% of feeds (303 of a 198,826-feed sample, ~19k corpus-wide). Within those, the `<wbr>`-split urls span many hosts, YouTube is only ~3%:

| Host | wbr-split urls (sample) |
|---|--:|
| *.blogspot.com | ~291 (one email-heavy feed) |
| lewrockwell.com | 45 |
| facebook.com | 44 |
| youtube.com + youtu.be | 23 |
| unz.com / globalresearch.ca | 18 each |
| off-guardian.org / lifenews.com / screencast.com / goo.gl / paypal.com / rt.com / flickr.com / drive.google.com / … | tail |

Ground truth on the YouTube slice (the one my scoped audit measured): of the 47 feeds carrying a `youtu.be/<wbr>` url, **5 produce a dead `youtu.be/` stub** through the current pipeline; with the fix all 47 come out clean. That is a lower bound: the same break happens on every host above.

author: andtii
body:
Closes #771.

Docs queued: signalxjs/signalxjs.github.io#312.

## The gap

On `sigx run:web` the WhatsApp/chat composer **rendered but its text field couldn't be focused or typed into** (the user's report). The composer's input is `MarkdownEditor` → `RichTextInput` → the custom element `<sigx-richtext>`, whose manifest declares `"platforms": ["android","ios"]` — a native element (UITextView / EditText) with **no web implementation**. On `@lynx-js/web-core`, `__CreateElement` does `document.createElement('sigx-richtext')`; with no custom element defined it's an inert `HTMLUnknownElement`. Every other part of the composer (buttons, emoji, drag) is web-capable; only the input was native-only.

## The fix — a real web element

A `contenteditable` custom element (`packages/lynx-richtext/src/web/element.ts`) that mirrors the native contract verified against `SigxRichTextUI.swift` + web-core:

- **Model:** the same `RichDoc` (`{text,spans,blocks,v}`), UTF-16 offsets throughout, mentions as one U+FFFC covered by a `mention` span, blocks on `\n` line boundaries.
- **Render + read:** model → editable DOM (block elements, inline wrappers, `contenteditable=false` mention chips) and back (tolerant of the browser's structural edits). Round-trips are unit-tested.
- **Events:** `change {doc,isComposing}`, `selection {start,end,activeFormats,activeBlock,headingLevel?,caretX,caretY,caretHeight}`, `heightchange {height,lines}`, and `lynxfocus`/`lynxblur` (the names web-core's binding maps `focus`/`blur` to — the one silent-failure trap).
- **Commands** (web-core calls `element[method](params)`): `setDocument` / `toggleFormat` / `setBlockType` / `applyFormat` / `insertText` / `setSelectionRange` / `insertChip` / `focus` / `blur`.
- **Version/echo:** a `localVersion` bumped per user edit; `setDocument` dropped + re-emitted while composing or when `doc.v < localVersion`, else applied with `max`.

**Registration:** the element registers in the host page's main document (where web-core creates elements — the MTS iframe isn't where the DOM lives). It ships as a self-contained, self-registering module `@sigx/lynx-richtext/web-element` (import-free, servable raw like `@sigx/lynx-web-host`'s `host.js`). `@sigx/lynx-cli` resolves it from the **app's** deps and serves it to the generated host page — gated on the app actually using richtext, so web-host stays uncoupled. (`resolveWebElements` is a fixed list of one for now; the scalable next step is a `web` section in `signalx-module.json`, noted for follow-up.)

Two subtleties worth calling out in review:
- The editor lives inside the `<lynx-view>` **shadow root**, so `document.getSelection()` can't see the selection (it reports the shadow host) — the element uses `ShadowRoot.getSelection()`. Without this, no `selection` events fire and mentions/caret break.
- A collapsed `toggleFormat` is a no-op on web (select-then-toggle; native's typing-attribute path is native-only). `confirm-type` is advisory (no on-screen return key).

## Verification (Chrome, `sigx run:web`)

- **Chat composer:** input focuses; typing lands with correct `change` events; placeholder shows/hides; the bar **auto-grows** as text wraps (up to the 4-line cap); `@` triggers the mention popup **anchored at the caret** (proving `selection` + `caretRect`).
- **Markdown editor demo** (not in a sheet): renders bold + the `@Andy` chip from the initial value with correct markdown output; selecting a word + tapping **Bold** formats it and round-trips to `**Hello**` in the markdown output — the Phase-2 toolbar commands work end-to-end.

Unit tests (`packages/lynx-richtext/__tests__/web-element-{model,dom}.test.ts`, happy-dom): codec parity, render↔read round-trips (multi-line, headings, inline formats, mention chips, emoji), full offset↔DOM-point mapping, the format/block commands, and the `setDocument` version/echo gating. Plus `hostHtml`/`resolveWebElements` wiring in the CLI. `pnpm typecheck` clean; `pnpm test` 2740 passed / 8 skipped (259 files); `pnpm lint` unchanged (73 pre-existing warnings).

## Known gap (separate issue)

Inside the composer's bottom sheet, tapping the **mention popup** or the **send button** is still dead on web — the sheet's `setPointerCapture` retargets the `pointerup`/`click` away from the descendant (trace: `pointerdown → popup`, `pointerup/click → the sheet`). Same root cause as the send button; filed and detailed on **#764** (which also needs to honor `ignore-focus` on web — prototyped there). The **input itself** — the reported symptom — is fully fixed.

Native is unaffected (web-only source + host-page wiring).

author: linxia0415
body:
closes #37118

PR is adding some context information to be available in the `access-token` without a need to introduce any additional custom claims. So far, it provides info about:

- session type (online, offline, transient), which was used to create the token
- token type (regular or lightweight token)
- grant type

These informations can be useful when token is later sent to some Keycloak endpoints (for example introspection, userInfo, admin/account REST API) to optimize something. For example:
- session-type will allow to lookup only correct session type based on the type of the session, which token was created from. As for example today, we need to lookup "online" session and if it is not found, then fallback to "offline" session. So possible unnecessary lookup. Related follow-up issue for optimize that: #37662

- Grant type knowledge can be useful for example for the token-exchange use-case: #37117

- Lightweight access token: We will be able to recognize more reliably if access-token is lightweight or not and do something based on that (EG. lookup roles from model instead of lookup roles from the token)

In this PR, I've made token ID to look something like `onrtac:1f65761e-1c69-40a2-82da-2d8aa5e39a8a` .
  - The first 2 characters is shortcut for "session type" - `on` is shortcut for "online" session
  - The next 2 characters is shortcut for "token type" - `rt` is shortcut for regular token (not lightweight token)
  - The next 2 characters is shortcut for grant type - `ac` is shortcut for "authorization code" grant

Shortcuts are used, so the token ID contains important info, but at the same time, it is limited in size and does not introduce much new characters to the token.

The encoding into ID is used only for access-tokens. Not used for refresh tokens or ID tokens or any others.

Introduced dedicated SPI in the end. Wanted to "cache" some objects (EG. shortcuts for grant types etc) and it seems clearer to me to cache them at the level of factory, rather than in the static fields, which is not very pretty. Moreover, provider adds ability for someone to introduce his own provider (and eventually encode some more info or encode stuff in the different way etc).

#### Note

I've used 2 commits in this PR. Originally, in the 1st commit, I've made the encoding a bit longer with token ID to look something like `st.on_tt.rt_gt.ac:1f65761e-1c69-40a2-82da-2d8aa5e39a8a` .
  - The `st` is shortcut for "session type" and `on` is shortcut for "online" session
  - The `tt` is shortcut for "token type" and `rt` is shortcut for regular token (not lightweight token)
  - The `gt` is shortcut for grant type and `ac` is shortcut for "authorization code" grant

But assuming that every "type" has always 2 characters long shortcut, I've rather updated it in the 2nd commit to have only 7 new characters instead of 18 characters. I planned to squash before merge (unless you think that we should rather use longer format for some reason, in which case the 2nd commit can be removed from the PR).

author: cesteral
body:
## Description

Follow-up code fixes from a cross-repo review of the governance decision-token lifecycle (mint → carry → verify → consume-once). These are the changes that were safe to make in-code on the verify/enforce side; the npm-republish, deploy-wiring, and Terraform items are tracked as issues (#165, #166, #167).

- **`verifyDecisionToken` no longer throws on a jti-store outage.** A `FirestoreJtiStore` propagating `UNAVAILABLE`/`PERMISSION_DENIED` previously escaped the (documented never-throws) verifier and, under `warn`, silently hard-blocked a legitimate write with no token verdict or metric. It now returns a distinct `JTI_STORE_ERROR` verdict: `warn` logs + proceeds, `enforce` blocks (fails closed — replay protection could not be established).
- **`resolveTokenMode` resolves per-contract list conflicts strictest-first** (`enforce > warn > off`). A contractId placed in both the `OFF` and `ENFORCE` lists previously resolved to `off`, silently un-governing a money-moving write; it now resolves to the stricter mode.
- **`executableArgsExclude ?? []` guard** in the factory before `canonicalizeExecutableArgs`. The field is required by the authoring type but optional in the loose release Zod schema, so a legacy annotation could reach here `undefined` and crash the write (even under `warn`) instead of verifying.
- **`InMemoryJtiStore` inclusive `>= t` expiry boundary** (with a matching strict `< t` sweep) so a replay landing on the exact token-expiry millisecond cannot pass both the expiry and store checks.
- **`FirestoreJtiStore` writes `expiresAt` as a `Date`** (Firestore Timestamp) rather than an ISO string, so a Firestore TTL policy can actually reclaim entries (a policy only acts on Timestamp fields).

## Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Test
- [ ] Refactor

## Server(s) Affected

- `shared` (`packages/shared/src/governance/*`, `packages/shared/src/utils/tool-handler-factory.ts`)

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm run build` passes (contract-hash, contract-schema, shared)
- [x] `pnpm run typecheck` passes (shared)
- [x] New functionality includes tests
- [x] No secrets in diff
- [x] Follows existing patterns
- [ ] If modifying `@cesteral/shared`: rebuilt all packages — **downstream servers not yet rebuilt in this env; CI should run the full fleet build/test**

## Testing Notes

`vitest run` on the governance + factory + contract-hash suites: **95 shared governance/factory tests + 45 contract-hash tests pass.** New regression tests added:
- `JTI_STORE_ERROR` verdict surfaced (not thrown) when the store rejects; earlier binding failures still never reach the store.
- `warn` mode proceeds and `enforce` mode blocks when the injected jti store throws (factory-level).
- Per-contract list conflict resolves to the stricter mode (`config`).

Related issues: #165 (contract-hash `__proto__` fix republish), #166 (wire the distributed jti store + boot-time safety check), #167 (Firestore DB + TTL policy in Terraform).

body:
### Description

When a group has more members than the panel is tall enough to show, the group side nav (`DockGroupSidebar`) previously just scrolled. This folds the members that don't fit into a bottom **"show more"** button that opens them in a flyout, driven by the rail's measured frame height — so the rail never scrolls.

- **Height-based capacity.** The rail root is measured with `useElementBounding` (mirroring `DockPanel`). A new pure `deriveSidebarCapacity` helper turns the available height into an integer capacity, then feeds the existing `docksSplitGroupsWithCapacity` split. It reserves the show-more button's slot only once overflow is unavoidable (two-pass), and budgets for sub-category dividers so a multi-sub-category group never clips.
- **Reused components.** The flyout reuses `DockGroupPopover` (passed only the overflowed members), opened through a dedicated `docksSidebarOverflowPanel` floating slot (placement `right`) so it stays independent of the dock bar's group/overflow popovers. The trigger matches the dock bar's `DockOverflowButton` — the same dots icon and a `9+`-capped count badge.
- **Hidden selection stays visible.** When the active tool is one of the hidden members, the show-more button lights up (also while the flyout is open), so a hidden selection remains discoverable.
- The rail switches from `of-y-auto` to `of-y-hidden`; all three hosts (`DockPanel`, `DockStandalone`, `DockEdge`) inherit the behavior.

### Linked Issues

### Additional context

- Unit tests cover the capacity derivation and the overflow split (`dock-sidebar-capacity.test.ts`).
- An `Overflow` Storybook story on a constrained-height shell demonstrates the folded rail with a highlighted show-more button.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm build` all pass. The `.generated/css.ts` change is the UnoCSS artifact regenerated from the new template classes.

author: rushirb2001
body:
Everything since `v0.5.14`: 35 commits covering per-branch data, a unified overlay
language, onboarding, and a CLI that teaches instead of erroring.

## Added

- **Per-branch CI and sync status.** Multi-branch repos expand into a row per branch,
  each with its own checks, ahead/behind, and status. CI is keyed by ref rather than
  the checked-out worktree, so this is a real per-branch fetch and not an echo of the
  default branch. Capped at 10 branches per repo to stay inside the rate budget.
- **Open PR counts land on their base branch**, so a PR shows against the branch it
  actually targets.
- **`P` on a multi-branch repo asks which branch to push.** Bulk push now targets only
  repos that actually have unpushed commits.
- **A first-run launch screen** in the plain terminal before the dashboard: a
  super-fleet view listing every detected folder, and a scoped view for `--root`.
  `--watch` skips both, so a live loop needs no keypress.
- **`cohors scan` prints a human report** grouped by urgency, with progress announced
  on stderr. Piped, redirected, or with `--json` it emits the same JSON it always did.
- **`cohors mcp` run by hand explains itself** instead of sitting silent: what it is,
  the registration line for Claude Code and the JSON `mcpServers` block for every other
  client (both with the absolute path, since agents spawn with a stripped `PATH`), and
  which tools each `--allow-*` flag unlocks.

## Changed

- **Every overlay shares one framed-table language.** Standup, detail pane, command
  palette, shell prompt, confirm dialog, open-with picker, and run output rebuilt as
  two divider-joined columns with no floating inner boxes.
- **Action commands teach instead of erroring.** A missing `--select`, `-m`, or
  `<COMMAND>` prints the verb's guide and exits 0 having touched nothing.
- **`cohors --help` carries the masthead**, a brand-matched clap palette, and a
  "start here" footer. `cohors web` gained the same grammar.
- **Readability pass:** bold repo names, italic branch rows with a hollow triangle
  marker, and a soft selection wash replacing the reverse-video block that swallowed
  dim cells.

## Fixed

- GitHub enrichment applies refreshed data even when a remote was already set; stale
  cache entries are evicted on access as well as insert.
- Open PRs counted via the REST `pulls` endpoint (5000/hr) instead of the search API
  (30/min), which was rate-limiting real fleets.
- MCP handles client disconnect gracefully instead of erroring on a broken pipe, and
  `--allow-open` is actually wired to the `open` tool.
- Content search runs in parallel across repos.

## Docs and assets

- Demo tape now emits both `tui.gif` and `tui-preview.png` from one run, so they cannot
  drift. Hero frame moved onto the multi-branch repo; 24fps to 20fps.
- README: corrected tool lists (`changes` was missing from reads, `push`/`commit` from
  actions), absolute-path MCP registration, per-branch rows, current keymap.

## Verification

All four gates pass: `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`cargo test --all`, and the WASM core build.

Known gap: `assets/web.gif` is still from July and was not regenerated (no tape exists
for it; it is a browser recording).

author: aishaalkldi
body:
## Purpose

A reusable, presentation-only `BlockRunner` for Warm-up and Cool-down blocks — the third block type (alongside Reach the Light's `movement-target` and D1's `movement-pattern`), needed for the Neuro Rehabilitation roadmap's 6-block session structure (Calibration → Warm-up → Reach the Light → D1 → Cool-down → Session Summary).

## Duration completion

Duration-based completion consumes a **required** `blockElapsedSeconds` tick-input field, supplied by the caller from `SessionOrchestratorSnapshot.blockElapsedSeconds` — which the orchestrator already guarantees excludes paused/safetyHold time via its own `PausableTimer`.

**There is no internal wall-clock duration calculation and no pause/safetyHold ticking convention.** An earlier version of this runner tried to reconstruct pause-aware duration internally (`accumulatedActiveMs` / `activeSinceMs` / a "freeze on inactive tick" mechanism) and remained incorrect whenever the caller simply didn't tick during a pause — which is exactly `InteractiveShoulderSession.tsx`'s existing, established convention for the target/pattern runners today (`if (sessionState === "active") { ...tick... }`, never ticked otherwise). That machinery has been removed entirely. The state model is now just `{ completed: boolean }`; `blockElapsedSeconds` is a required `number`, not optional, so there is no silent fallback path to detect or guard against.

Verified directly, at the raw-lifecycle, gating, and public-runner layers: a block ticked at `blockElapsedSeconds=0`, then `=3`, with **zero calls of any kind** for a simulated 30-second pause, then resumed at `blockElapsedSeconds=3` — does not complete on resume, and completes only once `blockElapsedSeconds` reaches the target (`10`), regardless of how far `nowMs` has advanced.

## Acknowledgement completion

Also supported — an explicit `acknowledged: true` signal completes immediately regardless of `blockElapsedSeconds`, exactly once (completion-once guarded, mirroring `target-lifecycle.ts`/`pattern-lifecycle.ts`'s existing pattern).

## Clinical isolation

Emits no repetitions, target contacts, patterns completed, valid repetitions, ROM, compensation, or any measured clinical data. The completion event carries only `{ capturedAtMs, reason: "duration" | "acknowledged" }`; the state carries only `{ completed: boolean }`.

## No production call-site wiring in this PR

`InteractiveShoulderSession.tsx` has zero diff. The registry (`registerInstructionalBlockRunner` / `resolveInstructionalBlockRunner`) mirrors `target-block-runner.ts`/`pattern-block-runner.ts` exactly — additive only, not consumed by any production call site yet. Reach the Light, D1, `SessionOrchestrator`, and all database/treatment-plan code are untouched.

## Tests

- `instructional-lifecycle.test.ts` — 26/26 pass
- `instructional-lifecycle-gating.test.ts` — 6/6 pass
- `block-engine/instructional-block-runner.test.ts` — 13/13 pass
- `instructional-copy.test.ts` — 1/1 pass
- All `block-engine/*.test.ts` (target + pattern + registry + instructional) — 34/34 pass
- `interactive-shoulder/*.test.ts` (top-level regression) — 69/69 pass
- `interactive-shoulder/motion-patterns/*.test.ts` (D1) — 30/30 pass, unchanged
- `session-orchestrator/session-orchestrator.test.ts` — 29/29 pass, unchanged
- `cv/*.test.ts` (full suite) — 555/555 pass, unchanged

## Build

`npm run build` — success, no errors.

## Explicitly out of scope

- PR 2 (wiring this runner into `InteractiveShoulderSession.tsx`) is not started.

author: anveio
body:
## What changed

- classify QEMU `io-error` as a recycle-required VM state and capture the failing block devices through QMP
- recycle unowned unusable workers and refill the warm-pool slot in the same convergence pass
- cordon ZFS-capacity-starved hosts before launching or offering listeners, with a second admission check before durable-volume materialization
- emit nanosecond-resolution storage-admission and QEMU block-failure evidence

## Why

A six-job Turborepo benchmark filled the hostd dataset while the underlying pool still appeared to have free space. QEMU paused all affected guests in `io-error`; hostd treated the processes as alive but not running, so assignments remained stranded and summary jobs queued indefinitely.

This change makes the failure explicit and bounded: an affected assignment fails closed and its VM is recycled, while low ZFS dataset headroom removes the host from schedulable capacity before another listener is offered.

author: nwparker
body:
## Problem

In the mobile **native / rich chat** (not the terminal chat), attaching an image did nothing visible — the photo never appeared while composing or after sending.

## Root cause

The native chat reused the **terminal** attach flow, which uploads the image and immediately pastes a bracketed host file path into the terminal. That's correct for the terminal chat (the path shows in the visible input), but in native chat the terminal is hidden, so there was no composer preview and nothing in the transcript. The desktop rich chat instead holds images as composer chips and **rides them along on submit** — mobile was missing that model entirely.

## Fix (desktop parity)

- **Compose:** picking an image uploads it and shows a **removable thumbnail chip** in the composer (no early paste). Send is enabled with an attachment even with no text.
- **Submit:** the ride-along is `Ctrl+U clear -> bracketed image paste(s) (no Enter) -> 300 ms settle -> text + Enter` (mirrors desktop's `sendNativeChatMessageWithImageAttachments`); the leading clear keeps a retry idempotent.
- **After sent:** the optimistic echo carries the local preview URIs and the renderer draws `image-ref` blocks as real `<Image>` thumbnails when the URI is loadable, so the sent user bubble shows the photo. Image-only echoes reconcile by ordinal against the next user turn after their tail (ignores agent replies / paginated history / the rare `unknown` ack-loss path).
- The **terminal chat** attach path is unchanged (both flows consolidated behind `useMobileSessionImageAttachments`).

## Proof — driven by real clicks, not hand-fed props

An interactive harness (`mobile/rnw-preview/`, reproducible) mounts the **real** components + hooks (`MobileNativeChatComposer`, `MobileNativeChatMessage`, `useMobileNativeChatImageAttachments`, `useMobileNativeChatDrafts`) under react-native-web. The **only** faked things are the two OS boundaries a browser/CI can't reach: the native photo picker and the paired-host RPC socket. Every state below is produced by the real code reacting to clicks; the bottom panel prints the actual bytes the real send pipeline wrote to the (faked) socket.

**1 — initial:** Send disabled, `terminal.send calls (0)`.

![initial](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/nwparker/mobile-fixes/mobile/docs/native-chat-image-attachment/flow-1-initial.png?raw=true)

**2 — after clicking Attach:** the real upload pipeline runs and a thumbnail chip appears, Send enables, and still `terminal.send calls (0)` (image held, not pasted early).

![attached](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/nwparker/mobile-fixes/mobile/docs/native-chat-image-attachment/flow-2-attached.png?raw=true)

**3 — after clicking Send:** the sent bubble shows the photo thumbnail, the composer clears, and the trace shows the real ride-along the code emitted:
1. `""` (Ctrl+U clear), `enter=false`
2. `"[200~/host/tmp/orca-attach-42.png[201~"` (bracketed image paste), `enter=false`
3. `"Here is the layout bug"`, `enter=true`

![sent](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/nwparker/mobile-fixes/mobile/docs/native-chat-image-attachment/flow-3-sent.png?raw=true)

## Tests / checks

- **`pnpm test` — 2311 pass** (2 pre-existing skips), incl. new coverage for pick+upload, the exact ride-along byte order (clear -> paste -> settle -> text/Enter), attachments-only submit, retry-keeps-chips on rejection, pending->image-ref echo blocks, image-only echo reconciliation (agent-reply / pagination / rapid-send), and the renderable-URI gate.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check` — clean.

## Honest limitation

A fully on-device run (real iOS/Android app + live agent transcript) can't be automated headlessly — the native photo-picker modal isn't drivable and the mock host lacks the upload RPCs. The iOS 26.1 simulator runtime was installed, but that path needs a paired desktop + live agent. The proof above therefore drives the real app *logic* end-to-end with only the OS boundary faked; the send/echo/reconciliation is additionally covered by unit tests.

author: kduma
body:
Authors can mark a fenced block with the `ext:<name>` namespace and have its
body handed to an external process declared in docset.toml, which returns
Markdown (and optionally generated image files) that is spliced back into the
page and rendered normally. This is the escape hatch for content the bundled
compiler can't produce itself (e.g. compiling a label definition into an
example plus a rendered visualization).

Design:
- docset.toml gains `[extensions.<name>]` tables (command + optional args);
  path-like commands resolve against the source dir, bare names via PATH.
- A new `render_extensions` stage mirrors `render_diagrams`' opaque-fence
  scanner: it recovers the block body, spawns the command over a JSON-stdio
  protocol (request on stdin, `{markdown, assets}` on stdout), renders the
  returned Markdown, and injects any generated files as `assets/ext/…`
  attachments (reusing the existing asset table + rewrite).
- Running extensions is opt-in behind `khb compile --allow-extensions`, since
  docset.toml may be untrusted; without it, ext: blocks are left as plain code
  with a note, so the default build stays hermetic and offline.
- The AI-facing `md` column keeps the raw ext: source unchanged.

Tests: config parsing, the pure splice/asset-injection path, the off and
undeclared behaviours (khb-core), plus an end-to-end subprocess test driving a
tiny `khb-ext-stub` helper (behind the `ext-stub` feature so it never ships).
Docs: new authoring/extensions.md, plus docset-toml, compiler, diagrams and
format updates.

author: muthuishere
body:
Part of the fundamentals-completion campaign (pre-bri gate). Fixes the confirmed bug where only `Throwable`/`Exception` worked in catch position — `(catch ArithmeticException e ...)` silently never matched and the throw escaped (the observed G5006 was the uncaught error itself; the matcher was fail-closed with 4 names).

## What works now (all byte-identical: JVM oracle / interpreter / compiled)
- **Typed built-ins catchable**: ArithmeticException, ClassCastException, NullPointerException, IndexOutOfBoundsException (+String variant), IllegalArgumentException, NumberFormatException, IllegalStateException, UnsupportedOperationException, clojure.lang.ArityException, ExceptionInfo.
- **JVM ancestry honored**: `catch RuntimeException` catches an arithmetic error; NumberFormatException/ArityException < IllegalArgumentException — hierarchy verified against the oracle via `.getSuperclass`, encoded as `errors.Is` edges.
- **`instance?` works on exception classes** via the same table; java.lang names added to the class-ref table.
- **Raise sites re-typed message-for-message** (nil op → NPE, non-number → CCE, nth/subs → IndexOutOfBounds, "Infinite or NaN" → NFE), diag codes preserved.
- Both legs share ONE matcher (corelib CatchMatches) — parity by construction.

## Conformance
4 new dual-harness files (typed catches / hierarchy / catch-miss fall-through / instance? matrix), each oracle-run file-for-file; 2 existing catch-all workarounds tightened to typed catches with citation. 19-case smoke matrix byte-identical across all three executions.

ADR 0039 addendum records the mapping + scoping (parents/supers stay flattened; fail-closed stands). No new ADR number.

Gates: build/vet/gofmt/full test incl. dual harness (324s) — green.

author: felixgeelhaar
body:
Integration branch bringing click-cms from a barely-booting prototype to a broad, tested, feature-complete flat-file CMS — while holding its load-bearing constraints: **zero runtime dependencies** (runs on shared hosting), strict DDD layering, and TDD throughout.

## What's here

**Content & editing**
- Pages with schema-driven sections, dependency-free rich text, SEO metadata, i18n (locale is part of the content key), draft-and-publish, version history, and signed preview links.
- **Collections** — repeatable content types (blog posts, team members, …) defined as a JSON field schema; an entry is a content document whose type is the collection id, so it inherits draft/publish, history, audit and authorization for free. Includes **declared ordering** (sort entries by a field, e.g. date desc) and **relations** — a `reference` field type linking an entry to one or many other entries/pages, resolved to titles at read time (dangling links surfaced, delivery published-only). Public `/published` delivery for headless.
- **Visual builder** — a real node-tree editor plus the server renderer that consumes it.
- Drag-and-drop reordering for sections and repeater rows (arrows kept as the a11y fallback).

**Media** — responsive variants, quality warnings, focal point, strict SVG sanitising, and a library that scales (search, virtual folders, bulk delete).

**Navigation** — a rebuilt public site header (brand, active state, dropdowns, mobile menu, sticky) and a grouped, collapsible, mobile-drawer admin sidebar.

**Editorial plugins** — forms (honeypot, stored as data), menus, redirects, full-text search, backup, and a polling-based **collaboration** plugin (presence + review comments).

**Platform & security**
- Two storage backends (JSON + SQLite) behind one contract, with a versioning/audit decorator stack and a **capability backstop at the storage layer**; a migration CLI moves content between backends.
- Deny-by-default API guard, CSRF on state-changing requests, forced first-login password change, per-session files, per-owner content permissions.
- Headless mode; runtime operator settings (site name, headless) in the writable data dir.

## Verification
- **810 PHP tests, 151 admin (Vitest) tests — all green.**
- Every capability exercised end-to-end in a Docker container against a real browser (draft/publish, delivery guards, collaboration presence/comments, media, collections lifecycle).

## Notes
- Large branch (integration, ~111 commits). Best reviewed by area; commit messages explain the *why* of each change.
- Demo content uses a neutral "Acme Studio" placeholder — click-cms is a standalone product effort, not tied to any specific site.

| **Total événements** | **67** | **50** |
| html-balcons-dauphine | 17 | **perdu** (salve de HTTP 503 Gemini) |
| Gemini | tient presque tout le run | quota mort en cours → bascule DeepSeek |

La chute vient quasi entièrement de `balcons-dauphine` : Gemini renvoie des **HTTP 503** (surcharge) sur cette page, et comme 503 n'était pas rattrapé (≠ quota), la source était perdue au lieu de basculer sur un backup.

## Corrections (côté code)

1. **`temperature=0`** dans `_make_agent` : extraction et clarify déterministes → deux crawls sur le même contenu donnent le même résultat. (`autoagent` transmet bien `temperature` au provider.)
2. **Bascule sur erreur transitoire** : `run_llm` distingue désormais trois cas —
   - **quota** (429/rate limit) → déclasse le provider pour tout le run + bascule ;
   - **transitoire** (5xx, surcharge, timeout) → rejoue l'appel sur les backups **pour cet appel seulement**, sans déclasser (l'erreur passe souvent au coup d'après) ;
   - **réponse vide** → idem.
   
   Helper `_try_alternates` factorisé.

## Complément côté config (hors PR, dans Settings → Variables)

La 3ᵉ cause de variance est le **provider principal instable**. Recommandé : provider payant/stable en tête, palier gratuit Gemini retiré ou relégué en dernier —
```
QUEFAIRE_LLM  = deepseek:deepseek-v4-flash
QUEFAIRE_LLM2 = groq:llama-3.3-70b-versatile,mistral:mistral-small-latest
```
Documenté dans `CLAUDE.md`.

## Tests

`python -m pytest pipeline/tests -q` → **26 passent** (+1 : bascule sur 503 sans déclassement ; fakes agents mis à jour pour accepter le kwarg `temperature`). Aucun fichier de données généré touché.

## Was geändert wurde

- Teigschaber-Produktdaten und Product-JSON-LD auf der deutschen und englischen Seite vereinheitlicht
- Preis auf 24,99 EUR mit der zentralen Produktdatei abgestimmt
- unbelegte statische Verfügbarkeit und kostenlose Versandangaben aus dem Markup entfernt
- belastbaren Brettfinder-Fallback für fehlgeschlagene `products.json`-Ladevorgänge ergänzt
- Cache-Version der zentralen Produktdatei an einer Stelle gebündelt
- 38 aktive, verifizierte Listings als verfügbar ausgezeichnet
- vier bestätigte Verkäufe als `sold` archiviert und als individuell anfragbar dokumentiert
- nicht verfügbare Vorschauen zur Maßanfertigung statt zu einem Kaufpfad geführt

## Ursache

Produktdaten wurden über mehrere Cache-Versionen geladen. Bei einem Ladefehler blieb der Brettfinder in einem deaktivierten Ladezustand. Außerdem waren sichtbare und strukturierte Teigschaber-Daten nicht konsistent, während Verfügbarkeiten teilweise nur indirekt aus Linkzuständen abgeleitet wurden.

## Wirkung

Der normale Brettfinder bleibt unverändert. Bei einem Datenfehler erhalten Nutzer auf Mobile und Desktop zwei funktionierende Alternativen. Suchmaschinen sehen für den Teigschaber dieselben belastbaren Angaben wie Besucher. Verkaufte Produkte erscheinen nicht als verfügbar und führen nicht zu veralteten Etsy-Kaufpfaden.

- `git diff --check`

- `node --check assets/js/product-grid.js`
- `npm run audit:indexability`
- `npm run audit:assets`
- `npm run audit:products`

- hreflang-/Canonical-Prüfung
