author: rogeriochaves
body:
Post-merge dogfood batch from testing the codex provider and Langy in production (#6000 follow-up). Twelve reported issues, fixed across the settings flow, the Langy panel, the trace pipeline, cost tracking, the command palette, the agent's own behavior, and the support widget.


## Codex settings flow

**1. The coding-defaults dialog popped before Save, then Save was dead.** Connecting codex already persists the provider row at poll completion, so the drawer now closes on connect with a "Codex connected" toast and the ask moved to a page-level host that survives the drawer. Re-authentication skips the ask when Langy already runs on codex. The Langy and onboarding sign-in entry points are unchanged.

**2. Codex icon rendered tiny.** The icon was a span hard-sized to 1em instead of a bare viewBox svg like its siblings, so it never filled its slot. Rebuilt with identical artwork.

| Provider menu | Model picker |
|---|---|
| ![codex icon in provider menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langwatch/pr-screenshots/main/langy-polish-codex-icon-menu.png) | ![codex icon in model menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langwatch/pr-screenshots/main/langy-polish-codex-icon-model-menu.png) |

**3. The open Langy panel's model pill did not follow the new default.** The panel pins the resolved default into the store at open and never re-followed. Applying the coding defaults (from the dialog or the sign-in-with-defaults path) now snaps the pill immediately, unless the user had explicitly picked a model, which is never hijacked.

Plus from review: the paid-account recommendation blurb is removed (only "Langy uses this model to chat with you and help you work across the platform." remains), the "Open openai.com" label is white on the orange button, and first-party links no longer trigger the "This link leaves LangWatch" confirmation. Model-written links still do: the bypass is a marker attribute the markdown pipeline cannot emit, pinned by a test where an answer linking the same address still gets the dialog.

## Langy behavior

**4. "hi" was answered with "Can't do that yet."** The pre-send self-check discarded any draft with a user-aimed question mark unless it carried an executed result, so natural greeting replies died and the refusal fallback fired. The refusal is now defined as the answer to an out-of-scope request, never a default, with an explicit greeting path. Pinned by a dogfood scenario (hi, then who are you) that ran green end to end against a live stack.

**6.1. The system prompt said "You are OpenCode".** The engine has no identity config field, and overriding the whole prompt would drift with releases. A provisioned identity plugin now rewrites the name in place through the engine's documented system-transform hook, keeping every other byte of the stock prompt across upgrades. Verified live: newest spans carry "You are Langy, ...", zero spans with the old identity after the change.

**10. Trace searches counted Langy's own runs.** "what are my traces about?" answered "Mostly Langy conversations". Two-sided fix: the `langwatch` CLI gained `--origin` (comma-separated) on `trace search` and `trace export`, wired to the existing `traces.origin` filter where `application` also matches traces with no recorded origin; and the agent's rules now require origin scoping, defaulting to `--origin application`, adding `evaluation` or `simulation` when asked about those, and using `langy` only for explicit self-inspection.

**11. The performance skill dead-ended on empty evaluations.** "what has my agent been up to?" stopped at "No evaluation pass-rate data in last 24h" on a project full of traces. The skill now treats an empty metric as a coverage note: it answers from the sources that have data, traces first (origin-scoped), shares concrete observations, and closes by inviting a deep dive. Pinned by a second live scenario: on a project with traces and no evaluations the reply described real activity, flagged an errored trace and a latency outlier, and invited a follow-up.

**11.3. Empty replies to "Thanks!".** The model sometimes ends a turn with only reasoning output. Rule added that every turn ends with something visible, and the panel renders a thumbs up when a settled assistant message has nothing else to show (never for errored turns).

## Langy panel rendering

**5. The top fade dimmed the first message at zero scroll.** The mask now activates only once messages are scrolled off above.

| At rest | Scrolled |
|---|---|
| ![no fade at top](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langwatch/pr-screenshots/main/langy-polish-fade-top.png) | ![fade when scrolled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langwatch/pr-screenshots/main/langy-polish-fade-scrolled.png) |

**9.3 / 9.3.1. Reasoning titles littered the transcript and glued to the reply.** Codex reasoning-summary headlines stream on the same text channel as answer tokens and leaked into the durable answer ("Summarizing recent trace countsMostly Langy conversations..."). A conservative fold now peels them into the completed-actions receipt, shown as muted rows when expanded, and text parts always join with a paragraph break. The fold also repairs already-stored conversations, and the engine adapter now routes reasoning-part deltas as ephemeral reasoning frames by tracking part types, so they can never reach the durable answer again.

| Resting transcript | Expanded receipt |
|---|---|
| ![clean transcript](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langwatch/pr-screenshots/main/langy-polish-reasoning-folded.png) | ![reasoning titles inside the receipt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langwatch/pr-screenshots/main/langy-polish-reasoning-expanded.png) |

**9.2 / 11.4 / 11.1.** The thinking line no longer fades out at its tail; "Starting up", "Poking Langy", and the live thinking line share one geometry (same offsets, reserved orb slot) so the pre-work states stop jumping; plain prose blocks gained 2px horizontal padding to line up with card text.

**Later dogfood rounds in the same areas:** an empty settled reply (reasoning-only or stopped mid-turn) shows a quiet italic "No content" instead of a thumbs-up or an empty bubble; the empty streaming message shell renders nothing at all, so the transcript no longer jumps mid-startup; the drawer-vs-floating-panel choreography is sequenced both ways on one 450ms stagger (Langy dodges first, the drawer follows; the drawer leaves first, Langy glides back after); and the shift-hold context arming is removed entirely, the # latch being the one way into pointing mode.

## Conversations always continue

Switching models mid-conversation, or coming back days later, met a fresh worker that knew nothing: the turn carried only the last user sentence, so Langy forgot the whole conversation. Every turn of an existing conversation now renders the durable transcript into the system block (speaker-labeled, injection-hardened, bounded newest-first with an elision note, deduped against regenerates), and because the handoff stash carries the composed block, every recovery path seeds fresh workers automatically. Proven live twice: a cross-provider model switch answering from earlier turns, and a cold resume after the manager and every session workspace were destroyed.

## One trace per turn

Gateway model-call spans were rooting standalone gateway-origin traces beside the Langy trace, sometimes duplicating it. Root cause was propagation, not double emission: an unarmed tracer yielded an invalid turn context, so no traceparent was injected. The turn identity is now minted valid regardless, gateway spans parent inside the Langy trace, and as a drop net a Langy call arriving without a parent is dropped rather than exported standalone; plain gateway traffic (playground, API keys) keeps its own traces. Joining the spans surfaced a double count, the worker copy and the gateway span both metering the same call, so the gateway span is the single meter now. The redundant langy label is gone; origin is the on

body:
Closes **Item B** of the pefm-lab/rfx low-observable/RAM handover: make relative permeability μr a **differentiable design variable**, so magnetic RAM (ferrites — which match at a *thinner* layer than dielectric via η=ETA0·√(μ/ε)) can be found by gradient descent through `forward()`+TFSF. Follows #445 (Item A).

## Premise (handover-mandated — verified BEFORE any design work)
`forward()` had **no μr channel** (only `eps_override`/`sigma_override`) while the Yee H-update genuinely uses μr (`yee.py`: `mu = materials.mu_r*MU_0`; `h -= (dt/mu)*curl`). So μr was a live solver axis with no differentiable entry point — a **missing-channel no-op** (the `add_lumped_rlc`+forward footgun class the handover warned about).

## Fix (the "no-op fix")
Add `mu_r_override` to `Simulation.forward()`, threaded into the uniform-lane `MaterialArrays` assembly exactly like `sigma_override`; **fail loud** on the non-uniform/distributed lanes (which don't thread it) instead of silently dropping it to a zero gradient. No new public export (the TMM oracle is inlined in the test), so no AD-surface-contract change.

## Validation — ground-truth-first vs an analytic magnetic TMM oracle
The oracle (η=√(μ/ε)) is validated to machine precision before it gates any FDTD: μr=1 reduces to the dielectric oracle, two formulations agree, passivity holds, and the **physical witness** — a magnetic layer nulls ~42% thinner (2.33 vs 4.05 mm) — is reproduced. Then (CPU, f0=8 GHz, dx=0.5 mm, ε'=4, σ=1.4, μr=2, ~9-cell layer on PEC):
- **channel LIVE**: 18.7% output change μr 1→2 (not a no-op);
- **gradient**: d|Γ|/dμr AD==FD 0.0% (autodiff self-consistency) **and** sign+order match to the **independent analytic magnetic-TMM gradient** (ratio 0.65–0.78) — the real physics gradient check, applying the Item A lesson that AD==FD alone is a tautology;
- **|Γ|(f) vs magnetic TMM** (±half-cell thickness band): mean **3.2%** over 6–10 GHz, passive;
- lossless μr≠1 PEC-backed |Γ|~1 (energy conservation);
- `mu_r_override` **fenced fail-loud** on a non-uniform mesh.

8 tests pass (2 fast + 6 slow); ruff clean. Slow tests added to `scripts/vessl_gpu_validate_diffplanewave.yaml`.

<sub>Note: the GPU-lane edit touches the same line as #445; trivial conflict to resolve if #445 merges first. Reporting Item B per handover discipline; Item C (oblique/angle-window RCS) remains blocked on the #404/#413 oblique-RCS fence + #280 NTFF leakage.</sub> @BK3536

author: isaac-cf-wong
body:
## Summary

Fixes #140. `regularized_cholesky()` silently altered an ill-conditioned
Hermitian spectral matrix, so users of `CorrelatedNoiseSimulator` had no signal
that the requested cross-spectral structure was modified.

- **Regularization warning** — when the minimum eigenvalue falls below
  `regularization_epsilon × max_diagonal` and `εI` is added, log a warning with
  the eigenvalue, threshold, and added amount.
- **Fallback warning** — when Cholesky still fails after regularization and the
  factor degrades to an uncorrelated diagonal (dropping off-diagonal
  correlations), warn about the lost cross-spectral structure.
- Well-conditioned matrices stay silent.

## Testing

- New tests in `tests/test_spectral_covariance.py`: warns on regularization,
  silent when well-conditioned, warns on the diagonal fallback (Cholesky forced
  to fail).
- Spectral + correlated-noise suites: 100 passed. Ruff clean.

Fixes #140

## Summary

- pin `next` exactly to `16.2.11`, the July 2026 Active LTS security release
- update only the version-matched official Next.js lockfile entries (`next`, `@next/env`, and `@next/swc-*`)
- keep React and React DOM exactly at `19.2.7`
- keep `eslint-config-next` unchanged; its peer requirements remain satisfied and lint, typecheck, and build pass

No product behavior, application source, authentication design, authorization policy, API, data model, migration, UI, or CI threshold changed.

## Security evidence

Primary sources:

- https://nextjs.org/blog/july-2026-security-release
- https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories
- https://www.npmjs.com/package/next/v/16.2.11

Before the update, `next@16.2.10` was a direct production dependency and `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` failed with one aggregated high-severity vulnerability containing four high and five moderate advisories, all affecting Next.js `>=16.0.0 <16.2.11`:

- HIGH: GHSA-6gpp-xcg3-4w24 — middleware/proxy bypass
- HIGH: GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj — Server Actions CPU denial of service
- HIGH: GHSA-89xv-2m56-2m9x — Server Actions SSRF on custom servers
- HIGH: GHSA-p9j2-gv94-2wf4 — dynamic-host rewrite SSRF
- MODERATE: GHSA-68g3-v927-f742 — request-body cache confusion
- MODERATE: GHSA-4633-3j49-mh5q — invalid UTF-8 request-body cache confusion
- MODERATE: GHSA-4c39-4ccg-62r3 — unbounded Edge Server Action payload
- MODERATE: GHSA-q8wf-6r8g-63ch — SVG image optimization denial of service
- MODERATE: GHSA-955p-x3mx-jcvp — internal Server Function endpoint disclosure

After the update, the production audit exits successfully with zero info, low, moderate, high, or critical findings. No exclusion, override, ignore rule, or threshold change was added.

It does not use Server Actions, `use cache`, Cache Components, Edge runtime declarations, dynamic-host rewrites, remote image optimization, CSP nonces, WebSocket upgrades, or a custom server. author: 0x0c
body:
## Summary

The `xcuitest (codegen)` job is the one real-compile success among the three codegen emitters, but
it only compiles **`components.yaml`** — a deliberately narrow slice (`tap` / `wait` / `type` /
basic assertions). Everything else `bajutsu/codegen/xcuitest.py` emits — text-editing, gestures,
multi-touch, and compound selectors — was checked **only as substrings** of the generated Swift,
never compiled, so an emitter change could break the real XCTest API usage and every existing test
would still pass.

This PR compiles-and-runs that wider surface as a **non-gating slice** of the same job, reusing
scenarios already **proven on-device** by `bajutsu run` so only the *emitted* Swift is newly under
test. It lands **Units 1, 2, and the first half of Unit 4** of **BE-0297**; the item stays
*In progress* until the slice is promoted into the required gate.

## What changed

- **`demos/showcase/Makefile`** — new `ui-test-coverage` target generates native XCUITest from
  `text_editing.yaml` (`select` / `copy` / `clear` / `delete`), `gestures.yaml` (`longPress`,
  directional `swipe`, `drag`), `gestures_multitouch.yaml` (`pinch` / `rotate`), and the new
  `codegen_extra.yaml`, then runs **only the coverage classes** via `-only-testing` (an allow-list
  robust to a Components rename) with no retry (this is the deliberately-unstable slice).
- **`demos/showcase/scenarios/codegen_extra.yaml`** `(new)` — the three constructs no proven
  scenario reaches: a coordinate `swipe` (`from`/`to`), an element-anchored `drag`, and a compound
  `traits` + `index` selector, grounded on the proven Log-tab surface.
- **`.github/workflows/ios-e2e.yml`** — runs `ui-test-coverage` after the required Components step
  with `continue-on-error` (non-gating, like `actuation` / `golden`), then a follow-up step surfaces
  any failure as a **PR warning annotation** so the signal isn't silently swallowed.
- **`.gitignore`** — the generated `Coverage*.swift` are generation-only, never committed (the
  required `ComponentsUITests.swift` remains the only tracked generated UITest).
- **`tests/test_codegen.py`** — pins the Linux-checkable half: every coverage fixture stays
  codegen-able and emits its construct's distinguishing Swift primitive.
- **`roadmaps/BE-0297-…`** (both languages) — tick Units 1 / 2, log the non-gating landing; Status
  stays *In progress*.

## Scope

Only the **compiled-coverage** landing. The remaining half of **Unit 4** — promoting the slice into
the required `E2E` gate once it proves stable on the metered Simulator lane — is a follow-up. Unit 3
(fail-loud on `if` / `forEach` / `extract`) already merged as #1278. `within` stays unsupported by
design and is out of scope.

## Prime-directive compliance

- **AI never judges** — no LLM anywhere on the `run` / CI path; this only compiles more of the
  deterministic codegen output. `make check` and `xcodebuild test` remain the only verdicts.
- **Determinism first** — no fixed `sleep` (condition waits only); the added non-gating step
  surfaces its failures loudly (a PR annotation) rather than hiding them.
- **App-agnostic** — no per-target behavior; reuses the existing showcase surfaces and config.

## Verification

```
make check
  ruff format --check + ruff + mypy (strict): Success · lint-roadmap: all links resolve
  4611 passed, 3 skipped — coverage 92.61% (floor 89%)
```

New `tests/test_codegen.py` cases assert each coverage fixture (text-editing / gestures /
multi-touch / coordinate-swipe / drag / compound traits+index) generates without a `CodegenError`,
carries no `unsupported` degradation, and emits its distinguishing XCTest primitive.

> [!NOTE]
> The **on-device compile and run** cannot be exercised by the Linux gate — it runs only in the new
> non-gating `xcuitest (codegen)` step on macOS. This PR's `make check` proves the Python, codegen
> output, and workflow syntax; the compiled slice's pass/fail surfaces on this PR's CI (non-gating),
> which is exactly the per-PR signal BE-0297 Unit 4 wants before promotion to the required gate.

author: shadowshtr
body:
## Summary
Applied `saas-foundation-shadowshtr`'s rules to NEXORA. This PR now covers both the initial small fix and the follow-up structural remediation requested afterward.

### 1. `/api/health` proves the deployed commit
- Ran the foundation's two read-only audit scripts (`audit-repository.mjs`, `check-sql-safety.mjs`) against this repo to get a baseline. All 5 flags raised were manually verified as false positives:
  - `.env.local` — correctly gitignored, never committed.
  - "admin privilege in a Client Component" (`src/lib/supabase/admin.ts`) — the heuristic matched the literal string `'use client'` inside an explanatory **comment**, not a real directive.
  - "destructive SQL" (`0004_audit_logs_immutable.sql`) — matched "DELETE FROM tenants is not a designed..." inside a **comment**; the migration actually adds triggers that *block* deletes.
  - 2× "admin client without visible tenant scope" — one is the admin client's own definition file, the other is `resolveBookingByLookupCode`, a legitimate anonymous public-lookup RPC call, already correctly `security definer` per ADR-008.
- Comparing against the foundation's Next.js template surfaced one real, small gap: `/api/health` didn't expose the deployed commit. Fixed: the endpoint now reports `commit` (short SHA), `branch`, and `environment` from Vercel's build-time env vars, alongside the existing `status`/`service`/`timestamp` fields.

### 2. Write confirmation on direct Supabase mutations (ADR-010)
The audit also surfaced a larger, structural gap, fixed in this PR per follow-up instruction: NEXORA's most critical mutations (agenda, payments, reminders) already go through `security definer` RPCs with row-locking + not-found exceptions. But ~13 *other* mutations across 6 files (catalog/services/categories/packages CRUD, client preferences, onboarding steps, photos, reminder template, no-show policy) used plain Supabase `.update()/.delete()` calls that checked `error` but never verified affected-row-count — under RLS, a stale/wrong `id` reports success with zero rows changed, so the action would tell the dona "guardado com sucesso" without anything actually changing.

- New `hasAffectedRows` helper (`src/lib/write-confirmation.ts`, unit tested) plus `.select()` chained onto every affected call site.
- Two files (`clients/photo-actions.ts`, `app/b/[slug]/draft-actions.ts`) already followed the correct pattern — untouched.
- Full rationale, the list of every fixed call site, and the two deliberate exceptions (a `package_services` delete where zero rows is legitimate, and onboarding's void `moveStep`) are in `docs/adr/ADR-010-write-confirmation-standard.md`. `CLAUDE.md` updated with the new rule for future mutations.
- No new integration tests per call site: `tests/integration/rls-tenant-isolation.test.ts` already proves the underlying mechanism (cross-tenant update → `error: null, data: []`) at the RLS layer, which is identical across every `tenant_id`-scoped table (generic policy in `0001_initial.sql`), so it generalizes to every fixed call site without duplicating the proof 13 times.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run verify` (format, lint, typecheck, unit tests, build) — all green, twice (once per commit)
- [x] 2 new unit tests for `/api/health`
- [x] 3 new unit tests for `hasAffectedRows`
- [x] Confirmed the RLS-layer proof this relies on already exists and passes (`rls-tenant-isolation.test.ts`)

author: baileyrd
body:
## What

Adds Swift as a supported language for `repowise-parser`/`repowise-graph`:

- New `crates/repowise-parser/src/swift.rs` tree-sitter-based extractor:
  classes/structs/enums/actors (all share one `class_declaration`
  grammar node, distinguished by its `declaration_kind` field) map to
  `Class`/`Struct`/`Enum`/`Class`; protocols map to `Trait`. Extensions
  re-open an existing type rather than declaring a new one, so they
  don't get their own symbol — but their name is still pushed onto the
  `class_stack` so extension methods are correctly attributed to the
  extended type. Protocol method requirements have no body at all (a
  distinct `protocol_function_declaration` node, not
  `function_declaration` with an absent body) — recorded as symbols
  with 0 complexity, same treatment as Java/Kotlin/Scala's bodiless
  methods.
- New `Language::Swift` variant (`.swift` extension, `"Swift"` label) in
  `repowise-core`.
- New end-to-end test in `crates/repowise-graph/tests/resolution.rs`.
- `README.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` updated (language lists, resolution-
  convention notes, extraction-seam table).

Closes #37.

## Why

Continues the parity-loop's B1 language-support backlog (tracked under
umbrella issue #11) — Swift is a Good-tier language in repowise's real
docs.

## Import resolution: module-level, not file-level (by design)

Swift's `import` is module-level (`import Foundation`), not file-level
— there's no per-file relative-import syntax the way TS/JS/Ruby have,
and a module name has no direct file mapping without a full build graph
(package manifests, target dependencies). So imports **are** recorded
(for visibility/stats), but always left unresolved by design — this
issue's own acceptance criteria called this out explicitly, and the
graph-layer test asserts it directly (`swift_module_imports_correctly_stay_unresolved`)
rather than treating it as a "resolves" case that happens to fail.

## Notable grammar quirk

Unlike every other language done so far, Swift's `function_declaration`
has no wrapping parameters-list node at all — `parameter` nodes are
direct children of the function declaration itself, interspersed with
its name/return-type/body children. `param_count` is counted directly
rather than via the shared `metrics::count_params` helper, which
assumes a dedicated list node to take `named_child_count()` of (using
that helper here would have silently counted every child, not just
parameters — caught before it shipped).

## Dependency note

Follow-up to the non-adiabatic output (#99), three maintainer requests.

## 1. Option-A dressed-reference column
`calc_nex_nonad` now returns **two** BZ-averaged measures from the same per-k dressed diagonalisation, written as two columns in `_sbe_nex_nonad.data`:
- **col 2 `nex_proj`** — dressed-conduction projection (still carries some dressing);
- **col 3 `nex_dref`** — the Option-A `delta0`-subtracted, clamped density the **ring dissipators actually see** (`dressed_ref_delta`, wiki/10 §3A).

When `yn_sbe_checkpoint_restart='y'`, all SBE output `.data` are opened with `position='append'` (`status='unknown'`) and the headers + the `t=0` block are skipped — a resumed run **appends** instead of truncating, so the pre-checkpoint rows are no longer lost. A fresh run truncates (`status='replace'`) as before.
Verified: run to t=30 fs with checkpoints, restart to t=60 fs → `nex.data` holds t=0..60 with the header intact.

author: prateek-singhwy
body:
# fix(schema-util): handle null content type in ContentTypeUtil.parseJsonOrYaml

## Summary

Fixes #8768.

`ContentTypeUtil.parseJsonOrYaml` throws a `NullPointerException` when the content it
receives has no content type. Several callers deliberately pass content through with a
null content type, expecting it to be parsed anyway, so this bug quietly breaks artifact
type auto-detection: a valid Model Schema or Prompt Template uploaded without a content
type gets silently treated as "not this type".

This PR null-guards the content type so a null is treated as unknown and falls back to
JSON parsing — which is exactly what the callers already assume.

## Root Cause

`parseJsonOrYaml` reads the content type and immediately calls `toLowerCase()` on it
before doing any null check:

```java
String contentType = content.getContentType();
if (contentType.toLowerCase().contains("yaml") || ...) {   // NPE when contentType is null
```

The content accepters, on the other hand, let a null content type through on purpose.
For example `ModelSchemaContentAccepter.acceptsContent`:

```java
String contentType = content.getContentType();
if (contentType != null && !isJsonOrYaml(contentType)) {
    return false;                                          // only rejects a *known* wrong type
}
JsonNode tree = ContentTypeUtil.parseJsonOrYaml(content); // contentType can still be null here
```

That `contentType != null` guard means "if there is no content type, don't reject it —
just try to parse it and see." But `parseJsonOrYaml` then throws the NPE on the null,
the accepter's surrounding `try { ... } catch (Exception e) { }` swallows it, and the
method returns `false`. So the content is dropped during auto-detection, and because the
NPE is caught and discarded, nothing shows up in the logs — which is part of what makes
this easy to miss.

`PromptTemplateContentAccepter` follows the same guard-then-parse pattern, and the
matching reference finders and validators (`ModelSchemaReferenceFinder`,
`PromptTemplateReferenceFinder`, `ModelSchemaContentValidator`,
`PromptTemplateContentValidator`) reach the same method the same way, so they are all
affected.

## Changes

- `schema-util/common/.../content/util/ContentTypeUtil.java`
  - `parseJsonOrYaml`: added a `contentType != null` guard around the content-type
    checks. A null content type now falls through to the JSON branch (parse as JSON by
    default) instead of throwing an NPE — matching what the callers already assume.
  - Added `Locale.ROOT` to the `toLowerCase()` calls in `parseJsonOrYaml` (and the one
    in `isTextPlain`), since locale-less `toLowerCase()` is disallowed by the project
    code style.
  - Added the `java.util.Locale` import.

- `schema-util/common/.../content/util/ContentTypeUtilTest.java`
  - Added three test cases (the class previously only covered `isParsableXml`):
    - `testParseJsonOrYaml_nullContentType_parsesAsJson` — a null content type parses a
      JSON document without throwing, and the parsed value is correct.
    - `testParseJsonOrYaml_nullContentType_jsonObject` — a null content type with a
      multi-field JSON object returns the expected field values.
    - `testParseJsonOrYaml_yamlContentType` — an explicit YAML content type still routes
      through the YAML branch.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `testParseJsonOrYaml_nullContentType_parsesAsJson` — reproduces the NPE on
      `main` and passes with the fix.
- [x] Added `testParseJsonOrYaml_nullContentType_jsonObject` — asserts specific parsed
      values (`a == 1`, `b == 2`), not just non-null.
- [x] Added `testParseJsonOrYaml_yamlContentType` — confirms the YAML branch is unchanged.
- [x] `./mvnw checkstyle:check -pl schema-util/common` passes (0 violations).
- [ ] Full module test run (`./mvnw test -pl schema-util/common -am`) — please run in CI;
      the local sandbox could not resolve some upstream build artifacts.
- [ ] Storage variants: not applicable. The change is in the `schema-util/common`
      content-type utility and is independent of the persistence type.

## Notes

PR #8558 is currently open against the same file, but it changes `determineContentType`
and adds GraphQL detection rather than the null handling in `parseJsonOrYaml`, so this is
a separate, non-overlapping fix.

author: miodvallat
body:
### Short description
As reported in #17292, there are still situations where cleanup of the LMDB backend causes a double-free.

Further analysis shows that, when `mdb_txn_commit` fails and returns an error, it will have invoked `mdb_txn_abort` before returning, causing the adequate transaction cleanup to occur.

Because of this, in this particular situation, we must consider the transaction as having been aborted, so as not to invoke `mdb_txn_abort` on it a second time in the destructor, causing that infamous double free.

You also get bonus cleanup commits making sure the schema migration code does not leave dangling transactions in case of error, free of charge! That's a real bargain! (better review with whitespace disabled)

author: vicnaum
body:
Closes #45.

## Root cause

Airbnb's legacy `GET /api/v2/explore_tabs` path now returns HTTP 400 for every viewport request. The search code treated those failures as retryable at two layers, refreshed the scraped homepage API key, and only then invoked the still-working SSR parser. A single UI search therefore waited minutes for Airbnb even though Booking had already completed.

## What changed

- Promote Airbnb's existing server-rendered `staysSearch` deferred-state parser to the only viewport-search path.
- Remove the dead `explore_tabs` request, API-key bootstrap, key-refresh loop, and nested error backoff from `src/airbnb/search.ts`.
- Keep quick-search pagination and exhaustive adaptive quadrant subdivision behavior.
- Forward guest and Airbnb filter parameters through the SSR URL.
- Limit each SSR page fetch to one request so an upstream failure returns promptly instead of recreating a retry chain.
- Add a regression test that exercises the public `searchAirbnb` entry point and proves it uses `/s/.../homes`, passes no API key, requests one attempt, parses pin-ready coordinates, and preserves filters.

## Impact

Viewport searches no longer depend on Airbnb homepage API-key scraping and no longer call the retired endpoint. Airbnb results can complete independently in a few seconds, allowing the combined quick-search response to reach the map well inside its 60-second budget.

## Validation

- `pnpm test` — 63/63 passing.
- `pnpm run build` — passing.
- `npm --prefix web run build` — passing.
- Patched direct `searchAirbnb` call using the previously failing New York bbox: 20 results, 20 with coordinates, 1 page, 3.14s.
- Patched combined `/api/quick-search` replay: HTTP 200 in 21.6s; 20 Airbnb + 97 Booking; 117/117 with coordinates.
- Independent exact UI-payload replays by the orchestrator: 15.6s cold (20 Airbnb + 91 Booking) and 6.2s warm (20 Airbnb + 90 Booking), all results with coordinates.
- Patched server logs contain zero `explore_tabs` calls, API-key refreshes, or HTTP 400 retry chains.

The browser extensions were unavailable during final verification, so the last two checks replayed the exact UI request payload at the API boundary and verified every returned result was pin-ready; the draft remains available for the post-merge visual retry on the live `:3000` stack.

body:
## Summary

One documentation/governance PR for #1925:

- **RIPR-SPEC-0069**: the stale flat 13-command closed vocabulary is replaced by the three-family reconciliation — (a) the 7 server-executed standard/compatibility commands (matches `SERVER_EXECUTED_COMMANDS`, adds the previously-omitted `ripr.collectRepairPacket` / `ripr.collectTopLimitation` / `ripr.collectReceiptStatus`), available to every client including headless agents; (b) negotiated client-executed commands, owned by RIPR-SPEC-0129 + the extension's `riprEditor` advertisement, explicitly **never headless-agent authority**; (c) reserved typed `riprAgent` requests, owned by RIPR-SPEC-0131, fail-closed until #1602/#1603. Adds the `collect*` → typed-request migration statement, the read-only default edit policy with the #1571/#1902 guarded-edit boundary, and the which-spec-changes-when rules (server command → 0069+0129; client command → 0129+extension; riprAgent request → 0131; edit policy → #1902).

author: rushleighconsulting
body:
## Summary

- adds a fail-closed WordPress updater using HTTPS metadata, Ed25519 signatures and SHA-256 package verification
- stores the site-specific repository credential encrypted and never renders it back to administrators or visitors
- makes automatic updates an explicit administrator opt-in
- adds deterministic production ZIP/checksum generation and a semantic-tag GitHub Release workflow
- excludes tests, CI, scripts and development dependencies from installable packages
- adds tests for signature failure, checksum failure, compatibility, credential protection and auto-update opt-in

## Release boundary

This PR does **not** create a tag, GitHub Release, deployment or production update. After merge, release preparation still requires:

1. setting an exact release version in the plugin header and `UCCM_VERSION`
2. configuring the repository secret `UCCM_MANIFEST_PRIVATE_KEY`
3. distributing the corresponding public key to authorised WordPress sites
4. separately approving the semantic version tag

## Security notes

- update metadata must be signed with Ed25519
- package URL and manifest URL must use HTTPS
- mismatched metadata, signatures or checksums block installation
- the credential is site-specific, encrypted using WordPress salts, omitted from packages, and cleared on opted-in uninstall
- the signing private key exists only as a GitHub Actions secret

## Validation

CI validates PHP 8.2–8.5, unit tests, WordPress coding standards, static analysis, and a production-package smoke test.

Jira: UCCM-9

author: leseb
body:
## Summary

Adds the `openai_file_search_callout` filter — a hosted executor for OpenAI Responses API `file_search_call` output items. When the model emits a `file_search_call`, this filter fans out OpenAI-compatible `/v1/vector_stores/{id}/search` requests to a vector store backend, aggregates and ranks results, formats them as model context with file citations, and replays the completed items back to the response pipeline.

The filter runs inside `iterative_request_router` so a model response can trigger vector store search and another inference within the same client request. Authentication is delegated to upstream header injection or cluster-level `request_headers_to_add`.

vLLM backends that emit `function_call(name=file_search)` instead of native `file_search_call` are automatically translated before execution.

Closes #29.

## What it does

- **Bounded fan-out**: Cartesian product of `vector_store_ids × queries`, capped at 64 specs with 8-way concurrency
- **Ranked aggregation**: Cross-store results merged, sorted by score, truncated to `max_num_results`
- **Citation tracking**: `file_id → filename` mappings stored in `ResponsesState.citation_files` for downstream annotation
- **Failure policies**: `on_error: reject` (502, default) or `on_error: ignore` (log + continue with partial results)
- **SSRF-safe config**: Rejects localhost, private/link-local/CGNAT/zero-network IPs, DNS hostnames, userinfo, malformed bracketed IPv6, query strings, fragments, and invalid ports at startup
- **Status-aware execution**: Only processes `searching` and `in_progress` items; terminal statuses are skipped
- **Partial failure tracking**: Cap-interrupted and per-spec-failed calls marked `incomplete` (not `completed`)
- **Hybrid search rejection**: `ranking_options.hybrid_search` rejected with 400 rather than silently degrading to vector-only
- **vLLM translation**: `function_call(name=file_search)` items automatically translated to `file_search_call` before execution
- **Continuation state accounting**: `web_search_calls` and `accumulated_output` included in state size budget

## Architecture

```
iterative_request_router
  └─ inference step
       ├─ openai_file_search_callout (on_request: execute pending searches)
       ├─ openai_responses_proxy → router → inference backend
       └─ openai_file_search_callout (on_result: check for pending flag → loop)
```

## New files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `apis/src/openai/responses/file_search_callout/mod.rs` | Filter implementation and orchestration |
| `apis/src/openai/responses/file_search_callout/client.rs` | Vector store callout client with bounded concurrency |
| `apis/src/openai/responses/file_search_callout/config.rs` | YAML config parsing, URL/SSRF validation |
| `apis/src/openai/responses/file_search_callout/citations.rs` | Citation formatting and annotation |
| `apis/src/openai/responses/file_search_callout/model_context.rs` | Model context builder for search results |
| `apis/src/openai/responses/file_search_callout/tests.rs` | 100 unit + functional tests |
| `examples/configs/openai/responses/file-search-callout.yaml` | Example pipeline configuration |
| `docs/filters/openai_file_search_callout.md` | Generated filter reference |
| `tests/integration/tests/suite/examples/file_search_callout.rs` | 4 integration tests |

## Test plan

- [x] 100 unit/functional tests (`cargo test -p praxis-ai-apis -- file_search_callout`)
- [x] 4 example integration tests (`cargo test -p praxis-tests-integration -- file_search_callout`)
- [x] vLLM file_search translation test in CI (`test_file_search_with_vllm_translation`)
- [x] `make lint` clean (clippy + nightly fmt + xtask checks)
- [x] `make build` and `make doc` pass

author: imaginethegames
body:
## What & why

CI's mobile-emulation job failed on **`touch drag on the left half moves the ship (field pixel diff)`** for both phone profiles (`iphone` 390×844, `pixel` 412×915).

Both phone projects declare **portrait** viewports — the orientation the new m1-05 ROTATE overlay treats as a *non-play* state (`shouldShowRotateOverlay` returns true when `innerHeight > innerWidth` on the no-lock path). Booting a **gameplay** assertion in portrait races that guard:

- portrait is the squashed / blocked layout the overlay exists to intercept, so the follow-camera field the test samples is not the playable field; and
- the first-gesture `requestLandscape` path (`main.ts` → `orientation.ts`) fires fullscreen/lock on `touchstart`, perturbing layout mid-drag.

Either way the field pixel-diff is meaningless in portrait, so the assertion is flaky-to-failing there.

## Fix (tests only — no `src/` changes)

Gameplay/affordance assertions now boot in **landscape**; portrait is reserved **exclusively** for the overlay-visibility test.

- New helper `useLandscape(page)` swaps the project's portrait viewport to landscape (**844×390 / 915×412**) *before* `boot()` runs `goto`, so the app lays out playable from frame one and `shouldShowRotateOverlay` is false (`w ≥ h`) regardless of lock capability. No-op when already landscape (the desktop control).
- Applied to both play-mode touch tests: the FIRE/ghost-stick **render** test and the **drag** test.
- The `portrait shows the ROTATE overlay; landscape hides it` test is unchanged — it remains the sole portrait case (it still emulates iOS via `emulateNoOrientationLock` and internally rotates to landscape to assert the overlay dismisses).
- Desktop control unchanged (already landscape, non-touch).

Header docstring updated with the orientation contract.

## Verification

Definition of Done — all green locally:

- ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit`
- ✅ `npm test -- --run` — 100 passed (12 files)
- ✅ `npx playwright test --list` — 12 tests enumerate

**Live mobile suite (`npm run test:mobile`) could not be run on this host:** the Playwright Chromium binary installs, but the sandbox lacks the system libraries to launch it (`libdrm2` et al.) and has no root to `install-deps`. The browser fails to *launch* (not a test failure). CI has these deps (the browser-cached mobile job) and is the source of truth for the pixel assertions; this PR is scoped precisely to make that job's failing case run in the correct orientation.

Only `tests/mobile/emulation.spec.ts` changes (+33/−1). Branched from `origin/main`.

author: sea-shunned
body:
I've moved some functions into the utilities to centralise and change how we are doing naming.

The `image_id` is a bioio-file extension-aware utility to strip known file extensions and get a clean stem. So this should catch silly things like "my_data.v2.ome.tiff", leaving the .v2 intact.

A hash is now created from the processing string, avoiding any '.' issues and making it smaller.

`get_mask_name` now just gives us a filename in the form:
```
{image_id}{'_' + preprocess_hash}_masks_{run_hash}
```

where the preprocess_hash is added if present, and the run_hash is what Napari generates or Nextflow does if not present, and embeds all information including the model version.

author: kylebeggs
body:
Fixes #21.

## What

`scatter!`/`reduce!` moved ghost slabs with direct device-to-device `copyto!`, which silently produces zeros on hosts where CUDA P2P is broken (IOMMU/ACS misconfiguration) — `can_access_peer` reports `true`, nothing throws, results are just wrong.

`GhostExchange` construction now runs a small data round-trip probe per ordered device pair (a real data comparison — the driver API can't be trusted here), cached module-wide with a one-time `@warn` per failing pair. Pairs that pass keep the direct D2D copy at full speed; pairs that fail route through pre-allocated pageable host staging buffers (`_transfer_slab!`).

## Why no pinning / no extra sync

Verified against CUDA.jl 5.11.3 source: the D→H copy runs `synchronize(src)` against the stream that produced the source buffer, and H→D from *pageable* memory stages through a driver-owned pinned buffer before returning — so the staging buffer is safely reusable by the next exchange. Pinning it would make the H→D copy truly async and create a reuse race, which is why the buffers are deliberately plain `Vector{Tv}`.

**This conclusion was re-litigated and re-confirmed.** A later investigation doc claimed MDLA had a cross-stream race here and proposed four `CUDA.synchronize()` insertions plus deleting the `_transfer_slab!` docstring sentence above. That analysis is wrong: CUDA.jl wraps every `CuArray`'s memory in a `Managed` struct that implicitly synchronizes on cross-stream and cross-device access (`memory.jl:571-575` and `:550-552`; every `CuPtr` conversion routes through it at `array.jl:464-467`), and MDLA never opts out via `enable_synchronization!`. Verified in CUDA.jl 5.9.6 and 5.11.3. The retraction is recorded in `handoffs/2026-07-27-1604-gpu-comms-validation-findings.md`.

## Notes

- Host buffers are allocated unconditionally (they're ghost-slab-sized) so the new tests can force the fallback path on healthy hardware by flipping `p2p_ok` flags — the tests pass both on healthy hosts and on the affected 9×A30 host, where the probe-derived flags are already `false`.
- `copy_exchange` carries probe results without re-probing and allocates fresh staging buffers.
- Also fixes the stale CLAUDE.md formatting note (CI enforces Runic, not JuliaFormatter/BlueStyle).

Needs a run of `Pkg.test()` on the multi-GPU host to confirm — expected: the 44 previously-failing ghost-exchange tests pass, plus one warning per broken device pair at first construction.

## Additional commits (investigation follow-through)

The branch has grown past the original single commit:

| Commit | |
|---|---|
| `53d8d07` | the P2P probe + host staging described above |
| `f41d1b5` | `docs(claude)`: CLAUDE.md rewritten to gotchas-only |
| `d7007df` | `docs(readme)`: "Host requirements for multi-GPU" — documents the IOMMU/VT-d requirement this probe exists to catch, and that `can_access_peer` can't be trusted |
| `295299d` | `chore(repo)`: ignore the 875 MB vendored `gpu-comms-validation/` tooling tree (untracked *and* unignored — one `git add -A` from being committed), keep its 176 KB of reports under `docs/gpu-p2p-validation/` |
| `de2d393` | `docs(handoff)`: retract the refuted stream-race analysis, per the section above |

No `.jl` files change in the added commits, so Runic and the test suite are unaffected.

---
<sub>🤖 Claude again — same probe, now with documentation and 875 MB less baggage.</sub>

author: l0stcontrol
body:
…on Node >=22

The --approx sandbox force-executes library code with `theProxy` placeholders standing in for unresolved values. On Node >=22, passing such a placeholder into the Blob family aborts the whole process with a native SIGABRT instead of a catchable JS exception:

  - `new Blob(<proxy>)`             -> Blob::New
  - `URL.createObjectURL(<proxy>)`  -> Blob::StoreDataObject

Any analysed path that constructs a Blob/File or creates an object URL takes the whole analysis down (common in React Native / web app closures).

patchGlobalBuiltins() already neutralises the other risky host globals (Worker, window, document, fetch, ...); Blob, File, and URL.createObjectURL / revokeObjectURL were simply missing. Stub them with the same theProxy; the `g.URL` guard keeps it safe where URL is absent.

Copilot (and any LM-consuming extension) can now call Nimbus for the user's **private local context** — the 2d "value per install" multiplier from the ecosystem roadmap. Zero new RPCs; both APIs are stable at the existing `^1.95.0` engines floor (no proposed-API flag).

Note: gated actions triggered through `nimbus_ask` still hit the gateway's structural HITL consent flow — the out-of-chat toast/modal surfaces already handle approval, so Copilot cannot silently trigger consented actions.

`typecheck`, `biome`, 603 unit tests, `build`, `check-bundle`, `check-settings-docs`, `package` + `check-vsix-contents` — all green locally.

**HELD draft correction PR from `main` @ `c642da3` (the merged PR #205). STOP for the NARROW Phase-3 re-review — Phase 4 does not begin.**

The final Phase-3 independent review returned **BLOCKED NARROWLY — PHASE 3 NOT YET CLEARED** (Tasks 1–6 remain valid; PR #205 is additive, no rollback) with five findings: the pilot Materials frontend was **observational, not operational**, and the readiness projection **counted the wrong unit** and **mis-dated a forecast**. This is ONE focused correction from `main`; it does not modify or redesign Tasks 1–6. **No domain schema; no migration** (read + UI + a corrected read projection over already-cleared facts).

## Vision-alignment statement

The pilot's promise (§25) is *one site running without a separate material spreadsheet, on facts the later phases inherit.* Task 7's first cut rendered those facts but did not let a user OPERATE on them. This correction makes the Materials hub **operational** — reserve, issue, consume, and a shortage's corrective all run through the existing Task 4/5/procurement commands under their existing authority and idempotency — and makes the readiness view **canonically correct**: totals are counted per ACTIVITY (stock is activity-reserved), forecasts measure the covering delivery against the EARLIEST need date, reservations fold the §C ledger (reversals included) with exact decimal arithmetic, and an older refresh can never overwrite a newer one. One fact keeps one owner; the `material-readiness` read is still the SAME `coverageFor` verdict `activities.start` authorizes (a live canonical read, never a projection), capability-gated (404 off-pilot).

## Findings → resolution

| # | Sev | Resolution | Reproduce-first (RED @ `c642da3` → GREEN) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | P1 | **Operational, not observational.** The hub drives the existing commands: reserve on-hand stock to an activity, issue to site, record consumption, and a shortage corrective (raise a requisition / reserve covering stock) — idempotency-keyed, reconciled by `loadMaterials`. | `materials-pilot.spec.ts` browser-driven reserve → issue → consume with a visible BLOCKED→READY transition (both sender modes). |
| 2 | P1 | **Latest-request ownership** on `loadMaterials`: a monotonic token; an older success OR failure that resolves late is dropped — never overwrites a newer result or its load state. | `materials.test.ts` older-late-success + older-late-failure never overwrite a newer result. |
| 3 | P2 | **Activity-level totals.** `MaterialReadinessResult.activities`; `summary` counts activities; `shortages` is one per affected activity; per-requirement rows are supporting detail. | `phase3-t7-readiness-read.test.ts` "one activity, two short requirements → ONE shortage; totals per activity". |
| 4 | P2 | **Earliest need date.** Forecast measures against `min(plannedStartDate, requiredBy)`; a commitment after `requiredBy` is never `covered-in-time`, even before the planned start. | `phase3-t7-readiness-read.test.ts` "commitment after requiredBy is delays-start even when it precedes the planned start"; the covered-in-time test was rewritten to a legal scenario. |
| 5 | P2 | **Reversal-aware, decimal-safe reservations.** `foldActivityReservations` folds `fromBucket`/`toBucket` (reversals + issues included) with exact BigInt fixed-point (`lib/decimal.ts`). A reversed reservation nets to zero and is not shown. | `reservations.test.ts` reversed reservation not shown; issued reservation not shown; lossy-precision folded exactly. |

## Instruction coverage

1. Minimum operational workflow over existing commands (no new domain tables). ✔  2. Shortage action → corrective command. ✔  3. Latest-request ownership. ✔  4. Activity-level readiness/shortage totals. ✔  5. Forecast against the earliest need date. ✔  6. Reservations from ledger buckets, reversals included, exact decimals. ✔  7. Browser-driven command steps through consumption + visible readiness change (API for fixtures/assertions only; non-pilot no-nav/404 kept). ✔  8. Reproduce-first probes for all five findings + packet + full legacy/outbox battery + stop for one narrow re-review. ✔

author: fa1dz
body:
## Summary
Fixes an issue where mixed-case or PascalCase environment variable values (such as `SHARPEMU_LOG_NO_COLOR=True`) were ignored by `SharpEmuLog.IsTrueLike`.

## Problem
In `SharpEmuLog.cs`, `IsTrueLike` previously checked exact string equality against hardcoded literals (`"true"`, `"TRUE"`, `"yes"`, `"YES"`, etc.). 

Because Windows environment variables and CLI tools often pass PascalCase strings (e.g., `True`, `Yes`, `On`), `text.Trim()` failed to match any branch in the `switch` statement and defaulted to `false`. This caused flags like `SHARPEMU_LOG_NO_COLOR=True` to be silently ignored.

## Changes
- Updated `IsTrueLike` in `SharpEmuLog.cs` to normalize strings using `.ToLowerInvariant()` prior to pattern matching.
- Streamlined the pattern matching logic for cleaner readability.

## How Verified
- Tested `SHARPEMU_LOG_NO_COLOR` with various casing patterns (`True`, `true`, `TRUE`, `Yes`, `on`, `1`).
- Verified that setting `SHARPEMU_LOG_NO_COLOR=True` now correctly disables colored console output as expected.
- Verified project builds clean with zero warnings.

body:
## Problem

The 'check-stalls' job in chain-health.yml has been failing on every scheduled run (every 30 minutes) with:

`
gh: To use GitHub CLI in a GitHub Actions workflow, set the GH_TOKEN environment variable.
##[error]Process completed with exit code 4.
`

Root cause: two setup steps for the chain-health automation were never completed:
1. PROJECT_OWNER/PROJECT_NUMBER in the workflow are still literal placeholders - setup-github-project.sh was never run.
2. The CHAIN_BOT_TOKEN repo secret is unset.

## Fix

Added a 'Check board setup is complete' step that detects either condition, emits a warning annotation pointing at the setup docs, and skips the rest of the job instead of erroring out every 30 minutes.

## Still needed (follow-up, not part of this PR)

- Run .orchestrator/scripts/setup-github-project.sh and record the real PROJECT_OWNER/PROJECT_NUMBER values.
- Add the CHAIN_BOT_TOKEN secret in repo settings.

author: roromukuro-afk
body:
## 概要

`daigaku-juken-tango` は静的フォルダページ(`src/app/guide/daigaku-juken-tango/page.tsx`)と動的ルートのARTICLESエントリ(`src/app/guide/[slug]/page.tsx`)の両方が同一URLを生成する状態でした。ルーティング競合を解消する前に、動的版固有の内容(CSVインポート・AI解説機能・継続支援機能への言及)が製品として実際に裏付けられているかを監査し、裏付けが取れた範囲に限定して静的版へ統合したうえで、この1slugのみルーティングを安定化しました。

## 静的版と動的版の差

**動的版固有だった内容(既知)**
- 市販単語帳3冊(ターゲット1900・システム英単語・DUO3.0)の特徴比較
- CSVインポート機能への言及
- AI解説機能の項目別説明(レベル別例文・語源解説・語呂合わせ・ニュアンス解説)
- 継続のコツ4項目
- ストリーク・正答率グラフ・苦手リスト・バッジ進捗への言及

**静的版の独自内容(維持)**
- 3段階の志望校レベル別語彙説明
- 受験生がよくやる失敗4選
- スキマ時間の具体例
- `ExamInfoDisclaimer`
- `GuideEmailCapture`
- 3件の`GuideMaterialCTA`(動的版と同一の3件)
- Article・BreadcrumbList JSON-LD
- `/signup`・`/vocab-check`のCTA

## 各製品機能の事実確認結果

リポジトリの実装・料金プラン・UIコードをread-onlyで調査しました。

**CSVインポート機能**: 実装あり(`src/app/api/wordbook/[id]/csv-import/route.ts`、`src/components/wordbooks/CsvImportPanel.tsx`)。ただしUI上はPremium限定(`CsvImportPanel.tsx`が`isPremium`でない場合は常にアップセルモーダルへ誘導、無料枠を実質的に使えない)。また、ユーザーが自分でCSVを作成してアップロードする汎用インポート機能であり、市販単語帳(ターゲット1900・システム英単語・DUO等)の見出し語リストをLoop側が提供・facilitateするものではない(`CONTENT_SOURCE_POLICY.md`が第三者教材の見出し語選定・配列の逐語的再現を明示的に禁止)。→ 「市販の単語帳の単語リストをそのまま取り込める」という動的版の表現は統合せず、「自分で整理した単語リストや授業・過去問で確認した語をまとめる」という一般化した表現に置き換え。

**AI解説機能**: 実装あり(`src/app/ai/AiPanel.tsx`、`src/app/api/ai/route.ts`)。レベル別例文・語源解説・覚え方(語呂合わせ)・ニュアンス解説の4つの選択可能なパネルが存在(「ニュアンス解説」と「入試での出方」は実際には1つの生成モードにまとまっている)。ただし`/ai`ページ自身に「(現在はモック)」という開示文言があり、AI出力の品質・正確性を断定できる状態ではない。→ 機能の存在(例文・語源・覚え方・ニュアンス/入試での出方をAIが解説する機能がある)は事実として記載しつつ、出力の精度・効果を断定する表現は追加していない。

**継続支援機能(ストリーク・正答率グラフ・苦手リスト・バッジ進捗)**: すべて実装あり、無料・ダッシュボードで可視の機能として確認(`src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`、`src/app/weak/page.tsx`、`src/app/stats/StudyWeekGraph.tsx`)。バッジは3日/7日/30日の連続学習日数に基づく3段階のみ(広範なバッジカタログではない)。→ すべて事実として直接記載。

## 統合した内容

静的ページへ3つの新セクションを追加しました。

1. **英単語を深く理解する方法**: 語源・例文・ニュアンスを合わせて確認する意義を一般的に説明し、Loop VocabularyのAI解説機能(事実確認済みの4カテゴリ)を選択肢として紹介。出力品質の断定は避けた。
2. **単語帳の選び方**: ターゲット1900・システム英単語・DUO 3.0の構成の違いを、優劣ではなく特徴として説明(出る順/ミニマルフレーズ/560本の例文にまとめた構成)。商標・出版社との提携は示唆していない。CSV機能は事実確認結果を踏まえ一般化した表現で言及(レビュー後さらにPremium限定であることを明記、下記「レビュー後の追加修正」参照)。
3. **継続するためのコツ**: 小さな目標設定・同じ時間帯の習慣化・苦手優先復習・記録確認という一般的アドバイスを中心に、事実確認済みのストリーク・正答率グラフ・苦手リスト・バッジ進捗機能と接続。

また、今回編集した内容の直前(SRSセクション)にあった既存の過剰断定表現「最小の復習回数で最大の定着率を実現します」を「効率よく記憶を定着させやすくなります」へ修正しました(専用テスト実装中に自テストの禁止フレーズチェックで検出、ユーザー指定の禁止パターンと完全一致するため修正)。

## 統合しなかった内容と理由

- 「市販の単語帳の単語リストや先生が作ったプリントの単語をそのまま取り込んで」という動的版の具体的表現: CSVインポート機能の事実確認結果(ユーザー自身がCSVを作成する必要があり、Loopが第三者教材の内容を提供するものではない)と矛盾するため統合しなかった。
- AI解説の出力品質・精度に関する断定的表現: `/ai`ページの「現在はモック」という開示と整合しないため、機能の存在のみを記載し出力効果は断定しなかった。
- バッジシステムを幅広いカタログであるかのように示す表現: 実際は3日/7日/30日の3段階のみのため、動的版のような一般化した「バッジ」表現は避けた。

## レビュー後の追加修正(commit `be6d0b0`)

本文レビューで、統合した内容のうち3か所が修正されました。ルーティング・`DYNAMIC_ROUTE_EXCLUDED_SLUGS`・`FIXED_SLUGS`・残る保留5件は変更していません。

1. **CSVがPremium限定だと本文上でも明確化**: 「Loop VocabularyではCSVでまとめて追加する使い方もできます」という表現は、無料ユーザーも利用できるように読めました。CSV一括インポートはUI上Premium限定という事実確認結果と揃え、「Loop VocabularyのPremiumでは、自分で整理した単語リストをCSVからまとめて追加できます。」へ修正。
2. **CSVはユーザー自身が整理したデータを対象とする表現へ修正**: 上記と同じ修正の一部として、「使用する語句や内容は、自分で利用できる範囲のものにしてください。」を追記し、第三者教材をそのまま複製できると示唆しないようにしました。料金金額はこの記事へ追加していません。
3. **DUO 3.0の「ストーリー仕立て」を、560本の例文へ重要語句をまとめた構成へ修正**: 「1つの例文に複数の重要語を詰め込んだストーリー仕立てで」という不正確な特徴づけを、「560本の例文に複数の重要単語・熟語をまとめた構成で」に修正しました。出版社との提携・公式関係は示唆していません。
4. **月400〜500語の習得断定を削除**: 「1日合計30分のスキマ学習で、1ヶ月に400〜500語を習得できます。」という断定表現を、「1日合計30分は学習時間の一例です。実際に身につく語数は、既習度や復習回数、学習方法によって異なります。」へ修正しました。

body: A sweep of the tarball's prose -- the source comments, the threat model, the architecture and spec docs -- to remove development-process voice in favor of plain descriptions of the store's behavior. Comments that named internal build artifacts a reader cannot resolve (numbered internal-rule and fragile-area references), narrated when a feature was added rather than what it does (milestone and version tags like `(M4)` or `implemented in M2`), or described planned-but-not-yet work now state the current, shipped behavior directly. The code, the API surface, the on-disk format, and every documented guarantee are unchanged -- this release only makes the shipped explanations read for someone encountering the store for the first time.

author: jakebromberg
body:
## Summary

`catalog-popularity-freetext-resolve` (#1491) builds each LML bulk item with only `{artist, album}`, dropping the track title even though `BulkLookupItem` supports `song` and LML has a dedicated track-search arm. Album-title-only matching is a much weaker signal than track-aware matching, and the resolver's match rate sits at a flat ~5.6% (only 6,869 of 122,023 attempted pairs carry a release id).

A controlled A/B probe against LML prod (50 random distinct unlinked `(artist, album)` pairs, mirroring the resolver's population) confirmed the lift:

| Arm | Match rate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| album-only (mirrors the resolver) | **6.0%** (3/50) | reproduces the observed ~5.6% steady state |
| album + representative track | **22.0%** (11/50) | **+16 points, ~3.7x** |
| regressions (matched album-only, lost with track) | **0** | the track never hurts |

## Changes (all in `jobs/catalog-popularity-freetext-resolve/job.ts`)

1. `enumerateFreetextPairs` — carries a representative track into the LML lookup. Picks each `(artist, album)` pair's **most-played non-empty** `track_title` (the album's canonical track — an alphabetically-first 'A…' bonus/intro title is an arbitrary, low-signal representative that resolves worse). Shape: an inner `GROUP BY (artist_name, album_title, track_title)` play-count feeds `DISTINCT ON (artist_name, album_title)` ordered `non-empty-first, play_count DESC, track_title ASC`. Cardinality is unchanged (one row per pair — the GROUP BY only picks a better representative track); the subquery measured ~17s on prod, within the raised `statement_timeout`. No `track_title IS NOT NULL` filter — a wholly track-less pair still enumerates and falls back to album-only. `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` transaction wrapper preserved.
2. `RawPair` / `NormalizedPair` interfaces — added `song: string`.
3. `normalizePairs` fold — carries the representative pair's `song` through (same first-encountered determinism contract as artist/album).
4. Single "usable track?" boundary: the enumerate map trims once (`song = (track_title ?? '').trim()`), so `buildBulkItems` is a plain truthiness check (`...(p.song ? { song: p.song } : {})`) — `song` is populated only when the representative track is non-empty.

The `(norm_artist, norm_album)` dedup key is unchanged — this is a pure recall improvement to *which release* LML resolves to, with no semantic change to what gets attributed. Zero extra LML cost (same item count, same batch size).

Added a "Post-deploy re-drain" section to the job's `README.md` with the ops SQL to re-arm the existing no-match cohort (`attempt_at = NULL WHERE discogs_release_id IS NULL`) so the gain lands now instead of waiting out the 30-day no-match TTL. That SQL is **not** run by this PR — it's a manual ops step for after deploy, scoped to `discogs_release_id IS NULL` only (never touches a matched row).

## Tests

- Unit (`tests/unit/jobs/catalog-popularity-freetext-resolve/job.test.ts`): the enumerate SQL shape (GROUP BY play-count, DISTINCT ON, non-empty-first / play_count DESC / deterministic ordering, no track filter), the `song` mapping/trim at the boundary (NULL → `''`, whitespace-only → `''`, surrounding-whitespace trimmed), the `normalizePairs` fold carrying `song`, and `buildBulkItems` including `song` only when non-empty. 47/47 passing.
- Integration (`tests/integration/catalog-popularity-freetext-resolve-enumerate.spec.js`, new): real-Postgres assertion of the modal-track selection the unit tests can only regex-check — a pair whose most-played track is empty still resolves to its most-played *non-empty* track, and a wholly track-less pair still enumerates with `song === ''`. Follows the repo's pure-SQL integration convention (mirrors `enumerateFreetextPairs` + a `bs1767` marker scope). CI's integration-tests job runs it (changed `jobs/**` + `tests/**` set `run-integration=true`).

## Test plan

- [x] TDD: failing unit tests first, then implement, then green (47/47 in the job's suite)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p jobs/catalog-popularity-freetext-resolve/tsconfig.json` — clean (jobs/** isn't covered by the root `typecheck` script)
- [x] `npm run format:check` — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — no new errors (same pre-existing warnings on `job.ts`; the 7 pre-existing errors elsewhere in the repo are in untouched files)
- [x] Integration query behavior validated against real Postgres (dev DB): Pair A → `Modal Track` (most-played non-empty, beating a 5-play NULL track), Pair B → `''`, cardinality 2; all changes rolled back. The full jest integration harness gates on backend+auth healthchecks (not brought up locally); the spec is wired to run in CI's integration-tests job.

Closes #1767

Related: #1486 (parent epic — catalog-popularity Phase-2), #1768 (offline enrichment drain — its Child 2 reuses this track-aware approach)

author: scouten
body:
Fixes #866.

## Problem

The `non_normative!` block in `parser/src/tests/asciidoc_lang/directives/ifdef_ifndef.rs` stated a normative rule from the spec:

> The two combinators cannot be combined in the same expression.

…but no test asserted what the parser does with a mixed `,`/`+` expression, and investigating that surfaced a divergence from Asciidoctor.

## Asciidoctor's actual behavior

Asciidoctor does **not** reject or warn on a mixed expression. Its [`ConditionalDirectiveRx`](https://github.com/asciidoctor/asciidoctor/blob/main/lib/asciidoctor/rx.rb):

```ruby
/^(\\)?(ifdef|ifndef|ifeval|endif)::(\S*?(?:([,+])\S*?)?)\[(#{CC_ANY}+)?\]$/
```

captures **only the first** `,`/`+` in the target (the leading `\S*?` is non-greedy). That single delimiter selects the combinator — `,` → any set (or), `+` → all set (and) — and the full target is then split on that delimiter alone, so a segment containing the *other* delimiter becomes a single literal attribute name (never defined). Precedence is therefore **first-delimiter-wins**, not comma-wins:

| Expression | First delimiter | Split | Effective meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ifdef::a,b+c[]` | `,` (or)  | `["a", "b+c"]` | include if `a` set |
| `ifdef::a+b,c[]` | `+` (and) | `["a", "b,c"]` | `a` AND `b,c` → effectively never |

## What was wrong here

`eval_ifdef` checked `contains(',')` **before** `+`, so comma always won regardless of order. That agreed with Asciidoctor when `,` came first (`a,b+c`) but diverged when `+` came first (`a+b,c` was treated as an "or" instead of an "and").

## Change

- **`parser/src/parser/preprocessor.rs`** — select the combinator by the earlier delimiter *position* (`str::find`), matching Asciidoctor's first-delimiter rule. Expressions using a single combinator are unaffected; the vendored Asciidoctor `reader_test` cases (leading/trailing/repeat operators) still pass.
- **`ifdef_ifndef.rs`** — split the normative sentence out of the `non_normative!` block into a `verifies!` block, and add `combinators_cannot_be_mixed`, asserting both orderings:
  - `ifdef::a,b+c[…]` → "or" on the comma (included iff `a` set).
  - `ifdef::a+b,c[…]` → "and" on the plus (excluded even when `a`, `b`, `c` are all set, because `b,c` is a single never-set name).

Note this is a behavior change confined to **invalid-but-tolerated** mixed expressions, which the spec leaves undefined; single-combinator expressions are unchanged.

author: hughscott2002
body:
## Summary

**SEO**
- Add a visually-hidden (`.sr-only`) static content section to `index.html` with real crawlable text for About, Projects (Agent Jae, MassivCart, Vulta, Omni), Experience, and Contact. The terminal only reveals this content when a visitor types commands, so crawlers never saw it — this section stays in the rendered DOM permanently, so it lands in Google's post-JS snapshot. Bonus: screen-reader users get the full content without typing commands.
- Add the Hugging Face profile to the JSON-LD `sameAs` array (was missing vs. the banner links).
- Bump sitemap `lastmod` to 2026-07-23.

**Performance**
- Font Awesome kit script now loads `async` instead of blocking the parser. `async` (not `defer`) so app boot isn't serialized behind the third-party CDN fetch — the kit is order-independent and its MutationObserver handles late-injected icons.

**Accessibility**
- `tabindex="-1"` on the hidden section's links so sighted keyboard users don't tab through invisible focus targets. Screen readers use the virtual cursor, so SR access is unaffected.

## Test Coverage
No new application code paths — the diff is static HTML content plus a sitemap date. Existing suite: 10/10 tests pass; production build succeeds.

## Pre-Landing Review
7 findings from the adversarial pass — 3 auto-fixed (the async, tabindex, and sameAs items above), 4 informational/accepted:
- Hidden keyword-rich links are in Google's "hidden text" gray zone — accepted; content mirrors what the terminal exposes and sr-only is a legitimate a11y idiom.
- Site content now lives in three hand-synced places (`config.json`, `<noscript>`, sr-only section) — drift risk; consider generating the static section from `config.json` at build time.
- Plaintext `mailto:` now crawlable (one already existed in `<noscript>`) — accepted for a portfolio.
- Hand-edited sitemap `lastmod` will go stale silently — consider generating at build time.

Codex adversarial pass timed out (5 min) — Claude adversarial subagent only.

## Test plan
- [x] Vitest: 10/10 pass on merged code
- [x] `bun run build` succeeds; `dist/` now includes `og.png`, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`

author: bghira
body:
## Summary

Ports the Krea2 validation LoRA loading fix from whitejt2/SimpleTuner@fca592c638090deaa8bfbf193c5f093b35a2ead0.

Krea2 validation adapters can be serialized with external transformer prefixes and KREA module names such as `transformer.blocks.*` or `diffusion_model.blocks.*`. The current vendored loader passes those keys directly to the transformer adapter loader, which does not target SimpleTuner's Krea2 module graph correctly.

This change normalizes Krea2 LoRA keys, infers exact PEFT target modules, injects the adapter into the transformer, and preserves the existing hotswap path for compiled validation.

## Notes

The later fork commits for target alignment and compiled lifecycle are stacked on top of this loader rewrite and should be reviewed after this branch.

author: gichigi
body:
Triage fixes from Natalie's Sprint 9 v1-audit E2E test (scoreboard on the ticket). Decisions were made with Tahi round-by-round.

## Why a PR (not a direct push to `audit-v1-phase1`)
Your fallback-extraction commit `2e72b5f` is still local/unpushed, and it also touches `run-pipeline.mjs`. To avoid clobbering it, these land on a branch and target `audit-v1-phase1`. Merge after you've pushed `2e72b5f` (or rebase this on top).

## Changes
**Correctness — soft-404 false positives (highest priority)**
- `run-pipeline.mjs`: Stage 4 link check now probes `pages_used` first. If the server returns 404 for a page we successfully audited, the origin soft-404s (returns 404 status for pages that still load via client-side render/redirect), so status-based broken-link detection is suppressed. Exposes `link_check.soft_404`.
- Evidence: on `anglianphe.co.uk`, `/contact` returns 404 to a GET but JS-redirects to a live `/contact-us/`, and the audited `/locations/colchester/shower-repair` returns the **same** 404. The old report told the client `/contact`, `/terms`, `/privacy-policy` were "broken, customers cannot reach the business" — all live pages.
- `regression-traps.mjs`: new `soft-404-no-phantom-links` trap (anglianphe). **Needs a live run to verify** (Chrome + engine); I couldn't run the live pipeline from my environment.

**Copy / UX (from her general feedback)**
- `render-email.mjs`: default teaser → "The worst offenders are below"; count-aware intro for ≤3 issues; the 0-issue CTA no longer says "Want these fixed".
- `render-report.mjs`: closer points to `hey@mooch.agency` (works for a cold-forwarded reader); **Book a call** is now the primary button and the email is plain text (the mailto button looked dead in PDF viewers); `text-wrap: balance/pretty` pass to fix the widow/orphan line breaks she flagged.

## Verified
- `node --check` on all 4 files; renderer smoke test across big / ≤3 / 0-issue variants (old strings gone, new copy present, mailto button removed, `closer-contact` + `text-wrap` present).
- Not verified: the soft-404 trap live run, and PDF visual (no local Chrome/puppeteer deps).

## Not in this PR
- Hiut `THE HACK@` naming FP: ignore (two separate products).
- Email sender avatar (Tahi photo on mobile): sender-side, not code. Alias can't carry its own logo → BIMI (needs DMARC at quarantine/reject + a CMC/VMC cert) or make `hey@` a real mailbox with `M.png`. Parked per Tahi.
- Mobile scoreboard row: Natalie confirmed mobile is fine, row just not updated.

body:
This PR completely redesigns the countdown experience from an elaborate boarding pass ticket to a minimal, focused countdown display.

## Summary
Replaced the ornate "Boarding Pass N° 001" design with a clean, minimal countdown timer for 18 September 2026. The new design strips away all decorative elements and focuses purely on the countdown numbers with a two-tone color scheme inspired by the loktev.co brand identity.

## Key Changes

**Visual & Branding:**
- Changed color palette from dark indigo/cream to warm paper (#f5efe9) background with Bondi Blue (#0095b6) and Dragon Fire orange (#fb5607) accents
- Replaced IBM Plex Mono + IBM Plex Sans Condensed with Inter font family
- Removed all decorative elements: ticket styling, barcode, perforation, crop marks, grain texture overlay
- Simplified layout to a centered flex container with four countdown cells

**Layout & Typography:**
- Redesigned countdown grid from 4-column layout to responsive 2×2 on narrow screens
- Increased number font size significantly (up to 8.5rem on desktop) for bold visual impact
- Changed from monospace to sans-serif typography throughout
- Removed all dashed rules, separators, and visual dividers

**Color & Animation:**
- Implemented alternating two-tone coloring: Days/Minutes in blue, Hours/Seconds in orange
- Simplified tick animation from glow effect to subtle scale pulse (1.05x → 1x)
- Removed pulsing status indicator and complex shadow effects
- Reduced animation complexity while maintaining reveal stagger

**Content:**
- Removed all ticket metadata (flight number, gate, seat, departure time, etc.)
- Removed route information ("YOU → ME")
- Removed ticket stub section
- Kept only the four countdown units with minimal labels

**Responsive Design:**
- Maintained mobile-first approach with clamp() for fluid scaling
- Adjusted breakpoint from 820px to 560px for 2×2 grid layout
- Simplified media queries by removing desktop-specific ticket transformations

## Implementation Details
- Updated target date to 18 September 2026 at 00:00 UTC+8
- Maintained countdown logic and tick animation triggering
- Preserved accessibility with aria-live regions and semantic HTML
- Removed grain animation and related keyframes
- Simplified reveal animation from 1.15s to 0.85s with staggered delays

author: geoffchurch
body:
Records the design conclusion from co-reasoning about whether the cockpit should support mycooc-style "cells" / `--status` grouping.

## What changed

**`multi-run-remainders.md`**
- New section **Generic grouping (facet sections) — resolver-declared, deferred**. Decision: grouping is **resolver-declared only**; forgo file/path-derived grouping. Rationale — the core can canonically derive *labels* (minimal-backtrack → unique) but not *groups* (coarsening depth is semantic, resolver-owned); no consumer needs core-derivation uniquely (`cells` needs an explicit facet regardless since its `root` is the content-addressed home; `glob`/translation are resolvers we own); and it unifies with the label-override seam `cells` forces anyway. Rejects id-embedding; gates on a second grouping consumer.
- **`cells` scope correction**: enumeration is a manifest cross-product, not a tree walk; it can't reuse `disambiguate` (root → hash-garbage labels, resolver must supply its own label); and "show cells like `--status`" is a **data-plane superset** (metric table + facet + seed-aggregation), not the resolver — the control-plane half is already the status column + fleet strip.

**`index.md`** — multi-run bullet now lists two deferred features (cells + generic grouping).

Docs-only; no code touched, test suite unaffected. Both features remain YAGNI-deferred — this records the shape, not a commitment to build.

body:
## Problema (relatado)
Ao editar a hierarquia da **Sonia Cristina** (Coordenadora de Compliance) e escolher o **Gestor direto**, o dropdown só oferecia "Renata cristina" — e não o **Alberto**, que é o gestor real dela.

## Causa (confirmada no código + banco)
1. O diretório do RH busca **server-side** (`loadFuncs` refaz a query quando muda a busca). Ao procurar "cristina", `funcs` ficou com só 2 registros (Renata cristina, Sonia Cristina). A `HierarquiaSection` montava o dropdown a partir desse `funcs` filtrado → só "Renata" aparecia (o Alberto nem entrava na lista).
2. Mesmo na lista completa, `ativos = funcs.filter(status === 'ativo')` **excluía** o Alberto, cuja ficha está `status='em_admissao'` (o único em_admissão da base).

## Correção (`src/pages/admin/rh/RH.jsx` · HierarquiaSection)
- Carrega o **roster completo** (`rh.funcionarios.list({})`) ao abrir a ficha e usa ele nos dropdowns E no cálculo anti-ciclo (ancestrais/descendentes) — independente da busca do diretório.
- Elegível pra hierarquia passou de `status==='ativo'` → **`status!=='inativo'`** (inclui em_admissão, férias, licença; só exclui desligados). Assim o Alberto (em_admissão) aparece como opção de gestor.

Só frontend. Sem migration.

## Test plan
- Build ✅.
- Editar a Sonia Cristina → Hierarquia → "Gestor direto": o Alberto agora aparece na lista (mesmo com a busca "cristina" ativa). Selecionar Alberto e salvar.

author: wass08
body:
## Problem

Since #535, clicking in the 3D editor stopped working once the camera was at rest: wall placement clicks didn't start the build, and clicking items didn't select. Clicks only sneaked through while camera damping was still settling.

## Root cause

#535 made `beginLocalCameraInteraction` set `cameraDragging = true`, and it runs on camera-controls' `controlstart`. But camera-controls dispatches `controlstart` for **every pointerdown, even for buttons mapped to `ACTION.NONE`** (plain left click in edit mode — verified in camera-controls 3.1.2 `onPointerDown` → `startDragging`, which dispatches unconditionally). A stationary click never wakes the camera, so no `rest`/`sleep` ever fires to clear the flag — and `controlend` wasn't wired. Every pointer gate that checks `cameraDragging` (`use-grid-events`, `selection-manager`, door/window/measurement tools) then swallowed all clicks.

## Fix

- `handleControlStart` only flags dragging when `controls.currentAction !== ACTION.NONE` (the state is set before `controlstart` dispatches, so it's reliable there).
- Wire `onControlEnd`: a mapped-button tap with zero movement (e.g. stationary right click) never wakes the controls either, so clear the flag on release when the controls aren't `active`; while damping is settling, `rest`/`sleep` still clears it precisely, keeping the #535 outline-suspension win.

## Verification

- Headless Playwright against Wawa House: first idle left click starts wall placement (start point + snap guides), clicks complete the wall, click after orbit+rest selects it.
- Confirmed working interactively by @wass08.
- `tsgo --noEmit` clean on `packages/editor`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small, targeted change to camera interaction lifecycle in custom-camera-controls; low blast radius beyond editor pointer gating.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **3D canvas clicks dying after the camera rests** (selection, wall placement) caused by `cameraDragging` staying true when `controlstart` fired for left-clicks mapped to `ACTION.NONE` without a following `rest`/`sleep`.
> 
> **`beginLocalCameraInteraction`** now takes an optional `dragging` flag so pose cancellation and `interaction-start` still run, but **`cameraDragging` is only set when the pointer maps to a real camera action** (`currentAction !== ACTION.NONE` in `handleControlStart`).
> 
> **`onControlEnd`** clears the dragging flag on pointer release when the controls never became `active` (e.g. a stationary right-click), while **`onRest`/`onSleep`** still clear it during damping so outline suspension during real camera moves is unchanged.
>

author: naor-segman
body:
Rebuilds the collaborative guest list as a **live shared table** (the user's real vision — an Airtable-like surface, not a blind submission form) with real-time editing and two-way sync into the guest list. Built in three stages, each committed and build-green.

## What it does
- **One shared link per event** → everyone who opens it edits the **same table together, live** (Supabase Realtime). They see each other's rows and changes.
- **Name + phone are typed; side / group / count are dropdowns** bound to the exact seating enums, so rows ingest into seating without matching errors.
- **Per-row error marking** — an incomplete row is flagged ("חסר: טלפון, קבוצה") and does **not** sync until complete.
- **Two-way sync, keyed by a shared row id**: a complete row (name+phone+side+group) auto-appears in the owner's guest list; owner edits/adds/deletes in the app push back to the table; deletes sync. A per-id signature breaks echo loops; app-only fields (meal/rsvp/notes/companions) are preserved on merge.
- **Download-to-Excel** of the full list, from both the shared table and the in-app hub.
- The old manual review/import screen is replaced by a **shared-table hub** (link + QR + live counts + open + export).

## Stages

Supabase Realtime facture **chaque message × chaque écran qui écoute**.
