author: ar-may
body:
Fixes #13943

### Context

The TaskHost read loop deserialized each incoming packet directly from the pipe stream wrapped in a 1 KB BufferedReadStream. Small primitives were served from that 1 KB buffer, so a real pipe read only happened on a buffer refill (roughly once per 1 KB) - but for a large TaskHostConfiguration (tens of MB of task-item metadata) that still meant thousands of small pipe reads, since each refill requests at most 1 KB.

It also defeated InterningBinaryReader.ReadString's MemoryStream fast path, which reads straight from the backing buffer and decodes the whole string in one shot. That path only fires when the translator's BaseStream is a MemoryStream; backed by BufferedReadStream instead, each string was copied through an intermediate byte buffer and, because a refill returns at most 1 KB, larger strings took the slower multi-chunk decode path with a pooled char buffer.

### Changes Made

- Under ChangeWave 18.11, client side communication uses a 64 KB read-ahead buffer and reads each complete packet body into a reusable `MemoryStream` before deserialization.
 - The packet-body buffer is allocated lazily with an initial 128 KB capacity. Buffers larger than 2 MB are released after the packet to avoid retaining unusually large allocations.
 - The non-APM parent-node read path also uses 64 KB read-ahead buffering. The .NET Framework APM path remains unchanged.
 - `BufferedReadStream` now supports any `Stream` and configurable buffer sizes.
 - Opting out with `MSBUILDDISABLEFEATURESFROMVERSION=18.11` preserves the legacy read paths: TaskHost uses its 1 KB buffer, while the parent-side path reads directly from the pipe. No packet-body buffer is allocated.
 - Corrupted extended-header packets now fail through the normal logged link-failure path instead of allowing the exception to escape the read loop.

### Testing
Existing unit tests + exp runs + perfstar runs (passed, see comments)

## Summary

This PR continues the moving-seam path after the dual multiscale result. It derives the exact transfer between two seams separated by a fixed number of zero-emitting blocks and proves that the common interior remains constructively free.

### Branch-independent bulk rule

During a hypothetical final zero tail, the normalized state obeys

```text
x_(m+1) = q_m(p(x_m >> 2)),  q_m in {t,u}.
```

For every branch and every output bit `i >= 4`, the update is the same radius-two Boolean rule

```text
Phi(a,b,c,d,e)
 = [e XOR (d OR c)]
   XOR ([d XOR (c OR b)] OR [c XOR (b OR a)]).
```

Its algebraic normal form is

```text
a + b + ab + ac + bc + abc + ad + bd + abd + e.
```

The extreme-right input `e` occurs alone, so `Phi` is right permutive. The actual `t/u` schedule affects only the four-bit low boundary layer.

### Exact k-block causal cone

For any branch word of length `k` and every output index

```text
i >= 2k + 2,
```

the final bit is independent of the complete intervening branch word. It is the `k`-fold iterate of `Phi` and depends only on initial bits `i-2k` through `i+2k`.

The iterated rule remains permutive in the extreme input bit `x_(i+2k)`.

### Constructive block surjectivity

For a later target block of width `r`, fix every earlier bit in its dependency rectangle except one extreme-right input bit per output position. Every target word has a unique assignment to those free bits.

Therefore a fixed-lag local comparison of two seams cannot bridge the arbitrary growing middle. The middle is not merely unobserved: every finite target word remains realizable with the surrounding context fixed.


This PR does **not** analyze lags growing with the complete seam width, prove the alternating inverse lift has infinite support, exclude eventual center period two, or solve Rule 30 center nonperiodicity.

It closes bounded-lag local multi-time seam strategies. The next admitted targets require a lag growing with state width, a genuinely nonlocal spacetime quantity, or an identity special to the unique actual fringe orbit.

body: ## Summary ### Problem Strapi's Media Library stores alternativeText/caption on the upload file itself — a single global value shared across every locale and every place that image is used. There was no way to give the same image different alt text per locale, or to swap in a translated image (e.g. a graphic with baked-in English text) for a specific locale. ### Solution Added a new reusable Strapi component, shared.localized-media (image + alternativeText, both pluginOptions.i18n.localized: true), and migrated the components/content-types that carry meaningful content images to use it instead of a bare media field: - `blocks.image-block` - `image`/`altText` → media component (tablet/mobile variants stay plain media fields, sharing the primary's alt text) - `blocks.split-layout` - `image` → `media` component (previously had no alt field at all; relied solely on the native upload's global alt) - `blocks.image-row` - same pattern (currently not wired into any content-type's dynamiczone, so no live data affected) shared.article-bio - `profileImage` → `media` component - `foundation-blog-post` - `featureImage`/`thumbnailImage` → `featureMedia`/`thumbnailMedia` components (`featureImageMobile` stays a plain field) - `profile-page` - `photo` → `media` component - `shared.hero` - `backgroundImage` → `media` component; `backgroundImageMobile` stays plain and **shares the same alt text as the desktop image** (single `heroImageAlt` field, not a separate mobile one) **Out of scope**: `shared.hero`'s image stays decorative (`alt=""`) for `foundation-page`/`summit-page`, which render it as a CSS background-image, not an — no alt attribute applies there. Only `grant-page`/`grant-overview-page` (which render an actual `` via `PageHero.astro`) get `heroImageAlt` in their frontmatter schema. ### Sync pipeline & Astro - `mdxTransformer.ts` (MDX→Strapi) and `mdx.ts/blogLifecycle.ts/profileMdx.ts` (Strapi→MDX) updated on both directions so `alt`/`imageAlt`/`photoAlt`/`featureImageAlt`/`heroImageAlt` frontmatter fields round-trip correctly through the new nested shape. - All affected `populate` configs updated (dynamiczone blocks, hero, article bio, profile relations) — component fields aren't populated by Strapi by default, so several were previously under-populated. - Astro-side live-preview pages (`blog/preview.astro`, `es/blog/preview.astro`, `profile-preview.astro`) and `ProfileBlock.astro/profiles.ts` updated to match the new Strapi response shape. - `PageHero.astro` takes one `imageAlt` prop, applied to both the desktop and mobile hero `` elements. - Admin UI (Content-Type Builder field labels/descriptions/edit-layouts in `cms/src/index.ts`) updated for every migrated component. ## Related Issue Fixes INTORG-878 ## Manual Test - run the sync script locally - test different components and existing pages ## Checks - [x] `pnpm run format` - [x] `pnpm run lint` ## PR Checklist - [x] PR title follows Conventional Commits (e.g. `feat: ...`, `fix: ...`) - [x] Linked issue included - [ ] Scope is focused (target ~10-20 files when possible) - [ ] Screenshots for UI changes (if applicable)

body:
Fixes https://github.com/eclipse-platform/eclipse.platform.ui/issues/4202

~This PR contains 2 commits: 1 that adds the `Progress Service` view, making it easier to show the buggy behavior, and 1 that fixes the issue.~ 1 single commit.

# How to test
Either run the tests in `org.eclipse.ui.tests.progress.ProgressServiceTest` or use the newly added `ProgressServiceView`:

1. Open `ProgressServiceView` (`Window > Show View > Other... > Progress Examples > Progress Service`).
2. Check **"Always run in background"** (or set it under `Preferences > General` — the view's checkbox
   stays in sync either way).
3. Check both **fork** and **cancelable**, set a duration long enough to exceed the short-operation
   threshold (e.g. 3000 ms), click **Run**.

**Expected behavior:** 
- When running the tests: they should all pass. The test that emulates the bug in #4202 is `testRun_fork_cancelable_runInBackground_callFromUIThread_notPumpingUiEvents_noDialogShown`.
- When using the new view as described above: No progress dialog should appear.

Ajout du checkout Stripe (session hébergée + pages succès/annulation) pour la commande Audit SEO Expert.

- [x] feat — nouvelle fonctionnalité
- [ ] fix — correction de bug
- [ ] chore — tâche technique
- [ ] docs — documentation

## Issue liée
Closes #224

## Détail

- `src/lib/stripe.ts` — client Stripe singleton, initialisation paresseuse (`getStripe()`) pour ne pas faire échouer le build quand `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` est absente
- `src/app/api/audit-order/[id]/checkout/route.ts` — crée la session Checkout à partir d'un `AuditOrder` pending : 404 si introuvable, 409 si déjà traité, montant TTC recalculé depuis le HT stocké (`amountEur` × `AUDIT_ORDER_VAT_RATE`), `invoice_creation.enabled`, `metadata.auditOrderId`, `stripeSessionId` persisté avant redirection

## Problem
Two concurrency bugs in the episodic vector store (`src/kiro_crew/vector_memory.py`):

1. **FAISS index / id-map desync.** `write_episodic` added the vector to the FAISS C++ index *before* appending the row id to the Python `_faiss_id_map`. If the `add` succeeded but the process was interrupted (or a later step raised), `index.ntotal` drifted ahead of `len(_faiss_id_map)`. A persisted, desynced pair was then loaded blindly by `load_faiss_index`, so subsequent lookups returned wrong/missing memories or raised `IndexError` when resolving a search hit to an id.
2. **Unlocked `last_accessed_at` UPDATE.** `search_episodic` ran its `UPDATE episodic_memories SET last_accessed_at = ?` loop and `commit()` *outside* `self._db_lock`, unlike every other write in the store. Under concurrent readers/writers the transactions interleaved (metadata writes could be lost or clobbered) and sqlite could raise `database is locked`.

## Why it matters
Both bugs surface only under concurrency or after an interrupted write — exactly the conditions that are hard to reproduce and easy to ship. Bug 1 silently corrupts recall (the agent retrieves the wrong memories, or a search crashes); bug 2 causes intermittent `database is locked` errors and lost `last_accessed_at` updates that skew memory decay/eviction.

## Fix (symptoms → root cause → change)
- **Desync → non-atomic add → atomic add + load-time gate.** Root cause: the index mutation and the id-map append were not a single unit. Fix: in `write_episodic`, append the id to `_faiss_id_map` first (a cheap, reliable list op), then `add` the vector inside `try/except`, and `pop()` the id on failure before re-raising — so `index.ntotal` and `len(_faiss_id_map)` never diverge. Belt-and-suspenders: `load_faiss_index` now compares `index.ntotal` to `len(id_map)` on load and, on divergence, logs a warning and rebuilds from SQLite (the source of truth) instead of serving a corrupt pair.
- **Locked → unserialized UPDATE → single locked transaction.** Root cause: the metadata write path skipped the store's lock. Fix: wrap the `last_accessed_at` UPDATE loop and its `commit()` in `with self._db_lock:` as one transaction, matching the rest of the write path. The lock is a reentrant `RLock`, so re-acquiring it is safe regardless of caller, and `busy_timeout` (set to 5000ms at connection init) already waits out contention.

## Tests
Adds 6 regression tests (205 lines) in `test/test_vector_memory.py`:
- `TestFaissIndexIdMapSync` — verifies id-map rollback when `add` raises, load-time desync detection + rebuild-from-SQLite, and that a consistent index loads without a rebuild.
- `TestSearchLastAccessedLocking` — verifies `busy_timeout` is configured, that `self._db_lock` is held during the `last_accessed_at` UPDATE, and a concurrent-search stress case that no longer hits `database is locked`.

Full module suite: 121 passed, flake8 clean. `faiss-cpu` is installed in the worktree venv so the FAISS-backed tests execute rather than skip.

## Manual verification
N/A — the failure modes are concurrency/interrupt races reproduced deterministically by the added unit tests (fault injection on `add`, desynced-file loading, and a threaded search stress case); no UI or external-service path involved.

author: fritzoid
body:
Both halves of D2.

**Synchronous commit**: `[replication] synchronous_commit = true` makes every commit wait (after local fsync) for a standby acknowledgement, with the documented availability-first timeout — a stalled link degrades to NOT_SYNCHRONIZED and commits proceed until an ack catches back up.

**Readable standby**: standby reads now resolve through the Stage-13 version store at the last-applied-commit snapshot. The apply mirrors shipped changes into the store using the pre-images already present in every WAL record's undo payload — no WAL format change, no version-store schema change, and the existing scan/seek merge paths enforce visibility unmodified. Aborted shipped transactions unwind via the existing rollback machinery; the store rebuilds at reopen from the retained ring; a failed apply feeds it nothing.

`cargo test --workspace` green, clippy `-D warnings` clean.

author: auerbachb
body:
## Summary

Closes #680

PR #661 shipped `issue-dedup.sh` and the strong/weak/none threshold contract for `/wrap` and `/issue-maker`. This PR makes the dedup check a property of the repo, not of one skill — every autonomous `gh issue create` path runs the same check.

### Key finding: `/pm-clean` is a non-filer

The issue premise said `/pm-clean` needed wiring. After an actual `grep -rn "gh issue create" .claude/` sweep, `/pm-clean` only calls `gh issue close` — it never creates issues. The real autonomous filers that needed wiring were `pm-worker` (agent) and `/start-issue` (human-in-the-loop).

### Changes

**`.claude/reference/autofile-dedup.md`** — rewired as a repo-wide contract:
- States explicitly that the rule applies to every `gh issue create` path, not per-skill
- Adds a grep-verifiable filer inventory table classifying all sites (autonomous vs. human-in-the-loop vs. non-filer)
- Makes the asymmetry rule explicit: autonomous filers suppress + report; human-present callers surface only
- Generalises the "never silent" obligation to every autonomous caller (not `/wrap`-specific)
- Generalises the comment template (removes `/wrap` branding)
- Adds Issue #677 reconciliation note

**`.claude/agents/pm-worker.md`** — adds dedup Step 2 (autonomous path):
- Runs `issue-dedup.sh` with the three-path fallback before `gh issue create`
- Strong match: comments on the existing issue, does NOT file, reports suppression
- Weak match: files with `Possibly duplicates #N` pointer
- No match / helper missing: files normally (notes degraded check once)
- Adds `issue_deferred` to the OUTCOME enum and exit-report template

**`.claude/skills/start-issue/SKILL.md`** — adds surface-only dedup in Step 1a (human-in-the-loop):
- Strong match: surfaces the candidate to the user and waits for confirmation
- Weak match: notes it once and continues
- Removes the stale edge-case note "does not dedupe — that is the user's responsibility"

**`.claude/scripts/issue-dedup.sh`** — updates callers comment to list all four callers with their classifications.

### Deferred (pinned scope)

The question of extending the same check to PRs-in-flight (the PR-layer duplicate that triggered Issues #661/#673) is explicitly deferred by Issue #680 as a candidate follow-up ticket.

### Reviewer availability note

Both local review CLIs unavailable: CodeRabbit CLI returned exit 127 (not installed), CodeAnt CLI not installed. Self-review performed. CodeAnt GitHub App is unaffected and will cover the GitHub-side review.

## Test plan

- [ ] Inventory every path that can call `gh issue create` without a confirmation step; list them in `.claude/reference/autofile-dedup.md`
- [ ] `/pm-clean` (and any other autonomous filer found in the inventory) runs `issue-dedup.sh` before filing, applying the strong/weak/none rules unchanged
- [ ] Each such caller reports suppressed filings the way `/wrap` does — naming the issue deferred to, never silently
- [ ] `.claude/reference/autofile-dedup.md` states the rule applies repo-wide, not per-skill
- [ ] Reconcile with #677 — decide whether it is subsumed, still needed, or should be closed as stale
- [ ] A `/pm-clean` run proposing a ticket that duplicates an open issue defers to it instead of filing
- [ ] The same run with no match files normally
- [ ] Suppressed filings appear in that skill's report with the target issue named
- [ ] Inventory in `autofile-dedup.md` matches an actual grep for `gh issue create` across `.claude/skills/`

body:
Closes #96.

## What

Mark `AbstractLiteral` and `ListLiteral` `@internal` + `@psalm-internal Eventjet\Ausdruck` — they move as a pair. `ListLiteral` was the last published leaf pinning the abstract base open, and `AbstractLiteral::value()` was an accidental public extension point.

This brings the literal nodes in line with their already-`@internal` siblings `Literal` and `StructLiteral`. All three AST base hierarchies — `BinaryOperator`, `UnaryOperator` (#95), and `AbstractLiteral` — are now uniformly sealed, leaving `Expression` as the one intentional `@api` extension point.

`AbstractLiteral` also gains a short docblock (in the `BinaryOperator` style) explaining why `value()` exists and why no external subclass is warranted.

## BC impact

Structural break — removes `ListLiteral` and `AbstractLiteral::value()` from the public surface. Scoped to the **0.3.0 breaking release**; shares the same policy ruling as #95.

`cs-check`, `psalm`, `phpstan`, and `phpunit` (1130 tests) all pass. `infection-diff` generated 0 mutations (comment-only lines), accepted by the `--ignore-msi-with-no-mutations` policy.

body:
## Summary

- makes cart and preflight VAT quotes consume the same customer tax-profile evidence and billing country as persisted order/invoice paths
- fails closed when an EU business context lacks explicit VAT-payer evidence
- sends the operator VAT identity to VIES, persists the returned consultation reference, and refreshes validation timestamps on every check
- registers a daily VIES revalidation sweep that drains the complete expired set in bounded database batches and reports unmatched evidence
- gives PDF and e-Factura reverse-charge output one shared Article 196 legal basis
- repairs three PostgreSQL status-transition fixtures that persisted an invalid long-form country name

## Root cause

The quote endpoints reconstructed only part of the VAT context, while TaxService treated a missing optional evidence field as permission for the EU B2B path. Separately, VIES validation retained neither an attributable request identifier nor a fresh validation timestamp, and its dormant sweep was capped before it could report the real backlog. PDF and XML generators also encoded different legal bases for the same AE tax category.

The PostgreSQL-only failures were fixture defects: SQLite accepted `"Romania"` for a model field whose production schema is `varchar(2)`.

## Behavior and safety

- This PR does not decide the legal policy tracked by #389; it only makes incomplete evidence conservative and existing paths consistent.
- VIES network calls remain behind the existing SSRF-restricted gateway policy.
- Revalidation is batched at 500 records without truncating the overall queryset.
- Issued fiscal amounts remain immutable; the document change only unifies explanatory wording.
- The migration adds a nullable-by-default evidence column and changes `validation_date` from insert-only to explicitly refreshable.

## Migration ordering

This branch currently adds `billing.0040_vatvalidation_consultation_reference`.

Open PR #402 independently adds `billing.0040_recover_remaining_legacy_refunds`. Whichever PR merges second must be rebased and renumbered to the next billing migration. There is no runtime dependency between those two migrations; this is sequencing hygiene for the open branches.

## Verification

- `make test-file FILE='tests.orders.test_calculate_cart tests.orders.test_order_flow_preflight_and_server_guard tests.common.test_tax_service_scenarios tests.billing.test_vies_gateway tests.billing.test_billing_tasks tests.billing.test_billing_ownership tests.billing.test_pdf_generators tests.billing.test_tax_configuration tests.orders.test_orders_services tests.orders.test_orders_views'` — 383 passed on the final rebased HEAD
- `make lint` — passed, including Ruff, MyPy (417 source files), Django, audit, i18n, code-health, FSM, and architecture checks
- `make test-ci` — 7,469 tests executed against PostgreSQL; the three #315 failures are fixed. The remaining 26 failures exactly match the unmodified-master baseline and are unrelated recurring-payment race/ticket-scanner failures.
- rebase fork-point audit found no files shared with the two post-fork master commits
- `git diff --check` passed
- DCO `Signed-off-by` verified after rebase

Closes #315
Closes #404

author: bobmatnyc
body:
## Summary

Owner-requested UX rework of the `tm ls`/bare-`tm` session picker.

Bob's verbatim feedback: "remove 'restart/resume', that's confusing. Use
colors to indicate their current state. Confirm we're dynamically syncing
with actual session, and let's provide a workstream rename facility."

- **Verb removal**: rows are now `[N] <name> (<state>)` — the restart/resume
  verb was an implementation detail of *how* the session gets reached
  (decided at selection time by `guided_resume::plan_resume`), not a
  property of its current state.
- **Color-coded state**: TTY-aware ANSI, respects `NO_COLOR` and non-TTY
  (falls back to plain text). Mapping: active=green, attached=bold cyan
  (distinct from plain active), stopped=dim/gray, errored/dead=red,
  provisioning=yellow.
- **Sync audit**: see "Staleness root cause" below — the picker already
  consumes server-reconciled state; no picker-side fix was needed for that
  part.
- **Duplicate-index fix**: `next_launch_slot` now takes the true maximum
  slot across the whole (possibly `sort_sessions`-reordered) list instead of
  `sessions.last().slot + 1`. See "Duplicate-index root cause" below.
- **Rename facility**: `r<N> <new-name>` / `r <N> <new-name>` picker input
  mode, routed through the existing `commands::rename::do_rename_request`
  (same PATCH `/api/v1/sessions/managed/{id}` `tm sessions rename` uses,
  including its #3692 auto-suffix-on-collision behavior) — no tmux-rename
  logic reimplemented in the picker. Note: `SessionManager::rename`'s own
  tmux-retarget step still resolves the live session by name on THIS
  branch — it inherits #3714's pane-scoped resolution once PR #3719 merges
  (see "Staleness root cause" below); no picker-side change is needed for
  that either.

Closes #3723
Closes #3724

## Staleness root cause

Traced the picker's data path: `run_tty_picker`'s session list comes from
`fetch_live_sessions` → `GET /api/v1/sessions/managed` →
`list_managed_sessions` → `numbered_summaries` → `checked_summaries` +
`reconcile_against_tmux` → `reconcile_live_state`. **The picker already
consumes the daemon's server-reconciled `state`/`attached` fields — it does
NOT read a raw persisted record and does NOT re-derive liveness itself.**
No picker-side change was needed to fix the sync path itself.

The specific symptom Bob reported (`[11] restart tm-tagents (stopped)` for
session `f443c12d`, live/attached earlier the same day) traces to a bug in
`reconcile_live_state` itself, in `daemon/managed_routes/summary.rs` — prior
to #3714, it reconciled `state` via a bare tmux-session-NAME-STRING
membership check (`live.contains(name)`), with no per-record pane-identity
check. Under the duplicate-session-name condition the daemon has hit
historically (#3692/#3698), a name-only check cannot distinguish which of
several same-named records is the one actually alive.

This is fixed **upstream**, not in the picker, by PR #3719
(`fix-3714-relaunch-resolver`, open as of this PR): it makes
`reconcile_live_state` resolve liveness via the record's own `pane_id`
(`ManagedTmuxDriver::pane_exists`/the new tri-state `pane_exists_checked`,
which distinguishes "confirmed absent" from "probe failed" so a transient
tmux hiccup never flips a live record to `"stopped"`). Because the picker
already routes through this same shared `reconcile_live_state` call, **it
inherits #3719's fix automatically once that PR merges** — no additional
picker-side wiring is required. I rebased this branch onto latest
`origin/main` before opening; #3719 was still open at that point, so this
diff does not depend on it and will pick up the fix on the next rebase after
it lands.

## Duplicate-index root cause

Confirmed and reproduced: `[N]` appearing on both a real session row and the
"launch new session" row. The picker computed the "launch new" number as
`sessions.last().slot + 1` in two places (`parse_picker_choice`'s
`next_slot` and `run_tty_picker`'s `new_idx`). That was only safe while
`sessions` stayed in the daemon's ascending-slot order end-to-end — but
issue #3483 added `sort_sessions` (`Recent`/`Alpha` inline `tm ls` sort
keywords), applied to that SAME slice before either call site sees it. After
a reorder, the highest-slot session is no longer necessarily last — e.g.
`Recent` sorts by `last_activity_at` descending, so a LOW-slot,
least-recently-active session can land last, making `.last().slot + 1`
collide with an existing session's own slot elsewhere in the list. That's
exactly the `[31]`/`[31]` collision in Bob's paste.

Fixed by `next_launch_slot`, a single shared helper (`session_picker.rs`)
used by both call sites, taking the true maximum `slot` across the whole
slice regardless of order. Regression tests
(`next_launch_slot_survives_recency_reorder`,
`next_launch_slot_survives_alpha_reorder`,
`parse_picker_choice_launch_new_uses_max_slot_after_reorder`) reproduce the
exact defect shape and assert the fix.

## Files changed

- `crates/trusty-mpm/src/bin/tm/commands/session_picker.rs` — `PickerDecision::Rename`,
  `next_launch_slot`, verbless row loop wired to the new renderer, rename
  input-mode parsing, menu hint line.
- `crates/trusty-mpm/src/bin/tm/commands/session_picker_render.rs` (new) —
  verbless/color row formatting (`format_session_row`, `state_color`,
  `colorize`, `picker_use_color`).
- `crates/trusty-mpm/src/bin/tm/commands/session_picker_rename.rs` (new) —
  picker rename I/O driver, calls `commands::rename::do_rename_request`
  directly.
- `crates/trusty-mpm/src/bin/tm/commands/session_picker_tests.rs` (new) —
  29 unit tests (row formatting, color, duplicate-index fix, rename parsing).
- `crates/trusty-mpm/src/bin/tm/commands/rename.rs` — `do_rename_request`
  visibility `pub(super)` so the picker can call it directly.
- `crates/trusty-mpm/src/bin/tm/commands/mod.rs` — register the two new
  modules.
- `crates/trusty-mpm/CHANGELOG.md` — Unreleased entries.

Both new files are extracted (rather than growing `session_picker.rs`
further) to stay under the 500-SLOC production cap — see each file's `Why`
doc comment.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p trusty-mpm` (full surface, no `--lib`): 3517 lib tests +
      1200 `tm`-binary unit tests + all integration test binaries, 0 failed.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p trusty-mpm --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- [x] `scripts/check_line_cap.sh`: `line-cap: 8 allowlisted, 0 violations — OK.`
- [x] 29 new unit tests, all passing:
  `format_session_row_*` (verbless output, color on/off, deleted/unresumable
  notices), `state_color_*`/`colorize_*` (mapping + NO_COLOR fallback),
  `next_launch_slot_*` (duplicate-index fix, including the exact
  Recent/Alpha-reorder repro), `parse_picker_choice_rename_*` (the new `r<N>
  <name>` input mode, including deleted-slot/missing-name/bad-slot
  edge cases).

🤖🤖🤖 Generated with trusty-mpm — https://github.com/bobmatnyc/trusty-tools

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a full, permission-gated Reports area that surfaces operational and financial metrics derived from immutable order and payment records. 
- Push reporting aggregation to the database for correctness and performance while enforcing access via RLS and permission checks.

### Description

- Navigation and access: added a Reports navigation link visible only when the user has `reports:operational` or `reports:financial` and enforced server-side permission checks; modified `app/app/layout.tsx` to query `user_has_permission` for report visibility.  
- New server page and UI: added `/app/reports` server page and a client reporting component with date range, staff/payment method/category filters, date shortcuts, refresh control, summary cards, breakdowns, and CSV export links (`app/app/reports/page.tsx`, `components/reports-client.tsx`).  
- CSV export: added a server-side CSV export route that calls the DB RPC and is gated by `reports:financial` (`app/app/reports/export/route.ts`).  
- Database migration and API: added one new chronological migration that creates reporting indexes and a permission-gated reporting RPC `public.reporting_dashboard(...)` which aggregates by payments, uses item snapshots for historical prices, separates internal-only orders, and strips financial details for operational-only callers (`supabase/migrations/20260723050000_financial_reports.sql`).  
- Files changed: `app/app/layout.tsx`, new `app/app/reports/page.tsx`, new `app/app/reports/export/route.ts`, new `components/reports-client.tsx`, and new `supabase/migrations/20260723050000_financial_reports.sql`.  
- Route implemented: `/app/reports`.  
- Reports availability: Reports are available after applying the migration and honoring RLS; admins see both operational and financial data, users with `reports:operational` see operational views, users with `reports:financial` see financial views, and unauthorized users receive an access-denied page.  
- Exact migration to run in Supabase: run `supabase/migrations/20260723050000_financial_reports.sql`.  
- Permissions required: `reports:operational` for operational data and `reports:financial` for financial data and CSV exports (the database RPC enforces these checks).  
- Manual test steps: (1) apply `supabase/migrations/20260723050000_financial_reports.sql`; (2) sign in as admin and visit `/app/reports` to confirm both tabs and exports; (3) sign in as manager without `reports:financial` to confirm only operational data; (4) sign in as a worker without report permissions and confirm access denial; (5) create paid/open/cancelled/internal-only/partial/split payments and verify displayed totals and CSV exports; (6) change a product price and confirm historical reports use `unit_price_snapshot`.  
- Anything not implemented: restaurant-timezone configuration is not wired (date boundaries use UTC currently), there is no per-row detail drawer for item/payment/print-job inspection, and client-side sorting/pagination for large result sets is not implemented yet.  

### Testing

- Ran `npm run typecheck` and it completed successfully.  
- Ran `npm run lint` and it completed successfully (no remaining lint failures after fixes).  
- Ran `npm run build` (Next build completed and type checks passed), with Next.js emitting an existing Supabase Edge Runtime compatibility warning from middleware dependencies but build succeeded.

   `prior/subsequentEventIds` 對每個事件都是空的。修後實測填充率 **0% → 100%**
2. **`textEvidence` 恆空** — 對 `VectorSearchResult`（Pydantic model）呼叫 `.get()`，
   `AttributeError` 被外層 `except Exception` 吞掉
3. **選到未分析事件噴 404** — `#7d` query gate 補上「該 id 在 analyzed 清單裡」
4. **`beneficiary` 被歸進 `witness` 灰階色桶** — 把「因此事件受益」讀成「只是旁觀」

## API 變更 `[api-contract updated]`

- **`#7g`** 新增選填 body `{ eventIds?: string[] }`（語意同角色批次 `#7c` 的 `entityIds`；
  不改任何 response schema，不帶 body 的既有呼叫端行為不變）
- **`#7i`** 新增唯讀端點 `GET /books/:bookId/events/:eventId/source`

## 兩個值得 review 的判斷

**骨幹圖沒照設計稿的版面演算法。** 稿用固定 430px + 百分比位移，那是 mockup
只有 16 個事件撐出來的；真實資料一章可達 12 個事件，該公式在 4 個以上就溢出重疊。
改為每帶高度依該帶最密集章節撐開、節點以 px 定位。

**未分析事件的 `importance` 恆為 `null`。** 設計稿的示範資料給了它們值，真實資料沒有。
因此「只生成核心 (N)」在生成前 N 必為 0（按鈕自動 disabled 並說明原因），
骨幹圖也不能只有核心／衛星兩帶——未判定者放在中央虛線上，不宣稱它們是衛星事件。

## 驗證

- `ruff check backend/` 全過
- `pytest -m "not integration"` **1082 passed**（新增 17 支）
- `npm run lint` 0 error、`tsc --noEmit` 通過
- 全部功能以 seed book（62 事件 / 13 已分析）實機驗證，console 0 errors；
  批次觸發以 route mock 攔截，未消耗實際 LLM 額度

> `npm run build` 有 7 個 TS 錯誤，但**在本分支切出前就存在**（位於 graph/upload/hooks，
> 本 PR 未觸及這些檔案）。已確認乾淨樹上完全相同，建議另開任務處理。

## Summary

This PR addresses the provider registration findings reported by the automated Pattern Analysis for Issue #1178.

After investigating the reported providers, I found that this is not a case of missing registrations. The concrete providers are already registered through the existing `ProviderRegistry` using `ProviderFactory.registerProvider(...)` with dynamic imports. The remaining flagged files are either abstract/internal components or are not present on the target `release` branch.

Instead of introducing duplicate registrations, this PR improves the documentation around the current registration mechanism and adds regression coverage to verify that all concrete providers remain correctly registered.

## Changes

* Added documentation to `ProviderRegistry` explaining the dynamic provider registration pattern and intentional non-registrations.
* Added a registration completeness test that:

  * Verifies every concrete provider module is registered.
  * Detects stale or missing dynamic imports.
  * Ensures provider IDs remain unique.
  * Confirms aliases resolve correctly.
  * Keeps `AUTO` and intentionally unregistered helper/base modules excluded.

## Validation

* ✅ `pnpm check`
* ✅ `pnpm validate`
* ✅ Prettier and ESLint for modified files
* ✅ Registration completeness test passes
* ✅ `pnpm test:credentials` passes (credential-dependent tests skipped where expected)

The remaining test failures are existing integration tests that require external provider credentials and are unrelated to the changes in this PR.

## Notes

This PR preserves the existing provider registration architecture and does not change runtime behavior. Based on the investigation, the reported findings appear to be false positives caused by the Pattern Analysis rule not recognizing the repository's dynamic registration pattern. The added regression test helps ensure future changes do not accidentally introduce real registration issues.

body:
## What
The deterministic **repo factory** — create a new service repo from a language template with **no LLM grep/replace** — plus the ephemeral **infra agent** that drives it and verifies releases. First consumer: upcoming website repos, each needing their own repo.

## Pieces
- **`gate/tools/repo_factory.py`** — literal-rename scaffolding. Grounded against the live templates: the kebab name is the sole placeholder (+ its snake DB variant); the module path/image/hostnames all contain it. Skips `.git`/`node_modules`/binary. `create_repo`, `render_template`, `scaffold`/`push_main`, `open_scaffold_pr`, `scaffold_working_tree` (overlay into a clone → `open_pr` gates on merge).
- **`gate/tools/source_config.py`** — deterministic repo registration: a **comment-preserving, idempotent, minimal-diff** text append into `spec.groups[].repositories[]`; `register_source_config` opens the per-cluster PR.
- **`gate/agent/infra_agent.py`** — cluster-side write-mode entrypoint (`create-repo`, `register-source-config`, `scaffold-pr`, `release-health-check`) routed at the deterministic tools; `obslog` run_start/run_end.
- **`gate/agent/mcp_catalog.yaml`** — `infra_agent` role.
- **`examples/plans/repo-factory-hello-go.yaml`** — worked-example Plan.

## Drift discipline
The load-bearing tests assert **zero old-name survives** post-rename and a **byte-minimal source-config diff** — if a template/schema grows a placeholder the tools miss, the test fails and names it.

## Verification
26 new tests; full suite **1357 passed**, ruff + mypy clean.

body:
«Меньше прыжков между приложениями» был лозунгом, не метрикой. Теперь измеряется.

## Как
- `UsageJournal` (app-private: JSONL + маркер-файл согласия) пишет **обезличенные** события: **SHARED** (пришёл объект), **ACTION** (действие), **COMPLETED** (доведено до terminal в Point).
- Метрика Северной звезды = действий-на-объект (глубина цепочки) + доля COMPLETED (задача закрыта в Point, а не уходом в другое приложение).
- **Только по согласию** (opt-in, дефолт off; выключение стирает данные), **только на устройстве** — ничего не отправляется. Тумблер + сводка на экране ключа.
- Ранжирование подсказок уже питает `CapabilityUsage`; журнал — про измерение, не дублирует.

## Инвариант / приватность
- [x] Side-effect за контрактом (`UsageJournal`); `Mutex` сериализует согласие+запись (opt-out выигрывает гонку, строки не переплетаются); `@Singleton`.
- [x] `:core:flow` без `android.*`; тестируется на JVM (dir инжектится, согласие — файл).

## 何を直したか

TiDB CR への疎通確認をしたところ、**ポートは 3306** で、TiDB 標準の 4000 は接続できなかった (TCP タイムアウト)。前提が誤っていたので、スクリプトのデフォルト値とドキュメントの記述を直す。

```
$ TIDB_PORT=3306 op run --env-file=terraform/.env -- ./scripts/db-count.sh tidb
==> counting: tidb (blog5@blog5.tidb-is1.db.sakurausercontent.com:3306/blog5)
==> テーブルが1つもない (移行前の TiDB ならこれが正常)
```

## 疎通確認で判明したこと (runbook に反映)

- ユーザ名は仮定どおり **データベース名と同じ** (`blog5`)
- **TLS 必須** — `ssl-mode=REQUIRED` で接続できる
- **`allowed_networks` は未設定 = 制限なし** — 手元から素で繋がる。AppRun 共用型の送信元 IP が不定でも困らない
- テーブルが 1 つもない = 移行前の正常な状態

## 変更点

- `scripts/lib/db-common.sh` — `DB_PORT` のデフォルトを 3306 に

author: kyleseaman
body:
## Problem
Two data-loss bugs in the memory subsystem (`src/kiro_crew/memory.py`):

1. **FTS self-heal nuked the index on ordinary lock contention.** `_get_db()`
   caught *any* sqlite error during index init and responded by deleting
   `memory_index.db` (plus `-wal`/`-shm`) and rebuilding from scratch. Under
   concurrent access a transient `database is locked` / `database is busy`
   error would hit that path, so normal contention silently wiped the entire
   FTS index — all indexed memory gone.
2. **`append_history` did an unlocked read-modify-write.** It read today's
   history file, appended one entry in memory, and wrote the whole file back.
   Two concurrent appends (multiple sessions/threads/processes) would read the
   same base content and the later write would clobber the earlier entry — lost
   history.

## Why it matters
Both turn routine concurrency into permanent, silent data loss of the user's
persistent memory. Bug 1 can erase the whole searchable memory index on a
momentary lock; bug 2 drops history entries whenever two writers overlap. There
is no error surfaced to the user — the data is just gone.

## Fix (symptoms → root cause → change)
**Bug 1 — symptom:** memory index occasionally emptied under load. **Root
cause:** the self-heal treated transient lock errors as corruption. **Change:**
- Added `_is_corruption_error()` which returns `True` only for genuine on-disk
  corruption markers (`database disk image is malformed`, `file is not a
  database`, `malformed`, `not a database`) and explicitly returns `False` for
  anything containing `locked`/`busy`, and for non-`sqlite3.DatabaseError`.
- Gated the delete-and-rebuild in `_get_db()` behind `_is_corruption_error(e)`;
  every other error now re-raises untouched instead of destroying the index.
- Gave the connection a `connect(timeout=5.0)` + `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000` in
  `_try_create_db()` so transient locks are waited out rather than surfacing as
  errors at all.

**Bug 2 — symptom:** history entries lost when writes overlap. **Root cause:**
the read-modify-write was not serialized. **Change:** wrapped the whole
read+rewrite of `append_history` in an exclusive advisory lock via
`kiro_crew.platform_compat.file_lock` (real cross-platform locking — `flock` on
POSIX, `msvcrt` on Windows, so the serialization holds on every supported
platform). The lock is released before indexing and cache invalidation. The
sole on-event-loop caller (`HistoryConsolidator._consolidate`) now invokes
`append_history` via `run_in_embed_pool` — matching the adjacent structured-
memory writes — so the blocking lock/IO never runs on the gateway event-loop
thread.

## Tests
`test/test_memory_selfheal.py` — 9 new tests:
- `TestCorruptionDetection` (5): `_is_corruption_error` returns `False` for
  `locked`/`busy` and non-sqlite errors, `True` for `malformed`/`not a
  database`.
- `TestFtsSelfHealGating` (3): a forced `database is locked` error propagates
  and leaves the index file byte-for-byte intact (bug 1 regression); genuine
  on-disk corruption still auto-rebuilds and stays searchable; the connection
  carries `busy_timeout >= 5000`.
- `TestConcurrentAppend` (1): 40 threads appending simultaneously behind a
  barrier — every distinct entry survives exactly once, `#### ` header count
  equals the entry count (bug 2 regression).

## Manual verification
N/A — the regression paths (lock-vs-corruption gating, byte-identical index
survival, and concurrent-append integrity) are directly reproduced and asserted
by the unit tests above; no integration/UI surface is involved.

author: jlobue10
body:
Full test report for the `ally` branch (b9a5f6e0a78b) on a **ROG Xbox Ally X (RC73YA)**, plus fixes for the two bugs found. Everything below was verified live on hardware, on a 7.2-rc4 base with the series applied (the patched `hid-asus` is the sole claimant of `0B05:1B4C` on that tree); fixes were validated by rebuilding the module out-of-tree and re-testing.

## Requested checks — all pass (with the fixes in this PR)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `find /sys -name 'gamepad*'` | attrs present on iface `.0003` |
| `gamepad_mode` desktop/gamepad round-trip | OK, readback + index correct |
| turbo timing write/readback (`btn_a/turbo_period` 4, 10) | OK; out-of-range 21 rejected |
| remap write/readback (`btn_a/remap` → PAD_B, restore) | OK; bogus name rejected |
| evdev coverage, all buttons press+release | OK (see front-button notes) |
| FF rumble on "ASUS ROG Ally X Gamepad" node | OK (felt on device) |
| suspend/resume, then all of the above again | OK |

## Commit 1 — `CMD_SET_MAPPING` packet malformed; writing any remap/macro attr kills BOTH buttons of the pair

Writing e.g. `btn_a/remap` sent a packet the MCU parses as garbage: it unmaps A **and** B (the packet always carries the full pair), the buttons stop emitting events entirely, and the state **persists in MCU NVRAM** until a correct mapping packet is sent. Two independent errors in `ally_set_button_mapping()`, either one alone is fatal:

1. **Block misalignment.** The mapping block is four consecutive **11-byte** entries starting at `buf[5]`: first remap 5–15, first macro 16–26, second remap 27–37, second macro 38–48 (cf. `__btn_pair_to_pkt` / `BTN_CODE_LEN` in hid-asus-ally). The code copied the remap blocks as **10 bytes** and wrote the macro type bytes at `buf[15]`/`buf[37]` — one byte early.
2. **Wrong value-byte position for pad codes.** The value position is per-type: **pad = byte 1**, kb = 2, media = 3, mouse = 4. The code lumped pad/kb/media together at byte 2, so a pad mapping went out as `{0x01, 0x00, code, ...}` and the MCU read value `0x00` = unmapped.

Empirical proof: only the AB pair was ever written during testing, and only A/B died while every untouched pair kept working. Fixing only error 1 did **not** restore them; fixing both and re-sending the pair restored A/B immediately (clean `BTN_SOUTH`/`BTN_EAST` press+release in raw evdev capture).

## Commit 2 — Xbox Ally X front-button long-presses (verified codes)

| Button | Short press | Long press (hardware code) |
|---|---|---|
| Left | `0xA6` → KEY_F16 | keyboard usage **0x70 (F21)** |
| Right | `0x93` → KEY_PROG1 | keyboard usage **0x71 (F22)** |

The original Ally's `0xA7`→F17 and `0x38`→F19 paths **never fire** on this hardware — long-presses arrive as plain keyboard-page usages through the generic HID path. The commit remaps 0x70→KEY_F17 and 0x71→KEY_F19 (scoped to `QUIRK_ROG_ALLY_XPAD`) so userspace sees the same codes across Ally generations. `MSC_SCAN` still carries the raw usage. Behavioral note: these are real held keys (press/autorepeat/release), unlike the synthetic instant press+release from `handle_ally_event()`.

## Not fixed here, for your consideration

- **Trigger range min/max never initialized at probe**: `ally_config.left/right_trigger_min/max` are only written by the sysfs stores, so readback of `range_upper_limit` shows `0` (outside its own advertised `70 100` range) — and worse, the first write to any ONE trigger-range attr calls `ally_set_trigger_ranges()` with the other three cached **zeros**, pushing a zero-width trigger range to the hardware until all four attrs are written once. Suggested: init mins=0/maxes=100 at probe (or query the device).
- `0x38` is mapped to KEY_PROG1 in `asus_input_mapping()` ("ROG key") but to KEY_F19 in `handle_ally_event()` — two contradictory handlers for the same code.
- RGB LED work is enqueued on a deprecated workqueue (7.2 API warning at probe).

## Test environment

7.2-rc4 (CachyOS base; mt76/mac80211 untouched by its patches) + this series. Unrelated: 7.2-rc4 has an mt76/MT7922 regression on this device (WiFi MCU dead at probe → rtnl-held D-state cascade); all testing was done with `mt7921e` blacklisted — being reported to linux-wireless separately, mentioned so nobody chases phantom hid-asus hangs.

body:
Third PR of the classifier program, on top of #268 + #269 (both merged). Ships dark: with `minima_cluster_key_read_versions` empty (the default), every path is byte-identical to main — pinned by test.

## What it does
When PR-9 eventually flips the key space to v2, no request may ever see an empty deterministic-evidence set because of the deploy. This PR builds that guarantee:

- **One round trip, both key spaces**: the keyed lookup's OR-combined match list carries clauses for the active version AND each configured legacy version — never a second lookup, never a stacked timeout.
- **Thin-cell admission**: per candidate model, legacy-key evidence enters only when the active-version cell has fewer than `minima_dual_key_min_n=3` rows — thick v2 cells ignore v1 entirely.
- **Discounted, not trusted**: admitted legacy rows enter aggregation at `minima_legacy_evidence_weight=0.7` through a new `extra_weights` seam in `aggregate_by_model` (weight mass only; counts and provenance untouched). The 0.7 prior gets pinned by the {0.5, 0.7, 0.9} RouterBench sweep in PR-6.
- **Feedback survives the flip**: `_previous_record` falls back to legacy sibling keys, so the read-modify-write accumulation base can't silently reset to n=1 across the migration.

## Tests (6 new)
Single-round-trip clause coverage · byte-identical when off · thin-cell admission (legacy entry ids surface in the candidate's evidence refs) · thick-cell drop · feedback fallback key sequence · aggregate discount math.

`make test` 515 pass · `make lint` + mypy clean. Server-only.

Deferred to PR-6 by design: calibration-report version slices + the discount sweep.

author: alex-de-haas
body:
Final slice of **Phase 3**. Export what the provider is missing, re-read, then make its history authoritative for the items the run could safely act on.

**The order is the design.** Projecting from a snapshot taken *before* the export would erase the very plays that were just sent.

## Nothing half-applied

Anything not safely actionable keeps **all** of its local state — watched flag, resume point, history and count. A half-applied item is worse than an unapplied one. That covers:

| Skip | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `LocalStateChangedDuringSync` | A play recorded while the job ran; its own outbound work carries it |
| `AmbiguousLocalIdentity` | Two editions share one provider identity — acting on either is arbitrary |
| `UnidentifiedLocally` | Cannot be described to the provider |
| `ExportFailed` | **A test caught this one**: I was counting the skip but still projecting the item, wiping the history the export was meant to preserve. A remote snapshot cannot be authoritative for a play that never made it across. |

## Export rules follow from what the data can honestly say

- A play the provider **already has at the same instant** is not re-posted — providers do not deduplicate.
- A local count of five with **no recorded times** exports at most **one** timeless mark. Five `unknown` entries would invent four viewings.
- An **unwatched** row is never exported even with a retained count: re-uploading would undo the user's unwatch on the provider's side.

## Import mirrors it

- Any number of remote `unknown` entries **collapse to one** locally; their individual times are unknowable, so more carries no information.
- A watched item loses its resume point; one the provider **does not know keeps it**, because it is still genuinely useful.
- A **legacy count the provider knows nothing about is preserved**, not recomputed to zero — that would discard the only record those viewings happened.
- `LastPlayedDate`, favorites, catalogs, metadata and source ordering are untouched. Imported history would otherwise reshuffle Continue Watching and Next Up.

## Guards

Apply is blocked by **stuck** outbound work (it will never reflect those local changes, so applying would overwrite them with a snapshot that predates them), refuses an expired preview, and cannot run twice on one run. Applying the same state again changes nothing and posts nothing.

18 tests. Suite green (728). Version `0.30.1` → `0.31.0`.

**Phase 3 is complete.** Remaining: Phase 4 (Settings UI), and the live owned-history-ID verification, which needs a Trakt application and a dedicated test account.

author: coreyphillips
body:
## Problem

Two live failures between two beignet daemons on Umbrel (mainnet):

1. **Every beignet-to-beignet v2 open deadlocked.** A plain (no-lease) acceptor never registered an interactive-tx contribution, so the drive was a no-op on its turns and it never sent tx_complete. Both sides sat in DUAL_FUNDING_V2 forever with no funding tx negotiated. CLN acceptors reply on their own, which is why interop never caught it.
2. **Max funding refused v2 peers**: `max funding is not yet supported on a dual-funded (v2) open`. Since both beignets negotiate dual funding by default, Max in the dashboard always failed beignet-to-beignet.

Plus a display bug: mid-negotiation v2 channels listed an empty peerPubkey (peer map keyed by temp id, listing looked up the derived channel id), which the dashboard rendered as an unknown, offline peer whose Reconnect button sent an empty pubkey.

## Fix

- `handleOpenChannel2` registers an explicit empty contribution for plain accepts (and withdrawn leases); the contribution computation treats zero inputs + zero contribution as owing no fee and producing no outputs, so the acceptor answers each opener turn and completes.
- `openChannel(..., fundMax)` toward a dual-fund peer now quotes the engine's own v2 max from the funding provider and funds by contributing every spendable UTXO. The quote and the channel's change derivation share one weight formula (`dualFundingContributionWeight`), so change nets out to exactly zero. New optional `IFundingProvider.quoteDualFundingMax` / `selectMaxDualFundingInputs`, implemented in `WalletFundingProvider`. Max + requestFunds is rejected (lease fee unknown at commit time).
- Channel listing and diagnostics fall back to the temporary id for the peer lookup; the open response reports `capacitySats` from channel state.
- `POST /channel/open`, the CLI and the openapi spec gain `max` and `satsPerVbyte` for parity with connect-and-open.

## Verification

- New `tests/lightning/dual-fund-beignet-acceptor.test.ts` wires two ChannelManagers directly: reproduces the exact DUAL_FUNDING_V2 stall when the acceptor fix is reverted; asserts the max open funds with a single-output funding tx at the quoted amount; asserts an underfunded max aborts cleanly.
- Full suites green: 4120 lightning tests, 955 CLI tests, lint and typecheck clean.
- CLN interop on regtest: both v2 dual-fund tests pass (cln-lease-seller fails identically on unmodified master, pre-existing environment flake).
- Live two-daemon regtest replay of the field scenario: max connect-and-open at 1 sat/vB committed 499825 of 500000 sats (175 sat fee, exactly the shared formula), single-output funding tx with no change, NORMAL on both sides after 6 confirmations.

author: miharp
body:
Implements phase 3 — poll, fetch, verify, atomic swap, reap — and corrects a design error in the plan along the way.

## The plan was wrong about ordering

It had the agent write `state/<env>.codeid` alongside the environment symlink, with the note *"Symlink swap must land before the state file is updated."*

**With two sources of truth, no ordering is safe:**

| ordering | window |
|---|---|
| swap first | `code-id` reports the **old** id while OpenVox Server serves the **new** tree |
| write first | `code-id` reports the **new** id while the **old** tree is still live |

Either way a catalog is compiled from one version and stamped with another, and its file content then resolves against the wrong tree — exactly the failure static catalogs exist to prevent.

The fix is to delete the second source of truth. **`code-id` now derives the id from the environment symlink**, so a single `rename(2)` changes what OpenVox Server serves and what `code-id` reports at the same instant. It remains one syscall (`readlink`), which the per-compile spawn cost requires.

The state file is gone; packaging and docs updated to match.

## Verification is by resealing, not a checksum

The agent re-derives the `code_id` from the extracted tree and compares.

A transfer digest would only prove the bytes arrived intact. Resealing proves the *tree on disk* is the one the `code_id` names — the claim every catalog compiled against it depends on. It catches corruption, truncation, extraction bugs, **and a publisher serving content that does not match its advertised id** (tested).

## Atomicity

Extraction goes to a temporary directory renamed into place, so a partial transfer never leaves something resembling a valid version.

The environment link is swapped with `rename(2)`, not `ln -sf` — the latter unlinks first, leaving a window where the environment does not exist and catalog compilation fails outright.

## Reaping

Retains the current version, the most recent `--keep`, and anything younger than `--min-age`. The age rule is the important one: an in-flight agent run holding an older `code_id` still requests content for it, and deleting that tree turns a successful run into a failed one.

## Verified with real binaries

`TestTwoCompilersConverge` builds the binaries, runs a publisher and **two compilers with separate SSL material**, takes one offline across a deploy, and checks it catches up with no replayed event:

```text
both compilers at 7b05ff28279c54d2...
both compilers converged to 73433dde9ecef3ab... after catch-up
```

`TestAgentWithoutCompilerRoleIsRefused` confirms a node with a valid certificate from the same CA but the wrong `pp_role` cannot fetch code, and deploys nothing.

Plus unit coverage for idempotence (no churn on unchanged content), multi-environment sync, tamper rejection, and both reaping rules — 12 new tests.

## Not yet done

Nothing has run against a real OpenVox Server. That is the next step, and it needs `compiler02` added to the ovadm compose file.

body:
## What & why

Claude Code on the web starts from a fresh, ephemeral container with no Flutter SDK, so `flutter analyze` / `test` / `build` can't run out of the box. This adds a `SessionStart` hook that installs Flutter automatically at the start of every web session.

## Changes

- **`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`** — installs pinned stable Flutter **3.44.7 / Dart 3.12.2** (matches `customer-app`'s `sdk: ^3.12.0`), adds it to PATH via `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, enables the web target, and warms `flutter pub get`. Guarded to remote sessions only (`CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE`), idempotent, non-interactive.
- **`.claude/settings.json`** — registers the hook on `SessionStart`.
- **`.claude/scripts/flutter-web-shot.sh`** — builds the web target (with local CanvasKit via `--no-web-resources-cdn`) and screenshots it with the pre-installed headless Chromium, as a device-preview substitute.

## Emulator note

This environment has no KVM / hardware virtualization and no display, so Android/iOS device emulators are not usable here. The web-target + headless-Chromium screenshot flow is the practical substitute.

## Validation (run in a web session)

- Hook ran from a clean container: full install + `pub get`, exit 0, PATH persisted (~90s).
- `flutter analyze` → No issues found.
- `flutter test test/notification_models_test.dart` → 8/8 passed.
- Web build served + screenshotted successfully (onboarding screen renders; backend API and Google Fonts are proxy-blocked in the sandbox, so network-driven screens fall back to loading/error state).

The hook only takes effect for web sessions once merged into `main`.

| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| **Freeze on clean/kill close** — viewer only tore down on error/state 5, so an admin-killed session (WS 1000) froze the overlay and left the portal inert | Also tear down on `tunnel.onstatechange==CLOSED` |
| **Clobbered errors** — `teardown()` always showed "SESSION CLOSED", overwriting the error the `onerror` handlers set | The message is passed *into* `teardown`, so the real failure surfaces |
| **Ctrl+Alt+Q leaked to the host** — the disconnect chord reached the remote before teardown | Handled inside `keyboard.onkeydown` via the tracked modifier state and swallowed — never forwarded |
| **Leaked document listeners** — `new Guac.Keyboard(document)` per session, undetachable in 1.5.0 | Keyboard/Mouse bind to the overlay element; removing it on teardown drops every listener |
| **Dead-end / eager import** — imported once at load with a swallowing `catch` (transient failure disabled RDP forever); 75KB for every visitor | Imported on demand inside `openRDP` (retryable; never loaded for sign-on / non-RDP roles) |
| **Stale-forever cache** — vendored client served `immutable` on an unversioned URL | Imported from a content-addressed path `…?v=<hash>` (`Index` substitutes `__GUAC_SRC__`); `immutable` is now sound because the URL changes with the bytes |

## Validation
`go build`, `vet`, `gofmt`, `staticcheck`, `gosec`, `go test -race` clean; the CSP test now also asserts `__GUAC_SRC__` resolves to the hashed path; `node --check` on the extracted inline script passes. Live smoke test confirms the page imports `…?v=b510695a7d30` and that path serves the module (200, `immutable`). Docs: `SECURITY-GAPS` no longer lists the viewer as deferred; low-level change log updated.

Completes the RDP-viewer review fixes (with #17, #18).

author: trungnghia112
body:
## What this changes

The four forked packages each declare:

```json
"build": "cross-env NODE_ENV=production tsup"
```

and every workflow bypassed it, calling `corepack pnpm exec tsup` directly. `NODE_ENV` was
therefore never set — and in `tsup.config.ts`, `minify`, `sourcemap` and `clean` are all
bound to `isProduction`.

So the **first published version** of `angulux-styled`, `-utils`, `-styles` and `-motion`
would have been a development build: unminified, no sourcemaps. A version number is burned
once published, `npm unpublish` included.

`angulux` itself was never affected — it builds through `pnpm --filter angulux run build`,
which sets `NODE_ENV` itself.

**Eight call sites, not five.** The first count was five; a scan found three more —
`release.yml` (3), `ci.yml` (2), `compat.yml` (1), `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Why

Found while packing tarballs from a clean checkout for the BL-11 publish dry run: the
forked tarballs came out *smaller* than a local build (`styles` 195 → 100 files,
`utils` 27 → 19). The difference was entirely sourcemaps, which led back to `NODE_ENV`.

No gate could have caught it. Every check in this repo inspects the build's *output*;
this is a defect in how the build was *invoked*. Worth a follow-up gate — a scan asserting
no tracked file invokes `tsup` for these packages outside their `build` script — but that is
an eighth gate and the "seven gates" line is load-bearing in the README, CONTRIBUTING and
the release docs, so it belongs in its own change rather than smuggled into this one.

---

## Provenance attestation (required)

By submitting this pull request I confirm that:

- [x] This contribution contains **no code, documentation, test fixtures or generated
      output derived from PrimeNG 22 or later**, from any PrimeNG LTS release, or from
      `@primeuix/*` / `primeicons` releases past the MIT boundary recorded in
      `PROVENANCE.md`. *(The diff changes one shell command in six places and two doc
      snippets. No third-party material.)*
- [x] It contains **no content copied from primeng.dev or primefaces.org**.
- [x] If I used an **AI coding assistant**, I reviewed its output for the above and I take
      responsibility for it as if I had written it by hand. *(Stated plainly: AI-assisted end
      to end, reviewed before submission. The diff is `pnpm exec tsup` → `pnpm run build`,
      eight times.)*
- [x] My commits are **signed off** (`git commit -s`), certifying the
      [DCO 1.1](https://developercertificate.org/).

## Evidence

- [x] `npm run check` — 7/7 gates green, from a clean checkout with this patch applied
- [ ] `corepack pnpm --filter angulux run test:unit` — CI runs it on this branch; no library
      source is touched
- [ ] `npx playwright test` — CI runs it; the live check below covers what changed
- [ ] Not applicable — *(not ticked: this changes build invocation, which is exactly the
      thing that reaches users)*

**The production output had never been exercised anywhere.** No CI run had ever built these
four packages with `NODE_ENV=production`, so minified-and-mangled output — with a
hand-maintained terser reserved list of `['theme', 'style', 'css']` — was unverified. Fixing
the invocation without testing that output would have swapped a known-suboptimal artifact for
an unknown one. So it was tested the same way BL-11 tests everything else:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Clean clone of `main` + this patch, `npm run check` | 7/7 |
| `corepack pnpm run build` in each fork | production output confirmed — minified (`import*as s from"angulux-styles/accordion"…`) and sourcemaps present |
| `check:publishable` | 5/5; `styles` 100 → 195 files, `utils` 19 → 27, `motion` 5 → 6 (the sourcemaps) |
| Production tarballs → local Verdaccio → **fresh** `ng new` Angular 22 app | installs clean |
| `ng build` | clean |
| Live in a browser: card, button, `aglInputText`, `agl-table` | renders themed, interaction works (click → row appended), **0 console errors** |

## Checklist

- [x] Title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] Everything is in **English**
- [x] No unrelated cleanup — one command, changed everywhere it appears
- [x] Does not promote a module out of `attic/`
- [x] Does not change public API
- [x] Adds no runtime dependency

author: nappa85
body:
## Why

This starts the firma-run side of FIR-429: the out-of-sandbox dictionary that keeps real secret values away from the agent, and the transport/PEP-client scaffolding the rest of the broker builds on.

## What Changed

- Add `secret::{Placeholder, SecretValue, SecretStore}`: a transport-free, domain-scoped placeholder ↔ secret dictionary. `SecretValue` zeroizes on drop and redacts its `Debug` impl. `Placeholder` mints/parses `firma-secret://<provider>/<name>` tokens with percent-encoding for round-trip safety.
- Add `secret::broker`: the out-of-sandbox JSON-line transport (Unix domain socket and TCP loopback) shims connect to.
- Add `secret::pep`: the broker's fail-closed client for `secret.mediate` decisions — treats broker-can't-reach-Sidecar and garbage responses alike as deny.
- 13 unit tests covering placeholder mint/parse round-trips, domain-scoped resolution, and PEP fail-closed paths.

## Risks / Notes

- Depends on `fir-429/01-secret-types` (base branch) for `firma_core::SecretDecision`. Part of the FIR-429 stack; `fir-429/07-run-gateway-integration` builds on top.
- **Fail-closed is load-bearing here too**: an unreachable PEP endpoint or a malformed response must resolve to deny, never permit — see `secret::pep` tests.

## AI Assistance

Carved out of a larger FIR-429 implementation branch into this stack with Claude Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5`) assistance; file contents are unchanged from the original implementation.

author: alistair3149
body:
Distributes the MediaWiki MCP Server as an installable plugin for **Claude Code** and **Codex**, mirroring the existing Gemini CLI extension, and documents installation for **Antigravity**. Closes #473.

## What this adds

- **Claude Code and Codex plugin marketplaces.** This repository doubles as a plugin marketplace for both clients, each with a catalog at the repo root pointing at one shared plugin:
  - Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add ProfessionalWiki/MediaWiki-MCP-Server` then `/plugin install mediawiki-mcp-server@professional-wiki`
  - Codex: `codex plugin marketplace add ProfessionalWiki/MediaWiki-MCP-Server` then `codex plugin add mediawiki-mcp-server@professional-wiki`
- **Antigravity** install snippet. It reads its own `mcp_config.json`, so there is no committed manifest (the same tier as the VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf snippets).
- **Metadata sync.** `scripts/sync-version.cjs` becomes `scripts/sync-manifests.cjs`, which now propagates the version *and* the shared metadata (description, keywords, author, homepage, license) from a single source into every distribution manifest, each write re-read and verified. `npm run sync-manifests` runs it standalone.

## Layout

The plugin is a thin wrapper over the published npm package (launched via `npx`), like the Gemini extension. Both clients share one plugin directory and one `.mcp.json`:

```
.claude-plugin/marketplace.json          # Claude catalog
.agents/plugins/marketplace.json         # Codex catalog
plugins/mediawiki-mcp-server/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json           # Claude manifest (auto-discovers .mcp.json)
├── .codex-plugin/plugin.json            # Codex manifest (mcpServers: "./.mcp.json")
└── .mcp.json                            # shared launch command
```

None of these leak into the published npm tarball, mcpb bundle, or Docker image; all three are allow-list based.

## Verification

- Full suite green (1572 tests); `lint`, `fmt:check`, and `validate:server-json` pass.
- `claude plugin validate .` passes (the real Claude Code tooling).
- An MCP `initialize` handshake over the exact `npx` command the manifests use returns a valid response, so the server boots and speaks MCP end to end.
- `sync-manifests` round-trip verified (version reaches 5 files, the shared description 6) and idempotent against the committed files.

A code review flagged one Critical item on `policy.authentication`, which I checked against OpenAI's own `plugin-json-spec.md` and real `marketplace.json` and found to be a false positive: `ON_USE` is the documented value and is what OpenAI's own plugins use. The review's valid point (plugin-scoped tool names such as `mcp__plugin_…`) is now noted in the README.

## Validated on both real CLIs

Installed via local-directory marketplaces (the dev install path, which exercises the exact committed manifests; the published-repo install resolves identically, only the source differs):

- **Codex 0.145.0** — `codex plugin marketplace add` + `codex plugin add` succeed; `codex mcp list` shows the `mediawiki` server (`npx -y @professional-wiki/mediawiki-mcp-server@latest`, enabled). Codex accepted `policy.authentication: "ON_USE"`, confirming that review flag was a false positive.
- **Claude Code** — `claude plugin install` succeeds; `claude plugin details` reports one MCP server (`mediawiki`), auto-discovered from the shared `.mcp.json` (the plugin manifest correctly omits `mcpServers`).

author: leannunez
body:
## Qué

Primer PR del slice 3 de Fase 2 (el último): **backend de Compras + costos + cuenta corriente de proveedor**. Cierra el lado proveedor que faltaba.

Encadenado: **este PR (backend) → PR2 (UI /compras)**. Mismo patrón que slices 1 y 2.

## Descubrimiento que moldeó el diseño

La ingesta OCR de remitos YA era una "compra rápida por papel" (actualiza costo, repricea, suma stock), pero sin documento formal ni cta cte de proveedor. Este PR construye la **compra manual formal** + la **cta cte de proveedor**, reutilizando la lógica de costo/reprice que la ingesta ya tenía (promovida a `catalogo`). La ingesta OCR queda intacta.

## Decisiones de diseño

- **Último costo pisa**: la compra setea `articulo.costo` = costo del renglón (consistente con la ingesta OCR).
- **Repricea con margen**: al subir el costo, recalcula el precio de cada lista con SU margen; las sin margen no se tocan.
- **Módulo nuevo `app/compras/`** (screaming architecture, espeja `app/ventas/`). `proveedores` queda como maestro.
- La compra **no tiene numeración interna**: se identifica por el **número del comprobante del proveedor**, con unique `(org, proveedor, numero)` que evita cargar dos veces la misma factura → 409.
- **cta cte de proveedor** (nuevo ledger append-only, saldo como vista): compra a crédito → **Debe** (lo que le debemos); pago → **Haber**; contado no toca. `saldo = SUM(debe) - SUM(haber)` = lo que le debemos.

## Qué hace `crear_compra`

Suma stock (`motivo='compra'`) · actualiza costo · repricea listas · upsertea el vínculo `articulo_proveedor` con el costo · Debe en cta cte si es a crédito. Todo en una transacción todo-o-nada.

## Endpoints

- `POST /compras` · `GET /compras` · `GET /compras/{id}`
- `POST /compras/pagos` · `GET /compras/proveedores/{id}/saldo`
- `GET /proveedores` (nuevo router, para el selector de la UI)

## Tests

16 tests nuevos contra Postgres real: IVA + stock + costo (último pisa) + reprice (lista con margen sí, sin margen no), cta cte (Debe/pago), factura duplicada (unique), proveedor/artículo inexistente, append-only, RLS entre orgs y atomicidad. **Suite completo: 177 passed.**

## Refactor incluido

`_recalcular_precios` se promovió de `ingesta_visual` a `catalogo.recalcular_precios_por_costo` (DRY, sin cambio de comportamiento; ingesta lo importa).

author: danlessa
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces the charter for **Sampa Pousada da Humanidade**, a parallel mission to the 300 KJ City Initiative focused on providing unconditional shelter and basic needs provisioning at scale within constrained geographic and material budgets.

## Changes

- **New mission charter** (`missions/sampa-pousada-da-humanidade.md`): A comprehensive 160-line document defining:
  - The mission's relationship to the 300 KJ City Initiative (parallel, not subordinate)
  - Geographic scope: the Alto Tietê watershed (~5,900 km²) as the resource base
  - **Goal 1**: Host Brazil's entire population (~210 million) sustainably within the Alto Tietê alone, with explicit constraints on space (no horizontal expansion), materials (demolition/waste streams only), water (closed-loop within watershed), and food (vertical/controlled-environment agriculture)
  - **Goal 2**: Extend to all humanity by enlisting only adjacent neighboring regions (Vale do Paraíba, Depressão Periférica, Vale do Ribeira, etc.) with strict rules on consent and sufficiency protection
  - Sequencing: Prove (district pilot) → Densify (metropolis) → Host (basin scale)
  - Six core principles emphasizing unconditional hospitality, physical ledger transparency, footprint shrinkage, and nearest-first sourcing
  - Current status: chartered phase, drafting the Alto Tietê ledger

- **Updated README** to reference the new parallel mission with a brief description

## Notable Details

The charter is deliberately ambitious yet constrained: hosting 210 million people at ~36,000 people/km² (Paris/Manila density) within a single watershed, with all material and water flows accounted for and published. The mission explicitly rejects distant extraction and frames the work as a replicable model (basin-by-basin globally) rather than a supply-chain expansion.

body:
This feature enhances the robustness of attachment downloads by verifying the writability of the configured export folder at two key points:

*   **During selection:** When a user chooses a new attachment folder in the settings, the application now immediately checks if it's writable. If not, the selection is rejected with a toast notification, preventing configuration of an unusable folder.
*   **At application startup:** The application now performs a startup check on the currently configured attachment folder. If the folder is no longer writable (e.g., due to permission changes or unavailability), it automatically resets to the default Downloads folder.

To provide clear user feedback, a new **"Settings restored" dialog** is introduced. This dialog centralizes notifications for any settings that were automatically reverted to their default values due to validation failures, ensuring the user is informed about such changes.

**Technical Changes:**
*   A new `CheckFolderWritable` function in the Go backend reliably tests write permissions by creating and deleting a probe file.
*   A new Svelte store (`settingsResetStore`) and associated dialog component (`SettingsResetDialog`) provide a unified mechanism for reporting and displaying multiple setting resets.
*   Frontend utilities are updated to integrate these checks and reporting mechanisms.

author: antoinetoussaint
body:
Fixes tracker #512.

## Summary

The GitHub `/notifications` `Last-Modified` cursor was committed the instant the notification LIST was parsed (`fetch_notifications_inner`), but the per-item deep-fetches (`fetch_single_pr`/`fetch_single_issue`) run later in the polling layer's `fetch_incremental`, where a transient `Err` was logged and silently dropped. So if PR #123 fired a notification and its deep-fetch timed out this tick, the cursor had already advanced past it — the next heartbeat returned 304 and never re-listed #123 until its `updated_at` bumped again, hiding the CI failure / comment until the ≤10-min full sweep.

The fix couples the at-most-once cursor advance to work completion:

- `NotificationsPoll::Modified` now carries the pending `Last-Modified` back to the caller instead of committing it inside the gh client.
- A new `GhClient::commit_notifications_cursor` performs the write.
- `fetch_incremental` fans out the deep-fetches, then commits the cursor **only when every entry resolved** — success or a definitive `Ok(None)` "not visible". Any transient `Err` holds the cursor so the un-fetched entry re-lists on the next heartbeat. `Ok(None)` does *not* hold the cursor, so a permanently-gone entry can't pin it forever.

Invariants preserved: the fan-out result set is unchanged on the success path (rescope / coverage tracking and the 0-result guard untouched), and only the exact server header value is ever committed (never a synthesized date).

## Test plan

- New `notifications_list_does_not_advance_cursor_until_committed` (gh-provider): parsing the list does not advance the cursor; an un-committed cursor re-lists the entry next tick (200, not 304); an explicit commit reaches the 304 steady state. Uses a hand-rolled conditional-GET mock (no new deps).
- `cargo test -p lazybox-gh -p lazybox-server --no-fail-fast` — green (128 + 357 + all integration suites pass).
- `cargo clippy -p lazybox-gh -p lazybox-server --all-targets` — clean (only the benign libghostty zig-SDK note).

author: thorwhalen
body:
## Index — embeddings, hybrid search, library façade & taxonomy (Closes #2)

The retrieval **keystone** (Epic #13, report 04 / report 10 §5): make every sound
findable by **keyword _and_ meaning**, behind small swappable protocols with
zero-config defaults. Builds strictly on the Foundation SSOT types (`SoundRecord`,
`Candidate`, enums) — no parallel structures.

### What's in it

- **`Embedder` protocol + `ClapEmbedder`** (`foley[clap]`) — LAION-CLAP
  `laion/larger_clap_general` (512-d, Apache-2.0); L2-normalized `float32`; lazy
  weights. Verified end-to-end against transformers 4.57.1 (correct shapes/norms,
  sane cross-modal ordering).
- **Hybrid search + RRF** (`foley.index.search`) — pure, deterministic Reciprocal
  Rank Fusion (k=60); fuses `knn()` + `bm25()` rank lists identically across every
  backend (never averages incompatible score scales).
- **Three index backends** (one `VectorIndex`+`KeywordIndex` contract):
  - `MemoryIndex` — numpy cosine + compact stdlib BM25; zero-extra, always
    available (the CI/test + small-lib tier).
  - `LanceIndex` (`foley[index]`) — LanceDB one table (vector column + native FTS,
    **no tantivy**); the recommended persistent default; local dir or `s3://`.
  - `SqliteVecIndex` (`foley[index-sqlite]`) — sqlite-vec `vec0` + stdlib FTS5,
    one file; capability-gated (needs loadable SQLite extensions).
- **`SoundLibrary` façade** — composes injected `sounds`/`meta`/`vindex`/`kindex`/
  `embedder` (all lazily defaulted); a read-only `Mapping` of records; `search`
  (text) / `search_clip` (reference clip) / `similar` (audio↔audio) / `filter`
  (facets) / `add` (the write path) / storage-mode-aware `audio`/`array`.
- **`foley.search()` / `foley.similar()` / `foley.library`** top-level entry points.
- **UCS + AudioSet taxonomy resolver** (`foley.index.taxonomy`) — staged
  `filename > keyword > audioset > none` resolution with word-boundary matching;
  a hand-curated seed table + AudioSet→UCS overlap map, **open/closed** for the
  full UCS master / EnvSound-UCS JSON drop.

### Design discipline
- `import foley` still pulls only `dol` — torch/transformers/lancedb/sqlite_vec are
  all lazy-imported inside the methods that use them.
- RRF is foley's SSOT (not the engine's), so ranking is byte-identical across
  MemoryIndex/LanceIndex (verified) and gate-able by the eval harness (#10).

### Tests
177 passed, 9 skipped (sqlite-vec env-gated; CLAP inference opt-in via
`FOLEY_RUN_CLAP=1`), ruff clean. Pure RRF + taxonomy tests need no extras; the
hybrid+façade path is parametrized across MemoryIndex and LanceIndex with a
deterministic fake embedder; LanceDB runs in CI (added to the `test` extra).

### Notes / follow-ups
- Seed UCS CatIDs beyond `DOORWood`/`WEATHRain` are marked `confident=False`
  (approximate) — reconcile against the UCS master when the full table drops in.
- sqlite-vec needs an interpreter with loadable SQLite extensions (macOS
  pyenv/system pythons lack this); LanceDB is the default.
- #16 fast-follows unchanged (qc inf-guard before #3, stores id-sanitize before #5).
