author: trentleslie
body:
## The bug
`Entity.update_from` and `Entity.from_input` feed `pd.Series.to_dict()` directly into the `Entity` constructor. A pandas `NaN` is a **float**, and the resolution fields (`chosen_kg_id_provided`, `chosen_kg_id_review`) are typed `str | None` — so pydantic raises `ValidationError: Input should be a valid string [input_value=nan, input_type=float]`.

This surfaced through the external-benchmark **Phase-0 gate**: its live smoke calls the single-entity `map_entity_to_kg`, which hit this on `fork/dev`. The gate catches the exception and labeled it **"Kestrel API unreachable"** — so every benchmark run had to pass `--no-gate`, even though Kestrel was reachable (~0.3s/endpoint) and the batch path `map_dataset_to_kg` worked fine. It cost real debugging time to trace a pydantic bug hiding behind a network-sounding message.

## The fix
- `_nan_to_none()` coerces scalar float `NaN → None` for Series-derived dicts (`v != v`, so only NaN; real values and list/dict fields untouched), applied in both Entity entry points.
- The gate's smoke now captures the first exception, and `run_gate` names it: `"Kestrel smoke call failed (smoke error: ...)"` instead of a blanket `"unreachable"` — so a non-network failure is diagnosable immediately.

## Verified live
The Phase-0 gate now returns **`proceed`** with its cost estimate (`~266s, ~267 external calls, ~$0.27` for Hajjar-100) instead of a false stop. `map_entity_to_kg("glucose")` → `RM:0003276`.

## Tests
`test_entity_model.py`: NaN→None on `update_from` and `from_input`, and that real values pass through. Gate + entity + models suites pass.

**Pre-existing, not from this change:** `test_map_entity_returns_dict` fails identically on clean `fork/dev` (a live-network integration test) — verified by stashing this diff. The 3 API-test collection errors are a missing `httpx` dev-dep in the minimal venv.

## Impact
Removes the `--no-gate` workaround for external-benchmark runs and restores the Phase-0 cost estimate. Fixes a real bug in the single-entity mapping path generally, not just the gate.

## Summary
Complete redesign of the portfolio website with a modern, professional aesthetic. Replaced the old Bootstrap-based layout with a custom, fully responsive design featuring gradient accents, smooth animations, and improved user experience.

## Key Changes

### Styling (style.css)
- **Design System**: Introduced CSS custom properties for colors, gradients, shadows, and typography for consistent theming
- **Modern Layout**: Replaced Bootstrap grid with CSS Grid and Flexbox for more flexible, responsive layouts
- **Navigation**: Implemented fixed navbar with backdrop blur effect, smooth scroll behavior, and mobile hamburger menu
- **Hero Section**: Created full-viewport hero with gradient background, animated text elements, and social media links
- **Component Styling**: Added comprehensive styles for:
  - About section with stat cards and info items
  - Skills section with animated progress bars
  - Timeline-based experience section with alternating layout
  - Project cards with hover overlays and image zoom effects
  - Contact form with proper input styling
  - Footer with social links
- **Animations**: Defined keyframe animations (fadeInDown, fadeInUp, bounce) for entrance effects
- **Responsive Design**: Added media queries for tablets (992px), mobile (768px), and small screens (480px)

### HTML Structure (index.html)
- **Language**: Changed from English to Turkish (lang="tr")
- **Navigation**: Added fixed navbar with logo and navigation menu with smooth scroll links
- **Hero Section**: Implemented full-screen hero with greeting, title, subtitle, description, CTA buttons, and social links
- **About Section**: Added personal introduction, info items, and stat cards showing experience metrics
- **Skills Section**: Created three-column skill categories (Front-End, Framework & Tools, Other) with progress bars
- **Experience Section**: Built timeline component with alternating layout showing job positions and responsibilities
- **Projects Section**: Added project grid with image overlays and project tags
- **Contact Section**: Implemented contact form and contact information with social media links
- **Footer**: Added copyright and attribution footer

### JavaScript (script.js - New File)
- **Mobile Navigation**: Hamburger menu toggle with active state management
- **Navbar Effects**: Scroll-triggered navbar styling and active link highlighting
- **Smooth Scrolling**: Anchor link smooth scroll behavior
- **Animations**: 
  - Skill bar animations triggered on scroll
  - Intersection Observer for fade-in effects on elements
  - Parallax effect on hero section
  - Counter animation for statistics
- **Form Handling**: Contact form submission with validation and user feedback

## Notable Implementation Details
- Used CSS Grid for complex layouts (timeline, about stats, projects)
- Implemented Intersection Observer API for performance-optimized scroll animations
- Added backdrop-filter blur effects for modern glassmorphism design
- Responsive design uses mobile-first approach with progressive enhancement
- All animations use CSS transitions and keyframes for smooth 60fps performance
- Turkish language content throughout for localization

author: kate-son
body:
## 📌 이번 PR 요약
- 주차: 5주차 — 상태관리 아키텍처 (홈 / 상품 목록)
- 무엇을 / 왜

> - 홈, 상품 목록 화면에 서버(TanStack Query), URL(nuqs), 클라이언트(Zustand), 로컬 상태의 경계를 직접 설계해 구현
> - Advanced 구현

## 📚 이번 주 학습
- 학습 주제: 상태의 Source of Truth를 먼저 정하고 도구를 고르는 순서, TanStack Query 캐시 정책, nuqs URL 상태, Zustand selector 구독, Next.js App Router의 Server/Client 컴포넌트 경계
- 배운 것 / 새로 적용한 것:
  - `queryOptions` 팩토리 + 이름 있는 상수(`PRODUCT_PRICE_STALE_TIME` 등)로 staleTime/gcTime의 근거를 코드에 남기는 법
  - nuqs `history: 'push'`와, 검색어처럼 즉시 반영하면 안 되는 값은 draft 로컬 상태로 분리하고 폼 제출 시점에만 URL에 반영하는 패턴 (3주차 `popstate`/`pushState` 경험을 그대로 재사용)
  - Server Component에서 `prefetchQuery` + `dehydrate`/`HydrationBoundary`로 초기 요청 중복 없이 데이터를 미리 채우는 법. 이 과정에서 클라이언트 훅과 서버 로더가 **같은 URL 파싱 규칙(parser)을 공유해야** 캐시 키가 맞는다는 것, `nuqs`(클라이언트 전용)와 `nuqs/server`의 차이
  - `Suspense` 경계는 `useSearchParams`를 직접 호출하는 컴포넌트(`NuqsAdapter`) 자신을 감싸야 한다는 것

## 🤔 고민한 점 / 막혔던 부분
- **Home의 인기/신상품과 목록이 같은 `Product[]` 데이터인데, staleTime을 어떻게 나눌지**: 타임세일이 1시간 단위로 돈다는 보장이 없고 25분처럼 더 짧게 도는 경우도 있어서, 가격이 안전하게 반영되려면 짧은 주기로 재확인해야 했습니다. 근데 Home 응답은 배너+카테고리+상품이 하나의 API 응답으로 묶여 있어서 필드별로 다른 staleTime을 줄 수 없었고, 결국 더 변동성이 큰 상품 가격 기준(1분)에 맞춰 두 쿼리가 값을 공유하도록 정리했습니다.
- **검색어처럼 "타이핑 중"과 "실제 적용된 값"을 어떻게 나눌지**: 검색어를 nuqs에 즉시 반영하면 한 글자 칠 때마다 히스토리가 쌓이고 요청도 매번 나가서, draft 로컬 상태로 붙잡아뒀다가 폼 제출(디바운스 포함) 시에만 URL에 반영하는 구조로 만들었습니다. 그런데 뒤로가기나 공유 링크로 `q`가 draft 외부(URL)에서 바뀔 수 있어서, `useEffect` 없이 렌더 중 `prevAppliedQuery` 비교로 draft를 재동기화하는 방식을 썼습니다.
- **Server Component 프리패치가 실제 URL 조건과 어긋나던 문제**: Advanced B(서버 프리패치)를 붙이면서, 서버가 하드코딩된 기본값으로 미리 데이터를 준비했더니 `/products?category=casual`처럼 실제 조건이 있는 URL에서는 캐시 키가 달라 프리패치가 통째로 무효화됐습니다. 클라이언트 훅과 서버 로더가 같은 URL 파싱 규칙(parser)을 공유하도록 분리해서 캐시 키를 맞췄고, 이 과정에서 `nuqs`(클라이언트 전용)와 `nuqs/server`가 따로 있다는 것도 알게 됐습니다.
- **`useSearchParams()`가 정적 빌드에서만 터지던 문제**: `pnpm build`에서만 `/products`가 프리렌더 에러를 냈는데(dev 서버에선 안 남), 알고 보니 `NuqsAdapter` 자신이 내부적으로 `useSearchParams()`를 호출하고 있어서 그 컴포넌트를 감싸는 `Suspense` 경계가 필요했습니다. 처음엔 페이지마다 View/Suspense를 나누려다가, `MainProvider` 한 곳에서 `NuqsAdapter` 전체를 감싸는 전역 방식으로 정리했습니다.
- **잘못된 `page` 값(범위 밖) 처리**: `?page=99`처럼 실제 `totalPages`를 넘는 값이 들어오면 1페이지로 되돌리는 방어 로직을 넣었습니다. 이 문제 자체는 3주차 때 같은 이름의 버그를 이미 겪어봐서, 이번엔 서버 데이터(`totalCount`/`pageSize`)가 도착한 뒤 `useEffect`로 검증하는 방식으로 다시 풀었습니다.

## 📝 판단 근거
**- docs > decisions-week05.md에 이번 주차 판단 근거 정리했습니다.**
- Home의 데이터는 한 API 응답에 묶여 있고, 다른 화면에서 재사용되지 않는 페이지 전용 조합 로직이라 분리하지 않고, app 안에 두었습니다.
- 프로젝트 규모상 아직 별도 테스트 디렉토리로 분리할 필요는 없다고 판단했습니다. 규모가 커지면 소스와 동일한 디렉토리 구조를 미러링한 테스트 디렉토리를 구성할 예정입니다.

## 🙋 피드백 받고 싶은 부분
다음 주차 "시스템 설계 & FSD 아키텍처"를 위해 미리 프로젝트를 FSD 아키텍처 구조로 배치했습니다.
GitHub Actions Playwright 오류 merge의 경우, 다음 과제에 적용하겠습니다.

- **검색어 draft 재동기화를 `useEffect` 대신 렌더 중 비교로 처리한 것**: "외부(URL)에서 값이 바뀌는 걸 언제 반영할지"를 렌더 중 조건문으로 판단하는 게 실제로 안전한 패턴인지 궁금합니다.
```
if (appliedQuery !== prevAppliedQuery) {
    setPrevAppliedQuery(appliedQuery);
    setDraftQuery(appliedQuery);
  }
```
- **서버, 클라이언트가 같은 기본값(parser)을 공유하는 구조**: 검색어/카테고리/정렬/페이지의 기본값을 서버(프리패치)에서도 써야 하고 클라이언트(nuqs 훅)에서도 똑같이 써야 해서, 그 정의(`productSearchParams.ts`)만 파일 하나로, 클라이언트 훅/서버 로더는 분리해서 정의 파일을 공용으로 사용하게 했는데요. 이렇게 "기본값 정의만 공용, 나머지는 따로"로 나누는 게 맞는 방향인지 궁금합니다.
```
productSearchParams.ts
useProductListParams.ts
loadProductSearchParams.ts
```
- **`/`를 `/home`으로 리다이렉트한 라우팅 선택**: `/`를 Home 콘텐츠로 직접 채우는 대신, `src/app/page.tsx`는 `redirect('/home')`만 하고 실제 Home 화면은 `/home` 라우트에 따로 뒀습니다. 홈이 사실상 유일한 진입점인 상황에서 이렇게 라우트를 분리하는 게 맞는 선택인지, 아니면 `/` 자체를 Home으로 채우는 쪽이 더 나은지 피드백 부탁드립니다.

author: elekktrisch
body:
Ships the operator-facing **scheduled-jobs console** (`/system/jobs`): a SYSTEM_ADMINISTRATOR sees every registered business job with its last-run status and can trigger **Run now**. Five jobs land through it end-to-end (PlanningDayNotification retrofit + DailyFlightValidation, DailyReport, LicenceNotification, AircraftDBSync, DeliveryCreation).

Carve/contract: `docs/modernization/stories/J-15-scheduled-jobs-console.md`

**Scope decision:** S-090 (DeliveryMailExport / zip) splits to follow-up **J-15b** — the carve's sanctioned escape hatch; it has no J-15 AC.

**Proof gallery:** https://elekktrisch.github.io/fls/alpenflight/proof-preview/integration-J-15/

### AC checklist
- [x] Console lists jobs + last-run status — *real-idp gate*
- [x] Run now → DailyFlightValidation → completed run; seeded flight VALID / ≥2d-old VALID → LOCKED (club-admin re-read) — *completed run + club-admin re-read in the gate; the specific VALID/LOCKED transitions in `DailyFlightValidationJobIT`, incl. the negative seeds (a flight one day inside the lock gate stays VALID, an incomplete flight goes INVALID). The gate's re-read asserts the pending-validation set never grows rather than naming one flight.*
- [ ] Run now → DailyReport → Mailpit email — **not proven via Mailpit; handed off as boyscout rider `[J-15-MAILPIT-REPORT]`** (`docs/modernization/stories/_BOYSCOUT.md`). `DailyReportJobIT` proves the mail against the captured outbox, incl. the opt-out negative; the gate does not drive it through Mailpit. Closing it needs a clean-seed floor (an opted-in pilot with an unreported flight in the job's window), which is why it rides the next journey touching the jobs console or the mail path rather than being bodged in here.
- [x] Run now → AircraftDBSync (recorded OGN fixture) → matched update, unmatched logged not created — *`AircraftDatabaseSyncJobIT`, recorded fixture served over real HTTP (transport + JSON binding exercised, no live network)*
- [x] Run now → DeliveryCreation → DELIVERY_PREPARED / DELIVERY_PREPARATION_ERROR isolated — *`DeliveryCreationJobIT`: both flights in one run, the failing one flagged without denying the other its delivery*
- [x] CLUB_ADMINISTRATOR redirected + POST run → 403 (load-bearing negative) — *real-idp gate; registry read and Run now both 403*
- [x] Instrumentation: started/completed/failed last-run status + histogram — *`MeasuredJobAspectIT`: completed and failed runs persisted, `fls_job_duration_seconds` tagged per job, a throwing job does not propagate*

Where an AC is ticked on an IT rather than the console, the behaviour is proven but not console-triggered in the gate.

### Deliberate divergences from legacy
- **Validation selection:** legacy narrows the INVALID arm to flights modified since last validation. Nothing maintains `t_flight.modified_on`, so that predicate would freeze at insert time and strand fixed flights as INVALID; every INVALID flight is re-validated instead.
- **Lock gate:** `FlightGatePolicy.canLock` (`flight_date <= today-2`, the J-2 parity decision), not legacy's `created_on` keying.
- **OGN sync:** writes only non-blank incoming values. Legacy assigns unconditionally, wiping a hand-maintained competition sign whenever the registry has none.
- **Daily report window:** never-reported flights within 2 days, which also bounds the rescan legacy got free from its created-today predicate.

author: lahiruudayakumara
body:
## Purpose

Ensure custom policy usages are consistently maintained for LLM providers and reduce database transaction overhead when storing multiple policy usages.

Resolves #2802

## Goals

- Reconcile custom policy usages for every LLM provider create and update operation.
- Store multiple policy usages using a single database insert.
- Preserve policy UUID deduplication and transactional rollback behavior.

## Approach

- Removed the conditional controlling custom policy usage reconciliation from the shared LLM provider create and update paths.
- Updated `replaceCustomPolicyUsagesTx` to build one parameterized multi-row `INSERT` instead of executing one insert per policy UUID.
- Retained the existing deletion-first replacement behavior within the transaction.
- Added regression coverage for deduplication, rollback, and unconditional reconciliation.

## User stories

- As a platform administrator, I want LLM provider custom policy usages to remain accurate so that policies currently in use cannot be incorrectly deleted.
- As a platform operator, I want policy usage persistence to minimize database round-trips.

## Documentation

N/A — this is an internal persistence and performance improvement with no user-facing API or configuration changes.

  - Added coverage for unconditional reconciliation through the standard update path.

author: hpol369
body:
The seven guide pages carried the most valuable links on the site and recorded **none** of their clicks.

Only `filter-cards.tsx` and `product-card.tsx` used `AffiliateLink`. Every guide had its own byte-identical copy of `ProductReview` with a bare `<a href={product.affiliateUrl}>`, and `ProductComparisonTable` had one too. The RO guide alone carries 18 Osmio links at a £50-75 bounty each, and there was no way to tell whether anyone ever clicked them.

Clicks are the only same-day signal we get. Sales show up days later in a partner dashboard. Being blind on exactly the pages with the expensive links is the worst place for that gap.

## What changed

- Six guides: bare `<a>` → `<AffiliateLink>`, following the attribution convention already used in `best-water-filters-uk`
- `ProductComparisonTable`: same, plus tracking props that are **required, not optional**, so a future caller cannot ship a table whose clicks land in analytics with no page attached. The compiler found all six call sites.
- One test pinning that our tracking never displaces a partner's

## The risk this had to clear

`buildAffiliateUrl` appends utm parameters to non-Amazon URLs. Osmio identifies a sale purely by `aw_affiliate`, so mangling that parameter would mean the sale still happens and we never get paid.

Verified in the production build:

- Osmio links with `aw_affiliate` intact: **18**
- Amazon links carrying utm: **0** (skipped by design — the Operating Agreement forbids decorating Special Links)
- Amazon links with the tag: **8**

99/99 tests, typecheck clean, build succeeds.

Completes the ontology leg of the dim_hospital -> Curavias 1:1 fold so the reference ontology, the Fabric IQ operational crosswalk, and the Data Agent grounding all express the org spine, the skills domain, and the bed/ops care-setting split (T14) that the semantic model (PR #339) already exposes.

## Summary
Store releases now build and submit in separate, traceable stages. A tag builds the commit it names, while store submission remains a deliberate manual action tied to the recorded EAS build IDs.

## Changes
- Validate tag and manual versions against `app.json` without committing back to `main`
- Run complete non-device checks and EAS builds against the same source commit
- Record release metadata and platform build responses as retained workflow artifacts
- Submit exact builds from a selected release workflow run without rebuilding or using `--latest`
- Require production migration confirmation and iOS E2E evidence before applicable submissions
- Scope release credentials through the `production-release` environment on `main` and `v*`
- Document build-number behavior, database checks, trace evidence, and recovery procedures

## Verification
- `npm run check` passed, including 2,261 unit tests, 638 component tests, security and sync suites, 58 local migrations, SQL vectors, and database contract checks
- `npm run test:ci` passed with 34 workflow contract tests
- `npm run lint` passed
- Workflow YAML parsing and `git diff --check` passed
- GitHub environment verification confirmed the three required secret names and deployment rules for `main` and `v*`; no secret values were accessed

## Risk
Moderate deployment-process change. Store submission now requires a separate manual workflow run and the successful build run ID. Invalid run metadata, missing confirmations, and malformed EAS IDs fail before credentials or shell commands are used. Reverting the release workflows restores the previous process. No EAS build, tag push, store submission, or production Supabase action was performed during implementation.

author: dasindusithmira2025-ops
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #16. The internal Preview release [run 30025361745](https://github.com/dasindusithmira2025-ops/forgemind/actions/runs/30025361745) got much further — the `assert-deploy-ready` gate passed and the staged payloads were confirmed present — but `firebase deploy` still failed:

```
Error: Directory 'D:\a\forgemind\forgemind\.artifacts\update-site-dist' for Hosting does not exist.
```

## Root cause

firebase-tools computes the Hosting public directory as:

```js
Config.path(public) = normalize(path.join(projectDir, public))   // projectDir = dirname(--config path)
```

It uses **`path.join`, not `path.resolve`**, so an **absolute** `public` value is concatenated onto the config directory into a nonexistent path. #16's "absolute, normalized public" change was therefore wrong. The pre-deploy assertion passed only because it used `path.resolve` (which honors absolute paths), diverging from firebase's actual `path.join` and hiding the defect.

Verified directly against firebase-tools 13.35.1 source: `detectProjectRoot` returns `dirname(--config path)` (`.artifacts`), and `Config.path` joins that with the raw `public`.

## Fix

- Generate a **relative** `public` (`update-site-dist`) derived from the staged directory (`relativePublicForConfig`), refusing any directory that escapes the config directory (firebase itself rejects a `public` containing `..`).
- `resolveConfigPublicDirectory` now mirrors firebase-tools **exactly** (`normalize(join(configDir, public))`), so the assertion validates the same path the CLI reads and can never diverge again — it would now catch the absolute-path bug before the CLI runs.
- Regression tests updated accordingly.

## Validation

- `oxlint` clean · `tsc -b` clean · `vitest run` **381/381**
- **End-to-end proof** through the real firebase-tools `Config` class: a config generated by this code resolves `public` to the staged dir with `MATCH: true` and `dirExistsSync: true`.

```
generated public value: "update-site-dist"
firebase resolved public: ...\.artifacts\update-site-dist
staged dir              : ...\.artifacts\update-site-dist
MATCH: true
dirExistsSync(resolved): true
```

## Risk

Low — release-script + workflow-comment change only; no product code. WIF/IAM, endpoints, signing, and Stable handling unchanged. The two-stage publish contract and idempotent publication from #16 are preserved.

author: alexey-milovidov
body:
Closes #892.

Adds a **Dask** entry. Dask is "pandas in parallel", so this mirrors the existing pandas port: a small FastAPI server wraps a Dask DataFrame behind the standard `install`/`start`/`check`/`stop`/`load`/`query`/`data-size` interface, and `queries.sql` holds one Python expression per line that the server `eval()`s — exactly the pattern used by `pandas` and `polars-dataframe`.

### Design
- **Parallelism**: a `dask.distributed.LocalCluster` of worker processes gives real multi-core execution. The frame is `persist()`ed into cluster memory (and `wait()`ed on) so load time is comparable to the pandas/polars in-memory model. `BENCH_DURABLE=no`, so the harness reloads before each cold query and rolls that into the cold try, as with the other in-memory dataframe systems.
- **Dataset**: reads the partitioned parquet (`hits_0..99.parquet`) — one partition per file is Dask's natural layout (`BENCH_DOWNLOAD_SCRIPT=download-hits-parquet-partitioned`).
- **Lazy execution**: the server materialises each result with `dask.compute()` and times `eval()` + `compute()` together (mirroring pandas, where `eval()` does all the work). `dask.compute()` recurses into tuples/lists, so the tuple queries (3, 7) and the 90-sum query (30) compute in one pass.

### Query translation
Queries stay close to the pandas port, diverging only where Dask's API does:
- **Q10, Q23** (`COUNT(DISTINCT)` alongside other aggregates): Dask's built-in `groupby.agg` has no `nunique`, so these use Dask's [documented custom `nunique` aggregation](https://docs.dask.org/en/stable/dataframe-groupby.html#aggregate).
- **Q39–Q43** (`LIMIT … OFFSET`): Dask has no positional `iloc`, so these take the small top-N with `nlargest` and slice in pandas after `compute()` (SQL-faithful, matching how `polars-dataframe` does it — not the pandas port's `nlargest(10).iloc[1000:]` quirk that returns empty).
- **Q8, Q26, Q27**: Dask `Series` has no `sort_values`, so these use `nlargest` / frame `sort_values`.

### Validation
All 43 queries were validated against a synthetic dataset under both the threaded scheduler and a real distributed `LocalCluster`, and end-to-end through the HTTP server. Verified that cluster teardown on shutdown leaves **no orphaned worker processes** across the harness's repeated stop/start/reload cycles. Real timings still need a run on a benchmark machine (aarch64 dev box can't produce the x86 result set).

## Summary

Implements #131 — `CHANGELOG.md` (Keep a Changelog 1.1) plus an in-app "What's new" changelog view.

**Part 1 — repo files**
- Repo-root `CHANGELOG.md` following Keep a Changelog 1.1 + SemVer, backfilled v0.1.0 … v0.3.0 (user-relevant entries with issue/PR refs, comparison links at the bottom) and an `[Unreleased]` section that already covers the pending develop features — including this one.
- CLAUDE.md branching section gains the changelog release ritual: feature PRs with user-visible changes add an `Unreleased` entry; a RELEASE cut rolls `Unreleased` into a new `## [X.Y.Z] - date` section and updates the comparison links.

**Part 2 — app (offline-first, no runtime fetch)**
- The About dialog gains a "What's new" `Disclosure` directly under the #125 version line; the content is the repo-root `CHANGELOG.md` baked into the bundle at build time via a Vite `?raw` static import — never fetched at runtime, so it works fully offline and always describes the exact bundle it ships in. `server.fs.allow` in `vite.config.ts` adds the repo root (a strict superset of the default Vite root) so the dev server can serve the out-of-root file.
- `app/src/lib/changelog.ts`: small dedicated parser for the constrained KaC subset (`## [version] - date`, `### Category`, `- entry`, link-reference block) — no new markdown dependency; output is plain structured-clone-safe data. Wrapped continuation lines are joined, never dropped.
- `ChangelogView` renders versions newest-first with date, category headings, and entries as plain text — "(#N)" refs deliberately stay text, not links (offline honesty). A one-line i18n'd note states the changelog is maintained in English; empty sections (e.g. `[Unreleased]` right after a release cut) are hidden.
- i18n: `about.changelog.title` / `about.changelog.langNote` in both dicts (`satisfies` parity); changelog content itself stays English by design.

## Verification

- `npm --prefix app run typecheck` — clean
- `npm --prefix app run lint` — clean
- Full `npm --prefix app run test` — 79 files, 807 tests, all pass (includes 13 new: parser unit tests with hand-pinned literal expectations + a guard parsing the real committed CHANGELOG.md, ChangelogView component tests, AboutDialog disclosure test)
- `npm --prefix app run build` — clean; changelog content verified inlined in the emitted bundle
- Real-browser pass (dev server, non-4173 port): About → "Was ist neu" renders all six sections with categories/entries in both light and dark themes; dev `?raw` serving confirmed working

Closes #131

body:
## Summary

- Gate external datastores, non-local vaults, and `swamp serve` (token/oauth modes) behind a swamp-club.com account
- Collective tokens (`swamp_org_` prefix) must carry the appropriate scope (`datastore:*`, `vault:*`, `serve:*`); personal tokens get full access
- Collective tokens with unknown scopes (cache miss / failed whoami) fail closed rather than granting access
- Persist token scopes in `auth.json` via `saveIdentityCache()` so scope checks work without an extra API call
- Render `UserError` directly to stderr instead of through LogTape for cleaner multi-line error output
- Error messages are prescriptive: they name the required scope and point to `swamp-club.com/collectives` for token creation

### What's NOT gated
- `local_encryption` vaults — the "hello world" for secrets, no account needed
- `swamp serve --auth-mode none` — deprecated mode, if you're brave enough to run it unsecured we let you
- `swamp worker token create` / `swamp worker connect` — workers are downstream of serve, already authenticated via the serve → swamp-club chain

## Test plan
- [x] No auth + external datastore → blocks with auth_required error naming `datastore:*` scope
- [x] No auth + non-local vault → blocks with auth_required error naming `vault:*` scope
- [x] No auth + local_encryption vault → passes (no gate)
- [x] No auth + serve token mode → blocks with auth_required error naming `serve:*` scope
- [x] No auth + serve none mode → passes (no gate, deprecated warning shown)
- [x] Personal token + serve token mode → passes both auth and scope checks
- [x] Collective token with `serve:*` scope → passes both checks
- [x] Collective token without `serve:*` scope → blocks with missing_scope error
- [x] Collective token with no cached scopes (cache miss) → blocks (fail closed)
- [x] 55 unit tests pass (auth_context, error_output, auth_repository)

author: migao2006
body:
## What changed

- Persist a strict, sanitized import result artifact that distinguishes source-date misalignment from permanent failures.
- Add a privileged `workflow_run` controller that creates or updates one deterministic GitHub Issue, closes it after recovery, and requests only bounded full workflow reruns.
- Retry only trusted current-`main` failures with verified transient evidence; stale, cancelled, permanent, unverified, mixed, or state-changing runs remain fail-closed.
- Qualify every Daily Research artifact by `github.run_attempt` so immutable artifacts cannot be overwritten or mixed across rerun attempts.
- Give immutable stored-snapshot publication a 60-second Data API timeout plus at most three whole-publish replays, only for `SUPABASE_CONNECTION_ERROR`; all other failures remain fail-closed.
- Treat a Production market as current only when its latest run, stock rows, summary counts, venue/status contracts, and all eight decision gates per prediction are complete. Incomplete latest-dated runs are selected for repair.
- Give the read-only Production resolver the same bounded connection-error retry without changing date, ranking, horizon, market, or point-in-time rules.

## Why

The import workflow already retried TWSE/TPEx date mismatch inside one job, but exhausted retries existed only in Actions logs and no later import was launched. Daily Research failures likewise had no durable report or bounded workflow-level recovery. A full rerun was not safe until every cross-job artifact was isolated by run attempt.

Production evidence also exposed a second failure chain: TWSE Data API reads repeatedly stalled at the original 30-second client timeout. One attempt committed the 2026-07-20 run and 1,068 predictions but stopped before its 8,544 decision gates. The public API correctly rejected that invalid snapshot, while the old resolver incorrectly treated the mere run date as current and would no-op forever.

Recovery mode is `RECONCILE_LATEST_VALID`: it reruns the validated resolver and never substitutes the calendar date, forces a snapshot date, weakens validation, or changes ranking, decision, venue, asset, point-in-time, or horizon semantics.

## Recovery policy

- Import mismatch: four existing in-job checks, then at most one delayed full workflow rerun (`run_attempt <= 2`).
- Daily timeout: at most two delayed full workflow reruns (`run_attempt <= 3`).
- Daily failure: rerun only when every failed job in the exact attempt is one of the supported feature/Production stages and every stage has a unique, bounded, attempt-qualified artifact with a strict failure schema and the sole reason `SUPABASE_CONNECTION_ERROR`.
- Stored immutable publish: at most three attempts with 1/2-second backoff, only for the same connection reason. Every attempt recreates the writer and replays the same prevalidated, hash-locked snapshot through idempotent RPC/upsert contracts.
- Resolver reads: at most three attempts with 1/2-second backoff, only for the same connection reason. Contract/validation failures do not retry.
- Unknown jobs, missing/duplicate/multi-file/invalid artifacts, mixed transient/permanent failures, and all non-allowlisted reasons are report-only and never rerun.
- Reports are sanitized and deduplicated; success closes the report, while exhaustion or non-retryable failure remains visible.
- Workflow identity, path, repository, head repository, event, branch, run state, attempt, and current default-branch SHA are revalidated server-side before any write.

## Validation

- Combined focused recovery, resolver, publication, workflow, ingestion, and snapshot tests: 128 passed.
- Ruff: passed.
- basedpyright: 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- actionlint: passed for all three affected workflows.
- Immutable Action pin and Python lock checks: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fast verification: passed.
- Full verification: 1,086 Python tests and 66 Playwright tests passed.
- Independent read-only reviews: no BLOCKER, HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW findings after repair.
- PR head Project tests, Test gate, frontend/browser tests, quality/security, and Vercel: passed.

## Production evidence

Current `main` resolved the newest aligned research date as `2026-07-20`; live `2026-07-23` sources were not a valid joint session (TWSE `2026-07-22`, TPEx `2026-07-23`). Both feature builds, both security-catalog exports, both Staging identity syncs, inference publications, manifests, and release verifications passed. TPEx Production advanced to `2026-07-20`.

TWSE Production then failed twice at the 30-second REST read boundary. Database evidence showed run 11 at `2026-07-20` with 1,068 predictions and zero decision gates; the API rejected it as `RESEARCH_DECISION_GATE_ATTACHMENT_INCOMPLETE`. Feature-branch reconciliation run [30033947665](https://github.com/migao2006/tool/actions/runs/30033947665) used exact head `94013ba` without a forced date and proved the fixed resolver selects only TWSE: aligned date `2026-07-20`, TPEx latest valid `2026-07-20`, TWSE latest valid `null`, `should_run=true`. The complete TWSE current-bars, feature, catalog, Staging, Production, and verification path then succeeded. Production run 12 contains 1,068 predictions and all 8,544 decision gates. Both live TWSE and TPEx APIs now return `as_of_date=2026-07-20`, `decision_at=2026-07-20T17:00:00+08:00`, horizon 5, `RESEARCH_ONLY`, and `Cache-Control: no-store,max-age=0`. Deployed GitHub Pages source renders the validated snapshot fields and calls the API with `cache: "no-store"`; it does not substitute the calendar date.

author: bjliefers
body:
# Enface segmentation projection — PR summary

## Summary

Live **B-scan → enface segmentation projection** for OCT volumes.
Drawing, undo/redo, and slice loads incrementally update client-side GPU thickness textures; the top-row enface viewer renders them in **mask** or **heatmap** mode.

Supports **Binary**, **DualBitMask**, **Probability**, **MultiClass**, and **MultiLabel** segmentations. MC/ML get one R8 thickness texture per drawable subfeature layer, with visibility, opacity, and hover highlight mirroring the B-scan panel.

## How it works

- **`EnfaceProjection`** — GPU projection into per-layer R8 textures (one row per B-scan)
- **`EnfaceProjectionManager`** — attach segmentations, `projectAllWhenReady` on init, incremental slice updates on draw/undo/redo
- **`EnfaceProjectionOverlay`** — renders visible layers on the `_proj` top-row viewer
- **Top-row toggle** — cycles off → binary mask → heatmap (default: binary on load)

## Visibility & MC/ML behavior

- Parent segmentation must be shown in the panel (`shownSegmentations`)
- Per-layer eye toggles and active/highlight opacity match B-scan MC/ML shaders
- Hover highlight is scoped to the **hovered segmentation** (not global feature index)
- Background subfeature index **0** is excluded from UI, projection, and bit math

## Refactor & cleanup (same branch)

- Removed dead code: `createEnfaceMask`, legacy layer-thickness enface pipeline (`LayerThicknessEnface`, `LayerBoundaries`, `fs_render_layers_enface`)
- Split helpers: `enfaceProjectionKeys`, `enfaceProjectionVisibility`, `subfeatureBits`
- Consolidated mask projection dispatch; fixed init projection bug (`markGPUCurrent` after FBO writes)
- Heatmap uses **min–max stretch** over foreground pixels per layer

## Docs

- Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-21-enface-projection-design.md`
- Refactor review: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-enface-projection-refactor-design.md`
- Plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-21-enface-projection.md`, `2026-07-23-enface-projection-refactor.md`

## Test plan

- [ ] Open OCT instance; enface shows existing segmentations on load (not only after drawing)
- [ ] Draw / undo / redo on B-scan → corresponding enface row updates
- [ ] Mode cycle: off → binary → heatmap; heatmap uses full min–max range
- [ ] Hide segmentation in panel → removed from enface
- [ ] MC: radio selection, eye toggles, inactive alpha, hover highlight only on hovered segmentation
- [ ] ML: checkbox selection, eye toggles, hover highlight scoped correctly
- [ ] Multiple segmentations on same instance; no cross-segmentation highlight bleed
- [ ] Background (index 0) not listed in subfeature selector

Closes [#128](https://github.com/Eyened/eyened-platform/issues/128) (step 1 — client-side B-scan → enface projection).

author: ghettocyborg
body:
## Problem

Extensions generated from this template do not show up as usable nodes in the Editor.

The example nodes declared their `NodeTypeInfo` namespace as `SWITCHBOARD_NODE_NAMESPACE`, which is **not** a per-extension macro — it's a hardcoded SDK constant:

```cpp
// SwitchboardSDK/include/switchboard_core/NodeTypeInfo.hpp
const std::string SWITCHBOARD_NODE_NAMESPACE = "Switchboard";
```

But the node factory's `getNodeTypePrefix()` returns the extension name (`"ExampleDSP"`), and the namespace declared on a node must match its factory's prefix. They didn't.

**Enumeration path** — `NodeRegistry::registerNode` registers each node under `namespace + "." + type`. With namespace `"Switchboard"`, the nodes register as `Switchboard.ExampleProcessor` etc., lumped in with the built-in SDK nodes and never grouped under the loaded extension.

**Instantiation path** — `SwitchboardObjectFactory::createNode` requires the requested namespace to equal a factory's `getNodeTypePrefix()`, so these nodes can only be created as `ExampleDSP.ExampleProcessor`. The advertised name (`Switchboard.*`) routes to the built-in factory, which has no such node, and returns `nullptr`.

The advertised name can never be instantiated and the instantiable name is never advertised, so generated extensions never usably appear in the Editor.

Shipping extensions (Waveshaper, Sox, …) match namespace to prefix and do not use `SWITCHBOARD_NODE_NAMESPACE`.

## Fix

Use the literal `"ExampleDSP"` string as the node namespace in the three example node headers, matching the factory prefix.

This is **generator-safe**: `scripts/rename.sh` does a literal `ExampleDSP` → project-name substitution across all files, so the node namespace and factory prefix rename in lockstep when a project is generated.

## Testing note

Verified by source trace against the SDK (`NodeRegistry`, `SwitchboardObjectFactory::createNode`, `NodeTypeInfo::getFQTypeName`) and by comparison with working extensions. A follow-up build + Editor smoke test of a generated extension is worth doing before close.

Fixes SWI-6715.

body:
## Summary

Found the actual bug behind lab extraction failing, thanks to the error surfacing added in the last PR — the Files panel showed "AI did not return valid JSON" for the lab report.

Root cause: both `extract-lab.ts` and `generate-draft.ts` called `JSON.parse` directly on Claude's raw response text. The prompts say "reply with ONLY a JSON object, no markdown fences," but models don't always obey that — Claude sometimes wraps JSON output in ` ```json ... ``` ` fences (or adds a stray sentence before/after) anyway, and a strict parse throws immediately on that.

- `lib/ai/parseJson.ts` strips a wrapping code fence if present, and as a last resort extracts the outermost `{...}` substring, before parsing
- Verified against fenced/unfenced/leading-prose/trailing-prose response shapes — all parse correctly
- Confirmed genuinely invalid input (e.g. a refusal message) still throws rather than silently returning garbage
- Applied to both `extract-lab.ts` (this was the confirmed failure) and `generate-draft.ts` (same exact risk, same fix)

El ticket estaba "Finalizada" y con razón: el ratchet (scrum113-migracion- fixtures.test.mjs) es sólido, withMerchant garantiza el registro antes de cualquier fallo de montaje, y la limpieza aislada por operación con reintento está probada con fault injection. Pero registrarBarridoFinal — la garantía nº3, "un after() global barre lo que quede vivo al terminar el fichero" — estaba escrita, documentada en el propio encabezado del fichero como una de las TRES garantías, y CERO ficheros la llamaban. Tampoco tenía test.

Fix: withMerchant activa registrarBarridoFinal sola en su primer uso por fichero (flag de módulo, sin llamada aparte posible de olvidar). Se extrae barridoFinal() de registrarBarridoFinal() para poder probar la barrida en sí sin esperar a que un proceso de verdad termine, y `after` pasa a ir por parámetro (mismo patrón que `prisma`) para poder inyectar un doble y probar que el REGISTRO ocurre. 4 tests nuevos: la barrida limpia huérfanos, no toca nada si no hay huérfanos, registrarBarridoFinal ata el callback al after() recibido, y withMerchant activa la red UNA sola vez por fichero (un segundo withMerchant no debe registrar un after() adicional).

Verificado contra staging real con ficheros ya migrados (scrum49 con dos merchants anidados A/B, scrum94): 0 huérfanos, la red activada queda en silencio cuando no hace falta, exactamente el comportamiento esperado.

author: haultraaisystems
body:
The empty-can correction buttons registered the tap (a timestamped note line was written) but showed nothing, so drivers tapped repeatedly thinking it was broken.

## What changed

**1. Selected state (visible on load, not just after tapping)**
- The active choice renders with a **solid orange fill + checkmark** ("✓ Carry to next"); the other two dim to ~72% opacity. This is server-rendered from the stop's current `empty_can_plan`, so it's correct the moment the card loads.

**2. Instant optimistic feedback**
- The picker is now JS buttons (was three full-page POST forms). A tap flips the selection **immediately (<100ms)**; the sync `fetch` runs in the background.
- On failure it **reverts** the selection and shows a small **"couldn't save — tap to retry"** toast. No silent dead tap.
- Works on weak signal: the UI never waits on the network.
- A plain-form fallback still works if JS is unavailable (endpoint redirects).

**3. Tapping the already-selected option does nothing**
- Guarded client-side (no fetch fired) *and* server-side (no note written). `changed:false` comes back.

**4. Note dedupe / replace**
- Switching the choice **replaces** the empty-can note line — one clean line reflecting the current choice — instead of stacking a new line per tap.
- Any pre-existing **stack** of empty-can lines on a stop is collapsed to the latest on the next interaction (`_collapse_empty_can_notes`), while human-written notes are always preserved (`_strip_empty_can_notes`).
- The endpoint returns JSON to `fetch` callers and a redirect to plain form posts.

## Verify (19/19 pass)

Flask `test_client` + temp SQLite:
- **Helpers:** collapse keeps exactly one (latest) empty-can line + human note; strip removes all empty-can lines, keeps human note.
- **Selected state on load:** active pill is a `<button>` with `✓` and `aria-pressed="true"`; non-active pills have no `✓` and `aria-pressed="false"`; optimistic `fetch` + `X-Requested-With` wiring present; picker uses buttons, not per-option forms.
- **Switch:** returns `{ok, changed:true}`, persists the plan, leaves exactly **one** empty-can note line, preserves the human note.
- **Re-tap same plan:** returns `changed:false`, adds **no** new note line.

author: dobby-coder[bot]
body:
Closes #110

## What

`retrieveUSKViaYivi` in `src/yivi/decrypt-session.ts` always waited a hardcoded 500 ms `setTimeout` before handing the host element to yivi-core, with the comment "Small delay to ensure DOM element is ready". That fixed delay ran on every decrypt session even when the element was already mounted.

This replaces it with `waitForElement`, which resolves as soon as the target element is present in the DOM. When the element is already there it resolves on the same tick, so the session starts immediately. When it is not yet mounted, a `MutationObserver` watches for it, with a bounded 5 s fallback timeout so a never-appearing element can't hang the session. This mirrors the signing flow (`src/signing/yivi.ts`), which builds `YiviCore` with no delay at all.

## Tests

Added a `waitForElement` regression suite to `tests/decrypt-session.test.ts` covering:
- resolves immediately in a non-DOM environment;
- resolves without any fixed delay when the element is already present (fails if a `setTimeout` is reintroduced on the ready path — verified against the old code);
- resolves as soon as the element appears via the observer, not before;
- falls back to the bounded timeout if the element never appears.

Full suite (`npm test`) and `npm run typecheck` pass.

author: maxusmusti
body:
Closes the three critical UX issues with `lidwatch watch --lid-close`:

## Changes

- **BUG 1 — Password shown in clear text:** Added `runInteractive()` method to `CommandRunning` protocol that connects Process stdin/stdout/stderr directly to terminal FileHandles. When `useSudo` is true, `enable()`/`disable()` now use this method instead of `SystemCommandRunner.run()` which piped stdout/stderr via `Pipe()`, disconnecting sudo from the terminal and preventing secure password input.

- **BUG 2 — No confirmation after success:** After enabling lid-close prevention, the watch command now verifies the state actually changed via `isEnabled` and prints `✓ Lid-close prevention is ON — safe to close your lid`. If the command succeeded but pmset state didn't change, prints an error.

- **BUG 3 — Ctrl+C doesn't clean up:** Added a file-level `_watchLidCloseActive` flag that stays in sync with the local `lidCloseActive` state. SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers check this flag and run `sudo pmset -a disablesleep 0` (with terminal-connected I/O) before exiting. Also covers the SIGTERM path.

- `Sources/LidwatchCore/LidCloseManager.swift` — protocol change + interactive runner
- `Sources/lidwatch/WatchCommand.swift` — signal handler cleanup + confirmation
- `Tests/LidwatchCoreTests/LidCloseManagerTests.swift` — test mock updated for new protocol method

author: dillon-kn
body:
## Root cause of the credit drain

The 400s in Slack turned out to be **"Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API"** (confirmed via run [30044938826](https://github.com/nicole-e-s/plan-a-monitor/actions/runs/30044938826) after #1 made the monitor surface the API's error body).

Credits drained because classification runs *before* the seen-ids dedup (aggregate counting needs labels on already-seen posts too), and fetch windows roll — so the same ~15 posts were re-classified with Sonnet 5 + Opus 4.8 (with thinking) every 5-minute run, ~288×/day, since the Jul 9 model upgrade.

## Fix

- `ai_labels.json` caches final (post-escalation) labels by `platform:id`; cached items skip both AI passes, so each post is paid for exactly once
- Keyword-fallback labels from an outage are **not** cached — posts get real AI labels once the API is back up
- Human re-tags also overwrite matching cache entries, so corrections can't be resurrected by the cache
- Cache capped at 20k entries and persisted by the workflow's state step

Tested with a stubbed API: repeat runs make zero API calls; mixed cached/new runs classify only the new item; failures aren't cached; recovery re-labels.

⚠️ **Credits still need topping up** — that part I can't do. Until then the monitor runs on keyword fallback.

author: slashdevcorpse
body: ## Summary - retry same-target post-update version probes for up to five seconds when an exit-zero updater initially reports the exact pre-update version - keep retry sleeps interruptible under the existing provider-update timeout and leave command preparation, Windows Job ownership, and update authorization unchanged - cover delayed native Droid self-replacement, bounded retries, and immediate short-circuits for success, unavailable binaries, target drift, downgrades, and missing pre-update evidence ## Windows evidence The installed Super Synara 0.5.5-super.14 flow launched `droid.exe update` through `synara-windows-job-launcher`, but the immediate probe still returned 0.174.0 while the binary became 0.178.0 a few seconds later. The new Windows integration fixture reproduces that sequence and verifies: - one update command - Job-launcher preparation - no `cmd.exe` in the prepared invocation - 0.174.0 on the immediate post-update probe - 0.178.0 on the bounded retry - final `succeeded` state with `Provider CLI update verified.` ## Safety - manual-only provider capability resolution is untouched (including Codex, OpenCode, and Command Code protections) - updater spawning and Windows Job supervision are untouched - timeout/cancellation still interrupts the update fiber and its Effect-native sleeps - target/settings evidence is re-read around every retry probe; drift stops retries and remains unverified - provider configuration files are never written by this path ## Validation - `bun run --cwd apps/server test -- src/provider/providerUpdateVerification.test.ts` (3 passed) - `bun run --cwd apps/server test -- src/provider/Layers/ProviderHealth.test.ts -t "waits for a delayed native Droid replacement"` (1 passed, 145 skipped) - `bun run --cwd apps/server test -- src/provider/providerUpdateOutcome.test.ts` (4 passed) - targeted `oxfmt --check` on the four changed files - `git diff --check` Base: `724b89f84687206a8caae2d3b42f0a48ce611fcc` --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes Windows provider updates by retrying post-update version checks to catch delayed self-replacements (e.g., `droid.exe`) and verify the new version within ~5 seconds. Keeps existing timeouts, authorization, and Windows Job containment unchanged. - **Bug Fixes** - Added `providerUpdateVerification.ts`: bounded, interruptible retries (250ms, 750ms, 1.5s, 2.5s) only when the immediate probe matches the pre-update version, the target hasn’t changed, and the binary is available. - Integrated into `ProviderHealth`: re-reads settings/evidence each probe; stops on success, unavailability, downgrade, or drift; preserves verification effect errors; leaves process preparation and spawning unchanged. - Tests: new unit tests plus a Windows integration test that reproduces delayed `droid.exe` replacement (0.174.0 → 0.178.0); confirms one update spawn, no `cmd.exe`, and a final “Provider CLI update verified.” state. Written for commit 18ad5ccde35e6d00b126141478ac22518cdd6da4. Summary will update on new commits.

author: rayair250-droid
body:
Closes #551.

## Summary

Adds `element_counts(mol)` to `skfp.descriptors.constitutional`, returning a vector of atom counts across all elements of the RDKit periodic table — useful as fingerprint features or for composition analysis, as requested in #551.

## Details

- Returns a length-118 `np.ndarray` indexed by atomic number: position `i` holds the count of the element with atomic number `i + 1` (index 0 = hydrogen, index 5 = carbon, …).
- Hydrogens are counted in total (explicit + implicit), **consistently with the existing `element_atom_count`** — the H bucket is filled by delegating to `element_atom_count(mol, 1)`, so the two functions never disagree.
- Exported from `skfp.descriptors`, added to `docs/modules/descriptors.rst`, and covered by parametrized tests (per-element counts, consistency with `element_atom_count`, absent-element zeros and total sum).

```python
>>> from rdkit.Chem import MolFromSmiles
>>> from skfp.descriptors import element_counts
>>> counts = element_counts(MolFromSmiles("CCO"))  # ethanol
>>> int(counts[5]), int(counts[7]), int(counts[0])  # C, O, H
(2, 1, 6)
```

## Notes

- Doctests use `int(counts[i])` because NumPy 2.x scalars repr as `np.int64(6)`; wrapping keeps the doctest output stable across NumPy versions.
- Happy to switch the return type to a dict keyed by symbol/atomic number instead of a fixed-length vector if you prefer that API — the issue said "vector", so I went literal.

author: gokhankizikli1-ai
body:
## What this is

A post-generation, **advisory** evaluation of the **rendered** page that **reuses** the existing quality pipeline, Experience Architecture and static Visual Evaluation. It is **not** a new generation system and **not** a new repair system — its findings feed the **existing** bounded repair.

## Inspection → reuse (no duplication)

- **`runFrontendBuilderQualityPipeline`** — the single shared quality pipeline; I add **one** flag-gated step, not a new pipeline.
- **`mergeDeterministicIssues` + `recomputeReviewWithMergedIssues`** — the existing mechanism that injects non-model issues into the initial review so the **existing** repair addresses them.
- **`evaluateVisualQuality` (#513)** — refactored to expose a flag-independent `computeVisualEvaluation` core that the rendered layer reuses for source-derived dimensions (no flag coupling, no duplicated logic).

## The artifact

```ts
RenderedVisualEvaluationArtifact {
  score: number
  passed: boolean
  issues: RenderedVisualIssue[]   // { code, dimension, severity, message, suggestion }
  screenshotReviewed: boolean
  runtimeReviewed: boolean
}
```

## The evaluator (`evaluateRenderedVisual`)

Consumes: **caller-captured screenshot metadata** (`viewport`, width/height, `blank`, `horizontalOverflow`, `whitespaceRatio`, `contentHeight`) + the build artifacts + the `ExperienceArchitecturePlan`. It evaluates eight dimensions — **composition, spacing, typography, hero impact, CTA visibility, template patterns, visual uniqueness, mobile readiness** — by combining the caller's measured signals with the reused static evaluation.

**No unnecessary model call:** the screenshot **image is never sent anywhere** — only the caller's measured signals are used. **Fail-open:** any problem returns a safe non-blocking artifact (`passed:true`, no issues).

## Integration with the existing repair (`webBuildFrontendQuality.ts`)

- New **optional** `opts.renderedVisualInput`. When the flag is on **and** the caller supplies it, after the initial review the evaluator runs and its **HIGH** findings are mapped to existing review categories (`major` → drives the existing repair; others advisory) and **merged by new category only** into `initialReview` — so the **single existing bounded repair** addresses them. **No new repair system, no extra model call.**
- The artifact is surfaced on accepted/repaired outcomes (`acceptance.renderedVisualEvaluation`).
- **Flag off or no input ⇒ the pipeline is byte-for-byte unchanged.**

## Preserved

- Existing feature flags; existing fail-open behavior.
- **Existing acceptance artifacts** — `renderedVisualTestStatus` stays `'pending-manual-test'` (an automated advisory review is not a manual certification); only an optional `renderedVisualEvaluation` field is added.
- No unnecessary model calls.

## Changed files

- `src/lib/webBuildVisualEvaluation.ts` — extract flag-independent `computeVisualEvaluation` (reuse).
- `src/lib/webBuildAgents.ts` — the rendered types + optional `renderedVisualEvaluation` on the acceptance artifact.
- `src/lib/webBuildRenderedVisualEvaluation.ts` (new) — the evaluator + flag + review-issue adapter.
- `src/lib/webBuildFrontendQuality.ts` — optional `renderedVisualInput` + one flag-gated merge into the existing repair + artifact surfacing.

## Validation

- ✅ **14 vitest tests pass** (`webBuildRenderedVisualEvaluation.test.ts`): **successful evaluation**, mobile-overflow / blank / static-reuse detection, **empty-screenshot handling**, **evaluator failure fallback** (never throws), **repair integration** adapter (HIGH→major, category dedup).
- ✅ The reused static suite + all #509–#515 suites still pass (**127 experience/evaluation tests total**); **`tsc -b` clean** (0 errors).
- ✅ The 4 failing `webBuildFiles`/`webBuildBrief` tests are **pre-existing** (unchanged, internal template-synthesizer — untouched here).
- ✅ **No model calls added**, screenshot image never transmitted. Diff scoped to `src/lib`; **no** backend / billing / auth / DB / deployment / builder-UI changes.

## Deployment

New frontend env var **`VITE_ENABLE_RENDERED_VISUAL_EVAL`** (default `false`). No updated/removed vars, no new dependencies, no backend/DB/schema changes, no Railway/Vercel/Docker changes. **Breaking changes:** none. **Rollback:** revert the commit (additive + flag-gated). Note: the pipeline consumes rendered findings only when the caller passes `opts.renderedVisualInput` (a screenshot-capture producer) — a natural follow-up wires that capture in the WebsiteBuilder runtime.

Do **not** merge automatically.

author: srbino
body:
## Problem

The three scheduling loops — the **agent cron scheduler** (`internal/scheduler`), the **pipeline/routine cron scheduler** (`internal/pipeline/schedules.go`), and the **recurring-issue dispatcher** (`internal/api/recurring_issue_dispatcher.go`) — were all written single-instance. Two replicas against one database would each tick and both fire, double-running scheduled agents and double-stamping recurring issues. Exactly-once until now rested **only** on the per-occurrence idempotency table.

## What this adds

A minimal, DB-backed **leader-election lease** in a new `internal/leader` package. One `scheduler_leader` row (new migration **v149**) gates all three loops so a multi-replica deploy fires each due occurrence on exactly one replica; per-occurrence idempotency stays as a second line of defence.

**Mechanism**
- Acquisition is one atomic upsert whose `ON CONFLICT(scope) DO UPDATE ... WHERE expires_at <= now OR holder = me` only lets a contender take a **free/expired** row. SQLite serialises the write, so two replicas racing a free row cannot both win. Portable to Postgres (same upsert-with-WHERE).
- **Clocks (consistent):** arbitration between replicas uses ONE clock — the **database's** (`strftime('%s','now')`, unix-second integers) — so host wall-clock skew can't double-elect. The `IsLeader()` freshness gate uses the **local monotonic** clock, so leadership lapses within one TTL if renewals stop even while the stale DB row lingers.
- **Intervals (documented):** TTL **60s**, renew every **20s** (renew ≈ TTL/3 → two missed renewals of headroom). A lone replica wins the lease **synchronously in `Start()`**, so single-instance behaviour is unchanged.
- No new infra dependency (no etcd/consul/redis) — the lease lives in the DB the schedulers already hold.

**Wiring**
- Each scheduler gains `SetLeaderGate(leader.Gate)`; a **nil gate = always-fire** (the prior single-instance behaviour, so every existing test call site is untouched).
- `cmd_start` constructs one shared lease and attaches it to all three loops. **Enabled by default**; opt-out via `CREWSHIP_SCHEDULER_LEADER_ELECTION=0`. `CREWSHIP_REPLICA_ID` sets a stable holder identity (else random).

## Tests (red-first)

`internal/leader/lease_test.go`: acquire-when-free, renew-while-held (expiry advances, `acquired_at` preserved), second-contender-blocked-until-expiry, expired-lease-stealable, lone-replica-wins-immediately, gate-expires-without-renewal, and the #1376 acceptance check — **two `Lease` instances against one DB → exactly one is leader**. Written failing first, then implemented to green.

## Docs

New "Running multiple replicas (leader election)" section in `docs/guides/scheduling.mdx` covering the mechanism, failover timing, the single-writer requirement when disabled, and both env knobs.

## Deploy note

New migration v149 adds the `scheduler_leader` table (instance-local runtime state — not workspace-scoped, so no `BackupTableIntent` entry, never in a backup bundle). **Dev needs nuke+reseed.**

Refs #1376

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
### Features
- Added DB-backed scheduler leader election via a single-row `scheduler_leader` lease with atomic UPSERT acquisition and periodic renewal.
- Enabled leader-gated execution for the agent cron scheduler, pipeline/routine scheduler, and recurring-issue dispatcher (on by default; opt out with `CREWSHIP_SCHEDULER_LEADER_ELECTION=0`).
- Wired leader election across schedulers in `cmd_start`, including optional stable holder identity via `CREWSHIP_REPLICA_ID`.

### Bug Fixes
- Prevents duplicate scheduled execution (and related recurring-issue side effects) across replicas, with failover driven by lease expiry and freshness.

### Breaking Changes
- Development databases require a nuke-and-reseed after applying the new `scheduler_leader` migration.

### Refactoring
- Introduced `internal/leader` (lease/store/gate) and `SetLeaderGate` plumbing to preserve existing single-instance behavior when leader gating is not enabled.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: robobun
body:
## What

`Bun.build()` and `new Bun.Transpiler()` leak the per-call transpiler and AST allocator state when option setup fails before the bundle runs.

## Repro

```sh
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 bun-debug -e '
  try { await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ["e.js"], define: { X: "{\"a\":" } }); } catch {}
'
# SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 5451 byte(s) leaked in 202 allocation(s).

ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 bun-debug -e '
  try { new Bun.Transpiler({ define: { X: "{\"a\":" } }); } catch {}
'
# SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 1004 byte(s) leaked in 6 allocation(s).
```

Every failed call leaks; a loop that retries a bad config grows unbounded.

## Cause

`BundleThread::generate_in_new_thread` owned its `ASTMemoryAllocator` via `bump.alloc(...)` + explicit `push()`/`pop()`/`drop_in_place`, which only ran on the straight-line path. When `create_and_configure_transpiler` erred (invalid `define` reaches `configure_defines` inside `configure_bundler`), the `?` returned before any of that teardown. The per-build `Arena` bulk-free reclaims the struct bytes but never runs `Drop`, so the transpiler's owned `Vec`/`Box`/`HashMap` fields (options, resolver opts, loaders, ...) and the AST allocator's pooled `mi_heap` leaked, and the AST-alloc thread-locals were left pointing at freed arena bytes.

Inside `create_and_configure_transpiler`, `configure_bundler(...)?` has the same shape: the transpiler is already `bump.alloc`'d but not `drop_in_place`'d on Err.

`new Bun.Transpiler()` hits a separate stale-pointer write: `Transpiler::set_log` re-points `self.log`, `linker.log` and `resolver.log` but not `options.log`. The constructor builds `config` on the stack, passes `&raw mut config.log` to `Transpiler::init` (which stores it in all four log pointers), moves `config` into the `Box<JSTranspiler>`, then calls `set_log` to reseat the log at the heap-stable address. `options.log` stays at the moved-from stack slot, so `configure_defines` writes the parse error there; the `Msg` is never freed and the thrown error loses the real diagnostic (generic `"ParserError Failed to load define"` instead of the JSON parser message with position).

## Fix

- `src/bundler/BundleThread.rs`: own the `ASTMemoryAllocator` on the stack with an `enter()` `Scope` guard (same as `RuntimeTranspilerStore`/`JSTranspiler` already do), so `Scope::drop` and `ASTMemoryAllocator::drop` run on every return path. The `bump.alloc` here was a Zig-port artifact (`new()` ignores its arena arg). Deletes one `drop_in_place` block and keeps `?`.
- `src/runtime/api/js_bundle_completion_task.rs`: on `configure_bundler` Err, `drop_in_place` the bump-allocated transpiler before returning (it must stay in `bump` since the trait returns `&'a mut Transpiler<'a>`).
- `src/bundler/transpiler.rs`: `set_log` also reseats `options.log` so all four aliased log pointers agree (matches `wire_after_move`).

## Verification

- `test/bundler/transpiler/transpiler.test.js`: new non-gated test asserting `new Bun.Transpiler({ define: { X: '{"a":' } })` throws with `"Unexpected end of file"` and the full `position` (was `"ParserError Failed to load define"` with no position).
- `test/bundler/bun-build-api.test.ts`: new `test.skipIf(!isASAN)` spawns the repro with `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1` for 1 and 21 iterations and asserts the leaked-byte delta is under 4 KB. Without the fix the 20 extra iterations leak ~447 KB; with it the delta is ~190 B (GC-owned `BuildMessage` wrappers LSan cannot trace).

Also ran `test/bundler/transpiler/transpiler.test.js`, `test/js/bun/transpiler/`, `test/js/web/workers/worker.test.ts`, and the sourcemap-leak / thousands-of-builds tests in `bun-build-api.test.ts`.

#35309 adds a `leak:generate_in_new_thread` suppression for this; with this fix that suppression is not needed.

<!-- robobun:evidence:begin -->

---

**no test proof** · iteration 1 · Platform-specific test(s) that do not run on this machine. Deferring to CI, which covers all platforms: test/bundler/bun-build-api.test.ts

<!-- robobun:evidence:end -->

<!-- Use "Fixes" to automatically close issue upon PR merge. Use "Work for" when UAT is required. -->
Work for #9549 

## Changes proposed

<!-- What was added, updated, or removed in this PR. -->

* Updates new relic to version 14, in the process resolving a bunch of vulnerabilities that were patched with manual sub-dependency overrides
* Updates frontend Dockerfile with some procedural and formatting improvements
* Updates .nvmrc to bump local node version
* Adds `make` tasks to make setting up a local "production-like" dockerized environment easier
* Fixes two new vulnerabilities (next and postcss)
* Removes a number of subdependency overrides from package.json, which are no longer necessary for addressing vulns when using NR 14

## Context for reviewers

<!-- Technical or background context, more in-depth details of the implementation, and anything else you'd like reviewers to know about that will help them understand the changes in the PR. -->

These changes may seem unrelated, but most have to do with supporting the upgrade to New Relic 14.

* Dockerfile updates
  * when running the app with NR 14 through a production docker container, I initially ran into an error related to the meriyah mjs file going missing from the build, but this was fixed by extending the base image to create the release image in the Dockerfile likely because in the existing setup the prune function was running out of sync with the npm dependency install. 
* Makefile / docker compose update
  * since we saw errors with New Relic last time we attempted to upgrade, but only once we dockerized for production, I wanted to test the production docker image locally. There was no easy way to do this using the existing docker-compose setup, so went ahead and fixed that up
* node version bump
  * ran into a bunch of issues with the lockfile getting out of sync when running `npm ci` in Github Actions, which were solved by making sure that the version of npm used to create the lockfile was in sync with the version of npm used by the bookworm-slim image within Docker
* postcss version override
  * fixes a vuln from April, not sure why this was not caught before. Probably related to the Dockerfile change
* next version bump
  * this is for fixing a new vuln that appeared while I was working on the branch, including it for ease

3. run `nvm use && npm ci && make build-prod run-prod` on this branch
4. visit http://localhost:3000/search
5. _VERIFY_: app starts and loads data as expected
6. perform a search
7. visit new relic, and view FE dashboard
8. _VERIFY_: a log for your search request appears

author: toastedcoffee
body:
## Problem

The barcode scanner failed silently in Chrome for Android — "Camera access denied or not available" with no permission prompt — even with the browser set to allow camera prompts, no per-site block, and after clearing all site data. It worked in Firefox (mobile and desktop).

## Root cause

`frontend/nginx.conf` sent `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`. `camera=()` allows the camera for **zero origins, including the site itself**. Chrome enforces this strictly and rejects `getUserMedia` immediately with `NotAllowedError` and no prompt. Firefox historically did not enforce the header's `camera` directive for the top-level document, which is why it still prompted there. This also explains why it was invisible to per-site permission state and clearing site data — it's a response header, not stored client state.

## Changes

- **`nginx.conf`**: `camera=()` → `camera=(self)`. The app's own origin can request the camera (browser permission prompt still required); microphone and geolocation stay disabled. This is the actual fix.
- **`BarcodeScanner.tsx`**: harden the failure UX — classify the `getUserMedia` error by name (denied / not found / in use / insecure / unknown) with tailored copy, add "how to allow the camera" steps on permission blocks, surface the raw error name (`Details: …`) so a remote user can read it back for diagnosis, and add a **Try again** button that re-acquires the camera in place.

## Test plan

Ran locally, all green:
- `npm run test` — 63 passed (8 files), including new coverage for the denied / not-found / insecure / retry paths in `BarcodeScanner.test.tsx`
- `npm run type-check` — clean
- `npm run lint` — clean

**Not verified locally** (Docker daemon unavailable in the dev environment):
- The nginx header value. Verify after build with:
  ```
  docker run --rm -d -p 8088:80 <web-image>
  curl -sI http://localhost:8088/ | grep -i permissions-policy
  # expect: Permissions-Policy: camera=(self), microphone=(), geolocation=()
  ```
- End-to-end on the deployed site: because the app sits behind a Cloudflare Tunnel (and Access-gating on the cellar host), a plain `curl` won't reach nginx. Confirm via browser DevTools → Network → document request → Response Headers after the web image is rebuilt and the stack pulls it. If the delivered header still shows `camera=()`, the override is upstream of nginx (check Cloudflare Managed Transforms / Modify Response Header).

author: rebel0789
body:
Fixes #75.

## What changed

- default `read_codex_session` to the newest transcript page while preserving chronological order within the page
- scan JSONL from the head or tail in 64 KiB blocks instead of rejecting files over 20 MB
- add byte-cursor pagination with `next_cursor`, `resume_cursor`, `has_more`, and source-size metadata
- add `exclude_tool_outputs` and strict UTF-8-aware `max_tool_output_bytes` handling
- apply message and byte limits to returned transcript content
- reject cursors beyond a truncated or replaced source file

## Root cause

The previous reader rejected any session JSONL over 20,000,000 bytes and always streamed from the beginning, so long-running sessions could not recover their newest messages.

## Validation

- `npm run build`
- `npm run smoke`
- `npm run stress`
- `git diff --check`

Regression coverage includes a 20.1 MB session, head and tail pagination, append-resume behavior, stale-cursor rejection, UTF-8 byte boundaries, tool-output filtering and caps, and source-file preservation.

author: dingding-leo
body:
## Concrete live defect

PR #356 correctly rejects stale quotes when callers use `bind_execution_quote()`, but the public `ExecutionQuoteBinding` constructor and `from_json_bytes()` replay path did not enforce the binding's own `maximum_age_ms`. A self-consistent binding could therefore record a quote observed 10 seconds before a decision under a 1-second freshness policy, receive a canonical `binding_id`, and survive replay until a later optional reconstruction step.

That is unsafe for paper execution because persisted market-timing evidence should fail closed on its self-contained freshness invariant rather than depend on every downstream caller remembering to reattach the original quote.

## Bounded test-driven fix

- validate `decision_at_utc - quote_observed_at_utc <= maximum_age_ms` inside `ExecutionQuoteBinding.__post_init__`;
- make direct construction and canonical JSON replay reject stale evidence;
- retain strict post-receipt ordering, exact quote/intent reconstruction, content addressing, and separate observed spread evidence.

## Evidence executed

Pre-fix exact Python 3.11 artifact `8578649679` accepted and replayed:

```text
age_ms=10000
maximum_age_ms=1000
stale_binding_accepted=true
replay_equal=true
```

Focused repaired source verification:

```text
python -m py_compile src/gpt_quant/execution_quote_binding.py tests/test_execution_quote_binding.py
PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q tests/test_execution_quote_binding.py
5 passed
```

The test reuses immutable public-OKX evidence hashes already present in PR #356 and creates no market-return or performance result. No credentials, accounts, endpoints or orders are accessed.

The judge-visible half of Epic O (1011101110/kairos-devotional#311): pick a devotional **content language** at signup, see and change it — and the translation — in Settings. Rides O2's preferences write path. The app chrome stays English (#311 decision 5); the language hint says so in as many words: "Your devotionals — Scripture, reflection, and voice — will be in this language. The app itself stays in English."

## What changed

### `packages/shared-contracts/src/language.ts` (additive only)
- **`VERSION_LABELS`** — abbreviation + title for all 24 catalog versionIds. Not written from memory: verified 2026-07-23 against bible.com's canonical version pages (`bible.com/versions/{id}-{abbr}-{slug}`, same numeric id space as the Platform API) and cross-checked with Foundation §4.3's per-language table. One flat map rather than a per-entry field — versionIds are globally unique across languages (already asserted in the test suite), and completeness is enforced by a new test instead of a shape the compiler can't check.
- **`versionDisplayLabel(id)`** → `"Berean Standard Bible (BSB)"` — the exact shape the web UI's one hard-coded option and iOS's `TranslationChoice.displayName` already use. Total: unknown id degrades to `"Version {id}"` rather than throwing (and a test pins that this fallback never shows for any catalog id).

### `apps/web/src/lib/preferences.ts`
- `WebPreferences` gains `language` + `translationId`; both round-trip through `GET`/`PUT /v1/preferences` like every other field (server-authoritative, no client-local state — Epic L ground rule 3).
- **The pair always rides together on PUT.** The server reads a changed `language` arriving alone as "snap `translation_id` to the default", which would silently discard an explicitly chosen alternate. Sending both makes the pair the client renders the pair the server stores.
- **`applyLanguageChange`** — the snap rule, mirrored client-side as one pure transition: a real language change snaps the translation to that language's default (so the O2 cross-language 400 is unreachable from this UI); re-selecting the stored language keeps an explicit alternate (no clobber, same as the server).
- `validate()` repairs an out-of-catalog `translationId` to the language's default. Legacy/corrupt rows only — and deliberately *not* the voice's preserve-verbatim rule, because preserving would 400 the whole save and take the user's other edits down with it.
- `TRADITION_TRANSLATION_NOTE` → `TRADITION_NOTE`: the "no API can change them yet" apology is now false for translation (O2), so the note names only the field it is still true of. Tradition itself stays read-only, unchanged here.

### `apps/web/src/components/PreferencesForm.tsx`
- **Language select** — native-script labels straight from `LANGUAGE_CATALOG` (English, Español, Français, Deutsch, Português, 中文（简体）), catalog order, derived so the picker can never fall a language short of the contract.
- **Translation select enabled** — the disabled hard-coded BSB option retires. Options are only ever the chosen language's catalog, human-readably labeled; changing language re-filters and preselects that language's default.
- Shared form = both surfaces at once: onboarding step 4 (`PreferencesStep`) and Settings render this component verbatim, so language lands in both with no new step and no second differently-shaped control.

## Acceptance mapping (#317)
- Onboarding in Español → PUT carries `language:'es'` + `translationId:3365` (default preselected by the snap) — server stores exactly that pair
- Settings shows stored language; edits persist through the same save-and-re-render-from-response path as every other preference
- Translation options always belong to the selected language; a language switch can never leave a stale cross-language `translationId` selected (`applyLanguageChange` + `validate`, both tested)
- Snap-on-language-change behavior unit-tested; happy-path e2e against the preview API deferred with the existing e2e posture (see notes)

## Tests
- shared-contracts: 148 passed (+4): label completeness over every catalog id, no out-of-catalog labels, display format, unknown-id fallback
- web: 254 passed (+14): six native labels in catalog order; translation options filtered per language with default first and no bare ids; snap on change / no clobber on re-assert; payload carries both fields; fromServer fallbacks (bad tag → en; out-of-catalog id → language default); round trip preserves a non-default pair (fr + Ostervald 131)
- **Mutation-checked** (per the story): dropping `translationId` from the PUT body fails 4 tests; dropping `language` fails 4; removing the snap in `applyLanguageChange` fails 2. All restored, suite green.
- `apps/api` suite: 1155 passed, 0 failed (16 DB-dependent integration files skip-fail on hook timeout locally — no Postgres in this environment; unrelated to this change)

## Notes / deviations
- **Component/e2e tests**: `apps/web` has no component-test harness (vitest is node-env, pure-function tests only; playwright e2e covers the dashboard preview page, which does not render `PreferencesForm`). Followed the repo's established idiom instead: the behavior lives in exported pure functions (`applyLanguageChange`, `translationChoicesFor`, `fromServer`, `toUpdateRequest`) and the component binds them 1:1 — same pattern as cadence/voice. The "happy-path e2e against the preview API" acceptance line is therefore not covered here; flagging for the coordinator rather than half-building a new harness inside this story.
- **Labels live in shared-contracts as a flat map**, not per catalog entry — versionIds are globally unique (asserted), and a flat map + completeness test beats a nested shape the compiler can't verify. Additive; no existing export changed.
- **A11y**: native `<select>`s with real `<label htmlFor>`, hints wired via `aria-describedby`, fieldset legend updated to name all three controls ("Language, tradition, and translation") so the group name stays honest for AT users. No color-only or custom-widget surface added, so the existing axe posture holds.

## What

The `control-slice` scope-note (emitted when `--cutpoint` frees nets to `$anyseq`) claimed a definite HOLDS *"transfers to the concrete RTL (safety + over-approx = sound)"* **unconditionally**. That's a *safety* rule: a cutpoint is a plain over-approximation (adds transitions), sound-transferring for a safety/universal HOLDS but **not** for an **alternating (νμ) recoverability** property (`AG EF good`), which collapses under a plain over-/under-approximation (CLAUDE.md soundness table; Bruns–Godefroid). Surfaced by the i2c `AG EF (wb_ack_o==1)` investigation.

## Fix

The note now states the property-class distinction — safety/universal HOLDS transfers; an alternating HOLDS is sound for the **abstract (cutpointed) model only** (decide those on the un-cutpointed cone). The νμ caveat is appended **only when the report actually carries an alternating property** (`alternation_depth() >= 2`, re-parsed from each property's formula; a parse failure conservatively omits it). The matching API-field doc (`models.rs` `cutpoint`) is updated to the same distinction.

## Validation

- Regression `control_slice_note_gates_holds_transfer_claim_on_property_class` (νμ report ⇒ caveat present; safety-only ⇒ absent).
