author: ecto
body:
## Summary

Documents tessellating to >120k triangles (e.g. large sphere patterns) now receive an actionable error from `render_view` instead of OOM-killing the server. The drafting renderer emits one SVG element per visible triangle, so a ~380k-triangle document serializes to a >100 MB SVG that exhausts memory before the rasterizer can report an error. This change tracks triangle counts from mutation integrity passes and refuses rendering up front.

## Key Changes

- **Triangle budget enforcement**: Added `MAX_RENDER_TRIANGLES = 120_000` constant and pre-render check in `renderView()` that consults the session's last known triangle count (from the most recent mutation's integrity pass). Documents exceeding the budget receive a structured error with actionable hints instead of crashing.

- **SVG byte cap for rasterization**: Added `MAX_RASTER_SVG_BYTES = 64 MB` guard in `rasterize()` to refuse SVGs before they reach resvg, preventing OOM inside the rasterizer itself.

- **Triangle count tracking**: New `recordTriangles()` and `getLastTriangles()` functions in `session-core.ts` store the triangle count from each mutation's integrity evaluation. All mutation entry points (`applyEdits`, `setParameters`, `dispatchRegistryTool`, `loon` macro execution) now call `recordTriangles()` after computing integrity.

- **Graceful degradation on rasterization failure**: When rasterization fails on an SVG too large to inline (>16 MB), `renderView()` now returns a structured error instead of silently omitting the SVG, giving the agent a way forward.

- **Test coverage**: Added `render-triangle-guard.test.ts` with three test cases:
  - Refuses rendering when triangle count exceeds budget
  - Still renders documents under the budget
  - `rasterize()` refuses SVGs beyond the byte cap

## Implementation Details

- Triangle counts are stored per-session in a `Map<string, number>` and cleared when session history is cleared.
- The triangle guard runs before complexity checks, failing fast on known-oversized documents.
- Error messages include hints to reduce pattern counts, use `focus` to render subsets, or switch to `inspect_cad`/`measure` for numerical inspection.
- The rasterization byte cap is a backstop for documents whose triangle count wasn't known pre-render (inline docs, cold sessions).

author: qingqishi
body:
Running `raise-pr` from inside an orca worktree used to interrupt with an unnecessary prompt. Orca worktrees live under `orca/workspaces/` (a git worktree of `~/.claude`), and the skill's branch-mode detection only recognised worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`. Any other location fell through to the "another branch" case, which fires an `AskUserQuestion` asking how to branch — noise, since the right answer for a worktree is always to rename the current branch.

The branch-mode rule now also treats any path containing `orca/workspaces/` as `worktree` mode. From inside an orca worktree, `raise-pr` renames the current branch and proceeds without prompting, matching how it already behaves in a `.claude/worktrees/` checkout.

author: ndemianc
body:
The x64 build failed in bootstrap (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND cdn.playwright.dev) while playwright-core's postinstall tried to download a Chromium. arm64 and the test job passed the SAME commit (v0.9.1 → 2e1b8570), so this is a transient network dependency, not a code defect — and an unnecessary one: no LevelCode build runs Playwright browser tests. playwright-core is pulled in transitively by the upstream `copilot` extension.

Set PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1 on the Build job env, alongside the GITHUB_TOKEN mitigation that already exists for the same class of problem (postinstall network fetches). Verified against the installed playwright-core: installBrowsersForNpmInstall() short-circuits on getAsBooleanFromENV of this exact var, so the Chromium fetch never runs. Scoped to the Build jobs, not global, so it can't affect the test job if that ever wants a browser.

Note: v0.9.1 is a TAG, so this does not retroactively fix that release build (a re-run of the flaked job does); it prevents recurrence for every future release cut from develop.

author: misterbisson
body:
## What & why

An agent pointed at a live incident — "look at what's firing", "the eu-central-1 alerts", "we're getting paged and I don't have a link" — had no way to *see* the active alerts. `get_alert_context`'s paste-a-link/JSON/webhook path was the only way in, even though the Grafana client already had `getFiringAlerts()` (Alertmanager `/api/v2/alerts`) — no tool exposed it. This closes that gap.

## The tool

`list_firing_alerts` enumerates the alerts currently active in Grafana's Alertmanager:

- Fans out across every configured connection, or one via `connection`.
- Filters by exact label matches, e.g. `labelFilters: {"region":"eu-central-1","severity":"critical"}`.
- Returns each alert in the **exact shape `get_alert_context` accepts as `alertJson`** (fingerprint, status, labels, annotations, startsAt, and a `source` link) — a chosen entry pipes straight into an investigation with no re-typing.
- **Read-only**: never silences or acknowledges. Unreachable connections surface as `failedConnections` so a clean result isn't mistaken for all-clear.

## Wiring & docs

Registered in `registerAll`; added to the README/`docs/TOOLS.md` tables, the Electron `--mcp-server` tool-set assertion, and step 1 of the investigate skill (call this instead of asking the person to paste a link Grafana already knows about).

## Tests

`test/listFiringAlerts.tool.test.ts` — ingestable shape, fan-out, label filter, sort/limit, redaction of identifiers in labels, `failedConnections` reporting, unknown-connection error. Full suite green (664).

author: cbortz
body:
## What

Adds three console endpoints to the SDK and bumps the version to 0.6.0. All additive — no existing signatures change.

## Methods added

| Method | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `client.console.credential_profiles.delete(id)` | `DELETE /v1/console/credential-profiles/:id` |
| `client.console.delete_template(id)` | `DELETE /v1/console/card-templates/:id` |
| `client.console.webhooks.verify(id)` | `POST /v1/console/webhooks/:id/verify` |

Deletes return `None`. `verify` returns a `WebhookVerification` (`.id`, `.verified`); both the 200 and 202 responses are treated as success.

## Signing

The request layer already attaches a signed `sig_payload` for no-body POST/DELETE, so these authenticate through the existing path. `verify` is added to the action-word list so it signs `{"id": "<webhook_id>"}` (consistent with `publish`), and the deletes sign `{"id": "<id>"}`. No changes to the signing layer beyond that list entry.

## Multi-family

No code needed — `issue`/`update` take `**kwargs` and pass through, so `multi_family` templates' resident fields already work.

## Tests

Four new tests (HTTP-level mocks, real response shapes): both deletes and verify assert the **exact** `sig_payload` value plus method/path; verify covers 200 → `verified True` and 202 → `verified False`. Full suite: 60 passed. flake8 / black / isort clean.

## Version

`0.5.0` → `0.6.0` (minor — backward-compatible additions). `setup.py` and `__version__` bumped together; version-consistency test passes.

## Qué

Una segunda cara para `/calendario`, revelada volteando una carta como en una tirada de tarot. Guarda para las historias que se publican fuera del calendario: puentes, contrapartes y lo que apetezca escribir en el momento.

Conserva la **forma** del calendario (mismo rail, mismos nodos, mismas placas) pero no su **promesa**: sin número de fase y sin fechas, para no crear un segundo calendario que también se pueda quedar atrás. El emblema de cada historia va girado 180°, la carta invertida.

## Cómo se decide el contenido

Un checkbox `Reverso` en la base **Fases** de Notion. Las fases marcadas, y sus historias, forman el reverso. La base Novelas no se toca: una historia se muda al reverso cambiándole la Fase. Si ninguna fase está marcada, no se pinta ni el botón ni la cara trasera y la página queda como antes.

- **`docs/` fuera del versionado** + `README` para el repo. Barrido preventivo del `.gitignore` (variantes `.env.local`, Wrangler, editores, SO, logs).

body:
## Summary

Adds Deluge as a third backend for the download-loop machinery: `torrent_session` can list a Deluge session and `torrent_control` can remove/pause/reannounce its torrents, and the `deluge` sink now writes grab records so `mark_failed` can resolve dead torrents back to their release URLs.

**Core implementation by @brunoga**: the Deluge Web UI JSON-RPC client (`internal/torrentclient/deluge.go` — list/remove/pause/reannounce) and grab recording in the `deluge` sink (commit a4c9392).

Review fixes applied on top:

- **State mapping** — explicit `"Queued"` → `StatePaused`. A queued torrent makes no progress by design; mapping it to `downloading` would let `torrent_failed` flag zero-progress queue backlogs as stalled after `stall_timeout` and falsely janitor them. The stray development comment was replaced with the mapping rationale (also documents why this backend never produces `stalled`).
- **Error field** — Deluge reports `message == "OK"` for healthy torrents; `Torrent.Error` is now blanked unless the state is `Error`, so `torrent_error` is no longer stamped on every healthy torrent.
- **Lint/format** — `ineffassign` in the state switch, trailing whitespace, and a doc comment rephrased so gofmt's doc-comment formatter no longer mangles a quoted Python literal.
- **Docs** — `torrent_session`/`torrent_control` READMEs, package docs, and Schema port hints list deluge (default 8112); deluge sink README gains the grab-recording note mirroring transmission/qbittorrent; user-guide backend lists (torrent_session intro + tables, mark_failed, download-loop bullets) include deluge; ROADMAP §3 "Deluge deferred" note replaced with shipped status; `configs/torrent-janitor.star` comments mention deluge as a valid backend (config unchanged otherwise, still checks clean).

- [x] Documentation update

## Testing

- New `internal/torrentclient/deluge_test.go` httptest suite: auth.login success/failure (no listing after failed login), full state-mapping matrix (all Deluge state strings incl. Queued and an errored torrent with a message; asserts `Error` empty for healthy/"OK" torrents), field extraction, negative-ratio clamp, `Remove` with `withData` true and false (per-hash params), `Pause` (+ empty-hashes no-op), `Reannounce`, RPC-error propagation across all four methods, endpoint defaults (http/8112, https/custom port).
- Deluge sink grab-recording tests mirroring transmission/qbittorrent: info-hash field → record with URL/series key/task, magnet URL → derived hash recorded, no determinable hash → debug skip with add still succeeding, failed add → no record.

body:
## Summary
- Adds `POST /api/v1/callouts/draft`: a few AI-drafted trash-talk lines for a claimed challenger targeting a past (or current-week) rival, grounded in lifetime record + shared xTrace memory, cached once per challenger/target pair per ET day (`companion_artifacts`, `kind: 'callout_draft'`).
- Target authorization requires either a completed pairing with the target (unbounded lookup) or the target appearing among the challenger's own call-out candidates (a current-week rival with no completed pairing yet) — otherwise `FORBIDDEN`. This pins the untruncated check against `getCalloutCandidates`'s one-page cap.
- Cache check happens before the daily rate limit (same reasoning as the XH-T6 banter route): generation is already bounded by the cache key, so the budget only guards the miss path.
- Degraded generation (unconfigured or filtered-to-empty) returns `503 COMPANION_UNAVAILABLE` — unlike the passive banter panel, the user explicitly clicked here, so silent nothing would be worse than an honest error.
- Extracts `shareCalloutLink` out of `CalloutButton.tsx` into `lib/callout-share.ts`, adding an optional `text` param (passed through to `nav.share` and the clipboard fallback). `CalloutButton`'s own behavior (no `text`) is unchanged.
- Adds `CalloutDraftButton`, rendered by `CalloutPanel` beside each candidate's existing `CalloutButton` behind the `callout_draft` flag (server-reads-flag, passes-prop). Click → fetch drafts → pick one → share the minted challenge link + draft text together via the same extracted share path. A draft failure never affects the plain `CalloutButton` right next to it (independent sibling components).
- New `calloutsCopy` strings (`draftButtonLabel`, `draftPickerHint`, `draftFailed`) and a new `callout_draft` rate-limit rule (`RL_CALLOUT_DRAFT_PROFILE_D`/day).
- **No contract change**: `createCalloutBodySchema` (`packages/core`) and the `callouts` table (`packages/db`) are untouched — no new columns or fields. Drafted text rides only the native share/clipboard payload, never the callout row.

author: giulianodolcetalianosantoro
body:
## Resumen

Arregla dos hallazgos de la validación en emulador de 1.7.0/vc24 sobre la pantalla de alarma full-screen (`app/alarm.tsx`):

### 1. Falta de atribución de perfil (multi-perfil, F2)

La pantalla de alarma mostraba `medication.name` pelado (p.ej. "Enalapril") sin decir de quién es la dosis. El helper `medDisplayName` que antepone "Mamá · " solo llegaba a los payloads de las notificaciones nativas — un cuidador con varios regímenes en el teléfono no sabía de quién era la dosis en la pantalla más importante.

- Nuevo helper `getProfileLabel(med, profiles, t)` en `src/utils`: devuelve el nombre del perfil dueño solo cuando hay 2+ perfiles en el dispositivo (con uno solo no hay ambigüedad y la etiqueta es ruido). El perfil default sin nombre cae al "Yo"/"Me"/"Eu" localizado.
- La pantalla de alarma ahora renderiza un chip con ícono de persona + nombre del perfil arriba del nombre del med.
- Las filas de "También a esta hora" (co-due) llevan el prefijo `Perfil · ` — esas dosis pueden ser de otros perfiles porque la pantalla resuelve meds de toda la DB.
- `medDisplayName` en `notifications.ts` ahora delega en `getProfileLabel`: una sola fuente de verdad, pantallas y notificaciones siempre de acuerdo.

### 2. Pluralización de unidades de dosis

La fila co-due y la ficha de emergencia renderizaban el string crudo `medication.dosage`, que concatena el valor de unidad fijo en plural: "1 comprimidos" en los tres idiomas.

- Nuevo `getLocalizedDosageLong(med, t)`: nombre completo de unidad pluralizado por cantidad vía i18next (`_one`/`_other`) para las unidades contables (comprimidos, cápsulas, gotas); las métricas (mg, ml, UI…) pasan sin tocar.
- Claves nuevas `dosageUnitsLong` en es/en/pt: "1 comprimido" / "2 comprimidos", "1 tablet" / "2 tablets".
- Lo usan: la fila co-due, la ficha de emergencia, la pastilla de dosis de la alarma y el recordatorio hablado (TTS), que antes leía "1 comp." en voz alta.
- El selector de unidades del formulario sigue usando las abreviaturas (`getDosageLabel`) — sin cambios ahí.

## Tests

author: joshrotenberg
body:
## Summary

Fixes finding GAP-AUTOMATION-03. Part of #1045.

`-o json`/`-o yaml` only affected the success payload. On failure, `print_diagnostic` always rendered the cargo-style human diagnostic regardless of output format, so a script wiring redisctl into CI had no stable error object to parse: no error code, no structured shape.

## Change

- `print_diagnostic(&self, format: OutputFormat)`: under `Json` it emits a JSON envelope, under `Yaml` a YAML envelope, both on **stderr** so the stdout success channel stays clean for `jq`. `Auto`/`Table` keep the existing human diagnostic.
- Each `RedisCtlError` variant has a stable `code()` string. The match is exhaustive, so a new variant will not compile until it declares a code.
- The envelope carries `code`, `message`, and `tips` (from `suggestions()`).

## Output

```
$ redisctl -o json --profile ent cloud database list 2>&1 1>/dev/null
{
  "error": {
    "code": "profile_type_mismatch",
    "message": "Profile 'ent' is type 'enterprise' but command requires 'cloud'",
    "tips": ["Available cloud profiles: ...", "..."]
  }
}

$ redisctl -o yaml ...   # same shape as YAML
$ redisctl ...           # default: unchanged human diagnostic
```

## Validation

- New `json_output_emits_structured_error_envelope` test parses stderr as JSON and asserts `error.code == "profile_type_mismatch"`, plus stdout empty.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`: all pass.

## Scope

Exit codes are still `1` across the board; the taxonomy that would add an `exit_code` field to the envelope (GAP-AUTOMATION-02) is a separate change and a "now or never" interface decision. The `code` strings introduced here are the natural anchor for that mapping and should be documented alongside it.

author: hemsoft
body: Closes #292 ## Root cause The packaged Windows app passed an OSC 7 prompt-initialization script on PowerShell's process command line. Windows process policy denied that command line before PowerShell started, and node-pty surfaced `Cannot create process, error code: 5`. The same packaged executable successfully launched `pwsh.exe` with plain interactive arguments. ## Fix - Resolve `pwsh.exe` and `powershell.exe` to the first accessible regular file on PATH, not a bare executable name. - Launch PowerShell with plain interactive arguments and send OSC 7 setup through the PTY after process creation. - Validate cwd readability and report safe requested/effective cwd booleans plus native launch stage on failure; no environment values are included. - Cover error code 5 diagnostics, inaccessible cwd fallback context, absolute `pwsh.exe`, and `powershell.exe` fallback. ## Verification - `bun run test:electron` — 44 files, 861 tests passed. - `bunx vitest run src/components/terminal src/components/terminal-workspace src/hooks/useTerminalPanel.test.ts src/utils/terminalPathUtils.test.ts` — 9 files, 215 tests passed. - `bun run test:coverage` — 291 files, 6536 tests passed; 99.83% statements / 99.62% branches / 100% functions / 99.91% lines. - `bun run typecheck` — passed all five TypeScript projects. - `bun run lint` — passed. - `bun run knip` — passed. - `bun run format:check` — passed. - `bunx vite build` — passed. - `bunx electron-builder --win --dir --config electron-builder.json5 --config.npmRebuild=false` — produced the Windows x64 unpacked package. - Packaged CDP smoke — `terminal.spawn` used the exact repository cwd; attach showed an alive session; startup output, a subsequent interactive write, and OSC 7 output all matched; kill succeeded. ## Residual risk The local packaging command disabled dependency rebuild because the locked `node-abi@4.29.0` does not yet identify Electron 43.0.0. The packaged node-pty prebuild loaded and passed the real terminal smoke, but CI's normal packaging path remains the authority for rebuild behavior. Post-spawn shell integration is intentionally written after a 500 ms delay to avoid process-policy denial; the packaged smoke verified it on this Windows host. > [!NOTE] > ### Harden Windows terminal startup by improving shell resolution and PTY error diagnostics > - `resolveExecutableOnPath` now scans PATH entries and returns the first accessible executable file path (skipping directories and inaccessible entries) for `pwsh.exe` then `powershell.exe`, falling back to the standard `WindowsPowerShell` path. > - `inspectCwdAccess` distinguishes between non-existent and inaccessible working directories; spawn failures now include a diagnostic context with launch stage, shell path, and cwd accessibility flags. > - PowerShell startup customization (OSC 7 prompt setup) is no longer passed via `-EncodedCommand` args; it is written to the PTY after spawn, joined with any user `startupCommand` via `;`. > - Behavioral Change: `buildTerminalShellArgs` for Windows PowerShell now returns only `['-NoLogo', '-NoExit']` instead of an `-EncodedCommand` argument. > > > > Macroscope summarized 6c8d0a6. > >

author: ovvo-financial
body:
## What changed

- added `RHLean.Analysis.QuadraticPhaseShiftSign`
- proved the exact half-turn exponential identity

```lean
theorem exp_int_mul_pi_mul_I_eq_neg_one_pow
    (n : ℤ) :
    Complex.exp (((n : ℂ) * (Real.pi : ℂ)) * Complex.I) =
      (-1 : ℂ) ^ n
```

- proved that adding `r * k` to a numerator modulo `2 * r` contributes exactly `(-1)^k`
- proved the full quadratic shift law

```lean
theorem quadraticPhase_shift_r
    (a r u : ℤ) :
    quadraticPhase a r (u + r) =
      (-1 : ℂ) ^ (a * r) * quadraticPhase a r u
```

- handled the degenerate `r = 0` case explicitly
- imported the new module from `RHLean.lean`

## Why

This completes the exact complex phase-period layer promised by the corrected modulus-`2r` architecture. It turns the previously merged integer shift dichotomy into the precise multiplicative sign law for the complex quadratic phase.

The theorem formally explains why reducing the phase modulo `r` is invalid when `a*r` is odd: the shift by `r` changes the phase by `-1` rather than preserving it.

## Proof structure

The proof expands

```text
a * (u + r)^2
  = a*u^2 + (2*r)*(a*u) + r*(a*r),
```

removes the full-modulus term using additive-character periodicity, and evaluates the remaining half-turn exponential as `(-1)^(a*r)`.

## Scope

This PR does not yet define the reduced quadratic Gauss factor over `(ZMod (2*r))ˣ`. That is the next focused layer after this sign law.

No `sorry`, `admit`, axioms, opaque constants, weakened statements, changed indexing, or RH assumptions are introduced.

## Validation

GitHub Actions runs:

```bash
bash scripts/audit_assumptions.sh
lake build RHLean --wfail
```

No local Lean toolchain validation was available; CI is the compilation check.

author: irafeek
body:
Closes #55432

## Problem

`BaseOperatorLink.get_link()` was an `@abstractmethod`, forcing every
subclass to implement it even when the link URL is a constant (e.g.,
a documentation link). This meant operators with static links still had
to push to XCom during `execute()` and read from the metadata database
on every task run, adding unnecessary overhead.

## Solution

This PR introduces an optional `static_url` property on
`BaseOperatorLink`:

- `static_url` defaults to `None` (no behavior change for existing subclasses)
- `get_link()` is no longer `@abstractmethod`; its default implementation
  returns `static_url` if set, otherwise raises `NotImplementedError`
  with a helpful message guiding the developer to override one or the other
- Subclasses with a constant URL can now override `static_url` instead
  of `get_link()`, with zero XCom involvement

## Backward Compatibility

Fully backward-compatible. All existing subclasses that implement
`get_link()` continue to work without any changes.

## Example

```python
class MyDocsLink(BaseOperatorLink):
    name = "Documentation"
    operators = [MyOperator]

    @property
    def static_url(self) -> str:
        return "https://myoperator.readthedocs.io"
    # No get_link() needed — no XCom push during execute()
```

## Tests

author: lifted-truck
body:
Sixth lab→core fold, and the first of the **new detune laws** — the supersets are done.

## What
The law the human reverse-engineered from the NI demo: pulling voices out one at a time at full spread walked them **down the harmonic series**. So the spread pattern *is* the series.

`law 4` → `f = f0·(1 + detune·harmReach·i)` — the voice **index** is the harmonic rung. At `detune·harmReach = 1` the stack is exactly f0, 2f0, 3f0…; below that it's a continuous unison→series morph. It deliberately ignores `dist`/`anchor` (the geometry is the integer series), and `harmReach` decouples the top harmonic from voice count (1.833 with n=7 → top at H12).

Named **`harmReach`**, not `reach`: the core's `reach = 5` is already the ring-topology neighbourhood radius, so a literal transcription of the lab's label would have been a duplicate member with a clashing meaning.

Reference-first per ADR-003: `swarmsaw.html` first, then mirrored bit-for-bit into `swarm_core.h`. Laws 0–3 take no new code path.

## Evidence
- `./verify full` EXIT 0 — parity **84/84 → 93/93** within ε, the 9 new at **rms 0.000e+00**; all 8 chains + notefuzz green.
- Geometry: detune 1 → 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 × f0.
- Anchor: bounded/NaN-clean 0.355; coupling entrains **0.462** (gate 0.2).

## The finding — a domain limit on bit-parity, not a porting bug
A fourth scenario (law 4, full spread, K 0.6) failed at **rms 9.736e-02**. Diagnosed, not assumed:

- Bracketed: divergence scales with coupling × spread — 3.7e-19 → 4.4e-13 → 3.5e-07 → 9.7e-02.
- **Falsified directly**: perturbing the **JS reference alone by 1 ULP** gave **rms 9.383e-02** — JS-vs-itself diverges as far as C++-vs-JS, and it grows over time (5.62e-2 @ 0–0.5 s → 1.147e-1 @ 1–2 s). Stable regimes under the same probe: 1.869e-19 and exactly 0.

Positive Lyapunov exponent + `Math.sin`/`std::sin` not identically rounded ⇒ sample-exact parity there is impossible **in principle**. The golden was **removed** (with an explanatory comment), not kept red and not given a loosened ε — never weaken a gate. The regime is covered by a behavioural anchor instead.

The anchor uses **K 0.9, not 0.6**: probed, K 0.6 lifts late-window R by only **0.006** on an octave-plus stack — indistinguishable from chaotic jitter, an anchor that could flip sign on any legitimate refactor. K 0.9 is the first value that actually entrains this geometry (R 0.24 → 0.70).

## Open — needs your call
`ACCEPTANCE.md` is a **protected path** and states the parity contract (L0-1, ε=1e-6 RMS) with no domain limit. It likely wants an amendment saying parity is a valid oracle only in non-chaotic regimes. ADR-065 records the limit; the protected file is untouched.

Not yet a CLAP param — batched at fold end, per the agreed cadence.

author: mantra-agent
body:
## Summary
`e656f6f` self-heals **nested** duplicate canonical metadata pages but still throws `409` ("multiple root canonical … pages; migration repair is required") when a vault has two or more canonical Index/Wiki/Log pages at the **root**. That residual throw keeps wedging every Library read, lint, move, opportunity-artifact, corpus-migration, and workflow-checkpoint path that bootstraps through `ensureCanonicalVaultMetadataPage` — the exact live failure behind blocked workflow creation.

## Fix
Remove the residual root-duplicate throw. The resolver already computes `canonical = rootCandidates[0] ?? candidates[0]` (earliest root wins, deterministic under the advisory lock) and demotes every other match via the existing `staleNested` loop. Extra root duplicates simply fall into that loop and are demoted to ordinary artifact pages (content preserved, canonical tags stripped). Convergence is idempotent and replay-safe: a second call sees exactly one canonical page and no-ops.

## Runtime evidence
`platforms.start_build_workflow`, `workflows.create_run`, and `library.lint_library` all failed on the live environment with `Vault has multiple canonical Index pages; migration repair is required`.

## Engineering principles
- Encode Invariants in Structure: convergence at the one canonical mutation boundary, not a guard that fails every consumer.
- Every Operation is Replayable: idempotent under `pg_advisory_xact_lock`.
- Fail Loudly, Degrade Gracefully: per-page warn-log on demotion; subsystem stays available.
- Multi-user safety preserved: visible-scope reads, writable-scope writes.

## Verification
- `npm run build` passed.
- No tests added/run per repo policy. No schema/migration; rollback is revert.

Live unblock requires a human publish to env 12 (`productionReleaseRequiresHuman`).

author: phillipjad
body:
## Summary

The entity-contract coverage check classified entity collectors as `type == collector AND resume_behavior == "none"`. That misclassifies a **stateless snapshot activity collector**: it emits to the shared `activity` space but has `resume_behavior: none`, so the check flags it as an entity collector and demands a `When{X}CollectorRuns` contract test it should never need.

This switches the classifier to the reliable signal — the spaces a collector emits to.

## Change

- An entity collector is a collector that does **not** emit to the `activity` space.
- Newer connector manifests declare per-feature `spaces` (see mesh-sdk PR #86); when present, activity-space membership is the signal.
- Falls back to the previous `resume_behavior == "none"` heuristic for manifests generated before per-feature spaces existed — those connectors have no stateless activity collectors, so the fallback stays correct.

## Compatibility

- Backward-compatible: manifests without per-feature `spaces` keep the old behavior.
- No effect until a connector both adopts the new SDK (so its manifest carries `spaces`) and ungates the affected collector.

## Validation

- Logic verified against fixtures: a new manifest with per-feature spaces (stateless activity collector no longer flagged), an old manifest without spaces (entity collectors still caught via fallback), and the empty-spaces edge case.
- The embedded Python compiles.

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Gap

There is no CI step that verifies `uv.lock` is in sync with `pyproject.toml`. If a contributor updates a dependency in `pyproject.toml` but forgets to run `uv lock`, the lockfile silently drifts and subsequent `uv sync --locked` will fail — but only when someone else checks out the branch.

`uv lock --check` exits 0 if the lockfile is current and non-zero otherwise. In this repo it runs in ~2ms. Adding it as an early CI step catches the drift immediately at PR time.

## Suggested fix

Add a `uv lock --check` step to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, either as a new job or as an early step in the existing `check` job (the reusable workflow). The CI already uses `uv sync --locked` in the setup action, so the lockfile must be fresh anyway — this just makes the check explicit and earlier in the pipeline.

## Files affected
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

I drove the whole Delegate send flow myself against a real running build and fixed every link until an email actually went out **and** the run completed truthfully.

**Verified in the DB:** run `completed`/`succeeded` + external_action `confirmed`/`sent` (via `browser`). Real emails delivered to the test address; Gmail's own UI showed "Message sent."

## Three real bugs, all fixed
1. **Delegate was treated as UNATTENDED.** `startCapability` runs `silent:true`, and the approval gate did `unattended = args.silent || …` → `email_send` (confirm tier) was **blocked** instead of prompting. author: nbbshaw
body:
## Symptom

The Gantt widget rendered unstyled on **both** embeds: the Project form's Schedule tab collapsed to a thin strip with its status-filter menu stuck open, and the Projects Dashboard portfolio Gantt showed a plain list of project names with no chart.

## Root cause (verified against production, not inferred)

Browsers were being served the **v1.163.0 copy of `gantt_widget.css`**. Probing the live site:

- `ETag: W/"6a627970-76c"` → `0x76c` = **1,900 bytes**, and `last-modified` from the v1.163.0 deploy — while `gantt_widget.js` in the same directory carried the **current** build (`0x5585`, later `last-modified`).
- The served text still defined the pre-rename `.ee-timeline-gantt` and contained none of `.ee-gantt-toolbar` / `.ee-gantt-filter-menu` / `.ee-gantt-chart-wrap` / `.ee-gantt-today-col`.
- `fetch(url, {cache: "reload"})` and a unique `?bust=` query **both** still returned the old bytes → stale at the server, not in the browser cache.

So every rule added in v1.164/v1.165 was missing client-side, which is exactly the observed rendering: no `.ee-project-gantt` height → collapsed chart; no `display:none` on `.ee-gantt-filter-menu` → checkboxes rendered inline; no flex/chart-wrap → dashboard laid out as text.

Two compounding causes, one rule broken: `/assets` is served with a 1-year **immutable** `Cache-Control`, **and** the deploy left the raw file stale on disk. This is the precise hazard `desk_addons.bundle.scss` and `kanban.bundle.js` were introduced for in v0.8.1 ("Kanban fix works on desktop, phones still broken") — **our own assets must ship content-hashed.** I put a mutable, app-owned stylesheet on a raw `/assets` path anyway; that was the mistake.

## Fix

- `gantt_widget.css` is now imported by **`desk_addons.bundle.scss`**, so it builds into a content-hashed filename resolved through `assets.json` — every deploy gets a fresh URL. It is no longer lazy-`frappe.require`d (~3.5K global, in line with `collab.css` / `triton_widget.css`).
- The **vendored** 140K DHTMLX skin stays a lazy raw include — a file that never changes cannot go stale (the same exception the vendored UMD libs already use). Both files' headers now state which category they're in and why.
- Height cap written as `height` + `max-height` instead of `min(65vh, 700px)`: sass shadows `min()`. Current dart-sass (1.77, verified) passes mixed units through untouched, so this is defensive, not a bug fix — the comment says so rather than overclaiming.

## Verification

- **dart-sass compiles `desk_addons.bundle.scss`** and the output inlines all four selectors that were absent in production: `.ee-gantt-toolbar`, `.ee-gantt-filter-menu`, `.ee-project-gantt`, `.ee-gantt-today-col`.
- eslint clean; 34 `test_gantt_api.py` cases pass.
- Post-deploy I can re-probe the live page to confirm the rules are present and the charts render.

> Worth a follow-up on the ops side: a deploy updated raw `.js` under `public/` but not the raw `.css` beside it. This PR makes the widget immune, but any other raw mutable asset would share the exposure.

author: futuroptimist
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent macOS `macos-26` runners from being allocated for PRs that do not touch the native Metal-capable embedded Python runtime by moving change detection off the macOS job. 
- Preserve the focused macOS Metal bootstrap for true runtime/bootstrap changes and manual `workflow_dispatch` runs while keeping the overall PR workflow visible and minimal.

### Description
- Add a new cheap detector job `detect-macos-metal-runtime-changes` that runs on `ubuntu-latest`, has `permissions: contents: read`, a 5-minute timeout, a full-history checkout (`fetch-depth: 0`), and exposes `outputs.run_macos_metal` from the detector step. 
- Move the changed-file detection logic to that detector and make `workflow_dispatch` always set `run_macos_metal=true`, while PRs only set it if the change matches the preserved path contract. 
- Gate the existing `macos-metal-runtime-bootstrap` job at the job level with `needs: detect-macos-metal-runtime-changes` and `if: ${{ needs.detect-macos-metal-runtime-changes.outputs.run_macos_metal == 'true' }}`, preserving the visible job name and `runs-on: macos-26`. 
- Remove the redundant macOS-side detection step, conditional `if` on setup/build steps, and the skipped-bootstrap summary step while leaving all Metal bootstrap commands and invariants unchanged, including `CMAKE_ARGS=-DGGML_METAL=on`, `FORCE_CMAKE=1`, the `arm64` assertion, runtime preparation, executable assertion, and `pip check`. 
- Add focused sentinel tests in `tests/unit/test_workflow_ci_sentinel.py` covering the new detector job, detector output consumption, job-level gating, the path contract, manual dispatch behavior, and removal of the macOS-side detection/skip steps.

Relevant path contract (detector will trigger macOS bootstrap when any of these change):
- `desktop-tauri/src-tauri/python/**`
- `desktop-tauri/scripts/prepare_*python_runtime*` (matching the existing prepare script regex)
- root `requirements.txt`
- `.github/workflows/run-all-tests-pr.yml` (workflow self-validation)
- Manual `workflow_dispatch` always requests macOS (`run_macos_metal=true`).

### Testing
- Ran unit sentinel tests with `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_workflow_ci_sentinel.py -q` and observed `32 passed` (all tests passed). 
- Parsed the modified workflow with the repo YAML loader using `python -c "import yaml; yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.BaseLoader)"` and confirmed the file parses and `jobs` exist (parsing passed). 
- Ran `git diff --check` and confirmed no trailing/whitespace issues (passed). 
- Ran repository checks via `pre-commit run --all-files` and observed the hooks passed (passed). 

Verification notes and limits:
- Verified locally that the detector job runs on Linux and exposes `outputs.run_macos_metal`, that the macOS job has job-level gating and retains `runs-on: macos-26`, and that the old macOS-side detection/skip steps are removed. 
- Environment note: this execution environment had no configured `origin` remote, so remote fetch/fast-forward against `origin/main` could not be performed here; all checks above were run against the local working tree.

Conclusion: irrelevant PRs that do not touch any of the listed path categories or that are not manual dispatches will now skip the `macOS Metal desktop runtime bootstrap` job before a `macos-26` runner is allocated.

author: ch4s3
body:
## Finding M1 — return-type `Cap(X)` false-accept

`CapCheck.capsInSignature` scanned only **parameter** annotations, so a module whose only capability defect is an uncovered **return-type** `Cap(X)` — e.g. `fn f(cap : Cap(IO.Console)) : Cap(IO.Network)` under `needs IO.Console` — was accepted by the cap checker while march **rejects** it (`check_module_needs` scans `param_tys @ ret_tys`). A latent `(march=reject, lean=accept)` gap.

Root cause: `Decl.dfn` carried no return-type field, so the decoder dropped the `ret_ty` march already emits.

### Change

author: prem-dharshan
body:
🛡️ Sentinel: [CRITICAL] Fix SSRF vulnerability in URL expansion

### 🚨 Severity
CRITICAL

### 💡 Vulnerability
The `/api/enrich` endpoint accepted arbitrary URLs and followed redirects manually using `fetch` without any hostname validation.

### 🎯 Impact
An attacker could provide a malicious URL that redirects to an internal endpoint (e.g. `http://localhost`, `169.254.169.254` on AWS) allowing them to perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), potentially accessing internal services, scanning internal networks, or exposing metadata.

### 🔧 Fix
- Added an `ALLOWED_HOSTS` allowlist specifically containing trusted Google Maps-related hostnames.
- Implemented `isAllowedHost` function to parse the URL and enforce `http:`/`https:` protocols alongside the hostname allowlist check.
- Added validation for both the initial provided URL and every single redirect URL parsed inside the redirect loop before executing the outbound `fetch`.
- Any invalid URL throws a secure exception without leaking internal data.

### ✅ Verification
- Type checkers run via `npx tsc --noEmit`
- Linter run via `pnpm lint`

author: mmcky
body:
The notebook-build step reports success when the build fails.

## Mechanism

The step runs three commands:

```
jb build lectures --path-output ./ --builder=custom --custom-builder=jupyter -n -W --keep-going
mkdir -p _build/html/_notebooks
cp -u _build/jupyter/*.ipynb _build/html/_notebooks
```

The step's exit code is `cp`'s, not `jb build`'s. `--keep-going` guarantees the `.ipynb` files exist for `cp` to succeed on even when the build failed, so a failing strict build reports green. `shell: bash -l {0}` is a custom shell spec, so GitHub injects no `-eo pipefail` of its own — it only does that for the bare `shell: bash` shorthand.

## Scope

This is the **last live instance** across the five editions. `lecture-intro.zh-cn` and `lecture-python.zh-cn` already carry the fix; the `.fa` and `.fr` editions are not affected because their builds are the last command in the step. The added comment matches the wording already used in `lecture-python.zh-cn` so the reason travels with the line.

## Risk

Bounded. This step's twin, `Build HTML`, runs the same `-n -W --keep-going` unmasked — it is the last command in its own step — and is green on `main`. So removing the mask can only reveal failures specific to the jupyter custom builder, not a long-broken build in general. If CI does go red here, that is a real finding and worth triaging on its own rather than reverting.

The structured organism/analyte stays its own reading. - **Radiology impressions folded in** — Epic packs a radiology report's prose in `Epic.ResultText` `IMP/NAR/…` siblings of the study's organizer; the impression is recovered per-organizer into the imaging study's `impression`. - **Lab reference range + abnormal flag** — every lab now carries its own `` and `` (H/L/N/A). An analyte the app has no canonical band for still shows the lab's range and its out-of-range flag. `reconcileFlags` refines a mapped lab against the canonical band and **leaves an unmapped lab's source flag intact**. - **`

Schema: migration **106** grows the `medical_records` category CHECK to admit `report` (rebuild, no backfill; columns verified byte-identical to live schema). ## Why Run against the full local corpus (7 CCD XMLs + 5 XDM zips), this recovers, per import: **8 narrative reports**, **5/6 radiology impressions** on the studies that have prose, **273 labs** with a reference range, and **17 flagged abnormal results** — all previously discarded. body:
- named funcs: reader threads look up ids at thread start while packet threads call funcs, guard the hash/arr with a lock and publish namedFuncsMax / arkime_has_named_func with release/acquire
- dedup: invalidate a slot's tv_sec before wiping its counts and publish it after, so the lock free searchers can no longer scan a slot mid wipe and match entries from dedupSeconds ago
- dll.h: count updates are relaxed atomic stores and DLL_COUNT a relaxed atomic load, making the lock free queue depth reads well defined; same instructions on x86/i686
- packet: only the first reader thread records initialPacket/initialDropped, the log threshold uses the counter value the increment returned, and inProgress is read/written atomically for arkime_packet_outstanding
- writer-null: atomically claim each packet's file position range, two packet threads could hand out the same position

body:
Closes #148.

The unit regression the Coding contract owes for the production fix that landed with the gh#135 QA suite — *"bug fixes are regression-first"*. **No production change here**; this is the missing guard.

## What it pins
`ComposeAsync` must hand `OrderExecutionService` the operator's **declared** account mode, not the one the **venue reports**. That is the gh#60 signal: the venue's own flag is not the stake signal — against a real login it misclassified **all 293 accounts**.

Until now the only guard was at the **integration** tier (gh#135). Reverting `OrderEndpoints.cs:361` left the entire unit suite green — the tier where a Coding Agent gets its red said nothing.

## The test
`SendOrder_ShouldAuthorizeAgainstTheDeclaredMode_WhenTheVenueClaimsADifferentOne` — persisted `Account.Mode = Practice`, venue roster claims `Live`, **Development** host. Practice trades anywhere, Live nowhere outside production, so the send succeeds **only if the declared mode is what reaches `TradingModePolicy`**. It also asserts the journaled `Order.Mode` is the declared one — what the gh#7 DB mode-guard trigger compares against.

- **Proven RED without the fix** → `409 RefusedByMode`; **GREEN with it** → 200 + placed. (Verified by reverting line 361 in a throwaway container copy — a guard that cannot fail on the defect is worthless.)
- Covers the whole `ComposeAsync` ladder, which now backs **send / arm / edit / take**.

## Verification
420 unit tests green (1 new), 0 warnings, `dotnet format --verify` exit 0 — container gates (Smart App Control blocks local unsigned builds; CI is authoritative).

## Two-tier split, restored
Unit proves the seam, integration proves the wiring. The gh#135 divergence test remains the integration-tier guard over this one.

## 概要

操作パネル（別ウィンドウ）を閉じても再生中の音（BGM・効果音・タブ音源）が止まらない不具合を修正します。

## 原因

音声再生の実体は、画面共有対象タブに注入される content script（`content.js`）の `AudioContext` 側にあります。操作パネル（`panel.html`/`panel.js`）は `PLAY`/`STOP`/`STOP_ALL` をタブへ送るだけの別ウィンドウ「リモコン」で、それ自体は音を鳴らしていません。

パネルを閉じたときの処理は `background.js` の `chrome.windows.onRemoved` のみで、そこでは `panelWindowId` を削除するだけで**対象タブへ停止指示を送っていなかった**ため、タブ内の音が鳴り続けていました。

## 変更内容

`background.js` の `chrome.windows.onRemoved` で、閉じたウィンドウが操作パネル（`windowId === panelWindowId`）のときに、対象タブへ `STOP_ALL`（`immediate: true`）を送るようにしました。

- `immediate: true` によりフェードなしで即停止し、`content.js` の `stopAll(true)` 経由でタブ音源のルーティング（`removeAllTabSources()`）も解除されます。
- 停止トリガーはサービスワーカー側（`onRemoved`）に置いています。`panel.js` の `unload` 系ハンドラは、unload 中の非同期 `sendMessage` が届かないことがあるため採用していません。
- `panelWindowId` の削除は従来どおりで、`targetTabId` は残すため、パネルを開き直せば同じタブへ再接続できます。
- 対象タブ未接続・content 未注入時は `sendToTab` が `{ok:false}` を返すだけで、`onRemoved` は例外で落ちません。

## 動作確認

このリポジトリに自動テストは無いため、手動で確認します。

- [ ] 音を再生した状態でパネルを閉じると、ファイル音源・タブ音源ともに即停止する
- [ ] パネルを開き直すと、同じ対象タブに再接続できる（`targetTabId` が保持されている）

author: claude[bot]
body:
Closes #90

_(This recreates the earlier PR #98 cleanly — that one conflicted with newer code and was closed; you re-approved it so I rebuilt it against current `main`.)_

## 1. What changed
Your app already had money-saving **prompt caching** switched on for the AI that writes each video's script. But on the **true-crime** and **history/business** factories it wasn't actually saving anything — this fixes that.

The catch: one line of the AI's instructions changes on **every single video** — the rotating "editorial angle" that keeps your videos looking varied so platforms don't flag them as repetitive. That changing line was sitting *inside* the big block of instructions that's meant to be reused between videos. So the reusable block looked "different" every time and got re-billed at full price instead of the ~90%-off cached price.

I moved that one changing line just **outside** the reusable block. The big, identical chunk is now genuinely reused. **Nothing about what the videos say or how they're written changes** — only the bill.

(The sports factory was already set up correctly, so I left it untouched.)

## 2. Why it matters
The Claude script call is the biggest controllable cost per video (your text-to-speech is already free). This makes the discount that was *supposed* to be working actually work — same videos, lower spend, no quality trade-off.

## 3. How to check it works — click by click
- This is a behind-the-scenes billing fix, so there's **nothing new to see** in the videos — that's the point.
- To confirm the saving after merging: open the app, generate **2–3 true-crime or history videos back-to-back**, then open the **spend tracker**. The Claude "input" cost per video should drop noticeably from the 2nd video onward.
- Automated proof is included: new tests assert the reusable instruction block is now byte-for-byte identical across two videos with different angles, while the rotating angle sits in a separate, uncached block. I ran the **full test suite (484 pass, 3 skipped), the linter (clean), and a production build (success)** — all green.

## 4. What could break
- **Very low risk.** The change is 4 files: two small edits to the script writers plus two new tests. The hard safety rules (never assert guilt, never name minors, always attribute claims) stay exactly where they were, in the reused block — only the *stylistic* framing line moved, and it still carries its own "never introduce a new accusation" guard.
- If Anthropic's cache minimums ever aren't met (e.g. a very short custom playbook), the effect is simply "no extra saving," never a broken video or a wrong bill.
- The offline/no-API-key path (the template writer) is untouched.

## What I deliberately left out
The issue also mentioned optionally routing very simple scripts to a cheaper model. I left that out to keep this change small and easy to review — happy to do it as a separate PR if you want it.

author: ethenotethan
body:
Closes the three gaps left from ensemble-model v1 (#208):

## Map + model PDF export

Maps were the last block exporting as an empty box (MapKit's `Map` is an NSViewRepresentable — the known ImageRenderer trap). New `MapExportRenderer`:
- `MKMapSnapshotter` snapshot with a 40%-padded auto-fit region
- group-colored pin dots + white-outlined labels drawn onto the snapshot (matches the live palette)
- graceful nil on failure (offline) → falls back to source text

Model blocks export **per view**: markdown/graph/chart/stats reuse the live views (all PDF-safe), map views look up their pre-rendered snapshot keyed by the projected map JSON (deterministic via `sortedKeys` serialization — pinned by a test), tables flatten to the static export grid.

## Graph view joins the selection bus

`NetworkGraphView` gains the same optional `externalSelection` binding `MapCard` got in #208. In a model, graph node ids are already `"set/key"` — the bus's ref encoding — so clicking a node now highlights the entity in the table and map, and vice versa. Standalone graphs unchanged (local state).

## Tests

1 new (projection-key stability the export lookup depends on); ensemble suite green. Both targets build; `swiftlint --strict` clean (the new renderer lives in Views/Blocks — `no_swiftui_in_services` correctly rejected it from Services, same home as `MermaidExportRenderer`).

author: bender0oo0
body:
Closes CosmicDriftGameStudio/phronexsis#134

`defaultCellRender` had no case for `type === "money"`. Money fields
rehydrate as `{ amount, currency }` objects on the read side, so the
function fell through to `String(value)`, printing `[object Object]`
in list columns (observed live on phronexsis.kumiko.rocks/app/line-item-list).

Adds a `money` case that formats the amount via `Intl.NumberFormat`
(currency style, decimals from `currencyDecimals`), mirroring the
existing `MoneyInput` formatting logic. Falls back to `String(value)`
for unexpected shapes via a new `isMoneyValue` type guard.

author: ggekos
body:
## Problem

A multi-member consumer group never converges: a 16-member and a 4-member group stay stuck with **0 partitions assigned** (broker shows the group never leaving the rebalance), while a single-member group converges in ~30s. Confirmed in production; coordinator metrics showed the JOIN path thrashing (`join=161, join_loop=2395, join_outdated=1675`).

#141 removed the no-op group-state write churn (heartbeat/steady-state) but the group still didn't converge — that fix was necessary but not sufficient. This PR adds the missing piece.

## Root cause

It is not primarily CAS contention — it is a **missing join-window barrier**, plus two protocol deviations that make partial rounds sticky:

1. `Controller::join` returned the **leader immediately** once its own CAS landed, so it computed assignments from whatever *partial* member list it had seen. Kafka instead holds everyone — especially the leader — until the rebalance window closes, so the leader sees the complete member list. `rebalance_timeout_ms` was stored but never drove any wait.
2. Every event bumped the generation, including the `MemberIdRequired` reply, which inserted a **phantom member** and bumped the generation (non-Kafka; KIP-394 parks pending ids without registering them). Stragglers therefore kept voiding the leader's round.
3. A member absent from the leader's assignment map was answered `error=None` with an **empty assignment**, so the client parked at "stable, 0 partitions" instead of re-joining.

## Fix (one file, `tansu-broker/src/coordinator/group/administrator.rs`)

- **(A) Join-window barrier.** Hold a still-`Forming` group's leader in the existing GET-first long-poll until the persisted member set has been quiescent for `JOIN_QUIESCENCE` (3s, matching Kafka's `group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms`), bounded by `rebalance_timeout_ms` (the Java client allows JoinGroup responses up to `rebalance_timeout + 5s`; falls back to the session timeout as Kafka does for old protocol versions). Quiescence is inferred purely from the loop's successive GET-first reads — **no on-disk format change**. Followers' existing wait is untouched.
- **(B) `MemberIdRequired` no longer mutates the group** (KIP-394): no phantom member, no generation bump; the wire reply is byte-identical.
- **(C) Missing-from-assignment is retriable**: a synced member absent from the assignments map gets `RebalanceInProgress` (state untouched) instead of an empty assignment, so it re-joins the next round.

## Tests

- **`multi_member_group_converges_across_replicas`** — 8 members driven concurrently (join → MemberIdRequired → re-join → sync) against **two `Controller` instances sharing one `memory://` store** (= two replicas behind one LB); asserts every member ends with a non-empty assignment and the persisted group is `Formed`/stable. Passes in ~5s. **Negative proof:** with the barrier disabled (`JOIN_QUIESCENCE = 0`) the test fails with the exact production symptom (`no assignment for member-05`).
- Focused tests for (B) (`MemberIdRequired` leaves generation/member-set/state/etag unchanged) and (C) (Formed and Forming-leader cases return `RebalanceInProgress`).
- Maintained group tests pass (`rejoin`, `sync_from_member_while_forming`, `forming_leader_leaves_group`, `member_id_required_error_code_joins_group`, and the ignored `lifecycle`). Two maintained tests' member-count expectations changed 1 → 0 to reflect KIP-394 (a MemberIdRequired reply no longer registers a member); `lifecycle`/`rejoin` generation arithmetic is unchanged.

## Behavior / compatibility notes

- Every leader join of a Forming group now takes ≥3s (as with Kafka's default initial rebalance delay).
- (C) is marginally more aggressive than Kafka: a Formed member missing from assignments loops `RebalanceInProgress` rather than receiving an empty assignment — strictly better than the silent 0-partition park, and made near-unreachable by the barrier.
- Pure control flow: no `{group}.json` on-disk schema change and no Kafka wire change, so replicas interoperate during a rolling restart (an old replica just releases its leader early — degrades to today's behavior for that one request).

Completes the multi-member convergence work from #139 / #141.

author: sgriffiths
body:
## What changed

Adds `docs/proposals/loops.md` — a position doc on whether/how OA should incorporate "loops", following the same decide-the-boundary format as `markdown-interop.md`. **Docs-only; no schema or runtime change.** Opening as a draft to get the direction agreed before any code.

## The core argument

"Add loops to OA" is really three different features wearing one word, and they land very differently against OA's boundaries (no orchestration, no conditionals, `depends_on` acyclicity):

| Loop | Termination | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Tool-calling loop** | Bounded cap, structured error | ✅ **Already runs** (`_MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS`) — just surface it |
| **B. Bounded map / fan-out** | Fixed by array length + ceiling | 🟡 Compatible if bounded — own design |
| **C. Conditional / until-good** | Runtime predicate | 🔴 Out — belongs above the spec (BCE) |

**Bright line proposed:** *OA iterates over data it can see before the first token; it never loops on a condition it can only evaluate at runtime.*

That line is drawn on **determinism of termination**, and it stays consistent with the deterministic-pipeline framing already in the 1.6 spec (§7 / §7.3 pre-flight checks) and the markdown-interop precedent.

## Recommendations in the doc

- **A (near-term, small):** promote the hardcoded tool-iteration cap to a declared, schema-validated `intelligence.config.max_iterations`. Names existing behaviour; no new semantics.
- **B (real design work):** a bounded map — run task `T` per array element, ordered results, **fail-closed by default**, with a **validated fan-out ceiling** enforced as a pre-flight error (§7). Ships as its own proposal + schema PR if this direction is accepted.
- **C (hold the line):** conditional/until-good loops stay out of the schema; the supported pattern is "the orchestrator loops and calls an OA spec each pass" — a BCE/caller concern, keeping OA the deterministic unit.

## For discussion

- Is the A/B/C split the right cut, and is "determinism of termination" the right dividing principle?
- Should **B (bounded map)** proceed to its own design proposal, or stay out for now?
- Anything in the "explicitly refuse" list that's too strict / not strict enough?

body:
## Summary

Starts unifying the fragmented Redis write path behind the execution engine. Adds an engine `RedisSink` that owns the pool/pipeline/flush plumbing and takes a per-row op lambda, relocates `RedisPool` into the engine, and adopts the sink in `UserEventStreamingJob` — behavior-preserving.

- **`com.demo.engine.RedisPool`** — relocated out of `UserEventStreamingJob` (fixes an engine→task layering problem); all 6 importers updated. Same executor-shared singleton, byte-identical behavior.
- **`com.demo.engine.RedisSink`** — `class RedisSink(host, port, poolMax, pipelineSize, writeRow: (Pipeline, Row) => Unit) extends Sink`. `write` borrows a pooled Jedis per partition, pipelines via the pure `RedisSink.foreachWithFlush`, closes in `finally`. The op (ZINCRBY/HSET/RPUSH/SET) rides in the `writeRow` lambda — no rigid data-structure taxonomy.
- **`UserEventStreamingJob`** — its hand-rolled `foreachPartition { Map-count → zincrby }` block becomes `itemClickCounts(batch)` (`groupBy("item_id").count()`) + `RedisSink` writing one `ZINCRBY` per item. The `global:item_popularity` ZSET end-state per batch is identical; the now-dead logger + malformed-row try/catch are removed.

## Behavior preservation

The final review verified equivalence against source: old per-partition `zincrby(partial)` sums to the same per-item total as new `zincrby(total)`; the dropped try/catch is safe (upstream `normalize` already null-filters `item_id`); empty-batch behavior is unchanged. Note: `ZINCRBY` is non-idempotent on a `foreachBatch` retry — this was already true and is **unchanged** by this refactor.

## Scope / follow-ups (deliberately deferred)

`MovieLensContextCollectorStreamingJob`'s HSET (needs read-before-write merge — a genuine limitation of a fire-and-sync pipeline), the offline `RPUSH`/`SET` writers, and folding `RedisWriter` are explicit later PRs. The `writeRow` seam is confirmed reusable for those write-only ops.

## Testing

`RedisSinkSpec` (flush cadence, all four n/size cases) + `UserEventStreamingJobSpec.itemClickCounts`; existing `parseEvents`/`dedupedClicks` tests unchanged. Full module suite: **98/98 passing**.

Built spec → plan → subagent-driven TDD (per-task spec+quality reviews + opus whole-branch review; the review's two cosmetic Minors — an unused import and import ordering — were fixed and re-verified).

author: ggekos
body:
## Problem

A consumer with a large assignment cannot fetch: `ListOffsets` (the `endOffsets` / `seekToBeginning` positioning path) times out. A `kafka-to-snowflake` target subscribed to ~1453 single-partition topics failed with `TimeoutException: Failed to get offsets by times in 60002ms`, and because `auto.offset.reset=none` positioning resolves through the same call, the consumer never established positions and fetched nothing. With ~90 partitions/consumer the same request finished in a few seconds — a clear per-request scaling problem.

## Root cause

`Storage::list_offsets` for `DynoStore` resolves the request's partitions **sequentially** (`for (topition, offset_request) in offsets { … .await? … }`), ~1 object-store round-trip per partition steady-state. 1453 partitions × ~40–80ms ≈ 60–120s, past the 60s client timeout. Not un-cached — **un-parallelized**, O(partitions × RTT).

## Fix (`tansu-storage/src/dynostore.rs`)

Resolve the per-partition lookups with **bounded concurrency (32-way, matching `FOOTER_FETCH_CONCURRENCY`)** via `stream::buffered`. `buffered` (not `buffer_unordered`) preserves response order identical to the sequential loop; error semantics are unchanged (first per-partition error fails the request); each per-partition lookup is byte-for-byte the old code (moved verbatim into a `list_offset_response` helper). Expected wall-time for ~1453 partitions drops to ceil(1453/32) × RTT ≈ 2–5s. No on-disk format change, no Kafka wire change; these paths already run concurrently across independent client requests, so no new interleaving is introduced.

## Test

`wide_assignment_earliest_and_latest` — 64 single-partition topics on `memory://`, each with a distinct record count; one ListOffsets over the whole assignment per sentinel; asserts every partition is answered and EARLIEST == log-start (0) and LATEST == that topic's own high-watermark, so any cross-partition mix-up under concurrency fails loudly.

## Residual (follow-up, not in this PR)

Per cold-hint partition, LATEST still pays a `watermark.json` conditional GET (now 32-way parallel). If very-wide `endOffsets` becomes a per-poll pattern, serving the persisted-watermark floor from the segment index on the coalesced read path would drop it toward ~0 RTTs — a slightly riskier change left out here.

author: waseemmirzaa
body:
## What & why

Mobile audit Major (privacy) — M1 of the trial-screen cross-wire cluster.

The chat **"View trial"** banner opened `Routes.trial` with **no trialId**, so `TrialController.displayed` fell back to `selected ?? active` = the **first** active trial. Since the app allows two concurrent trials, a nanny (or family) engaged with two families who tapped "View trial" in **Family B's** thread landed on **Family A's** trial *and its day-proof grid* — and could upload today's childcare proof against the **wrong family's** record. That's a privacy leak and a data-integrity bug.

## Fix
The banner now passes **this thread's** `trialId` as the route argument, which `TrialController.onReady` → `openTrialById` uses to select the correct trial deterministically. `trialId` is guaranteed non-null whenever the banner renders (`hasActiveTrial` requires `trialId != null`), so the argument is always valid.

One-line-of-logic change: `_trialBanner()` → `_trialBanner(ChatThread thread)` and `Get.toNamed(Routes.trial, arguments: {'trialId': thread.trialId})`.

## Follow-ups (same cluster, separate PRs)
- **M2** — the trial screen's "Family" card shows the nanny's own name when a nanny views it (needs family-name resolution).
- **M3** — `Routes.trial` runs `FamilyBinding` (puts family-only controllers) even for a nanny (needs a role-agnostic binding).

## Verification
- `chat_screen.dart` brace/paren balanced; `ChatThread` already in scope (used by `_hireBanner`). Full validation via CI (Flutter analyze + test).

author: pinin4fjords
body:
## Summary

Makes in-section fan placement follow `diamond_style`, fixes the #1426 collapse, and orders exit-port bundle lanes by source geometry so peel lines don't cross the trunk:

- **`symmetric` mode → symmetric fan.** Fan eligibility keys off the lines that traverse the section's own trunk (`_section_fan_trunk_lines`), not the raw union crossing its ports, so a line a station only sends *out* of the section no longer inflates the bundle and disqualifies the fan. This is the #1426 defect on the riboseq map.
- **`straight` mode → continuing-holds-trunk.** The continuing pass-through holds the row trunk; the dead-end chain peels. Two straight-gated changes (`ordering.py` multi-hop spur recognition, `off_track.py` full-bundle-dead-end competitor). `shared_cell_fork_trunk_align` moves to `straight`, demonstrating #1423's behaviour under the mode that owns it.
- **Exit-port lane ordering by source height.** `_compute_exit_port_offsets` mis-picked a re-tagging station (one that receives lines and forwards them under new IDs) as the trunk feeder, pinning every line to its Y and dropping the peel lines onto the bottom lanes — so they crossed the trunk on the way out. The trunk-feeder test now requires the candidate to actually forward the port's lines (or that the unforwarded ones are fed from its own row); otherwise it falls back to spatial ordering (higher-fed line → higher lane). Peel lines now ride the lanes matching their producer's height.

## Fixtures / regression locks

- `out_of_section_retag_fan` (symmetric): metamorphic invariant (out-of-section retag leaves secA's fan identical) **plus** an exit-lane-order assertion (lanes fed from above sit above lanes fed from below) — the latter reds on base. Render: Salmon peels up, X/Y ride the top lanes out with zero crossings of the `a,b,c` trunk (verified by routed-path geometry).
- `side_branch_ascent_label_strike` (symmetric): restores #1449 ascent-clearance coverage (load-bearing: the label is struck if the clearance is disabled).

## Blast radius

Corpus render delta: 3 straight-mode fixtures (continuing-holds-trunk improvements) + `out_of_section_retag_fan` (crossing 6→0). Symmetric-mode fixtures byte-identical apart from the intended ones. Full suite green (39574). Guard goldens + gate baseline regenerated; benign idempotence gaps reconciled after merging main (#1021 folded away Stage 3.5).

Fixes #1426

## Follow-up

The exit-lane fix removes the crossing for a single downstream consumer. When the peel lines fan to *two* downstream nodes at different heights, a residual crossing remains at the downstream section's entry (a peel line descending to the lower node) — that is downstream entry-node / target-row ordering, tracked in #1530.

## Test plan
- [x] Full suite green locally (39574, Python 3.11)
- [x] ruff + ruff format + mypy clean
- [x] Metamorphic, exit-lane-order, and #1449 strike tests fail without the fix, pass with it
- [x] Routed-path crossing check: x/y vs a/b/c = 0 crossings
- [x] Corpus diff vs main: only the intended fixtures (all improvements) + 2 new fixtures
- [ ] Visual review of render preview

author: antoinefrau
body:
## Why

HAR could prove what happened inside a slot, but its primary identity was operational: a slot, worktree, run, or telemetry session. Those identities are intentionally short-lived and fragment when work is retried, moved to another agent, or inspected after teardown.

This change adds a provider-neutral work layer so Mission Control can answer a durable question: **what work was attempted, by whom, at what cost, and which exact Git tree proved it complete?** Issue trackers and agent methodologies still decide what to build; HAR owns execution and verification evidence.

## Identity model

```text
External issue → WorkUnit → WorkAttempt → Slot/worktree → Runs → ValidationBinding
```

- `WorkUnit` is a stable caller-provided identity with immutable source metadata.
- `WorkAttempt` is a fresh immutable UUID for each launch, distinct from observational telemetry `sessionKey` values.
- runs, slots, usage, events, and OTEL resources carry both IDs for correlation.
- `ValidationBinding` joins an attempt to reusable exact-tree proof without assigning validation ownership to one task.
- active, failed, and verified state is derived from evidence; only business outcomes such as completed or abandoned are explicit decisions.

## What changed

### HAR runtime and interfaces

- add canonical Zod contracts and local persistence for work units, attempts, outcomes, and validation bindings;
- extend CLI and MCP launch inputs with `workUnitId`, source, URL, title, and parent identity metadata;
- generate an attempt ID at launch and propagate both identities through scripts, slot state, runs, telemetry, sync, verification, and completion;
- prevent concurrent launches of the same work unit and require full validation proof before completion;
- retain provider neutrality: identifiers can represent GitHub, Linear, a local plan, or another planning system.

### Mission Control

- make **Factory** the home view, organized around durable work rather than infrastructure;
- add per-work evidence timelines joining attempts, runs, exact-tree validations, time, and cost;
- move the existing infrastructure-centric view to **Operations**;
- ingest work records and validation bindings alongside existing slot, run, usage, and event data.

### Compatibility and documentation

- preserve historical data: records without work identity remain visible in Operations and repository detail and are never guessed into work units;
- add an ADR for the identity and ownership decisions;
- update CLI, MCP, architecture, Mission Control, README, FAQ, and agent workflow docs;
- add a skill-pack compatibility guide and runnable showcase demonstrating that HAR complements Skills/Superpowers-style methodologies rather than replacing them.

## New flow

![Mission Control Factory overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/os-factory/har/feat/factory-control-plane/docs/public/assets/factory-overview.png)

A caller launches with a stable ID such as:

```bash
har env launch 1 \
  --work-id "github:acme/widget#123" \
  --work-source github \
  --work-title "Add saved filters"
```

HAR creates a fresh attempt, correlates execution evidence, binds successful full verification to the exact Git tree, and records completion before teardown. Retries remain separate attempts under the same durable work unit.

## Test plan

- [x] `har env verify 2 --full`
- [x] schema and work persistence unit tests
- [x] launch flag, telemetry, slot sync, and preflight tests
- [x] Mission Control typecheck, database sync, and Playwright Factory/Operations coverage
- [x] Docker and documentation validation through the repository harness
- [x] manual review with seeded completed and active work units

body:
## Summary

Closes `umbrella-donemd-backfill`: `done.md` for both umbrella dirs per CLAUDE.md «Umbrella closure convention», plus the closure measurement as `report.md` §9.

**Stage 2 is dropped, not deferred.** Report §5 proposes zero OBSOLETE-CANDIDATE rows, so the operator-confirmation queue the stage exists to drain is empty.

**The umbrella's premise is disproved by measurement, not by argument.** Re-ran `priority-score.sh` against the live panel at HEAD `ee4c3ee03` (post-#1117):

| bucket | count |
|---|---|
| synthetic candidates (open-questions, code-TODOs — not umbrellas) | 78 |
| `kickoff=missing` — never reach classification | 40 |
| real umbrellas (`kickoff=exists`) | 248 |
| ├─ classified DONE | 193 (183 `basis=done-md`, 9 `jaccard`, 1 `branch`) |
| └─ **open — what the panel shows** | **55** |

The kickoff's «~99 open umbrellas» was `287 dirs − 187 done.md` computed over *all* directories; the panel counts umbrellas carrying a `kickoff.md`. The real figure was **55** both before and after this umbrella ran.

**Net effect of Stage 1's 12 `done.md`: zero, verified 12/12.** Every target dir emits `<name> kickoff=missing` and the line terminates — no status field, and the C3 `done.md` layer is never consulted (`priority-score.sh:177-192`, pre-filter at `:139`). Mechanically incapable of helping, which is exactly the `KICKOFF-AMBIGUOUS` the cold fidelity auditor raised at Round 1.

The `done.md` convention itself is vindicated, not indicted: 183 of the 193 closures rest on it. The error was where it was applied.

## Incidental finding — T-UDB-C fires inside the C2 layer

Before this closure the panel already reported both dirs DONE on **false** evidence:

```
umbrella-donemd-backfill … status=DONE done_pr=1107 basis=jaccard score=100%
umbrella-donemd-backfill-meta-launch … status=DONE done_pr=1109 basis=jaccard score=100%
```

PR #1107 is this umbrella's own **kickoff-authoring** PR; #1109 is an unrelated marker fix. The jaccard title-overlap layer reproduces exactly the defect trap T-UDB-C names — «a PR-title slug match is not closure evidence» — so the trap is not only a human-reasoning hazard. These two `done.md` files replace the false match with real evidence, and the `:139` pre-filter now short-circuits both dirs before the expensive C2 pass runs.

## Handed to follow-up (not fixed here)

1. Kickoff Goal-vs-population contradiction (auditor's `KICKOFF-AMBIGUOUS`) — future backfill kickoffs must scope the population to kickoff-bearing dirs or declare documentation-only intent.
2. The live-signal rule has no squash-merge carve-out — «unmerged branch with commits ahead» literally matches the stale post-squash branch of a landed PR.
3. Panel readability, if ever wanted, is a grouping problem, not a backfill one: ~22 of the 55 open rows are the fan-out of seven programs (`shipped-artifact-liveness-gap*` 5, `install-*` 4, `getff-*` 4, `beta-*` 3, plus `plan-currency-reconcile-*`, `r2-*`, `preset-react-*` pairs).

## Test plan

- [x] `done.md` schema conformance for both files (`# <name> — DONE`, `Final PR:`, `Closed:`, `Summary:`)
- [x] `priority-score.sh` re-run at `ee4c3ee03` → `rc=0`, 366 lines; all 12 Stage-1 dirs verified emitting `kickoff=missing` individually
- [x] `state.md` cleared of `PENDING|TODO|AWAITING` markers → the synthetic `umbrella-donemd-backfill-meta-launch-state-pending` candidate no longer fires
- [x] `markdownlint-cli2` clean; `report.md` 249 lines (≤600 gate)

### §1.7 Skipped: this PR writes two `done.md` files and appends a measurement appendix to a report, all under `.claude/orchestrator-prompts/**` — outside the §1.7 discipline-file set, with no rule, principle, skill, agent, template, or CLAUDE.md surface introduced or extended, so no forward/backward discipline sweep applies.

## Fidelity verdict

FIDELITY: skipped — non-stage PR; an umbrella-closure record plus a measurement appendix, produced in-session with no aif substrate and no factory stage output whose WHAT could be audited against a spec

## What

Rebuilds the **Classes** page from a read-only Branch → Programme → Grade grouping into a filterable overview: a four-card stats header, Branch/Programme/Grade filters, debounced search, a sortable server-paginated table, and CSV export. All list state lives in the URL (shareable, back-button friendly).

Also flattens the sidebar nav into a single ordered list (the carried-over nav work).

## Requires

**nexchool/server#25** — this page consumes the new `GET /api/classes/` envelope plus `/stats` and `/export`. Deploy/merge the server PR first.

## Notes

- **Pickers unaffected:** `classesService.getClasses` still returns a plain array — it unwraps the new envelope and sends no `page`, so the structured class pickers keep receiving every row. Covered by `classesService.test.ts` (the unwrap fails soft to `[]`, which would silently empty those dropdowns, so it's tested rather than left implicit).
- **Stats from `/stats`,** not summed from the loaded page, so the header describes the whole filtered set.
- Extracts `useDebouncedValue` into a shared hook instead of a fourth copy.

## Fixes found while dogfooding

- **"All Branches" was a no-op** — clearing the branch fell back through the active-unit context and silently re-applied it. Now uses an explicit marker.

- **Queried before the active year resolved** — the list/stats hooks gated on tenant only; the backend reads a missing year as "every year", so a fresh load briefly pooled rows across archived years. Now gated on the year too.

`origin/main` merged in and the one conflict (`useClasses.ts`, from the toast-redesign mutation migration) resolved — my query hooks + the `useAppMutation` mutations now coexist. Full suite green (146) and `tsc` clean on the merged tree.

author: futuroptimist
body:
### Motivation
- Avoid billing a `macos-26` runner on PRs that do not touch the Metal-capable embedded Python runtime surface while preserving focused macOS verification when needed.
- Keep the focused native Metal bootstrap for relevant changes and `workflow_dispatch` (manual) runs and make the decision cheaply on Ubuntu before any macOS runner is allocated.

### Description
- Added a cheap detector job `detect-macos-metal-runtime-changes` that runs on `ubuntu-latest` with a 5-minute timeout, `permissions: contents: read`, a full-history checkout, and a stable output `run_macos_metal` that is true for `workflow_dispatch` and when paths match the relevant contract in `run-all-tests-pr.yml`.
- Gated the existing `macos-metal-runtime-bootstrap` job at the job level using `needs: detect-macos-metal-runtime-changes` and `if: needs.detect-macos-metal-runtime-changes.outputs.run_macos_metal == 'true'` while keeping the visible job name and `runs-on: macos-26` so relevant runs still get the same macOS bootstrap.
- Removed the macOS-side change-detection step and skip-summary step from the macOS job but preserved all actual bootstrap commands and invariants including `CMAKE_ARGS=-DGGML_METAL=on`, `FORCE_CMAKE=1`, the `arm64` assertion, runtime preparation, executable assertion, and `pip check`.
- Updated `tests/unit/test_workflow_ci_sentinel.py` to assert the detector runs on Linux, exposes `run_macos_metal`, that the macOS job is job-gated and still `runs-on: macos-26`, that `workflow_dispatch` forces macOS, that irrelevant changes do not request macOS, and that the old macOS-side detection/skip-summary steps are removed.
- Path contract preserved: macOS Metal bootstrap runs when changes touch `desktop-tauri/src-tauri/python/**`, `desktop-tauri/scripts/prepare_*python_runtime*` (the existing prepare-* pattern), `requirements.txt` at repo root, or edits to ` .github/workflows/run-all-tests-pr.yml`.

### Testing
- Ran the focused sentinel suite: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_workflow_ci_sentinel.py -q` and it passed: `33 passed`.
- Validated workflow YAML parsing with the repo loader: `python -c "import yaml; yaml.load(open('.github/workflows/run-all-tests-pr.yml').read(), Loader=yaml.BaseLoader)` succeeded and the workflow parsed with `3` jobs.
- Ran repository checks: `pre-commit run --all-files` completed successfully (project checks passed).
- Ran `git diff --check` and no whitespace/patch errors were reported.

Verification result and confirmation: the detector job now executes on `ubuntu-latest` and emits `run_macos_metal` which the macOS job consumes at the job level; therefore irrelevant pull requests no longer request or allocate a `macos-26` runner (the job is skipped by GitHub before runner allocation), while changes matching the preserved path contract and manual `workflow_dispatch` runs still cause the macOS Metal bootstrap to run.
