author: njengah
body:
## Summary

- Adds `memQrag/ingestion/chunking.py`: `chunk_document()` turns an `ExtractedDocument`'s segments into `Chunk`s using sentence-level semantic grouping, then enforces size bounds:
  - split each segment into sentences (lightweight punctuation-based heuristic, no NLTK/spaCy);
  - embed sentences and start a new group wherever cosine similarity between adjacent sentences drops below `0.5`;
  - merge any group under `MIN_CHUNK_TOKENS` (200) into a neighboring group;
  - split any group over `MAX_CHUNK_TOKENS` (800) back into multiple chunks at sentence boundaries.
- Adds `memQrag/ingestion/embeddings.py`: `embed_sentences()`, the default production embedder, using [`fastembed`](https://github.com/qdrant/fastembed)'s `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` model — chosen over `sentence-transformers` because that library requires PyTorch even with its ONNX backend (~600MB+ vs. ~50MB for fastembed's ONNX-runtime stack).
- The chunking algorithm takes the embedding step as an injected `EmbeddingFunction`, so its own tests use a small deterministic fake embedder (no network, no model download) while production code wires up the real `embed_sentences`.
- No SQLite/ChromaDB persistence yet — those are the next two Phase 2 items.
- Records both the embedding model choice and the chunking algorithm design in `docs/DECISIONS.md` ("Sentence Embedding Model For Semantic Chunking", "Semantic Chunking Algorithm").
- Updates `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "Current Shape".

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check .` — passes
- [x] `ruff format --check .` — passes
- [x] `pytest` — 45 passed:
  - 11 new tests in `tests/test_ingestion_chunking.py` (deterministic fake embedder) covering sentence splitting, similarity-based grouping, forward/backward merge of undersized groups, splitting oversized groups, per-segment metadata isolation, and empty-input edge cases.
  - 3 new tests in `tests/test_ingestion_embeddings.py` exercising the real `fastembed` model end-to-end; these skip gracefully (not fail) if the model can't be downloaded in a given environment.
- [x] UI lint/build unaffected (backend-only change), verified via `./scripts/check.ps1`

author: namu-k
body:
## Problem

Installing a global Claude guard blocked every built-in Claude Code agent type. The runtime guard denied any Agent spawn whose `subagent_type` was not a contract role (`UNCLASSIFIED_ROLE` → exit 2), so `general-purpose`, `Explore`, `Plan` and every skill that spawns them were refused the moment a guard was installed.

This contradicted two things already in the design:
- **Install-time audit** reports roles outside the contract as `unmanaged` and leaves them untouched, blocking installation only under `--strict`.
- **The Tier 1 boundary** (spec §195) does not claim to intercept every spawn path.

The runtime guard was unconditionally strict while the rest of the system treated unmanaged roles as out of scope.

## Change

The guard now enforces only the roles the contract actually routes:
- An unmanaged `subagent_type` is **allowed** and logged with `reason: UNMANAGED_ROLE`, not denied.
- A routed role must still declare a model that matches; a routed role with no model is denied `INVALID_AGENT_TOOL_INPUT`, an unmanaged role needs none.
- A non-string `subagent_type` is still `INVALID_AGENT_TOOL_INPUT` — nothing to look up.

Spec §9.4 is amended (v2.1) to record the pass-through rule and tie it to the §176/§207 audit philosophy.

## Verification

Full suite: 174 tests, 173 pass, 1 skipped (Windows-only). Against the built-in agent types from a real session, `general-purpose`/`Explore`/`Plan`/`claude-code-guide` all pass through while a contract-routed `executor` is still allowed only with its exact model and denied on a mismatch or a missing model.

This is a guard-semantics change (loosening), so it is a minor bump at release time.

...

### Description

Follow-up to #111007 (@rschu1ze asked to move the check into `MergeTreeSettingsImpl::sanityCheck`).

The `allow_experimental_codecs` gate for the codec-valued MergeTree settings (`marks_compression_codec`, `primary_key_compression_codec`, `default_compression_codec`) was enforced on CREATE in `registerStorageMergeTree.cpp`. This moves that CREATE-time enforcement into `MergeTreeSettingsImpl::sanityCheck`, right next to the existing lossy-codec validation of the same three settings.

`sanityCheck` runs on CREATE only, so the metadata-load paths that do not call it (short/full `ATTACH`, `SECONDARY_CREATE`, values inherited from the current `<merge_tree>` config defaults) keep a minimal counterpart in `registerStorageMergeTree`. The initiator-side `ALTER MODIFY/RESET SETTING` gate in `checkAlterIsPossible` is unchanged.

The session-level `allow_experimental_codecs` is not readable from the storage's global context inside `sanityCheck`, so it is threaded from `local_settings` through the storage constructors. The ALTER-apply path (`changeSettings`, also runs on replicas), the projections path (codec settings are not allowed there) and the server-startup config-default validation pass it as satisfied.

One intentional minor tightening: the old check lived only in the extended-definition branch, so a deprecated-syntax `MergeTree(date, key, granularity)` CREATE could still inherit an experimental codec from a `<merge_tree>` config default without the setting. Since `sanityCheck` runs for every CREATE, that corner of the config-default bypass is now closed too. It only makes an experimental codec correctly require its flag, so no valid workflow breaks.

Existing tests `04616_experimental_codec_in_merge_tree_settings`, `04617_experimental_codec_attach_full_definition` and `test_experimental_codec_config_default` cover CREATE, ALTER MODIFY/RESET, full/short ATTACH, the config-default-on-load gate, the stored-codec exemption and restart; the integration test gains a deprecated-syntax CREATE case.

author: mmcky
body:
Backfills the shared assets that the translation sync path does not carry across, so that [#202](https://github.com/QuantEcon/lecture-python.zh-cn/pull/202) can build and the next sync that adds a citation does not fail the same way.

## Why this edition's bibliography drifts

The sync workflow watches `lectures/**/*.md` and `lectures/_toc.yml`. Assets referenced *by* lectures — the shared bibliography, `_static/lecture_specific/**` data files, `_admonition/*` includes — are outside that set and have never crossed. The drift is invisible until a newly-synced lecture happens to cite something missing, at which point the strict build (`-n -W`) fails. Tracked upstream as QuantEcon/action-translation#117.

As of today this bibliography was **70 entries behind** `lecture-python.myst` (405 against 472).

## What #202 exposed

The Phillips Curve series cites 57 keys that were absent here, and `lectures/phillips_drifts_volatilities.md` loads a data file that raises `FileNotFoundError` by design when it cannot be found:

```python
    relative = Path('_static/lecture_specific/phillips_drifts_volatilities')
    ...
    raise FileNotFoundError(f'NEWQDATA.csv was not found; searched {searched}')
```

That cell is the one that produces `fig-csdv-inflation-persistence`, so its absence also produced an `undefined label` warning for a `{numref}` 1300 lines further down — both the figure definition and the reference are present and correctly translated, and the label was undefined only because the data never arrived.

## What this PR does

| | |
|---|---|
| Bibliography entries added | 70 (all missing upstream entries, not only the 57 this PR needs) |
| Data files added | `lectures/_static/lecture_specific/phillips_drifts_volatilities/NEWQDATA.csv` |
| Entries removed or modified | none |

Backfilling all 70 rather than the 57 required is deliberate: the remaining 13 are the next occurrence of this failure waiting to happen.

## Verification

- All 57 keys the failing build reported now resolve against the merged file
- Key count 405 → 475, no duplicate keys, brace-balanced
- Additive only — the three target-only keys (`GilboaSchmeidler:1989`, `Whittle_1981`, `Whittle_1990`, cited by `robust_permanent_income.md` and `theil_2.md`) are untouched

Note that this fixes one of the two reasons #202 is red. The other is its `_toc.yml` entry for a lecture the sync run failed to translate — QuantEcon/action-translation#156.

body: Related to CHE-517 ## Proposed Changes For Jetpack Backup T1 products and Security T1 plans, the classic manage-purchase page showed a single "Upgrade" button that pointed at the storage upgrade page (`/plans/storage`), leaving no path to a full plan upgrade. This splits it into two CTAs in both the plan header and footer areas for Calypso purchase management. A follow-up will be created for the Dashboard. | Before | After | | ----------- | ----------- | | | | | | | * Updates "Upgrade" buttons to "Upgrade plan" * Adds an additional CTA for "Upgrade storage" for Jetpack Backup and Jetpack Security ## Why are these changes being made? Storage-eligible Jetpack products (e.g. Jetpack Security with a 10GB storage tier) previously only surfaced a storage-upgrade CTA (introduced in https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/pull/58300), which blocked customers from moving up to a higher plan such as Jetpack Complete directly from the purchase page. Showing both the plan-upgrade and storage-upgrade CTAs gives a path to either action. While applying this I also found and fixed a latent bug in the original work: the storage-button eligibility guard used `||` (`! isSecurity || ! isBackup`), which — since a slug can only ever be in one of the two disjoint lists — always returned early, so the button never rendered. Corrected to `&&` (bail only when the slug is in neither list). ## Testing Instructions TC: ``` yarn test-client client/me/purchases/manage-purchase/test/purchase-management-buttons.js ``` Manual testing: * On the classic manage-purchase page (e.g. Jetpack Cloud `/purchases/subscriptions//`) for a Jetpack Security T1 plan or a Backup T1 product owned by the current user. * Confirm two buttons render: "Upgrade" → `/plans/` and "Upgrade storage" → `/plans/storage/`. * Confirm non-storage products (e.g. a regular plan) still show only the single "Upgrade" button, unchanged.

The feature GIFs on the README were sampled at 12fps to keep them small, which made the screencasts look choppy.

**Why 25fps.** GIF stores frame delays in hundredths of a second, so only divisors of 100 land exactly. 25fps is a 4cs delay: the smoothest exact rate at or under the 30fps sources, and comfortably above the short-delay floor browsers clamp. Verified each output reports exactly 25.0 fps.

**Cost.** Total payload across the five clips goes from 4.4MB to 7.2MB.

No prose or markup changed, only the five `.gif` binaries.

author: spencer-zqian
body:
## Problem

The dashboard shows CLI calls as **SDK (JS)**. Both first-party wrappers — `sonilo-cli` and `sonilo-video-kit` — construct a `SoniloClient`, and the SDK hardcoded `X-Sonilo-Client: sdk-js` with no way to override it. So CLI and kit traffic was indistinguishable from direct SDK use.

CLI and SDK users are different populations (scripts/ops/evaluation vs. product integration), and the split **cannot be recovered retroactively** — mixed history stays mixed. Catching this before `sonilo-cli` is published means its very first release is attributed correctly.

This mirrors [sonilo-python#12](https://github.com/sonilo-ai/sonilo-python/pull/12); the two SDKs had the identical hardcoding.

## Change

```ts
new SoniloClient({ clientName: "cli-js", clientVersion: VERSION })
```

Both options are optional and default to `sdk-js` + the SDK version, so direct SDK use is unchanged. `DEFAULT_CLIENT_NAME` is exported for callers that want the default explicitly.

| Caller | `X-Sonilo-Client` | `X-Sonilo-Client-Version` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct SDK use | `sdk-js` | SDK version |
| `sonilo-cli` | `cli-js` | CLI version |
| `sonilo-video-kit` | `videokit-js` | kit version |

A **caller-supplied** client keeps whatever identity its owner gave it — only the kit's internally constructed default clients (`duck.ts`, `generate.ts`) are tagged.

## Two version bugs found while wiring this up

**1. `version.ts` had drifted.** It read `0.4.0` while the package was `0.5.0`, so every request under-reported the SDK version. changesets bumps `package.json` only, and `version.ts` was hand-maintained, so the two silently diverged at the 0.5.0 release.

The existing test could not catch it:

```ts
expect(headers.get("x-sonilo-client-version")).toBe(VERSION);  // self-referential
```

It compares the header to the same constant the header is built from, so it stays green no matter how far `VERSION` drifts from the published version.

**2. `sonilo --version` printed the SDK's version.** The CLI imported `VERSION` from `sonilo`, so it reported what it wraps rather than itself.

**Fix:** all three constants are now generated from their `package.json` by `scripts/sync-versions.mjs`, chained onto the root `version` script:

```json
"version": "changeset version && node scripts/sync-versions.mjs && npm install --package-lock-only"
```

so changesets cannot bump one without the other. Tests assert each `VERSION` equals its `package.json` version — compared against the file changesets actually writes, not against itself.

## Required follow-up outside this repo

The dashboard's `RECOGNIZED_CLIENTS` is an allowlist that collapses anything unlisted to `"direct"`, so these values must be registered there or the traffic is **silently misattributed as Direct** rather than showing up as unknown. That change is prepared alongside this PR and adds `cli-js` / `videokit-js` (plus the Python names), so it can land first and classify this traffic from its first request.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` → sonilo 127 passed, sonilo-video-kit 137 passed, sonilo-cli 20 passed (5 new)
- [x] `npm run lint` (tsc) clean across all three packages
- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] Verified the headers actually emitted from the built bundle:
  ```
  SDK direct   X-Sonilo-Client=sdk-js        version=0.5.0
  CLI          X-Sonilo-Client=cli-js        version=0.1.0
  video-kit    X-Sonilo-Client=videokit-js   version=0.3.1
  ```
  (`0.5.0` confirms the drift fix — this reported `0.4.0` before.)

author: jpierreribeiro
body:
## Phase 7.5, Track A — A1..A3 (of A1→A5)

The outbound `http_client` Composition Crystal — the hard **E8-7** Phase-8 blocker and the **P0** production gap. An HTTP/1.1 client over a vendored `laytan/odin-http` **client+openssl BRIDGE** (the outbound mirror of ADR-033's server vendoring), wrapped in the bounded/timed/cancellable contract the BOM requires, with **certificate verification as an inseparable, fail-closed part of every `https` connection**.

### What ships
- **`vendor/odin-http` (BRIDGE)** — upstream `http` root (unmodified) + client message layer + OpenSSL FFI. `openssl/verify.odin` adds the peer-verification / trust-store / RFC 6125 hostname / post-handshake-verdict calls upstream's default context omits. `VENDOR.md` records provenance + the deletable-at-`core:net/http` exit.
- **`http_client` (A1/A2)** — `open`/`get`/`close` over a bounded pool with typed `Pool_Exhausted`, per-connect + per-request timeouts under one deadline budget, socket registration so a drain cancels in-flight reads, `Connection: close`.
- **`http_client/tls.odin` (A3)** — `SSL_VERIFY_PEER` + system trust store (+ optional CA anchor), SNI, `SSL_set1_host` hostname binding, `SSL_connect` fails closed, and a belt-and-suspenders `SSL_get_verify_result == X509_V_OK` recheck. `Insecure_No_Verify` is opt-in behind `allow_insecure_tls` for the difference control only.

### 🔒 The security invariant, proven
`build/check_http_client_controls.sh` (wired into `build/check.sh`) starts real `openssl s_server` peers:
- self-signed → **REFUSES** (`Tls_Cert_Invalid`)
- trusted chain but **wrong hostname** (cert is DNS:localhost, connected by IP) → **REFUSES**
- trusted **and** hostname-matching → **ACCEPTS** (200) ← positive control
- same self-signed peer under explicit `Insecure_No_Verify` → accepts ← difference control

A bad certificate fails closed. **Green:** plaintext 6/6, TLS 4/4.

### Recovery note
This branch was started by a parallel agent that stalled mid-A3. On takeover I found the verify *logic* sound but the **positive path failing**: the host passed to SNI / `SSL_set1_host` was the authority (`host:PORT`), so a good `DNS:localhost` cert was rejected as a hostname mismatch (`X509_V_ERR_HOSTNAME_MISMATCH`, 62). Fixed by extracting the bare host with `net.split_port`; debug tracing removed; the harness the agent referenced but never wrote is now in place.

### Not included (follow-up)
**A4** (metrics — Prometheus exposition) and **A5** (composition freeze + BOM reclassification `ABERTO→CRYSTAL`, which is the formal E8-7 satisfaction). This PR is the `http_client` half.

author: sammygill
body:
#### 743de0ac207deefbce5b1a927f0c07b0cfa43807 
[GFC] Store a grid item's resolved placement in UnplacedGridItem::GridPosition
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=320130
rdar://problem/183069388

Reviewed by Alan Baradlay.

Currently, UnplacedGridItem holds the information needed to resolve a
grid item's position in two different fields. These two fields are each
a std::pair of Style::GridPosition which holds the computed style for
the item's start and end position. Then when we are trying to determine
the actual position of the item we query the computed values multiple
times to determine what type of position it is (e.g. a definite position
like grid-column-start: 1) or an automatic position.

Instead what we can do is we can store the position in a dedicated type
that represents the type of position that it is when we create the
UnplacedGridItem. This will then make the implementation for the code
that is actually used during layout a lot simpler since we figured out
all of this information before we run layout. So most of this patch is
just introducing this new type and moving the logic that was used to
determine the type of grid position so that it is instead used to
construct this new type.

* Source/WebCore/layout/formattingContexts/grid/UnplacedGridItem.h:
(WebCore::Layout::UnplacedGridItem::GridPosition::GridPosition):
GridPosition is the new type that will hold all of the information
needed to correctly place the grid item during layout. It replaces the
computed values that were on the item. This new type will hold a variant
which is one of the two possible types it could be: a DefinitePosition
(e.g. grid-column: 1 / 2) which represents a specific spot in the grid
it needs to be placed or an AutoPosition in which we will use an
algorithm to find the appropriate spot.

(WebCore::Layout::explicitLineToIndex):
The line numbers in the spec are 1-index based but we store the
information as 0-indexed so this is just a tiny wrapper to help us
convert.

(WebCore::Layout::UnplacedGridItem::GridPosition::create):
This is the core logic that takes in the two computed style values we
were holding onto earlier which were being queried during layout and
instead creates a DefinitePosition or AutoPosition based upon that same
set of logic we were using during layout.

body:
PR Description
## Summary
- Automatically deploy immutable application images after successful `master` image publication.
- Reach production through an ephemeral Tailscale workload identity and restricted OpenSSH command.
- Keep OpenBao and other stateful infrastructure outside application deployment automation.

## What Changed
- Add an `Application Service Deploy` workflow triggered by successful container-image publication or manual dispatch.
- Verify deployment commits belong to `master` and image OCI revision labels match the requested full SHA.
- Package and apply checksum-verified forward migrations before replacing services.
- Recreate only `matching-engine` and `platform-runtime` with `--no-deps`.
- Pull and pin the simulator image without starting a simulation.
- Add a forced-command deploy SSH key installer that prevents shell access and forwarding.
- Restore previous application image pins when post-deployment health checks fail.
- Verify the OpenBao container identity and unsealed state before and after deployment.
- Add deployment audit logging and comprehensive operations documentation.
- Restrict container-image workflow triggers to image and migration-impacting changes.

## Validation
- `npm run infra:test:service-deploy`
- `npm run infra:test:deploy-receiver`
- `shellcheck infra/hetzner-core/server/scripts/deploy-application-services.sh infra/hetzner-core/server/scripts/install-github-deploy-key.sh`
- `node --check scripts/deploy/hetzner-core.mjs`
- `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; ARGV.each { |path| YAML.load_file(path) }' .github/workflows/service-deploy.yml .github/workflows/container-images.yml`
- `git diff --check`

## Scope Notes
- OpenBao is never restarted, recreated, upgraded, sealed, or unsealed by this workflow.
- PostgreSQL, Caddy, and the deployment receiver remain operator-managed.
- Simulator deployment only updates its image pin; execution remains explicit.
- Applied forward migrations are not automatically rolled back and must remain compatible with the previous application version.
- Activation requires one-time Tailscale workload-identity, tailnet-policy, GitHub environment, and restricted deploy-key setup.

author: sentilesdal
body:
## Summary

The dashboard HTML was served with **no `cache-control` header**, so a browser could cache a live dashboard's shell — including its client JS.

That's why the dashboard still looked broken after the hang fix (#317) landed: the browser was holding the **pre-fix page** and re-running the old client, showing "Loading…" forever, while the server was actually healthy and answering in ~1ms. Only `Cmd+Shift+R` cleared it.

## Fix

Serve the shell with `cache-control: no-store, must-revalidate`, so a restarted or fixed dashboard can never be masked by a stale cached page. (`/api/observability` already sent `no-store`.)

## Verification

- Response headers now carry `cache-control: no-store, must-revalidate` (confirmed via `curl -D -`).
- Page and API still serve normally.
- Independently confirmed the server itself was fine throughout: a fresh browser load against the user's running instance rendered full live data, and sequential requests measured 0.0057s → 0.0019s → 0.00096s (stale-while-revalidate working).

body:
## Summary

Adds **printable / PDF pay stubs** — an ADP-style earnings statement per pay period, viewable on screen, printable in-app, and exportable as PDF. It shows gross, net, pre-tax deductions, and the tax breakdown (**Federal, Illinois, Social Security, Medicare**) for **both the current period and year-to-date**.

The QuestPDF earnings-statement generator already existed (from earlier work); this PR closes the three gaps that stood between it and a real pay stub, and wires it into the Tauri app.

*Terminology note:* payroll withholding is Federal income, Illinois income, Social Security (FICA), and Medicare. There's no "Medicaid" withholding, so the breakdown is built around those four.

## The three gaps closed

1. **Per-tax YTD showed `—`.** YTD federal/state/SS/Medicare aren't stored on the stub, so they're now computed as-of-pay-date (`AggregationService.GetEmployeeYtdThroughAsync`, posted runs only) and assembled once by a new `PayStubStatementService` — the **single source of truth** for both the on-screen view and the PDF, so they can't disagree.
2. **Hardcoded placeholder SSN + address.** `Employee` now has address fields and an encrypted SSN; the PDF prints the real ones.
3. **Nothing was wired into the app.** New `get_pay_stub` / `export_pay_stub_pdf` sidecar commands + a frontend statement page.

## SSN handled responsibly

- Stored **encrypted via Windows DPAPI** (`ISsnProtector` / `DpapiSsnProtector`) — the OS holds the key, so there's no hand-rolled crypto and no key file to protect. Only the **last four digits** are kept in plaintext for display.
- The full SSN is **write-only**: sent only when entered, never returned, logged, or placed in the audit trail. A blank on update leaves the stored SSN unchanged. Tests assert the full SSN never appears in any response.
- Tradeoff (documented in code): DPAPI CurrentUser ties ciphertext to this Windows user+machine; a copied DB or lost profile leaves SSNs undecryptable (last-4 still readable, SSN re-enterable). Acceptable for a local single-user app; W-2 generation is out of scope.

## Frontend

- A pay stub page with Current + YTD tax columns and period/YTD summary blocks. **Print** uses `window.print()` with an `@media print` stylesheet that shows only the statement; **Export PDF** uses the native save dialog. Reached by clicking an employee row in a posted pay run.
- Employee form gains an **Address & Identity** section with a write-only SSN field that shows "on file" without revealing digits.

## Testing

- **143 domain + 44 sidecar tests** (both up), covering YTD-through-date (excludes later + voided), statement assembly (rejects non-posted), SSN round-trip + never-leaked, and a valid `%PDF` being written.
- **The main risk — QuestPDF/SkiaSharp in the published self-contained single-file sidecar — was verified**, not just assumed: piping `export_pay_stub_pdf` through the 104 MB published exe produced a real 67 KB PDF with per-tax YTD (Federal $156.15, SS $124) and the masked SSN `XXX-XX-6789`.
- The desktop app launches, resolves the fresh sidecar, and routes the new commands.

## Not verified

- The **rendered pay stub's visual layout** and the actual **print / save-dialog interaction** — those only happen in the running app, which I can't drive. Please open a posted pay run, click an employee, and check the on-screen statement, Print, and Export PDF.

## Scope notes

- The legacy WinUI form won't collect SSN/address (it's being retired); the shared DB gains the columns and the Tauri path populates them. The old 2-arg `GeneratePayStubPdfBytes` overload is kept so WinUI still compiles.
- Voiding a *prior* run changes a later stub's reprinted YTD (consistent with how the dashboard/reports already treat voided runs).

## Problem

Signing out of the AI Chat demo in a Coded App build did **not** return the user to the app. It landed them on the real UiPath portal instead.

## Root cause

`handleLogout` built `post_logout_redirect_uri` from `identityOrigin`, which for a Coded App is the **platform host** (e.g. `staging.uipath.com`). So identity redirected to `staging.uipath.com/portal_/cloudrpa` (the platform portal), never reaching the app's own `/portal_/cloudrpa` bounce page that restores the pre-logout path.

## Fix

- Point `post_logout_redirect_uri` at the **app's own** host + base path (`window.location.origin` + `/<coded-app-path>/portal_/cloudrpa`). The endsession endpoint still correctly uses `identityOrigin`.
- New `AICHAT_CODED_APP_PATH` const exposes the baked base path.
- Bounce page (`app/portal_/cloudrpa/page.tsx`): switched `router.replace` → `window.location.replace`. The stored return path already includes the Coded App base path, so Next's router would prepend `basePath` again and double it. This matches the sibling `auth_callback` page. The bug was latent because the bounce page was never reached before this fix.

## Deploy sequencing (important)

Identity will reject the new `post_logout_redirect_uri` until the coded-app host's post-logout URI is registered on Uber.Client (stg). That registration (`https://engdogfood.staging.uipath.host/*/portal_/cloudrpa`) is folded into the open **first-party-service-metadata** Coded App callback PR. **That metadata change must deploy before this merges to production.** Until then, sign-out behaves as it does today.

## Testing

- Biome check + `tsc --noEmit` pass.
- Full sign-out round-trip to be verified in a real browser on the engdogfood staging deploy once the metadata registration is live.
